title: Eagles' Jordan Davis Trade Raises Big Question About Panthers Keeping Derrick Brown
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles received a massive return for defensive tackle Jordan Davis prior to Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Jacksonville sent the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the defensive tackle that the Eagles selected in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft.
This move should be of interest to Carolina Panthers fans, considering that defensive tackle Derrick Brown was mentioned in various trade rumors prior to the deadline. Reports stated that several teams had inquired about the Panthers’ best defensive player.
While the Eagles received an offer that was too good to turn down, the Panthers decided not to move on from Derrick Brown. General manager Dan Morgan chose to keep one of the Panthers’ best players on the team.
Did the Panthers miss out on an opportunity with Derrick Brown after seeing the return that the Eagles got for Jordan Davis? There are some differences between the two players and the situations of the two teams that must be taken into consideration.
The Eagles received two valuable draft picks from Jacksonville for Davis, who had become an important part of their defensive line.
Davis was a member of the Eagles’ Super Bowl-winning team and was named a team captain in 2026, according to Philadelphia’s official announcement of the trade.
But Philadelphia had other players on the defensive line that it could use as well.
The Eagles have several other good defensive players on the team, including former first-round pick Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, and Ty Robinson. The Eagles had the depth at the position to make trading Davis an option.
The Eagles were 2-7 before the trade deadline. Adding future draft picks makes sense for a team that is in a difficult position right now.
Carolina wasn’t in quite the same position.
While Brown’s name was mentioned prior to the trade deadline, the Panthers were clear that they were not interested in trading the defensive tackle.
According to Athlon Sports' reporting on NFL insider Jordan Schultz, several teams inquired about Brown, but Carolina wasn't looking to move him.
The organization clearly believes in Brown.
The Panthers are already struggling with issues in the secondary due to injuries, and Carolina’s defense is not consistently putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Removing Brown would create another hole on Carolina’s defensive line.
The Panthers already have Brown under contract through the 2028 season, and he can be part of Carolina’s core of players as the team continues to build around him.
The Panthers have been trying to build a complete team for years, and trading away one of the team’s best defensive players would be a huge risk. There is no guarantee that a first-round pick would turn out to be as good as Brown.
While the Eagles had several options to replace the production of defensive tackle Jordan Davis, the Panthers do not have the same luxury with Brown.
There is still a legitimate argument that Morgan should have at least considered what another team might have offered for Brown. Jacksonville gave up two premium picks for Davis, and Brown is one of Carolina's best players.
There was interest in Brown from other teams, but that doesn't mean Carolina would have received the same offer Philadelphia got for Davis.
While Carolina received calls on Brown, there has been no confirmed report of a team offering a first-round pick and a second-round pick in a trade for him.
Another problem with trading Brown is that it would have left the Panthers with approximately $33.15 million in dead money on their 2026 salary cap, according to Athlon Sports, citing Over the Cap . That is roughly $22.2 million more against the cap than keeping Brown.
That’s a lot of money for a team that was already working with limited salary cap space.
Carolina entered the trade deadline leading the NFC South with a 3-5 record. While the Panthers have a lot of work to do, they are still in a position to compete for a division title.
Morgan would have had to compare the value of the future draft picks to the value of having Brown on the team, as well as the salary cap hit the team would take on by trading him.
The Panthers have eight picks in the 2027 NFL Draft to add young talent to the team, so the need to trade away one of the team’s best defensive players is not as great as it would be for the Eagles.
The Eagles made a good move by trading Davis for two valuable draft picks. But Philadelphia was in a better position to absorb the loss of a starting defensive tackle.
For Carolina, the decision wasn't quite that simple.
Unless another team was willing to offer something that Morgan simply couldn't refuse, keeping Brown was the better decision for the Panthers.

title: Why the Panthers Stayed Quiet at the Trade Deadline and What It Means for 2027
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were open to exploring a trade leading up to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. The team has been plagued by injuries, particularly at cornerback, and the Panthers have struggled to string together wins of late.
But when the 4 p.m. deadline came and went, general manager Dan Morgan hadn't made a trade.
The fact that the team could have used help, particularly on the defensive side of the ball, is not lost on fans of the Panthers. However, the salary cap situation of the team, as well as the 2027 draft picks that the team currently holds, may help explain why Morgan stood pat.
After losing three straight games, the Panthers were 3-5 heading into the deadline. Despite their losing record, the Panthers still held first place in the NFC South.
Many of the Panthers' needs were at cornerback. With Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson dealing with injuries, the Panthers could have used help at cornerback as well as with their pass rush.
Panthers head coach Dave Canales had stated earlier that the team was open to exploring possible trades. However, according to Panthers Wire's reporting, Canales explained that the front office had to consider what the team needed as well as what it could afford.
That doesn't mean the Panthers were going to make a trade just to make a trade.
The Panthers are in the midst of building a roster for several years, and a trade for a player who would only be on the team for a few months and cost a valuable draft pick might not make sense for the team. There is still a lot of work to be done on the current roster, and that would cost the team more than just this season.
They can still get players back from injured reserve. That is not to say that they will return to their previous form, but they can still be of value to the team.
This does not mean that Morgan made the right move. If the secondary continues to be a problem and the Panthers miss out on the playoffs, fans will be left wondering why the team didn't make a move when it had the chance.
But keeping those future assets could also end up being the better move.
One of the biggest obstacles for the Panthers was their salary cap. Carolina had limited cap space heading into the deadline, which would have made it difficult to bring in another high-priced contract.
The Panthers eventually made a financial adjustment.
For reference, the Panthers restructured Taylor Moton's contract to convert $5.3 million of his salary into a signing bonus. According to NFL Trade Rumors, citing Spotra c, that created roughly $3.5 million in additional cap space for the 2026 season.
The restructure created more space for the Panthers to sign players in the second half of the season, but that doesn't mean a trade was in the cards for the team.
Moton's reported 2027 cap hit will be approximately $30.2 million.
And that's the part of the decision that shouldn't be overlooked.
Even if the Panthers used the extra space to bring in a player, they could be taking on another contract as well as possibly giving up some draft picks. There are still many holes to fill on the current roster, and making a trade for a player who would only be on the team for a few months might not make sense for the team.
As previously discussed, the Panthers have invested quite a bit in this roster already, and there will be more decisions to be made in the offseason. Having some flexibility in terms of the salary cap will be key for Morgan in free agency.
The Panthers also have eight selections in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The official breakdown of the Panthers' draft picks includes the following:
Carolina has its original first-, second-, third-, fourth-, sixth- and seventh-round picks, as well as an extra fourth-round pick from the Vikings and a conditional seventh-round pick from the Eagles.
The extra fourth-round pick came in the Adam Thielen trade with the Vikings. Carolina sent its 2027 fifth-round pick to Minnesota as part of that deal, which is why the Panthers currently don't have a pick in the fifth round.
The additional seventh-round selection came in the trade that sent quarterback Andy Dalton to the Eagles in March.
The eight picks that Morgan will have to work with in the 2027 NFL Draft will allow him to add more young players to the roster at positions of need. He can also use the picks in trades to move up in the draft to get a prospect that he believes can be a starter right away.
In terms of the current roster, the Panthers have a lot of needs at cornerback and pass rusher, as well as on the offensive line. They also have a lot of decisions to make on the current roster.
Having more selections at least gives the Panthers more opportunities to improve the roster without taking on expensive veteran contracts.
While some fans may have wanted the Panthers to make a trade before the deadline, it's worth noting that the team was still in first place in the NFC South. Another defensive player could have helped the team's chances of making the playoffs.
But the Panthers were also 3-5 and had shown there's still plenty of work to do before they could become a consistent contender.
As previously discussed in the Panthers on SI story about the loss to the Denver Broncos, Carolina was weighing whether to trade for a short-term fix to try to win now or to keep its assets to try to build a long-term contender.
Morgan didn't make a trade, so the Panthers will have to make do with what they have, as well as the injured players who return.
If the Panthers win the division and make the playoffs, there probably won't be many complaints about what happened at the deadline. But if injuries continue to pile up and the defense struggles, Morgan's decision will be a hot topic.
For now, Carolina still has eight draft picks in 2027 and some additional cap space to work with this season. Whether standing pat was the right move will depend on what happens over the next several weeks and how Morgan uses those resources when the offseason rolls around.

title: The Panthers Are Going to Regret Not Trading Away These 4 Players
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers watched the trade deadline come and go without so much as a peep. Reportedly, they received calls for Derrick Brown, but he was understandably unavailable (although the price Jordan Davis went for was pretty impressive). Whether or not they received calls on others, they might regret not flipping some players at the deadline.
It's certainly true that the Panthers may not have been able to get anything for these players, but it's hard to imagine that they couldn't have gotten a seventh-round pick or anything if they'd shopped them around at least.
In many instances, the Panthers have players who either aren't playing or shouldn't. And in some of those cases, addition by subtraction would be great, plus bringing back some more draft capital is always smart. Instead, the Panthers didn't make a single move .
Ja'Tavion Sanders has been a healthy scratch every week until last. It seemed like a showcase for a potential trade. No one in the NFL needed a depth tight end on a rookie deal with some upside? That's hard to believe, and anything would be better than a healthy scratch. He just doesn't seem to have a future, even though his immediate superior is 34-year-old Darren Waller.
The Panthers are currently healthy scratching AJ Dillon, and Jonathon Brooks is coming back soon. Why they didn't trade him is a shock. The NFL's worst running attack is his former team. Plus, those who missed out on Jonathan Taylor might've been fine with a seventh-rounder for Dillon to offset the loss. Dillon has been solid when called upon, and plenty of teams could use him for a low cost.
This would've been a tougher sell, but the Tennessee Titans got a second-round pick for Amani Hooker. Tre'von Moehrig isn't as good, but there was obviously room to bring back a decent haul. Plus, Moehrig seems like a likely cut candidate this offseason with Zakee Wheatley already a good replacement today.
The interior depth is in shambles right now, but the Panthers just might regret not checking about Robert Hunt's market. He's been much worse this year, perhaps a product of playing next to a rookie. In a situation where that's not the case, he'd likely be better, but as of now, he's a bad, bloated contract. The Panthers could've escaped a looming cap conversation with a move here.

title: Despite Doing Nothing, Panthers’ NFC South Title Chances Grew at Deadline
full_text:
There is one division in the National Football League where all four teams are each at least three games over .500. That would be the formidable NFC North, led by the 7–2 Chicago Bears, a pair of 6-2 teams in the Detroit Lions and the Minnesota Vikings and the 6-3 Green Bay Packers.
Then there’s the other side of the coin. There’s a division in which all four clubs are at least two games under 500. Both the Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints, who face each other this week in the Superdome, own 3-5 win-loss records. Just behind them are the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Atlanta Falcons, each with a 3-6 résumé.
It’s certainly anyone’s guess who is going to emerge as the winner of this mess, and with what record? Keep in mind that twice in the previous four seasons, the 2022 Buccaneers and the 2025 Panthers were crowned champions with 8-9 marks.
On Tuesday afternoon at 4:00 pm ET, the window closed when it came to trading players. Both the Saints and Falcons were involved in deals earlier this week. On Monday, New Orleans sent defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a conditional 2028 sixth-round selection.
Meanwhile, Atlanta traded former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates, tied for the team lead with 60 tackles, to Jacksonville for a second-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round choice in 2028. The Falcons were also involved in a deal on Tuesday in which they acquired guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick for center Ryan Neuzil from the Baltimore Ravens.
On the other hand, the Panthers, who suffered their third straight loss on Sunday, sat on their paws and made no deals to fortify their injury-riddled roster. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain on injured reserve, as does right tackle Taylor Moton. Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has missed the last three games. This is a banged-up football team.
Nonetheless, general manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales appear to be content with the hand they have been dealt to date. Perhaps an even bigger point is the fact that both the Saints and especially the Falcons were willing to part ways with performers that could certainly help a side of the ball that seems to be each club’s weak spot.
Entering Week 10, the Saints are 29th in the league in total defense, are allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game and giving up the fifth-most passing yards per contest. The Falcons are 23rr in total defense and have already surrendered 24 offensive touchdowns in nine games.
This Sunday at the Superdome, Bryce Young and company look to get back in the win column and raise their record within the division to 2-1 with a victory over Kellen Moore’s team, who swept Carolina in 2025. Apparently, the shorthanded but still-talented Panthers are content to play with the hand they’ve been dealt— and it may indeed prove to be the right strategy.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Panthers Made a Huge Mistake at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone , and the Carolina Panthers roster looks the exact same. No moves were made by a Carolina team that's on a three-game skid , sitting at 3-5 this season, and somehow still at the top of the NFC South.
No matter where a team sits in its division, 3-5 isn't good enough, especially for a Carolina team that made the playoffs in 2025. The roster is riddled with injuries, something no one wants to see.
However, Carolina could have addressed those holes in the roster with plug-in players who wouldn't cost absurd draft compensation.
Now, with the roster intact, Carolina has to roll with what they got, and in some areas, there's very little depth because the depth chart is so thin at positions like the secondary.
Another puzzling piece of this is that Carolina has its draft capital. The Panthers were never going to make some big swing at a Jonathan Taylor or someone else who warrants a first-round pick, but could've added some solid depth at areas that need it.
Carolina has four cornerbacks injured right now; three of them are on IR, including starters Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn. The secondary proved to be a massive problem against the Denver Broncos.
On obvious passing downs, such as third-and-long situations, the Broncos targeted Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton. Even when they didn't complete a pass, the Broncos drew penalties against defensive backs who don't get in-game reps against high-level opponents.
Adding a corner like Riq Woolen, a proven starter who was part of a Super Bowl defense in 2025, made perfect sense for Carolina. Other corners like Alonte Taylor or Keisean Nixon would've made sense.
Another helpful move would've been to address the pass rush, since Carolina only has only 12 sacks this season. The Panthers could've done so by targeting Will McDonald IV of the New York Jets. Khalil Mack from the Chargers would've been nice too, but it became clear leading up to the deadline that the Chargers weren't going to be sellers.
Speaking with the media on Monday, the Panthers' head coach said that he's opening the 21-day practice window for WR Xavier Legette. Furthermore, Canales added that both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn "are close," which is fantastic news.
However, Carolina needs to find wins now, and adding another corner while Jackson and Horn ramp back up would've been ideal. Over the next month, Carolina faces elite receivers like Chris Olave, Zay Flowers, and Justin Jefferson. Carolina will need its starting secondary sooner rather than later.
The Panthers head to New Orleans for a crucial division matchup with the Saints on Sunday.

title: The Panthers Trade Deadline Showed Us Exactly Who They Are
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers, for the second straight year, stood pat at the deadline. Despite having rampant needs on a first-place (shockingly) team and expendable players they could've used to bring in draft capital, they did nothing.
The division is so open that either path would've been smart. The Panthers could afford to offload a few players to get picks for the future without mortgaging their chance to defend the NFC South crown. But they're also in first place with a host of injury-related needs, so adding players to bolster the first-place roster would've been good, too.
Instead, the Panthers sat on their hands. They were aggressive over the offseason, signaling that they felt the division was theirs to take. Now, when they had another chance to be aggressive and take hold of the South, they balked.
It is so clear that this team is a playoff contender when semi-healthy. They have the offense to score with anyone so long as Bryce Young gets a modicum of time in the pocket. They have the pieces on defense to get stops when needed as long as they have functioning cornerbacks.
This is a team that beat the Detroit Lions with no cornerbacks . It's a team that nearly beat the Green Bay Packers despite a roughly 50% pressure rate surrendered by the offensive line. They are a couple of plays away from having a really good record.
Now, if they were 3-5 in the NFC North, you could dismiss the argument that they're close to being a good team because that division is so good. But in the NFC South, that argument should be everything. It should be evidence that a couple of additions would be game-changing.
It's not like the Panthers need to add Jonathan Taylor or Maxx Crosby. They're not looking for a quarterback like the Minnesota Vikings are. And they don't need superstar, long-term additions.
They need a cornerback who can play at the NFL level for a few weeks and some people who can block. Offensive line depth is low around the NFL, but we're not asking for Quenton Nelson here.
There's obviously a lot more to it than just seeing a need and addressing it, but the Panthers didn't seem to try. They were content taking advantage of being in a bad division and remaining a bad team.
But at the same time, not trading away Ja'Tavion Sanders or AJ Dillon makes little sense, either. They want to have their cake and eat it, too.
In other words, they showed everyone exactly who they are and who they want to be.

title: 3 Bold Panthers Predictions That Could Turn Their Season Around Against the Saints
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers must answer some questions as they take on the New Orleans Saints Sunday. The Panthers dropped their third straight game to the Denver Broncos but are still in first place in the NFC South with a 3-5 record.
This game is extremely important for both teams. New Orleans is 3-5 and won a tough game against the Browns 23-22 in overtime. Carolina is 3-5 and lost to the Broncos 26-21.
Both teams are having a very rough season, but the winner of this game can start to build something for the second half of the season.
Here are three bold predictions for the Panthers vs. Saints.
Young had a tough game against Green Bay, completing 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He was sacked six times.
Things were a lot better for Young in the Denver game as he completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. However, he was still sacked three times as the Panthers' offense struggled at times to get things going in the passing game.
Young has six games this year with more than 250 passing yards. The offense can be good when Young has time to make plays, but the offensive line hasn't been giving him enough time of late.
The Saints have struggled defensively the last few games, and Carolina must take advantage of that. If Young has time to throw the ball and the Panthers don't fall behind early, then Carolina should be able to make some plays against the Saints' secondary.
Prediction: Young throws for at least 251 yards and two touchdowns.
The defense has been playing poorly over the last three games, giving up 96 points during that stretch. Carolina cannot afford another game where the defense gives up too many points.
As for the defense, it doesn't have to be perfect, but it does need to get some turnovers for the offense. Young needs to get the ball back without having to drive the length of the field for every touchdown.
The Saints have struggled with turnovers this season, and the Panthers have to make them pay for it. A forced fumble or an interception in a key moment of the game could really turn things in the Panthers' favor.
One thing that the Panthers' defense must do is make the Saints earn every point. Carolina can't allow the Saints to have another big day on offense.
Prediction: The Panthers force two turnovers, including one in the second half.
The Panthers have lost their last three games to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Green Bay Packers, and Denver Broncos. Even with Young having a solid game against the Broncos, the Panthers were not able to get the win.
This is a game that the Panthers must win in order to continue their quest to win the division. The Saints are also struggling, and Carolina cannot afford to lose to another struggling team.
While the Panthers don't have to play a perfect game, they must avoid some of the mistakes that have cost them in recent games. If the defense can come up with some stops, Young and the offense should be able to put up enough points to win the game.
The Panthers need to win this game on the road to get back on track and start to build some momentum for the rest of the season. This game against the Saints will be followed by a game against the Baltimore Ravens, so it's important for the Panthers to get a win here.
Prediction: Panthers 27, Saints 24.
The Carolina Panthers are in a difficult situation, but it is still possible to turn things around. New Orleans would be a good place to start.

title: Jeffery Simmons' Leadership, Trash Talk on Display in Mic'd Up Video From Bears vs. Bucs
full_text:
Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was mic'd up for his second game with the Chicago Bears when they took on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night in Week 9.
Not only was it his second game with the Bears, but also the first Simmons has played as a member of the home team at Soldier Field.
In the video shared by the Bears, we see a bunch of notable things, including how thrilled Simmons is to be in Chicago.
We also get to hear Big Jeff trash-talking Bucs offensive linemen for their inability to stop him despite double- and triple-teaming him, and we get a good idea of the leadership Simmons brings.
Check out the full video below.
The Bears went on to win the game , 27-24, in what was a too-close-for-comfort finish.
Chicago looked to be in control early, but the Bucs slowly climbed their way back into the game as Caleb Williams struggled en route to tossing four picks .
Luckily, Simmons and the defense played at a high level and kept the Bucs from fully taking advantage of Williams' turnovers.
Simmons once again made a massive impact, with the superstar defensive lineman notching four tackles, one sack, one QB hit, three pressures, one pass defensed and one tackle for loss.
Simmons now has two sacks in two games for the Bears, which is one more than Bears interior defenders had combined in the first seven games.
He's also proving to be a huge asset when it comes to helping the guys around him, as the double teams he draws are freeing other defenders up to make plays.
With each snap, the Bears' decision to give up a historic package for Simmons is looking better and better.
As we noted, the Simmons trade was historic. That's because no team in the common draft era (since 1967) had ever traded multiple first-round picks for a defensive tackle.
As the trade deadline came and went, the Bears did not make another trade despite being linked to interest in cornerbacks .
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday that the trade for Simmons definitely played a part in Chicago's quiet deadline day.
"For the Bears, once they did the Jeffery Simmons deal, that was kind of it," Rapoport said . "That was kind of the only draft compensation they were gonna give up."
A quiet deadline would normally anger fans, but when it comes to Bears fans, they are so thrilled with the acquisition of Simmons that it's hard to have an issue this time around.
Fans wanted to see an all-in move from general manager Ryan Poles and they got exactly that. As a result, Poles is going to receive a lot more grace moving forward.
The one need we would have liked to see the Bears address was at cornerback, where Jaylon Johnson's struggles leave a major concern.
But Johnson did notch a pick-six against the Bucs, so maybe that will be enough to get him going. And, having Simmons getting after the quarterback should help the back end, also.

title: There's Actually More to Transformed Bears Defense Than Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
The Jeffery Simmons effect has been noticeable for the Bears defense in the last two games , as their own four-man pressure amps up and yards per rush against them declines.
There is more rush making the coverage aspect of rush-and-cover easier.
"He presents a physical presence on the inside of our defense, run and pass, and that's a good feeling to have," defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said.
Still, before Simmons this never was a defense struggling to simply get by while being propped up by the Bears offense, as many suggested during the last few weeks prior to the Simmons trade. It's reflected in their defensive team statistics. The trend was already positive for this group before Simmons and it only figures to improve in the second half.
Jeffery Simmons is a PROBLEM. 💪 📺 Sunday Night Football: Buccaneers at Bears on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/82MjdDopdn
Last year takeaways saved the Bears defense when it lacked the ability to stop the run or defend the pass. This year they've improved at both and haven't needed  takeaways to rescue them. This is where the critics of their offseason improvement failed to show any foresight whatsoever. They were saying the Bears couldn't repeat last year's "lucky" defense that took it away so much but they didn't see past the end of their noses to realize the defense was improved and wouldn't need to rely only on takeaways.
In fact, the Bears defense has been so good that they've been able to withstand an offense that has turned the ball over the third most times in the league (17).
JAYLON JOHNSON HOUSE CALL ☎️ 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/FVkfIjPwvQ
Considering how much criticism Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson receiver, or their supposed lack of a pass rush prior to Simmons was cited, they are ninth overall at 310.9 yards allowed per game, up 20 spots from last year when they were 29th at 361.8 yards allowed per game. Also, they're better against the run by far, at 91.3 rushing yards allowed per game for sixth in the league, 43.2 yards per game better than last year when they were 27th.
While their run defense needs to be better than 22nd in yards allowed per carry at 4.4, they are greatly improved there from 29th last year at 5.0. And they're trending up here because they have allowed just 82.4 yards rushing over the last five games and 4.0 per rush in the last five, which is 14th in the league. With Simmons now added, it only figures to improve.
OK defense this is more fun: I'm gonna start with a general pass D cutup. Lotta their staples. Mugs with c2 behind it, more quarters, some man. It has become very varied. Tons of execution errors by Baker/pass catchers too though. I liked our front/LBs play, as well as Lewis pic.twitter.com/eyTrdgDoC8
The end result of all of this has been a phenomenal improvement in third-down defense from 40.84% and 22nd in the NFL to No. 1 by a very wide margin. At 22.83%, the Bears are a whopping 7.75% better than Seattle, the next-best team. It makes up for fewer takeaways but more importantly fixes the league-high 17 turnovers their offense has committed.
Expect more of the same approach from Allen as the season goes on as in recent games. They'll continue to blitz, though not at the ninth-highest level in the league like they have (31.3%).
"I think in a perfect world scenario the more resources you can send back there in coverage and still be able to affect the quarterback, I think that's, you know, probably the greatest advantage and yet I think you have to have a combination and mixture of both," Allen said.
Jeffery Simmons doing some talking after that last third down stop for the Bears' defense. pic.twitter.com/6rTMd1GhRR
The defense is better because of better people. Beside Simmons, linebacker Devin Bush has gradually improved and finished the first half with three strong games.
"Our big guys are running out of the stack chasing after the ball; we have our little guys playing big and making tackless on the perimeter," coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday while making an appearance on Fox Sports' First Take with Danny Parkins. "I think its really raising the level of play from our whole unit."
Besides better overall play and Allen's defensive scheming between pressure and no pressure, there could be an added factor that has helped the Bears defense rise to ninth overall at 310.9 yards a game. Johnson talked about it in his First Take appearance.
Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya
"You know, you talk about being the head coach and certainly as the offensive play caller I'm more inclined on that side, and yet trying to bring all three phases together to play a complete game, I think that's where certainly I've grown from Year 1 to Year 2," Johnson said. "But having great, strong leadership on the pther phases really makes my job easier, as well."
With effective direction and impactful coaching, the Bears' defense is heading in the direction it needs going into the second half five four tough NFC North games to come in their final eight.
And it doesn't hurt having someone doing what Simmons has shown, whether he's running upfield chasing a quarterback or chasing a ball carrier downfield as he did so effectively to prevent Tampa Bay receiver Emeka Egbuka from scoring on a screen pass on Sunday.
@DannyParkins : “Does any part of you hesitate knowing that [wanting shutouts] is going to put a target on you and your team’s back?” Ben Johnson: “Absolutely not. If there’s any other offensive play caller in the league that doesn’t feel that way, then they’re full of BS." pic.twitter.com/UMXuIKeczK

title: How a Message from Ben Johnson's Dad Underlines Bears' Super Bowl Aspirations
full_text:
It's a good thing for the Chicago Bears that ugly wins count all the same as dominant wins. Their undeserved Week 9 win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday was about as ugly as it gets, and some fans and NFL analysts may be tempted to see it as a sign of worse things to come. The Bears finally got exposed by a good defense, so the doubters say, and others will simply duplicate that formula.
First of all, that's not going to happen. Not every team has a defensive genius like Todd Bowles calling the plays, or a game-wrecking defensive tackle like Vita Vea. You can also bet your bottom dollar that Caleb Williams' career-worst four picks in that game won't be repeated any time soon.
Second, head coach Ben Johnson received a message earlier this week that should resonate throughout the Bears' locker room and even the fanbase. While speaking to NFL analyst Danny Parkins on the First Things First sports show , Johnson said that his dad shared a quote with him after they beat the Bucs: 'Only mediocre people can be at their best all the time.'
There's a quiet brilliance in that quote that takes a moment to reveal itself. What Johnson's dad is really saying is that those who chase greatness will routinely fall short while those who are comfortable with mediocrity can coast along without much effort. That's what we saw on Sunday night from the Bears, or Caleb Williams in particular. Williams was chasing greatness, as he has before, but this time he failed. It's going to happen, and he's going to bounce back.
This message harkens back to arguably the most famous quote from the greatest athlete in Chicago sports history (for now), Michael Jordan, who said, "I've missed more than 9000 shots in my career. I've lost almost 300 games. 26 times, I've been trusted to take the game winning shot and missed. I've failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed."
As a matter of fact, Caleb Williams referenced this Michael Jordan quote after last year's Week 14 loss to the Green Bay Packers, when he had a chance to throw a go-ahead touchdown but threw an interception instead. Two weeks later, Williams responded by throwing an iconic game-winning touchdown to DJ Moore to beat the Packers in overtime.
This team was not built for mediocrity. General manager Ryan Poles could have played it safe in the past and drafted a different quarterback, one who didn't occasionally trust his arm too much. He could have hired a merely competent head coach, one who didn't take so many gambles on fourth-down. But he didn't. Poles pushed all his chips into the center of the table, betting on ambitious men to chase greatness, chase perfection even, and one day achieve it.
Sunday was a bad game for Williams and the Bears' offense, no doubt about it. And while fans never want to see bad games from their quarterbacks, it's going to happen. Even seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady has six four-interception games to his name. Falling flat on your face goes hand in hand with the pursuit of greatness.
That's the message that Ben Johnson's dad wanted to convey to him, and it's something that the entire team can take to heart. It's okay to fail on their quest for a Super Bowl title, especially if their failures still end up in the win column. That's the mark of a truly great team, and now it's on them to come back in Week 11 after their bye week and prove to the world that there is no formula to beating the Bears. You can only hope they'll beat themselves.

title: Bears Trade Deadline Decisions Create 3 Bold Predictions for Second Half of 2026
full_text:
Despite weeks of speculation, the Chicago Bears did not make any moves on the day of the trade deadline, not even a highly anticipated trade for Khalil Mack . But they can be forgiven their inaction, considering the fact that they already swung big with their blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons two weeks ago. For his part, Simmons has already provided a strong return-on-investment with two sacks in as many games while being double-teamed on almost every snap.
The Bears still have roster concerns that went unaddressed at the deadline, and they'll face some real challenges in the second half of 2026 , but Bears fans have every reason to be optimistic about the rest of the season. With that in mind, here are three bold predictions for the Bears after the trade deadline.
Simmons was already considered a strong Defensive Player of the Year (DPOY) candidate when he was still languishing on the one-win Tennessee Titans. Since his trade to Chicago, his arrow has pointed nearly straight up. As aforementioned, he already has two sacks in two games, and he came close on several other opportunities. And after the Bears' Week 9 win, Simmons officially put the NFL on notice .
If the Bears continue to win and Simmons' bright orange sleeves continue to be seen around opposing quarterbacks, I can't imagine any other defender claiming the top prize over Simmons. He was already considered an elite defender, and now he's finally getting to prove it on a national stage, playing back-to-back primetime games after going three years without one.
After the Bears' Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers, I wrote that Ben Johnson has a rivalry problem . He's just 2-6 in regular season games against NFC North rivals since becoming head coach of the Bears, and two of the losses were absolute blowouts.
However, I think there's reason to believe that this won't be a problem for much longer. In fairness to Johnson, his Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings was mostly due to heavy rain during the game and Caleb Williams tearing his hamstring. Against the Packers, he didn't have Williams at all. If he'd never been injured, it's reasonable to say that the Bears would be undefeated right now.
With that in mind, and with Williams now healthy and backed up by a superstar defensive tackle, I'm predicting that the Bears will win their final four rivalry games this year, which will be more than enough to boost them to their second straight division title.
I did say bold predictions, didn't I? Then let's get bold. The Bears are going to win Super Bowl LXI. It's practically written in the stars. Everything has been aligning for this moment, to seize a Super Bowl championship exactly 20 years after their heartbreaking loss to the Indianapolis Colts in Super Bowl XLI. Even the Roman numerals are the same!
And I'm not alone in this, either. Sports Illustrated published a midseason report on surprises, storylines, and Super Bowl predictions , and five out of their eight analysts picked the Bears to make the Super Bowl, with two, Mitch Goldich and John Pluym, picking them to win.

title: Bears Take Look at Former Starting Tackle Among Others With Tryouts
full_text:
Former Jeffery Simmons Tennessee Titans teammate Jordan Elliott wasn't the only player the Bears took a look at Tuesday during a bye-week tryout at Halas Hall.
A group of players worked out, including a former offensive line starter for the Raiders and 49ers.
Linebacker John Bullock, defensive back Darren Hall, tackle Ryan Hayes, center Michael Niese, tackle Brandon Parker and defensive back Robert Rochell all had Halas Hall tryouts, per the NFL daily personnel ticker.
Parker is 31 years old and was a third-round pick of the Raiders in the 2018 draft. He started 33 games out of the 59 he played for the Raiders from 2018-2023, including 12 at right tackle as a rookie and 13 in 2021 at that position.
Brandon Parker flat backs Bradley Chubb. He might struggle in pass pro but he’s been a mauler in the run game. Rookie on rookie crime. pic.twitter.com/q9P0AZIM9S
A torn triceps kept him from playing in 2022. An undisclosed injury cost him most of 2023 when he went on injured reserve.  He was out of the league in 2024 and 2025 and the 49ers had him on the practice squad this training camp before cutting him.
Hall, a cornerback and safety, was a fourth-round Falcons pick who spent four years there, then played for Arizona two years and Washington this season before being released. He had 12 starts in 49 games and 95 tackles.
Hayes was a seventh-round tackle for the Dolphins who came out of Michigan in the 2024 draft but has also been with the Colts, Titans, Falcons and Panthers, mostly on practice squads. He has appeared in only one game.
Darren Hall goes up and gets the INT for the @AZCardinals ! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wf7IFjq58l
Niese has some familiarity with Bears coach Ben Johnson as a former backup lineman for him in Detroit in 2023 and 2024. He was also with Detroit in 2025. He has been in 26 games without a start.
Rochell is a long-time NFL backup defensive back who was on the active roster for the Rams, Packers, Cowboys and Panthers between 2021-25. He made his only career interception as a rookie in 2021. He made 31 career tackles.
Bullock played in 15 games last season for Tampa Bay, playing a role in special teams.
Michael Niese right knee injury video -Concern for MCL sprain. Unlikely ACL. Able to hobble off. pic.twitter.com/xW79ba7yge
Elliott was easily the most well known of the group after he had 11 tackles this season with Tennessee in the first five games and 159 for his career in 102 games with 65 starts for the Browns, 49ers and Titans. He was said to have pulled out a gun after an incident several days earlier at the practice facility.
“He’s a good man, made a terrible, had a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act,” Titans coach Robert Saleh told Titans reporters, according to NFL.com. "He’s never committed a crime in his entire life and he pulled a gun, in the parking lot.”
While Saleh defended Elliott's character, he had to admit this lapse in judgment wasn't allowed.
Jordan Elliott signed a 2-year $8 million contract in March... 217 days later he got into a scuffle with teammate JC Latham, took off his pads, left the facility and went to the parking lot to get his gun🤯 All that money gone for what⁉️ pic.twitter.com/f2nxvwdE9P
“Unfortunately, rules are rules with regard to guns on property, and sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they’re down,” Saleh said.
The Bears could actually use someone like Elliott on their practice squad, as a 325-pounder who can be a run stopper when needed against teams with power running games and big lines.
Most Bears defensive linemen are in the range of 300 to 310 pounds. Their roster is fairly well packed on the defensive line with Simmons, Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Shemar Turner, Neville Gallimore, Grady Jarrett, rookie Jordan van den Berg, James Lynch, Jayden Loving and Daniel Hardy.
They also could have defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo back from injured reserve when they return to face the Saints. He was suffering from a quad injury and hasn't played since the Oct. 11 loss at Green Bay.
Whether they would deem Elliott the risk is the big question. He does have rather solid backing from a  reputable character witness in the Titans' head coach.

Much respect to #Titans HC Robert Saleh for explaining the DT Jordan Elliott gun situation. “My message to 31 other teams: If you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help on a playoff run, give me a call. I'll tell you everything you need to know about him.… pic.twitter.com/mdEMazedb7

title: Will the Bears Regret Standing Pat at Cornerback? Malik Muhammad II Is Their Answer
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made a massive move to acquire Jeffery Simmons ahead of their Week 8 clash in Seattle. It was a decision that clearly displayed their all-in intentions for the 2026 NFL season.
However, many believed they weren't done fortifying the roster for the stretch run. Some believed they could've landed another cornerback or edge rusher on defense, while others thought they might even add a blocking TE with Cole Kmet sidelined for the season.
The cornerback position, specifically, felt like a logical area where they could've improved their depth relatively cheaply. Their lack of urgency spoke loudly about how they feel about their room.
Will they come to regret their passive approach?
Cornerback has been the Bears' most glaring weakness over the first half of the season. Before a strong performance against Tampa Bay, Jaylon Johnson has struggled mightily to begin the season. Tyrique Stevenson's impact has been equally unimpressive.
Chicago was a popular landing spot for Nahshon Wright , who came out of nowhere to make the Pro Bowl with the Bears last season. They probably would've landed him for cheap, as he's still waiting to play his first defensive snap after signing a one-year deal with the Jets this offseason.
With that said, the Bears saw the warts in Wright's game last season. He was downright bad in man coverage and was stiff as a board against shiftier pass-catchers. Would he raise the bar for the cornerback room? Probably not much.
The Bears also could've poached Riq Woolen from Philadelphia or Alontae Taylor from Tennessee, but they also came with serious questions. Woolen hasn't looked great over the past month after a strong start, and they'd probably have to give up a fifth-round pick to get him.
Meanwhile, Taylor ( the only option I would've liked if they got him via a late-round pick swap ) signed a three-year, $58 million deal this offseason. He'd be cheap this season, but his cap number would jump up to $20.5 million next year. That's a number they could afford by cutting ties with Jaylon Johnson, but it'd limit what they could do in free agency.
The Bears are putting a lot of faith in fourth-round pick Malik Muhammad II, and it's not hard to see why. He's been their best cover man to begin this season.
We've also hardly gotten to see him play with Kyler Gordon at nickelback this season. The veteran nickelback was basically deployed as a glorified edge rusher in his debut against Atlanta, and Muhammad got hurt early in the third quarter of the following matchup against New England.
Notably, we haven't seen Muhammad on the field with Simmons. He was already outperforming expectations, and his life will be substantially easier the next time he takes the field.
NFL teams aren't built at the trade deadline ( besides the Jacksonville Jaguars, anyway ). The good ones are built in April, and the Bears know that. General manager Ryan Poles confirmed they wouldn't be abandoning that philosophy shortly after they acquired Simmons.
Sure, they shipped three draft picks, including two first-rounders, for Simmons (and a fifth-round pick), but that was a unique situation that saw them land one of the league's most dominant defensive linemen. He's signed through 2030, and that move will pay dividends for the duration of his contract.
Chicago has only five draft picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, including two over the first four rounds. It's hard to significantly improve the roster in the offseason (the right way) under those circumstances.
That's also not exactly ample competition when it comes to being players at the trade deadline. Will the Bears regret not mortgaging their future further? Personally, I don't think so. Not with the players that they could've gotten.
Sure, they would've been cheap, but there's a reason for that fact.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Ian Rapoport Confirms Why Bears Didn't Trade for Khalil Mack, Anyone Else on Deadline Day
full_text:
Trade deadline day came and went and the Chicago Bears did not make another move after pulling off the blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons a few weeks ago.
Now that the dust has settled, we have some information about why the Bears didn't acquire Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack, or anyone else, for that matter.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the reason behind Mack not being traded was simply because the Chargers didn't want to trade him, nor were they ever close to trading him.
"The Chargers never wanted to deal Khalil Mack. They never got close to dealing Khalil Mack," Rapoport said. "They wanted him in their locker room, they want him to help teach some of the young pass-rushers. They just want a good culture and he is a great guy and a great leader."
We would assume Mack wasn't lying when he said publicly that he wanted to stay in Los Angeles because it's logical to believe that if he had requested a trade, the Chargers would have given him what he wanted out of respect for what he has meant to the franchise.
There were reports out there that the Bears were at least exploring the cornerback market for an upgrade , but no trade ever materialized.
Rapoport said pretty much what we anticipated was the reason for the Bears not making another move: Chicago was pretty much done making trades after the Simmons deal.
"For the Bears, once they did the Jeffery Simmons deal, that was kind of it," Rapoport said. "That was kind of the only draft compensation they were gonna give up."
While the Bears certainly could have used another edge rusher, cornerback or even tight end, it's understandable why they ultimately stood pat.
The Bears made a historic, all-in trade for Simmons to address a need that was definitely the biggest on the team. It's rare teams have an appetite for more after such a blockbuster deal and it's understandable why the Bears didn't want to part with another selection or more.
Edge rusher won't be a problem as long as Dayo Odeyingbo gets back from his quadriceps injury. Montez Sweat has been OK but not great and Austin Booker has played well. Adding to that, the addition of Simmons offers a nice boost to the pass-rush.
Cornerback is the biggest concern right now given the fact that Jaylon Johnson has been a shell of himself . That is a situation in which the Bears have to hope it just sorts itself out. If Johnson is just average and Malik Muhamamd can continue playing at the level he has, Chicago will be fine there.
The bottom line is this: the Bears have been playing great defense overall this season and they have more than enough to complement the offense to make a Super Bowl run.

title: Three Greatest Challenges Facing the Bears in Season's Second Half
full_text:
Any disappointment Bears fans might feel from the lack of a trade at the deadline only shows how little they know about the NFL.
Multiiple in-season trades by teams are uncommon occurrences even at the deadline, and the Bears already made their massive one by bringing aboard Jeffery Simmons .
Instead, the roster Ryan Poles and Ben Johnson built will need to try to improve from within, or they could add an unsigned player. Few of those can be very impactful at this time of the year — they'd be on a roster already if they possessed the kind of talent to let them turn a team's fortunes.
Improvement needs to come, though, as the Vikings have just elevated their offense by signing 38-year-old Kirk Cousins. The Packers have apparently improved and also are bringing back Micah Parsons at whatever level of play he can contribute following his knee surgery. And Detroit added a safety, although it still has defensive issues.
NFL FILMS WITH A CINEMATIC MASTERCLASS: An incredible look at the #Bears epic Sunday Night Football victory over the #Bucs at Soldier Field. Ben Johnson has completely transformed Chicago’s culture alongside Caleb Williams. Building something special 🫡 pic.twitter.com/ljEiOQJ9vJ
The Bears face three overriding problems when they begin they play New Orleans in Week 11 after the league goes through the first week of the schedule's second half this weekend.
None of these should seem shocking and the order can be debated. Here's how it looks.
It's an issue they've begun to clean up by adding Simmons, although they did allow one deep ball for 58 yards on Sunday. QBs shouldn't have the time to attack them deep as often. They had a disastrous game at Green Bay that skewed their statistics somewhat, gave up a long one to Seattle, as well. But the number of deep passes has slowed.
Luke Goedeke and the Buccaneers complained that Jeffery Simmons was too physical in the trenches in the Bears' win Sunday. Neville Gallimore shared his perspective, calling it "a part of the game" and saying the Buccaneers were just frustrated that Simmons had such an impact. pic.twitter.com/wN85gRZc8m
It needs to continue. After a first half of the season when they r anked near the bottom of the league in preventing yards per pass attempt and were actually last for a while, they've come up to 26th and are 22nd over the last three games despite facing two Super Bowl teams.
Whether it means Tyrique Stevenson being benched for big plays allowed, or possibly a rotation of corners with Malik Muhammad returning from a toe injury and sharing time with Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson, the Bears might want to look at more change.
The safety position should be fine with improving rookie Dillon Thieneman and veteran Cam Lewis now getting more adjusted to the Dennis Allen scheme. It could really get effective if Coby Bryant returns at safety from his knee injury.
The Bears' defense is currently (with schedule adjustments): - 32nd in early-down EPA per play - 1st in late down success rate A Very Normal Team.
The stats say they're sixth against the run but as former defensive coordinator Greg Blache said, numbers lie. They 23rd in yards allowed per attempt and their overall rushing yardage is low because teams gave up on the run when they were being outscored by Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. They were also hard-pressed for time with the Bears piling up possession time and couldn't run.
The No. 1 third-down defense in the league is no fluke. They are getting opponents into passing situations and have been top three much of the month in forcing three-and-outs. That's because they're getting better at stopping runs on first or second down. Simmons' arrival should help them as much here as with his pass rush. They almost gave up a 100-yard game to Bucky Irving Sunday but there are plenty of defenses doing that. It's a matter of using Simmons well and the rest of their run stuffers continuing to work together better.
They're 20th in limiting rushing yards per attempt in the last three games, so there is a small amount of improvement. Their run defense is already on pace (46) for their most tackles for loss since 2018. It's more a matter of limiting the longer runs than stuffing more runs behind the line.
Jeffery Simmons hustle reel from Week 9. He has the 5th highest single play top speed (over 17 MPH!) among defensive tackles this season, per @SumerSports pic.twitter.com/YbzrnSxVJf
This is where Ben Johnson's offense is built. They started the year cruising a No. 1 and then came Kyle Monangai's injury, the knee injury to left tackle Braxton Jones and more recently a shoulder injury to Jones' replacement, Theo Benedet. All the while they're hoping to get left tackle Ozzy Trapilo back at full strength but he didn't play a down in the last two games.
The Bears still rank third in yardage and more importantly are No. 1 in attempts. Because they're now at nine games, this will drop after other teams catch up to there game total following the bye week. What they are not doing well is averaging solid yardage. They're at 13th in yards per carry at 4.2 and over the past five have failed to average 100 yards rushing per game (98.6).
The trend is definitely downward and it all began right after Monangai's injury in Week 4, when he was coming off his 146-yard rushing day against the New York Jets. Certainly facing three straight difficult run defenses hurt, but having him back in two weeks could make a huge difference.
Another Jeffery Simmons note from @NextGenStats , he was off the field last week for 8 snaps; the Bears allowed 106 yards and a TD on those 8 plays (13.3 yards per play) compared to 146 yards and just one score on 48 plays with Simmons on the field (3.0 yards per play).
Johnson speculates that it might just be the lack of explosive runs. "Being able to have nine games of sample size at this point is going to be really good for us to look into," he said.
The other difference would be a healthier Benedet as he played through a shoulder injury on Sunday. He still had the second-highest Pro Football Focus blocking grade and second-highest pass-blocking grade on the team.
They are still missing an important part of their run game Kyle Monangai. The teams running game  hasn't been the same without him. pic.twitter.com/qQ0DdcwvtL
"He’s tough as nails," guard Jonah Jackson said. "Guys all over the board are dealing with stuff, some things you guys just might not know about. Credit to him doing his job and doing it at a high level." It's a trait often mentioned as necessary by coaches. "We talk about how there are going to be games over the course of the season where you're not 100%, and yet we need you going out there and giving every little ounce you got in your 90% or you're 85%," Johnson said. "I think that was a case of him last night pushing through and being out there for his buddies." Not needing to overcome health issues would be a way to help kick-start the running game, whether it's at guard or at running back.
The Chicago Bears just got their own episode with Caleb Williams, Ben Johnson and Jeffery Simmons in the latest #GridironHeights 😂 🎥: @BleacherReport pic.twitter.com/ccDgkbCZ5c

title: Bears' Cam Lewis Quickly Becoming One of Ryan Poles' Best Offseason Additions
full_text:
Bears defensive back Cam Lewis was initially expected to provide quality depth at both nickelback and safety when he signed a two-year, $6 million deal this offseason.
However, an injury to Coby Bryant at the start of training camp opened the door for him to run with the starting job there. They initially weren't thrilled with that development, bringing in veteran Xavier Woods to compete with Lewis on the back end a week later.
However, Coby Bryant's injury at the start of training camp opened the door for him to grab a starting safety job. They initially weren't thrilled with that development, bringing in veteran Xavier Woods to compete with Lewis on the back end a week later.
Woods got badly exposed in their 31-7 loss against Green Bay, though. That marked the end of his uneventful tenure in the Windy City. Conversely, Lewis' role grew from that point, and he's made the most of the added opportunities .
Lewis has missed only one defensive snap over the past three weeks and has seemingly gotten more comfortable with his role in the scheme. He has an interception and two pass deflections over their past two contests, and has looked confident coming down and making plays in run support.
He's also displayed some physicality in coverage. Lewis is 5'9", and 183 lb, but you wouldn't know it by watching him play.
He set the tone on the first third-down against Seattle, laying a huge hit on Seahawks receiver Tory Horton over the middle.
Cam Lewis with a nasty hit and PBU pic.twitter.com/5k6aRBcjn3
Still, his most impressive play in coverage came on Sunday night against Tampa Bay. He read Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's eyes and jumped in front of a pass when they were driving ahead of halftime.
What an INT by Cam Lewis 🔥 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UiIkSO4Vjo
Lewis has become a jack of all trades for the Bears. In many ways, he has perfectly replaced the impact that C.J. Gardner-Johnson provided last season. He might not be as effective as a blitzer ( we actually called out that area of his game in Week 7 ), but he's more versatile and well-rounded.
Unlike Lewis, CGJG had no interest in playing safety . Lewis, on the other hand, has embraced the position switch after spending much of his time in the slot for Buffalo over the past few seasons. Much like they did last year when Kyler Gordon returned to the lineup in late November, they'll have another interesting spot when Bryant makes his debut next month.
Chicago's big-ticket free agent signing will obviously play a key role when he's ready, but Lewis' presence could allow them to ease him into the lineup. When he is ready to play a full complement of snaps, Lewis can also seamlessly transition to the slot (as we saw when Gordon briefly left the game on Sunday night) and play a key role in dime packages.
The Bears have made a few quality free agent additions since Ryan Poles became the team's general manager in 2022. Andrew Billings made a big impact on their run defense for a bargain-bin price, while T.J. Edwards and Kevin Byard III developed into key starters and filled leadership voids.
It's still too early to group Lewis with those players (although he's already squarely in Billings' tier), but he's well on his way to entering those conversations. He's been one of the Poles' best free agent bargains since taking over the job.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Face a New Division Threat After Vikings Reunite With Kirk Cousins at the Deadline
full_text:
The Chicago Bears let the NFL trade deadline come and go having made one major trade and letting the rest of the NFC shuffle the deck around them. After the Jeffery Simmons trade with the Tennessee Titans a few weeks ago, Ryan Poles and Co. were silent on November 10 .
The Minnesota Vikings certainly weren't within the division, reuniting with Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders to give the Vikings a reliable option under center. Neither were the Detroit Lions, who acquired safety Andre Cisco from the New York Jets on trade deadline eve.
How do these NFC North deals, and others from around the conference, change the game for the Bears in their quest for a first Super Bowl appearance in two decades?
Cousins was playing well in Las Vegas before being dealt back to the Twin Cities, owning a 6.7% negative play rate and owning a low 9.8% sack rate on drop-backs. Behind a suspect Raiders offensive line that has drastically overperformed, that is extremely promising.
Being back with Kevin O'Connell should only bolster Cousins' game over the next few months in a familiar professional place. Cousins' best statistical season was in 2022, O'Connell's first year as the Vikings' head coach.
He's a major upgrade over Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, who, despite leading Minnesota to a 6-2 record, gave the Vikings a lower ceiling.
Cousins was the most significant trade at the deadline and the only blockbuster involving a quarterback on deadline day. Jacoby Brissett was moved out of the NFC when the Baltimore Ravens landed him from the Arizona Cardinals.
Chicago is a trade deadline winner simply by virtue of the rest of the conference (besides Minnesota) largely sitting on their hands.
Detroit needed more help than Cisco but chose to run it back for the most part. The Green Bay Packers are clearly hoping injury returns, mainly Micah Parsons', is enough of an answer not to have further emptied the war chest.
Outside of the NFC North, there weren't many major moves in the conference. The AFC, however, stole the show.
The Jacksonville Jaguars were the biggest buyers, giving up five draft picks in deals for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
Elsewhere, the Indianapolis Colts continued their sell-offs, and the Titans and Eagles practically completed theirs.
This was a day and trade season where talent flocked to the AFC while largely leaving the NFC. Because of that, the Bears are arguably the biggest winners for their most significant league-shifting Simmons trade.

title: Joe Burrow Set for Rare First With Mike Tomlin, Last With Aaron Rodgers on SNF
full_text:
The Sunday Night Football game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers will mark just the third – and likely final – meeting between Joe Burrow and Aaron Rodgers.
Rodgers has said this will be his final season, so barring a meeting the playoffs, Sunday will be Burrow’s last chance to add him to the list of quarterbacks he’s beaten.
Burrow is 0-2 against Rodgers, losing to him and the Packers 25-22 in overtime in 2021, in addition to the 30-27 loss in Pittsburgh earlier this season in Week 3.
Despite it likely being a final meeting, Burrow said he doesn’t think he’ll ask the future Hall of Famer for a jersey swap.
“Probably not,” Burrow said when asked. “Don’t really think about that too much.”
He has, however, given a lot of thought to how well Rodgers has played throughout his career and especially in 2026.
“He’s one of the greatest that’s ever done it,” Burrow said. “He’s 41 or 42 and still doing it at a high level. I would have trouble calling it quits if I’m still playing like that, at that age.
“I’ve enjoyed watching him for a long time,” he added. “And this year, I think he’s playing so well. He really played great in that last game we played. Dang near perfect. I had to be perfect the whole time, too.”
While Sunday could be Burrow’s final game against Rodgers, he’s already faced Mike Tomlin for the final time, presuming the coach doesn’t return to the profession.
Burrow went 4-3 against Tomlin. Among quarterbacks with at least four starts against the future Hall of Fame coach, Burrow is one of only three to boast a winning record. The others are Josh Allen (4-1) and Tom Brady (7-3).
Tomlin stepped away from the Steelers at the end of last year and moved to NBC, the network that will broadcast Sunday night’s game.
That means Burrow will sit with Tomlin and the rest of the NBC crew for a production meeting ahead of the game.
“I didn’t even think about that,” Burrow said before heaping praise on Tomlin, who will be working his first Steelers game since leaving the coaching profession.
“I've always loved how he sees the game and attacks coaching,” Burrow added. “He's always attacked it with a lot of intensity that I have a lot of respect for. So to be able to get to know him in a setting like that, I think will be a little exciting for me.”
Those production meetings typically involve the television crew asking the players and coaches questions to get as much information as possible to use on the broadcast.
But they can be conversational at times.
Burrow was asked if there were any questions he would like to ask Tomlin after all the battles they have had against each other.
“Certainly,” he said with a grin. “Maybe more of an offseason off-the-record session than a production meeting.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Dylan Fairchild's Practice Status Revealed Ahead of Primetime Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals returned to practice today as the roster works through the lingering jet lag from last week's trip to Spain. Cincinnati is pretty healthy coming out of the first half of the season, and the latest injury report largely reflected that.
Dylan Fairchild was the only new addition to the injury report after he got dinged right at the end of Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
He was officially limited in the Bengals' injury report. They went through a walkthrough on Wednesday afternoon. DJ Turner was also limited due to an ankle issue.
Jonathan Allen (rest) and Kyle Dugger (quad) didn't participate. Check out the full report below, which included a handful of Steelers players.
Cincinnati had some veteran rest days mixed in to start the week but should have a pretty full-strength roster to attack the Steelers with on Sunday night. They are fresh off a great bonding experience in Spain.
"It seemed like they spent a lot of time together outside the hotel," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the trip. "My favorite part of winning a game like that and long travel is the plane. Just the volume on the plane, the camaraderie on the plane. That's generally when you know it's been a good day, good trip, and I certainly felt that last night.
"I'm sitting in my seat, and I'm watching all the players come by and the attitude they have, and they're joking with their teammates and telling stories about the week or telling stories about the game. That is probably my favorite part of any of the road experiences."
Getting as healthy as possible will help Cincinnati take control of the AFC North. Losing both games to the Steelers this season would make it even more difficult to win the AFC North.
Names on injured reserve like Andrei Iosivas (thumb), cornerback Ja'Sir Taylor (hamstring), and rookie offensive lineman Brian Parker (knee) are eligible to come off injured reserve but its unlear if they will get activated this week.
On top of the jet lag, Cincinnati has to overcome a Pittsburgh team fresh off of its bye week.
"I don't know what the stats are. I just know they're not great. I honestly can't even give you a ballpark of what they are," Taylor said about no international game team ever beating an opponent fresh off a bye the following week. "I just think common sense would tell you it's probably a little challenging. But I think we have a great mindset right now."

title: Zac Taylor Reveals Uncomfortable Message Duke Tobin Asked Him to Deliver After Bengals Trade Debacle
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals did not make de facto general manager Duke Tobin available following Tuesday’s trade fiasco and instead had head coach Zac Taylor address it during his Wednesday news conference.
Despite admitting it made him uncomfortable, Taylor addressed the subject without specifically being asked about it, responding to a question about the team’s depth at defensive end.
“Obviously we tried something yesterday, and Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed,” Taylor said. “I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m going to do what he asked.
“We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius (Howell),” Taylor continued. “As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. So he's really apologetic about it.”
With rookie second-round pick Cashius Howell on Injured Reserve due to wrist surgery, the Bengals agreed to trade a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for defensive end Arnold Ebiketie.
But because the Eagles acquired Ebiketie in free agency this past offseason, he would have counted against the Bengals in the compensatory pick formula, negating the third-round pick they are due to receive for losing Trey Hendrickson.
So the trade essentially would have been Ebiketie for a third and a sixth.
The Bengals backed out of the trade after compensatory pick expert Nick Korte posted on X that the team would lose their third-round pick as well.
Taylor said Tobin didn’t say when he became aware of the added cost, and Taylor didn’t ask, but it’s clear the front office was totally unaware until after Korte’s post. Otherwise, why even venture into trade talks for a player who would affect the comp pick formula.
“I certainly have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things, and they've given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now and playing at such a high level,” Taylor said.
“So we'll put that behind us and move forward,” he added. “Our locker room is in a great place right now.”
Taylor said Howell is still considered week to week following the wrist surgery after suffering the injury in Week 8 against Tennessee.
He said the injury won’t be season ending, but the timeline for Howell’s return is unclear.
The injury was the impetus for trying to acquire a depth piece such as Ebiketie, a 2022 second-round pick who has 16.5 career sacks in 76 games.
Taylor said he doesn’t expect the attempt to add Ebiketie to affect the other edge rushers who would have lost playing time after the acquisition.
“I would hope that everybody in our locker room wants us to be at our very best and trust that we're always doing things to make sure we're as good as possible,” Taylor said. “And we had an open roster spot, so it wasn't going to be addition and subtraction. It was just going to be (for) somebody that we've already put on IR.”
The botched trade could have an impact in Philadelphia, where Ebiketie remains, knowing the team tried to deal him.
The Eagles can’t be happy with how everything played out, and Taylor attempted to smooth over that relationship as well, saying that was another thing Tobin wanted him to convey rather than the director of player personnel addressing it himself.
“(Tobin) wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner,” Taylor said. “It was on our end. And that's just the way things go.
“We're always looking at the waiver wire every single week. We're always looking for practice squad additions, subtractions,” Taylor continued. “The trade deadline is obviously the biggest thing that can impact your season.
“We’re in a great spot where we’re at with our roster, where we’re at with our health. Obviously it's not perfect with the health, but it's about as good as you can ask for getting through Week 8. All that’s behind us. We have a tremendous opportunity Sunday here at home, and our focus should be on that right now.”

title: Zac Taylor Shares Encouraging Injury Updates on Several Bengals Players
full_text:
Zac Taylor confirmed on Wednesday that starting left guard Dylan Fairchild is day-to-day after suffering an apparent shoulder injury during the waning moments of the Bengals' victory over the Falcons. Fairchild appeared to suffer the injury just before the two-minute warning in Madrid and attempted to finish the game afterwards, though he tapped out immediately afterwards.
Taylor also shared an update on rookie pass rusher Cashius Howell, refusing to rule Howell out for the season and instead labeling him week-to-week. The Bengals placed him on injured reserve after he sustained a wrist injury that required surgery in Week 8 against the Titans. He is eligible to return from IR after the team's Week 12 game against the Saints on 11/29, though Taylor said Howell will miss time beyond that.
"Right now he's just on IR and we'll just see how the recovery process goes as we get down the road here, but that time tables to be determined," Taylor said. "Still weeks for him, lets clear through the IR window and it'll definitely go beyond that, and we'll gather more information as the season goes."
Taylor also updated the media on the possible return of several key players from injured reserve this week, leaving the door open for names such as Andrei Iosivas to return to the active roster.
"We're close, not today specifically but very shortly, those are some conversations we've had, a couple of those guys we'll see where it's at," Taylor said.
Rumors have surfaced that Iosivas could return soon after having thumb surgery earlier in the season. He is the most likely candidate for a return from injured reserve at the moment, with names such as Jalen Davis, Ja'Sir Taylor, and Brian Parker II also getting close to a possible return.
Davis landed on IR after sustaining a hamstring injury against the Steelers in Week 3, whereas the team placed Taylor and Parker on the list before the start of the season on August 30th.
The return of either Davis or Taylor would provide a solid boost to a corner room that is missing any sort of stability at nickel corner, as Dax Hill and Josh Newton have filled that role since Davis' injury.
As for Parker, his return may happen at the perfect time. If Fairchild misses any time, Jacob Bayer would likely slot into the left guard spot with Parker also in the mix.

title: Referee Report: Among Active White Hats, Sunday's Has Worked More Bengals Games Than Any
full_text:
No active NFL referee has called more Cincinnati Bengals games than the man who will be on the assignment in Week 10 against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
This will be Clete Blakeman’s 18th Bengals game since he became a head referee in 2010.
While Cincinnati is 8-9 with Blakeman on the call, the team has a three-game losing streak with the veteran referee, with all three games being memorable losses.
The most recent was last year in Week 9, the 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears. Prior to that was the Thursday night game at Baltimore in 2024 when quarterback Joe Burrow was hit in the head with no penalty called on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game. Instead, the Ravens prevailed 35-34.
And in 2023, Blakeman worked the season opener in Cleveland when the Bengals couldn’t master the Browns or the rain and dropped a 24-3 decision.
Blakeman also worked the 2021 Divisional Round playoff win against the Tennessee Titans.
This will be his fourth career Bengals-Steelers game and first since Cincinnati won 24-10 in Pittsburgh in Week 3 in 2021.
This year, Blakeman and his crew rank fifth with 15.75 accepted penalties per game. Last year he was seventh (12.82).
Blakeman and his crew are tied for first with six roughing the passer penalties this season. Their 11 defensive holding penalties also are tied for most in the league.
The crew has had at least 16 accepted penalties in five of the last six games.
Blakeman has earned postseason assignments in 12 of his 16 seasons as a referee, including Super 50 in 2015, the AFC Championship Game last year and the 2023 NFC Championship Game.
