title: Bengals' Unsung Trio is Dominating This Season
full_text:
When you think of the Cincinnati Bengals, you think of a star-studded offense with players like Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, and a hungry defense led by superstar Dexter Lawrence.
People often overlook the resilience and consistency of Darrin Simmons' three-man unit: long snapper William Wagner, punter Ryan Rehkow, and kicker Evan McPherson.
The three-man team has been perfect so far this season on field goals. Evan McPherson has not missed an extra point and is 12-for-12 on his kicks so far this season, including 6-for-6 on 50-plus-yarders. McPherson has made 24 consecutive field goals, breaking the previous franchise record of 21.
McPherson has also taken home two awards so far this season. He was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week after the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers in Week 1. McPherson was even named Special Teams Player of the Month for September after he converted all eight of his field goals, marking the second time he has won this award in his career.
Yet behind those headline-grabbing numbers lies a tightly coordinated, three-man operation. The snap must be executed perfectly, and the hold needs to have the laces facing away. The Bengals have been exceptionally consistent in this execution. In just their second year together, Wagner, Rehkow, and McPherson are one of the two teams, the other being the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, that have been Perfect in field goals and extra points this season.
Field goals are crucial in close games, but so is flipping the field. You never want to punt, but when Rehkow is called upon, he delivers. Just like McPherson, Rehkow brought home the honors of AFC Special Teams Player of the Week In Week 7, he placed 3 of his 4 punts inside the 10-yard line, including a 56-yarder.
Rehkow has placed more than half of his punts inside the 20-yard line this season, resulting in zero touchbacks. This transformation has turned the punt unit into a formidable defensive asset. Since this has created no explosive returns, the opposing team is forced to operate from its own end zone, giving the defense the ultimate advantage: a long field.
Ultimately, a team’s record relies on its capability to manage hidden yardage and high-leverage situations efficiently. In a game where margins are important, operational perfection on Special Teams isn’t just desirable; it’s the foundation of winning football. Cincinnati's three-man team of Rehkow, McPherson, and Wagner has been exceptional this year and looks to continue its dominance.

title: Reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford Makes Big Statement About Joe Burrow
full_text:
Joe Burrow's MVP campaign has support from the quarterback who won the award last season.
Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford believes the Cincinnati Bengals' star should be leading the race at the halfway point. Speaking with Jim Gray on this week's episode of SiriusXM's "Let's Go" podcast , the Rams QB picked Burrow when asked who he considers the current MVP leader.
Burrow has helped Cincinnati win four straight games, reaching 6-2, with the Bengals scoring at least 31 points in each victory.
"There are a lot of quarterbacks and a lot of people playing at a high level," Stafford said. "I think Joe Burrow, what he's done the last three, four, five weeks, whatever it is, I mean, he's been on fire.
“That offense has been clicking, throwing a bunch of touchdowns, keeping his team alive, playing well. Defense is playing good too, but I would say Joe Burrow, for what he's done this season, they've stayed healthy and he's rocking and rolling at a really good clip.
Burrow's latest performance in Madrid strengthened that case. He completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with no interceptions, in Cincinnati's 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Burrow also scored a touchdown on the ground in the second quarter.
Over the four-game winning streak, Burrow has thrown for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns, with just three interceptions. All three interceptions came against Tennessee, a game in which he threw five touchdown passes and ran for the winning score in overtime.
“So I'd give it to him halfway through, as we know [there’s] a lot of football to be played, but he's been special the first half," Stafford said.
Last month, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor called Burrow the most accurate passer in the world, but made it clear he has no idea how the star signal-caller is so accurate.
"I don't know," Taylor jokingly answered when asked about Burrow's accuracy. "Watching how he works in practice between reps. Watching how he works in pre-practice, watching how he throws in pregame, watching his body movements... It's really impressive."
As for the Bengals, Cincinnati is tied with Pittsburgh atop the AFC North at 6-2. They host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, with a chance to take control of the division lead.

title: 2 Winners & 2 Losers From Bengals 2026 Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has passed, and Cincinnati sat it out .
Director of Player Personnel Duke Tobin and the rest of the front office did not add any talent to bolster Joe Burrow's hot run.
Eagles defensive end Arnold Ebiketie looked like he was headed to Cincinnati in a deal this morning, but it got scrapped once Over The Cap's Nick Korte pointed out  Cincinnati would lose its 2027 third-round compensatory pick if they finalized things.
Then the rest of the AFC contenders (outside of Pittsburgh) added at least one new talent via trade. Jacksonville's flurry in recent days got matched by Kansas City (wide receiver Josh Downs), Buffalo (safety Amani Hooker), and Denver (linebacker Daiyan Henley).
Let's dive into Cincinnati's Winners & Losers from the deadline:
Cincinnati had a chance to make their first deadline addition in two years at clear positions of need like starting linebacker, safety depth, and tight end depth, but did nothing.
No one was asking them to go through with the rough cost for Ebiketie earlier in the day, but adding somewhere would've been huge for the team's depth on paper.
The cap appeared to be a sixth-round value or worse for what they were willing to dive into with this market. Maybe Burrow's good enough to carry this roster as is to the ultimate prize, but everyone they're directly battling against in this conference (outside of Pittsburgh) added to their talent pool, and Cincinnati bowed out.
Not knowing the rules around how adding players affects your draft-pick pool isn't an ideal look either.
Adding a running back like Jonathan Taylor had been the marquee talking point around the deadline in recent weeks, and now it's definitely Chase Brown's backfield for the rest of the season.
He and Samaje Perine ran well in Madrid on Sunday, and Brown has been steady overall all season (32nd in yards after contact per rushing attempt, 27th in PFF grade, sixth in pass-blocking grade). It never made sense to trade the curious haul the Colts wanted for a position that Brown and Perine have covered.
Now, he gets to play for some type of new deal in the offseason from Cincinnati or another team.
Burrow is playing better than any quarterback on earth right now and leading an offense miles better than any other in the NFL over the past month.
Since Week 5, Burrow's offense is notching 0.25 EPA/play (no other team higher than 0.16), and he is atop Ben Baldwin's EPA/PFF grade blend leaderboard this season.
He's going to win MVP if this heater keeps up against one of the three easiest schedules left in the NFL, yet Cincinnati did nothing. The fact his MVP competitors added around him while Burrow has to trudge on with this roster could help him a bit in that pursuit.
He wants a different trophy much more, and Cincinnati didn't do anything on paper to boost the chances they carry the Lombardi Trophy in February. We may look back on this February like we did with some roster choices on the last Super Bowl roster.
The front office has stamped their approval of this roster; now go show you can do it.
Linebacker's been a hammered talking point for over two years now for good reason. Barrett Carter is improving at a palatable rate this season, but Demetrius Knight's posting another sub-50 PFF grade like he did as a rookie. The missed tackles improved a bit from 14% to 12% this season, but he has to step up for Cincinnati's defense to really maximize.
The whole locker room reportedly bonded heavily across their trip to Spain, and the ultimate team sport can come down to those tight-knit bonds in the big moments. Cincinnati seems to have that and didn't throw any starter into an uncomfortable spot with a splash move.
They get the ultimate chance to reward the front-office faith facing the Steelers on Sunday.

title: Bengals Fail at Trade Deadline as AFC Contenders Make Moves
full_text:
The trade deadline came and went and the Bengals stayed pat.
It's the two words that head coach Zac Taylor used on Tuesday.
Their actions said otherwise. The Bengals agreed to a deal that would've brought Arnold Ebikete to Cincinnati. Instead, that deal fell through in embarassing fashion. Our own Russ Heltman has the details here.
That failed deal will get the attention it deserves, but it didn't have to be the story of the deadline for the Bengals. They still had hours to add to their roster.
The same roster that has Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level. The same roster that has Dexter Lawrence in position to make a real run at Defensive Player of the Year. Tee Higgins is playing the best ball of his career. Ja'Marr Chase is the best receiver on the planet.
The Bengals have a ton of talent and can make a real run at a Super Bowl. So why add?
That's what contenders do.
The Buffalo Bills are considered the top team in the AFC. They didn't sit on their hands at the deadline. They went out and got the guy that intercepted three of Burrow's passes in Week 8. Amani Hooker is a heck of a football player and gives the Bills a real playmaker at safety.
Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has a new weapon to throw to. Josh Downs is headed to Kansas City. The slot receiver has a chance to make a major impact for the remainder of the season. The Bengals face the Chiefs in December.
The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, including a deal for Jessie Bates that would've been a costly, but worth it type of deal for the Bengals. Bates was a great player for the Bengals. He got even better in Atlanta and would've been a plug-and-play piece in the back-end of Cincinnati's defense.
Even the Broncos got in on the fun. No, they didn't add another weapon for Bo Nix. Instead, they addressed arguably the Bengals' biggest weakness: linebacker. They made an in-division trade with the Chargers for linebacker Daiyan Henley.
All four of these AFC contenders addressed needs with big moves. All four of these teams are much better today than they were on Sunday. Meanwhile, the Bengals didn't get the deal done for Ebiketie after botching the compensatory pick implications and didn't follow it up with another move to bolster their roster.
Never count out Joe Burrow or Ja'Marr Chase, but the Bengals didn't get better on Tuesday. Their biggest competition did.

title: Bengals NOT Striking Trade Deal For Eagles Pass Rusher Arnold Ebiketie Due To Key Reason
full_text:
After NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Bengals are trading a 2027 sixth-round pick for Arnold Ebiketie, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported roughly an hour later that the deal was not happening.
Cincinnati got cold feet after it surfaced that they would lose their 2027 third-round compensatory pick if they struck the deal.
"Plot twist! The Bengals and Eagles deal for DE Arnold Ebiketie has fallen through and will not happen, per sources. The trade falling through is not physical or performance-related, per sources," Schultz posted on X .
Rapoport confirmed they are exiting the deal to retain the third-round compensatory pick.
"The Bengals have now called off this trade intending to keep a future comp pick they would've lost with this deal. Agreement was reached, but not official," Rapoport posted .
Back to the trade drawing board for Cincinnati, which clearly is putting a heavy premium on that top-100 pick they are slated to get back after Trey Hendrickson signed a new deal in Baltimore and triggered the pick for his old team.
The NFL rules state below how the Bengals would've lost the pick. Ebiketie was a CFA signing by the Eagles this past offseason.
"If a Club qualifies for more than four Compensatory Draft Selections, only the four highest selections will be awarded to the Club. If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above," the rules state.
A rough fake-out for Bengals fans, who thought they were about to get their defense beefed up, and a rough look for the team's front office.
They appear to not have known this compensatory pick language existed until Over The Cap's Nick Korte tweeted about it right after the announced deal.
"Arnold Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles. The Bengals lost 3 CFAs and signed 2 (Cordell Volson not qualifying); thus, while they gain a 2027 sixth-round comp pick, they lose a 2027 third-round comp pick that was via Trey Hendrickson going to Baltimore," Korte posted on X before expanding further. "Obvious correction here: the Bengals gave up a regular sixth-round pick, they did not gain one. The main point is of course about the third round compensatory pick that this trade would cancel out."
Cincinnati has less than four hours to add talent ahead of the deadline at 4 p.m. ET.

title: Browns Stood Still at Deadline, But Could Still Target These 2 Free Agents in 2027
full_text:
Well, it certainly wasn't a memorable 2026 NFL Trade Deadline for the Cleveland Browns.
After weeks of waiting to see what the Browns' front office would do at the deadline, the day came and went, and nothing was done . Not a single outgoing move or incoming addition, leaving just the same 53 guys that marched to a 5-4 record to try and create a playoff push in the second half of the season.
But that doesn't mean the Browns are a perfect squad. Honestly, they are far from it.
With holes on both sides of the ball, Cleveland obviously isn't in a contending spot, with the front office more inclined to carry their draft capital into the upcoming offseason.
Instead of making moves now, the Browns will likely explore what becomes available this offseason as a way to strengthen the group, especially considering the front office will have a much better feel of where big-time additions are needed.
Here are two 2027 NFL Free Agents the Browns could target this offseason:
Quenton Nelson ended up being traded at the deadline , going from the Indianapolis Colts to the Seattle Seahawks.
While Nelson is likely going to become a Hall of Famer by the time his career comes to a close, the Colts are actively entering a rebuilding period, and the contract Nelson is going to command is far greater than they feel comfortable paying.
If the Seahawks keep slipping down the NFC West standings, all while Nelson remains injured for the next couple of weeks, the two sides could call the deal a wash and part ways this offseason. After all, Seattle only gave up a third- and fifth-round pick, and if Nelson is asking too much money to be trusted after injury, he could enter the open market.
But that isn't something that should deter the Browns.
Instead, they should go in and make an offer for the 30-year-old to come to Cleveland.
For the past few years, the Browns have been trying to build the next era of an offensive line that was once anchored by the legendary Joe Thomas. While they seem to have two strong rookies in Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, they need someone to slide in and lead them.
Nelson would be the perfect fit, not just because of his experience and leadership, but because even if he takes a slight decline, he is a major upgrade to the Browns' lackluster group they currently have.
Quarterback Deshaun Watson is likely leaving this offseason, so the Browns will have much more flexibility in offering a free agent like Nelson a nice contract.
Whether or not the Browns really want to have a cornerback on their mind this offseason, they will have to.
Denzel Ward is continuing to age, all while Tyson Campbell and the rest of the squad continue to be rocky, Sunday-in and Sunday-out. The front office has attempted to build a relatively young, impressionable group over the past couple of years, but injuries and inconsistencies have broken up that group just as quickly as it formed.
This offseason, the Browns should make it a priority to at least sign one cornerback in free agency and take another in the 2027 NFL Draft.
In the case of free agency, Dallas Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant stands out as a big-time target.
Currently on a $5.5 million deal, Durant is expected to command a bigger deal after a one-year rental with the Cowboys. With where the market is right now, and based on his current play, the 28-year-old should see a three-to-four-year deal worth roughly $18-24 million in total. That would net him anywhere from $6-to-8 million a season.
Durant is having an okay season, making 10 tackles, two pass deflections and one forced fumble across five games, but has struggled to stay on the field due to injury.
As long as he finishes the year strong, he may be able to shoot that value up even more.
But as long as the price doesn't shoot too high, the Browns should look to sign Durant and make him one of the staples for the back half of Ward's career in the Orange and Brown.

title: Todd Monken Explains Comments on Shedeur Sanders and What That Means for the QB Position
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns cannot get out of their own way when it comes to quarterback controversies. Deshaun Watson cleared the concussion protocol before their game in New Orleans, but was still replaced by Shedeur Sanders. He led a fourth-quarter comeback that resulted in an overtime period where he marched the offense down for a touchdown.
However, Todd Monken would not commit to a starting quarterback for the next game until Wednesday.
During Sanders’ start, Monken told a sideline reporter that when he and Sanders were discussing which plays he wanted to run, Sanders requested plays that were not in the playbook. Monken had a playful tone that brought levity to the story, but that did not stop speculation that Sanders did not understand the offense.
Monken called for a quarterback competition between Watson and Sanders in training camp before eventually naming Watson the starter. He liked Watson’s “operations” of the offense and it was believed that Sanders needed more time to grasp the concepts. Sunday’s anecdote furthered that narrative.
#Browns HC Todd Monken was asked about the sideline report from Sunday's game regarding Monken joking about Shedeur Sanders suggesting things he liked that weren't in the playbook: "It's hilarious that it's gone this far. 'Shedeur, what do you like?' 'Well, I like this, this and… pic.twitter.com/0eNhUYeZfV
On Wednesday, Monken had an opportunity to clear the air on his game planning with Sanders. “I think it’s hilarious it’s gone this far,” Monken told the press. “I get a big kick out of it because it was really just a normal day-to-day of what a quarterback likes … It really isn’t a big deal.”
Monken chose to hand the offense to Watson instead of Sanders with just one game before the bye week. Watson’s late-game heroics had the Browns at 5-3, and Sanders’ play did not warrant a permanent change. The Browns are one seed out of the playoffs due to a tiebreaker.
The Houston Texans come to town in a crucial week for playoff implications.
The team is not interested in evaluating for the future, as they play in the now and the season is far from over. Monken is a first-time head coach, with any future opportunities very unlikely. He needs to gather as many wins as possible to prove his case to keep his job through tough times.
Starting Watson shows that Monken believes he gives them the best chance to win.
Monken has been open with the media and has been a stark contrast to previous head coaches. He tends to use bad phrasing as he speaks in the moment, and he clarified that any pre-game discussions did not factor into his decision to return to Watson.
The Browns need a win to start their four-game homestand to keep pace in the wild-card race.  He is most comfortable with Watson, as he has taken the first-team reps all year. They have struggled to run the ball the entire season, and his legs provide an opportunity to get anything going on the ground.
Watson may be on a short hook with the bye week looming . If they lose and Watson starts slowly again, they could make a change with the extra week of practice. This was reportedly the case in Week 2, but the team won, and Watson won enough games to keep his job.
Although the sideline report and the decision not to name a starter until Wednesday suggested a quarterback controversy, Monken made it clear that his only mission is to win.

title: 'The Intention Was For Deshaun To Start': Browns Open Up on Recent QB Decisions
full_text:
“I had no intention of Deshaun not being our starter."
All the speculation seems to have been for nothing.
Even though second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders showed up and showed out in a Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints in overtime , the Cleveland Browns never planned to give him another shot.
On Wednesday, Nov. 11, Browns head coach Todd Monken confirmed publicly that the plan was for Deshaun Watson to remain Cleveland's starter after he returned from concussion protocol.
"Everything you're considering, but ultimately Deshaun's done a really good job for us," he said in an X post from ESPN NFL Insider. "5-3 as a starter, and he's worked awfully hard to get back. There's a high belief in that ... the intention was for Deshaun to start. It's just when you come in on that Monday, you haven't really even met as a staff. You've just gone through the film, you've got with ownership and I just wanted to make sure we talked through as a staff, this is the way we're going forward.
"Great. That's all it was. It was pretty simple."
Todd Monken on if he gave real consideration to starting Shedeur Sanders this week: "Everything you're considering, but ultimately Deshaun's done a really good job for us. 5-3 as a starter, and he's worked awfully hard to get back. There's a high belief in that ... the intention… https://t.co/9HKHCzQKM1
Following Sunday's one-point loss, though, Monken's comments led to intense speculation, and understandably so. He had shared that he was not willing to talk about who the starting quarterback would be moving forward, which seemingly left the door open for Sanders.
He clarified why he said that on Wednesday.
"That was my intention," Monken said about eventually backing Watson. "I just wanted to make sure to run it by the staff before I said it publicly. I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But he played well enough to still be our starter."
Monken: "That was my intention. I just wanted to make sure to run it by the staff before I said it publicly. I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But he played well… https://t.co/9kHio8Vva4
This season, Watson has thrown for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions on a whopping 249 attempts. He has completed 65.5% of his passes , which is currently the fourth-best mark of his career across the last eight years.
While he still isn't looking like the former Houston Texans Pro Bowler, he is slowly but surely returning to that dynamic quarterback he once was.
On the ground, Watson has flashed his versatility, taking 51 carries for 217 yards and one score, which is the most since 2020.
If Cleveland really wants to get something out of Watson before his contract expires at the end of the year, continuing to let him thrive out on the gridiron is the best option. However, that would mean the Browns have some sort of belief that he will be around the team for the foreseeable future. Because why else would you then turn your back on the second-year Sanders?
Whatever is happening behind closed doors in the Browns' building has left a lot up for interpretation this season, especially at the quarterback position.
The only hope now is that Watson and the Browns don't waste the 2026 campaign and instead put together a strong push to make the playoffs.
The team returns to the field this weekend against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.
The two sides clash at 1:00 p.m. EST, with Watson getting a taste of his former side.
"It's a big opportunity for us to get back on the winning track, especially in front of our home fans," Watson said. "That's the ultimate focus is focus on that. On the outside things, going against my former team, that stuff was in the past. Four or five years ago, yeah, it was a big deal, but now I think both sides have moved on.
"We're just both trying to find ways to win and continue to put ourselves in position for later on down the road."

title: Browns Trade Deadline Update Sheds Light into Front Office's Decision To Stay Quiet
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline came and went.
And the Cleveland Browns remained quiet.
On Wednesday, Nov. 11, ESPN NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler released an update on where the Browns' headspace was at during the trade deadline. According to his report , the Browns were feeling out the market, but nothing ended up coming together by the time 4:00 p.m. EST rolled around.
The team was in the market for an extra edge rusher to pair with a squad that has been up-and-down this season, while also exploring the need for a blocking tight end.
Obviously, the Browns have one of the league's most exciting youngsters in Harold Fannin Jr., but he is better known for his pass-catching abilities and athleticism, not his ability to block. Landing a blocking tight end would have given him more flexibility and less strain on that end.
On the defensive side, Jared Verse takes most of the attention; however, he has struggled to begin the year. Adding another body across from him could have opened up more opportunities for him to get in the backfield.
According to @JFowlerESPN , the Browns “put out several feelers” for an extra edge rusher and blocking tight end, but nothing came together at the trade deadline. https://t.co/Nz8Pkt3jFh
"The Browns looked for an extra edge rusher and a blocking tight end and put out several feelers, but nothing came together," Fowler's report read . "This was the rare cycle in which Cleveland did not make a move."
And the latter is correct.
In recent years, the Browns' decisions to trade away wide receiver Amari Cooper in 2024 and trade for edge rusher Za'Darius Smith in 2023 stand out as team-altering moves. Cooper obviously went on to decline over the next few years due to age, but he could still have served a purpose in Cleveland, while Smith would end up becoming a nice complement to the Browns' pass rush.
Even if the Browns had shipped a few players out as they had in the past, with all four quarterbacks and wideout Jerry Jeudy being rumored to be on the block, it would have made things interesting.
But if the front office were really interested in shaking things up, they would have.
As Fowler mentioned, feelers being sent out shows that they were at least exploring different options and trade targets, but nothing coming to fruition means that either their own or others' values weren't met.
No trades for #Browns + a review of their 23-22 OT loss to the #Saints with @LanceReisland . What went wrong on the 2-point try? Did Shedeur Sanders give Todd Monken something to think about? What's going on the the defense late in games and more! WATCH: https://t.co/wLd95Bm9WS
Instead, the Browns are just going to keep the locker room intact and see if the 5-4 record through the first nine weeks was a fluke or not.
They did end up adding two players to the practice squad, increasing a bit of the depth, but neither is an eye-popping move. They signed tight end Zaire Mitchell-Paden and punter Wes Pahl, releasing tight end John FitzPatrick and defensive tackle Eric Johnson II in the process.
The #Browns have signed TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden and P Wes Pahl to the practice squad. The team also released TE John FitzPatrick and DT Eric Johnson II from the practice squad.
Neither are expected to play a big impact on the 53-man roster, but if injuries arise they may get a chance to play on Sundays.
Looking to put a Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints behind them, the Browns will look to chase the top spot in the AFC North this weekend when they meet up against the Houston Texans.
The two sides will play at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.

title: Browns' Silence at Trade Deadline Means One Thing for Deshaun Watson Moving Forward
full_text:
The NFL’s trade deadline for the 2026-‘27 season flew by, and the Cleveland Browns mostly stayed pat , save for a few practice squad moves.
Among other things, that means that the Browns remain unchanged at the quarterback position, headlined by starter Deshaun Watson and backed up by Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green.
While most of the conversation regarding Cleveland and potential trade targets revolved around other positions, mainly defensive line help, some league observers suggested the Browns could move on from one of their quarterbacks, even bringing up the possibility of trading Watson away.
Since no deal was struck, Watson is now expected to reclaim his starting job after missing last weekend’s start with a concussion as Sanders returns to the bench, pending head coach Todd Monken’s official announcement .
Well, for starters, Sanders didn’t exactly set the world on fire during his only start of the season, last Sunday against New Orleans. While the second-year passer did have his moments and only a failed 2-point conversion in overtime prevented him from leading the Browns to his first win of the season, he needed much more than what he offered to warrant a longer stay in the top position.
The club’s inaction at a point in the season when the team is still very much in the thick of the playoff hunt at 5-4, despite woeful quarterback performances all season long, would seem to point to the team believing it’s not just one passer away from true contention. This theory gains traction when you look at the offensive line and running game performances through the first nine weeks.
Most importantly, it signals that the Browns are still in audition mode with Watson. If the front office’s mind were already made up about these being definitely the last few games with Watson at the helm, why not try to get something in return? It was known across the league that at least one playoff contender was looking to add a seasoned quarterback after a miserable Monday Night Football outing.
At the same time, the Browns are staring down the barrel of a gun with a pending $86 million dead cap hit for next year due to void years tacked on at the end of his contract, and if the Browns don’t designate him a post-June cut before March 13 —allowing the team to split that hit over two years— it would automatically trigger an unfathomable $200 million salary guarantee .
That’s the one thing we can all bet won’t happen in Cleveland. Then again, it’s the Browns we’re talking about .
Likewise, if Monken and the team were truly convinced he’s the franchise quarterback, the Browns would already be negotiating with him to decrease his cap numbers and allow the team to find help at other positions.
So, it looks like the audition isn’t done. While the expectation is that the Browns will use the draft capital acquired from the Myles Garrett trade to find a new passer, the team seemingly wants to keep its options open with Watson, just in case.
Again, the Browns don’t seem to be completely sure about Watson beyond the next eight games. Therefore, keeping a couple of cheap young passers with starting experience in the fold while determining where the team’s next franchise quarterback will come from sounds like a plan.
Maybe the Browns will try the veteran route once again, as they did with Watson. Sanders and Gabriel’s very palatable deals make them great backup candidates, with Green as a developmental option for the future. And if Cleveland tries going back to the draft well once again, then Sanders and Gabriel would be asked to step into a mentor role for whoever comes in.
In any case, Cleveland really didn’t look like it was seriously considering moving on from any of its quarterbacks at the deadline. At 5-4, the Browns' front office seems a little nervous about risking their current playoff chances, and opting to stay stuck with a below-average quarterback situation that has shockingly produced last-second wins seems to support this thesis.
The problem is that the quarterback play that led to those surprising last-minute wins is unsustainable in the long run, as Cleveland is about to find out .
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Make Big Decision on Deshaun Watson's Future in a Cleveland Browns Uniform
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns will not give Shedeur Sanders another chance at the starting quarterback job.
After speculation stole the headlines the last few days, ESPN Browns Insider Daniel Oyefusi has officially confirmed that the Browns will turn back to Deshaun Watson to be the team's starting quarterback. The 31-year-old was out last weekend due to concussion protocol, but will now return following a nice break to get healthy.
"[Jeremy Fowler] reported on Monday that Watson was expected to return to the starting lineup after missing the Saints game," Oyefusi continued in his X post announcing the decision. "Though Todd Monken declined to name a starter two days ago , it will be Watson."
The Browns will start Deshaun Watson at quarterback against the Texans, per source. @JFowlerESPN reported on Monday that Cleveland was expected to return to the starting lineup after missing the Saints game. Though Todd Monken declined to name a starter two days ago, it will be…
Sanders nearly led the Browns to an overtime win on the road in New Orleans, but came up just short on a failed two-point conversion. He did pass for nearly 300 yards with two touchdowns, though, as the Browns lost 23-22.
This decision may seem like a simple one, especially considering the Browns are 5-3 with Watson as the starter this season; however, it will have massive implications for the future of the team.
Obviously, it felt like this decision was always going to be made.
The Browns made it clear that Sanders was pretty much just filling in for Watson until he was healthy enough to return. But with how the 24-year-old played, questions were obviously raised on whether or not he did enough to get another week as the starter.
Turning right back to Watson, though, means that the plan is for Watson to be the team's starting quarterback for the rest of the season.
If Monken and the rest of the organization believed what they saw from Sanders on Sunday was enough to make him the long-term quarterback of the future, they would have made the change. After all, Sanders is in just his second season of NFL ball, while Watson is approaching the back half of his career and on an expiring deal.
The decision may be the best one for the short-term success of the team, but when it comes to the long-term side, it just continues to cast a dark cloud over the franchise.
#Browns will start Deshaun Watson at QB Sunday against the Texans, source confirms.
Because now, how do you open back up the quarterback battle this offseason? If Sanders were truly meant to start, wouldn't he have had the job by now, especially after a pretty strong outing last week?
Whatever is going on behind the scenes, especially in the decision-making process, only continues to drag out the Watson era in Cleveland.
If he finds success and leads the Browns to the playoffs this season, great. But no matter what happens, questions are going to be asked this offseason about what the future at the position looks like.
And it is hard to tell if the Browns even have any answers.

title: One Game’s Enough To Remind Browns What They Gave Up by Trading Myles Garrett
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are currently a Top-10 team in the NFL when it comes to sacks (26) and pressure rate (32.7 percent) against opposing offenses.
Sounds pretty good, right? Not when you expected to be so much better.
If the Browns keep up their current pace, they would end the regular season with 49 sacks, four less than last year’s total. And their pressure rate is around 2.4 percent worse than last year’s.
The big difference, of course, is that Myles Garrett no longer plays for Cleveland. Garrett, who set the single season sack record last year with 23, was traded to the Los Angeles Rams during the offseason for a 2027 first-round, 2028 second round and 2029 third round pick, along with edge defender Jared Verse.
And this is the real concerning part: the Browns have been able to generate decent 2026 pass rushing numbers without Garrett on the roster, and without Verse making a noticeable contribution.
Thread on Browns DE Jared Verse's production this season: In addition to not registering a sack yet, Verse has been credited with six initial pressures. His pressure rate (3.3%) ranks 185th out of 198 qualifying players. His EDGE pass-rush win rate (10.8%) ranks 57th out of 58…
After nine games with the Browns, Verse has been credited with 15 pressures by Pro Football Focus, while ESPN analytics had him ranked 185th out of 198 qualifying players with a pressure rate of 3.3% before this weekend’s Saints game. During this matchup, Verse also saw his snap count percentage dip below 60.0 on defense (57.3) for just the second time this year.
Meanwhile, Garrett has appeared in just two contests so far in the season--the Week 1 game in Melbourne where he came away with zero sacks and tackles, and last Sunday’s monster performance against Washington, where he literally took over.
In 309 fewer defensive snaps, Garrett has already produced three sacks and one forced fumble more than Verse, as well as one tackle for a loss and three quarterback hits less than his counterpart. Just to be clear: yes, those numbers for Garrett have come in seven full games less than Verse.
. @RamsNFL @Flash_Garrett Superman was back in uniform and played like he was trying to make up for lost time in rehab... #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/1fms3ZUbTk
Since Day 1, Cleveland has made a point of talking up how much of a positive impact Verse has had since arriving on the Berea campus, especially in the locker room.
Everybody pointed to how Verse stayed after practice to help rookie Spencer Fano during summer workouts, or how his in-practice fight with Fano a few days later helped the team gain full confidence in the first-rounder and his readiness for the starting job.
He’s also been a very vocal leader, even prompting Browns’ captain and arguably the team’s best defensive player, Denzel Ward, to say this about the two defensive ends back in early October:
"Definitely brought a lot of juice and just mentality, as well," said Ward regarding what Verse brings to the table , according to Rams Wire. "Myles is a heck of a player, great player, but I think Jared, he's more vocal, more of a vocal player, vocal leader out there for us. Since the first day he stepped in the building, just yelling, screaming and making his mark out there in meetings and on the practice field, kind of rallying guys. So definitely respect who he is as a player and the way he approaches the game and how he brings guys along."
All that sounds great. But you know what else would be great? It would be great if Verse’s notable leadership skill came accompanied by the kind of on-the-field production that led to him being appointed Defensive Rookie of the Year and an essential condition in order for the Browns to go along with the Myles Garrett trade.
Of course, Cleveland has yet to execute three high draft picks, and depending on who they select over the course of the next few years, they could come out clearly on top of this deal. But as things stand right now, the Browns might even feel forced to invest one of those picks at the defensive end position, either on a trade or through the draft .
There’s no way of knowing how good the Browns’ defense could be this year if Garrett were still on the team, playing alongside pleasantly surprising contributors such as Michael Hall or Sam Williams . His injury this year creates an enormous "what if?" scenario. But we will know, in time, what Verse’s eventual output for the club will be.
And we also know beyond a shadow of a doubt, that what he’s done for the team after the first nine games in a Cleveland uniform is quite simply not enough.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: What Jerry Jeudy Keeps Doing for the Browns Explains Why He Wasn't Traded
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has come and gone.
And after weeks of speculation about what the Cleveland Browns would do, the answer was ultimately nothing.
The front office decided to keep all four quarterbacks, controversial wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and their 2027 draft picks. Rumored to be in the market for a backup edge rusher and a blocking tight end, the Browns are keeping the core group that has led them to a 5- 4 record and trust the guys in-house.
Of everything that was possible at the deadline, the Browns sticking with Jeudy stands out the most.
Currently projected to have career-lows in nearly every statistic, all while being practically a non-factor on game day up until the fourth quarter, it seemed that the two sides' best fit was going in different directions.
But instead, the Browns stuck by the 27-year-old.
There is a reason the Browns have kept Jeudy around, even if he has just 18 catches for 208 yards and zero scores this season.
While his numbers don't jump off the sheet , not by any means, he has continued to show up when Cleveland needs him the most.
This past weekend, in a one-point loss to the New Orleans Saints, Jeudy was one of Shedeur Sanders' go-to targets down the stretch. He had zero catches going into the team's final drive, but hauled in a 30-yard pass to help set the Browns up for a game-tying field goal a few plays later.
His ability to make plays down the stretch, especially in close-knit contests, has become an underrated part of what he brings to the Browns' offense this year.
Whether it is his ability to find space, make a difficult catch with a defender right on top of him or just simply situational understanding, his experience has become invaluable, especially with so many youngsters playing alongside him.
The Browns had many obvious reasons to move on from him, most notably the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, all while second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr. continues to dominate, but it is the overlooked parts of his game that make it worthwhile to keep him into the back half of the season.
And after all, Jeudy being your third option in the wide receiver room and fourth target in the passing game isn't a bad thing at all. The more depth, sometimes, the better.
While Jeudy and the Browns could reassess the current situation in the offseason, the conversation should revolve around his long-term plans in the league.
If Jeudy believes he is still a No. 1 option, then a trade should be made to give him the opportunity to go and do just that . The last thing Cleveland needs is a guy frustrated with his role, especially if his targets remain on the decline as Boston and Concepcion continue to grow.
However, if Jeudy is understanding of where he is at in his career and what the plans for the Browns are moving forward, the two sides should discuss a potential contract restructuring.
It isn't that the Browns want to take away his money, but rather to find a way to spread his cap hit out across a few years, giving the team less financial strain on a third or fourth option offensively. He is under contract through the 2027 season, where he will have a cap hit of roughly $13 million.
It seems unlikely that the two sides will ever part ways, especially considering the Browns stood by Jeudy at this year's trade deadline.
However, if the 2027 NFL Draft rolls around the bend and it makes sense to flip Jeudy for a late-round draft pick, he could end up in a new uniform by the time next season begins.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: What the Browns Standing Pat at the Trade Deadline Means for the Bigger Picture
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and a handful of teams upgraded their roster. The deadline provides an opportunity for teams to upgrade their rosters and fill positions of need to help them improve their playoff and Super Bowl chances.
But the Cleveland Browns, whom many expected to be somewhat active, decided to stay quiet and stick with the guys they already have on the roster.
However, others made their phone calls and strengthened their sides before the back half of the season gets underway.
The Minnesota Vikings sent a third-round pick to reunite with quarterback Kirk Cousins, and multiple first-round picks were used by teams looking to upgrade their defense. Other teams sought veterans to fill injury-plagued position groups.
The Browns, who have multiple areas that they could have addressed for a playoff push, chose to stay with their current roster and future picks.
#Browns made no trades by Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline despite working the phones.
Andrew Berry may have made the correct call by not giving up any assets prior to the deadline, though.
The team got off to a hot 5-2 start, and the playoff conversation was very real, but they have dropped two straight games, and the outlook of the season may be shifting.
They showed that they want to take a real look at Shedeur Sanders at some point this season. Deshaun Watson was cleared from a concussion protocol prior to Sunday’s game, but they still chose to start Sanders.
The bye week is coming up, and a shift to permanently start Sanders could end up being sooner rather than later.
The Browns do not have a projected starting quarterback for next season, and Sanders is the closest person that it could be. They have two first-round picks next season, and there are multiple quarterbacks expected to go in the first round.
The Browns more than likely have played themselves out of a top pick, meaning a quarterback is off the table, and they will need as many assets as possible going into the draft to build around who they already have.
The defensive line could use help to stop the run, but the two linemen who were traded at the deadline went for first-round picks. That price is too steep for a team with no real Super Bowl aspirations this season.
A player like Los Angeles edge rusher Khalil Mack, who is older and on an expiring deal, could have been landed for a low-round pick, but the Chargers seemed to be asking a lot for him.
Currently, Browns edge rushers Isaiah McGuire and Jared Verse are having a quiet season and would be better off getting all the reps for the remainder of the season, then bringing in a fresh face who would be looking to learn a new scheme as well.
The offense could have used a run-blocking tight end to allow Harold Fannin Jr. to do what he does best by catching the ball.
Although a tight end would be cheap on the trade market, the Browns have three fourth-round picks and two fifth-round picks next year. A good blocking tight end can be had in the middle of the draft and would be under team control for four years under a rookie contract. That could be Cleveland's mindset.
The Browns could have also used a running back to help spark their offense. Tony Pollard would have been a good option for this season, but he is older and on an expiring contract. Other running backs would cost a high draft pick, like Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor, which the Browns would probably rather use to get a running back on a rookie contract.
Standing pat at the deadline was Berry’s best decision.
He has had two fantastic drafts in a row and has kept all of his ammunition to try and run things back a third time.

title: 'They’re Drowning Right Now': Former WR Jarvis Landry Rips Browns' Recent Loss
full_text:
Down 23-22 in overtime against the New Orleans Saints, Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was faced with a decision: kick the extra point for the tie, or go for two for the win.
After Shedeur Sanders failed to connect with Denzel Boston in the end zone, the two-point try cost Cleveland the game .
On Monday, former Browns wide receiver Jarvis Landry didn’t hold back when sharing his thoughts on the head coach’s play call.
“I’m gonna say this. A tie is better than a loss,” he said on the 4th and South podcast. “You can’t go into these games, into these situations… I listened to the Todd Monken press conference after the game, he said it was either a tie or lose, or tie or win, or some s— he said. I don’t know what he said, it’s just that confusing, as confusing as the decision he made to go for two.”
“A tie is better than a loss… I think it was a horrible call.” 😤 Jarvis Landry says Todd Monken’s two-point gamble against the New Orleans Saints cost the Cleveland Browns 🏈❌ #Browns #DawgPound #Saints #NFL pic.twitter.com/BfymFeVvfC
The Saints had possession to start overtime, putting together an 11-play, 5:43 drive that ended in a touchdown.
Sanders then took the Browns down the field and capped off Cleveland's drive with a 39-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. to bring the score within one point with a minute on the clock.
“You’re on the road, you have your backup quarterback who is doing the best he can to stay on his feet to throw the ball down the field, and you're gonna go for two?” Landry said. “I think it was a horrible call… Calls like that is what defines a season. That tie could be something that could help them get into the playoffs. They’re drowning right now.”
Despite the failed attempt, Monken defended his decision after the game.
“You make the decision as the clock winds down a little bit, because you’re at that point to where they still have their two timeouts. So if you kick the extra point, the way the overtime rules are with 10 minutes is that they’re going to be in two-minute with two timeouts and need a field goal to win it. So, you’re not going to get the ball back, probably. So you’re really saying, tie or lose.”
Monken also gave credit to Sanders, who, despite completing just five passes for 38 yards in the first half, put together a performance that kept Cleveland in the game. He finished with 297 yards after completing 19 of 31 passes for two touchdowns .
“He gave us a chance at the end, he really did. Made some plays, made some plays with his legs to extend plays and get us first downs,” Monken said. “I’m really proud of him.”
Sunday’s loss gives the Browns a 5-4 record and the No. 3 spot in a tight AFC North race.
They’ll look to avoid a three-game losing streak on Sunday, Nov. 15, as they host the 3-5 Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field.

title: Stephen A. Smith Changes Tune on Cowboys Because of Pity For 'My Buddy' Jerry Jones
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys fans might have a new member added to their group moving forward and it is none other than notorious Cowboys hater Stephen A. Smith.
Smith is always relentless in his criticism and mockery of the Cowboys, who have been unable to flip the script on the ESPN host because of how bad they've been this season and for the better part of the past 30 years.
But Smith revealed he might actually start rooting for the Cowboys moving forward and the reason has to do with his relationship with owner Jerry Jones.
During the latest episode of "First Take," Smith explained why he may start rooting for the Cowboys.
"I don't have any problem with the misery associated with the Dallas Cowboy fans," Stephen A. explained . "They're the most disgusting, nauseating fan base in American history. I have no problem. I get joy out of seeing them miserable.
"But Jerry's my buddy and I'm tired of seeing him suffer like this. I'm getting to the point where I might have to start rooting for the Cowboys because it's so predictable and it's been 30 years and I'm starting to feel bad about how they just fall in line with everything that I predict."
Smith and Jones indeed have a friendship , something we saw recently when Stephen A. was sitting next to Jerry in his box during a game this season.
Despite their friendship and what he's saying about rooting for the Cowboys, we're quite confident Smith isn't going to stop trolling the team anytime soon.
Smith shouldn't feel bad for Jones because a lot of the ills we've seen from Dallas over the years are no doubt the Cowboys owner's fault.
Instead of hiring a general manager, Jones continues to insist on staying in that role, and his decision to hire Brian Schottenheimer and keep him despite the obscene amount of dysfunction this team has seen since 2025 is another stain on Jones.
Despite the fact that he might start rooting for the Cowboys, Stephen A. doesn't think Dallas is going to win in Week 10.
"I just want to be nice. I mean, it's getting to the point where I think I'm going to start rooting for them because I know they're going to lose this weekend," Smith said. "They're going to find a way to lose this weekend and I'm just at the point where I just don't think Jerry Jones deserves this."
Hard to argue with that prediction based on what we've seen from the Cowboys and Niners this season.
After all, we've seen the Cowboys lose to what should have been lesser opponents like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Arizona Cardinals, and they nearly lost to an abysmal Indianapolis Colts team last week.
Their chances of beating an elite team like San Francisco are slim, at best. Even Jones has acknowledged the tough test Dallas has this week.
"And overall, we’re not playing very good. And we’re sure going to have to take what we’ve done over the last several weeks, put the best parts of it together, because we’ve got a real challenge coming up this weekend with San Francisco," Jones said .
The Cowboys have lost multiple trap games this season. Maybe they can be on the other end of that against the Niners, but we wouldn't bet on that happening.

title: George Pickens Injury Update and More From Cowboys' Wednesday Practice Report
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have put out their first injury report of the week ahead of the Week 10 game against the San Francisco 49ers.
The Cowboys' injury report is once again lengthy this week, with the team having a whopping 16 players on the list, including wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
Pickens and Porter are two of the biggest names to keep an eye on this week, especially after both of them sat out in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts.
Here's how their practice day went and more as we take a look at the Wednesday injury report for Dallas.
It was status quo for Pickens, who turned in a limited practice on Wednesday. The star wideout was limited all week last week before he was inactive .
Because he didn't play after turning in three limited practices last week, we won't be confident Pickens will go on Sunday until he turns in a full session.
He'll have two more opportunities to do that on Thursday and Friday before Dallas puts out its final injury report.
A total of eight players did not practice on Wednesday, including Porter, edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku, tight end Jake Ferguson and safety P.J. Locke, who suffered his second concussion in as many weeks, which makes him unlikely to play.
We already know that running back Tyler Goodson and Ferguson are going to miss multiple weeks , as head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Monday.
Ezeirauku picked up his injury against the Colts and is considered day-to-day, the Cowboys said .
The lack of practice participation for Porter is a downgrade from last week, when Porter finished off the week with a limited practice before sitting out on Sunday. That's a bad sign for his chances of suiting up in Week 10 against the Niners.
Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who missed yet another game in Week 9 and even committed a boneheaded penalty despite being inactive, was status quo with his limited session.
The limited practice for Turpin, who has missed multiple games, is an upgrade and gives him a chance to return, as does the full practice for tight end Luke Schoonmaker.
Rookie cornerback Devin Moore was designated to return from injured reserve and turned in a full practice, so that gives him a chance to play.
There's a chance he could see some action if Porter is ruled out, but we know Cobie Durant would start in Porter's place
As is the case with Moore, defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard is in the midst of his 21-day practice window after it was opened a few weeks ago.
Bullard was able to practice in full all three days last week and another full practice keeps him on track. If he can return, Bullard could offer a boost to Dallas' putrid run defense .

title: ESPN Confirms Why Dallas Cowboys Didn't Trade George Pickens on Deadline Day
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were one of the teams that decided to stand pat at the trade deadline on Tuesday, so it's status quo for the team the rest of the season.
Ahead of the deadline, the belief was that if the Cowboys did make a trade, it would be for an edge rusher. However, as the deadline drew closer and closer, owner Jerry Jones made it clear he expected a quiet deadline .
As the Cowboys sank further and further into the depths of despair this season, many wondered if the Cowboys might consider trading George Pickens.
But, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , that was never in the table for the Cowboys, who just didn't want to trade Pickens. Adding to that, Pickens didn't want to be traded, either.
What's more interesting is Fowler noting that the Cowboys didn't so much as receive a call on Pickens.
"The Cowboys did not receive any trade calls on receiver George Pickens, who is happy in Dallas and didn't want to be traded," he said. "Teams in the receiver market weren't shopping in the high-end aisle, either, so the idea of a Pickens trade was a nonstarter. Plus, Dallas had no plans to deal him."
It's surprising that the Cowboys did receive any calls on Pickens. Granted, it's possible teams simply knew he wasn't available, but we saw other teams inquire about players who were never going to be traded, like the Denver Broncos did with Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, and the New York Giants did with Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson, per reports.
Pickens garnered a bad repuation around the NFL after his messy stint with the Pittsburgh Steelers. The lack of calls about him at the deadline might be a sign that things haven't changed on that front, or at least not enough for teams to trade for him.
That really has to make the Cowboys wonder if there will be much of a market for Pickens in 2027 if they decide to take the tag-and-trade route. That's a problem because if the Cowboys tag him and nobody is looking to trade for him, they will be hampered by the franchise tag money being on the books and could also have a situation in which Pickens holds out if he isn't amenable to the franchise tag for a second consecutive season.
This now at least opens the door slightly for the Cowboys to just let Pickens walk and pick up a compensatory pick if they aren't interested in keeping him long term.
We suspect teams will have much more interest in adding the veteran wide receiver if he doesn't cost draft capital to acquire.
If Pickens were to hit the open market, he should garner enough in a contract to net the Cowboys a third-round compensatory pick, but that will depend upon how active the Cowboys are in free agency, also.

title: Cowboys' Lack of Deadline Trade a Sign Reality Has Sunk in For Jerry Jones
full_text:
NFL trade deadline day came and went and the Dallas Cowboys did not make a trade after months of talk from owner Jerry Jones that he was interested in making another move.
Jones had said so in training camp after making a flurry of moves during the offseason, and he held his stance even after the trade for Joey Porter Jr. with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
But a lot has changed since back in training camp, and even since the Porter trade.
We've discovered that, despite everything Jones did during the offseason and into the regular season, none of it worked.
On 105.3 The Fan , Bryan Broaddus said that he thinks the lack of a move at the deadline is a sign that Jones finally realizes his team just isn't any good.
"I think that Jerry has come to the realization that his team isn't any good," Broaddus said. "I think he understands where the defense is at."
"I think there's a lot of those guys, the lieutenants and stuff, that tell him stuff and he's probably a little bit disappointed in them," Broaddus added.
The writing was on the wall for days leading up to the deadline that the Cowboys wouldn't do anything. After all, Jones went out of his way to temper expectations and said "I don't look for us to make a significant trade" on deadline day.
Based on everything we have heard from Jones recently, we agree with Broaddus that the Cowboys owner didn't have any motivation to make another move after what has transpired in 2026.
Jones has definitely sounded more disappointed of late, which is a change because, even with all of the terrible play this season, he usually tries to stay optimistic.
After the Cowboys barely defeated a lowly Indianapolis Colts team in Week 9, Jones called the win "bittersweet" and admitted that his team isn't "playing very good" and needed "some help to get that win."
Jones also wouldn't give a direct answer when asked if his lack of aggressiveness at the trade deadline was a result of the team's inconsistent play this season.
"I cant answer that. I don’t know," Jones said before admitting that the team hadn't had any meaningful talks about adding a player in multiple weeks.
That sure sounds like an owner who realizes that there is nothing he can do to save this team, and we can't blame Jerry if he feels that way.
There has been no indication that the Cowboys are even close to righting the ship and they aren't one player away from fixing their issues, which are no doubt systemic.
So, giving up another draft pick or more for a trade that probably wouldn't have helped, anyway, wouldn't have been a wise idea.
The fact of the matter is, the Cowboys are going to need at least another offseason to fix their issues on defense, and that process should start with an overhaul of the coaching staff, starting with head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

title: Dallas Cowboys Signing Former Saints Running Back After Tyler Goodson Injury
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys lost running back Tyler Goodson to an injury after the Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts, but they have now added a replacement.
With Goodson on the shelf for now, the Cowboys only had one healthy running back on their active roster, which is of course Javonte Williams, and two on their practice squad in Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin, so they needed more help.
Well, the Cowboys have now added someone.
According to Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News , the Cowboys are signing former New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller to the practice squad.
"The Cowboys will do something today, a person with knowledge of the situation said the team will sign RB Kendre Miller to practice squad," Watkins reported.
Miller was a 2023 third-round pick of the Saints out of TCU.
He has spent all four years of his career with the Saints, compiling 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns to go along with 29 receptions for 217 receiving yards in 27 games.
Miller's most productive season was actually his rookie year in 2023, when he posted 156 rushing yards and career-highs in receiving yards (117) and scrimmage yards (273).
The former Saints draft pick is a decent runner and pass-catcher, but he doesn't do anything special in either area. He also struggles in pass protection, so he won't be an ideal option to play on obvious passing downs.
Miller does have good size at 6-foot and 220 pounds, but that size has not helped him avoid injuries. Over his three-plus seasons in the NFL, Miller has missed a total of 29 games, including 10 last season due to a torn ACL.
Thankfully, Goodson, who suffered a knee injury in Week 9, did not come down with a major injury, but he is expected to miss multiple weeks. It isn't yet clear if he'll need an injured reserve stint.
According to his dad, Maurice, it's "just a sprain" for Goodson, and ESPN's Todd Archer reports it's a sprain of his MCL and ACL .
It's a shame for Goodson, who was starting to emerge with Dallas after a strong showing against his former team, the Colts, that saw him tally 77 yards on 12 carries.
Goodson was claimed off waivers by the Cowboys back in September and has appeared in seven games since then.
In those seven contests, he's tallied 163 rushing yards and over four yards per carry, and he has also added 23 receiving yards.
Prior to his stint with the Cowboys, Goodson had spent the last three seasons with the Colts.

title: Why Dallas Cowboys Didn't Make a Trade on Deadline Day and What NFC East Rivals Did
full_text:
After a lot of talk from owner Jerry Jones about his willingness to make a trade, even after the deal for Joey Porter Jr., the Cowboys remained quiet on deadline day.
The 4 p.m. ET deadline came and went and the Cowboys did not make a deal on Tuesday. To be quite honest, that really wasn't a surprise, as Jones had said on a few occasions that he didn't expect anything to happen.
Jones was still open to a deal when he spoke to 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday, but he also stated he didn't expect anything significant for the Cowboys on deadline day.
“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling. It’s really not ringing," he said. "But don’t count it out," Jones said. "A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
Now, let's dive into what might have led to the Cowboys standing pat, and we'll look at what the rest of the NFC East did.
There could be a whole host of reasons why the Cowboys didn't make a deal.
For starters, the Cowboys needed a major move, especially for an edge rusher, but those guys are rarely available. And, if they are, the price is astronomical.
Even if there was a trade available for an elite edge rusher, Dallas would have had a tough time making it work given their lack of draft capital as a result of trades in recent years.
There were probably smaller trades to be had, but, again, Dallas was likely in the market for something big because of how poorly the defense has played this season. A lesser move would not have been worth giving up the draft capital for.
There is also the possibility that Jerry realizes there was probably no trade that can help this team and he might have sworn off a deal entirely in order to salvage the draft picks he has left.
Like the Cowboys, the Giants and Commanders did not make a move on deadline day. The Giants in particular were involved in plenty of rumors, but in the end they didn't do anything.
As for the Eagles, they almost made a trade on deadline day by sending Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, but hilariously, the Bengals pulled out of the deal after realizing it would cost them a third-round compensatory pick they are due to get after the departure of Trey Hendrickson in free agency.
The Eagles did, however, pull off a blockbuster trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Monday that sent Jordan Davis to Duval. That's good news for the Cowboys because now they won't have to deal with the mammoth interior defensive lineman twice a year anymore. Philly did, however, get a nice haul of a first- and second-round pick.

title: Dallas Cowboys Showing Interest in Signing Former Saints RB Before Week 10
full_text:
It feels unlikely that the Dallas Cowboys will be making any trades ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday at 3 p.m. CT.
But that hardly means Dallas will stay quiet when it comes adding some new faces to the roster through free agency.
The Cowboys will be without backup running back Tyler Goodson for multiple weeks after he suffered a knee injury in the win over the Indianapolis Colts. As a result, Dallas faces some legitmate depth concerns behind running back Javonte Williams. The Cowboys recently signed former training camp running back Jashaun Corbin to the practice squad but Dallas needs a more immediate solution.
Now, ahead of Week 10's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, the Cowboys could be on the brink of getting exactly what they need at the backup running back spot.
The Cowboys are hosting former New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller for a visit on Tuesday, per reports from ESPN's Todd Archer.
This comes after Jerry Jones said that the Cowboys would be adding a new running back through free agency, a move that became obvious once Goodson went down.
Miller, 24, has been with New Orleans since 2023, playing primarily as a backup. Despite running back injuries of their own, the Saints waived him on Saturday.
In 27 career games and three starts with the Saints, Miller posted 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns along with 29 catches for 217 yards.
A native of tiny Mount Enterprise High School in East Texas, Miller was a little-known recruit before bursing onto the scene with the TCU Horned Frogs.
After 10 total touchdowns combined across his first two seasons, Miller helped lead TCU to the College Football Playoff National Championship game in 2022, finishing that season with 224 carries for 1,399 yards and 17 touchdowns. This production motivated the Saints to take him in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft.
Cowboys fans that double as TCU fans in the Fort Worth area are all too familiar with Miller and have likely kept watch of his journey through the NFL since leaving college.
After the Cowboys-Saints preseason game in August, Miller gathered with three former TCU teammates on the Cowboys -- linebacker Dee Winters, wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end DJ Rogers -- for a postgame picture.
Fast forward a few months later, and it's possible he could be joining Dallas, though time will tell. Don't expect Miller to be the only free agent running back the Cowboys show interest in.

title: Trades Dallas Cowboys Could Make Today & Chances Deals Happen
full_text:
NFL trade deadline day is here and this will be the last chance the Dallas Cowboys have to make a deal to improve their roster for the second half of the season.
Jerry Jones has maintained over and over again that he is open to making another trade, even after the Joey Porter Jr. deal, but in recent days he has expressed pessimism about getting something done.
"If it's substantive for sure... you don't have any idea until you have the meeting of the minds and it's done. At this point I don't see it," Jones told 105.3 The Fan .
Edge rusher remains the Cowboys' biggest need ahead of the trade deadline. With that in mind, here's a look at some possible targets for the Cowboys and the chances Dallas will acquire them.
Crosby recently reiterated that he wants to stay with the Raiders and reports suggest Las Vegas won't deal him .
However, we've already seen the Raiders trade him once for a big package, so we wouldn't rule it out from happening again if the Raiders get an offer they can't refuse.
The Cowboys will have to throw at least two first-round picks at the Raiders, which they have, and we could see Jerry doing it because adding an elite edge rusher is the only kind of move Dallas can make to even have a chance to save its defense.
That said, we find it hard to believe Crosby is going anywhere.
Sweat is a more realistic option than Crosby given the state of things over there in Arizona, as the Cardinals are having a bad season and are in the midst of a rebuild. Sweat will also be far cheaper than Crosby, so that's another reason.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz recently reported that the belief is Sweat is open to a trade, but it remains to be seen if Arizona actually wants to move him, Schultz added.
It sure would make sense for Arizona to move him because the team needs more draft capital for its rebuild and Sweat could decline before the Cardinals are good again.
The problem is the Cowboys might have to overpay in order to get him and we're not sure they're willing to do that given the team's dwindling stable of picks.
McDonald has reportedly requested a trade , but rumors suggest the New York Jets aren't interested in trading him and head coach Aaron Glenn has also said that publicly.
If the Jets are willing to move McDonald, he's probably the most realistic option on this list because of cost. Because he's less proven than Sweat, McDonald should come cheaper, and potentially for a fourth-round pick.
We could see Jones having the stomach for this kind of trade more than overpaying for Sweat.
Speculation has run rampant about a Pickens trade in recent weeks as the Cowboys have struggled mightily.
However, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports the Cowboys have no interest in trading Pickens.
"The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason. Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources," Harris said.
That said, as we saw with the Chicago Bears' trade for Jeffery Simmons, just about anyone can be had if the offer is big enough. Knowing that, we wouldn't rule out a team throwing an offer at the Cowboys that they can't refuse.
The Cowboys may look to add at cornerback, safety or linebacker, but needs at those spots aren't dire as long as Dallas' injured players can get back.
At cornerback, the Cowboys aren't benching DaRon Bland even though he's terrible, and they obviously have Joey Porter Jr. and Cobie Durant, so there's enough there, assuming Porter can get past his ankle injury .
When it comes to safety, the Cowboys just lost P.J. Locke to yet another concussion, so that's a concern, and Jalen Thompson remains on injured reserve and we don't know when he'll be back, although he is now eligible to return off IR.
At linebacker, DeMarvion Overshown is hurt again and clearly the Cowboys can't depend on him. Dallas has also apparently lost faith in Jaishawn Barham after he played just three snaps in Week 9.
All that said, we continue to believe if the Cowboys pull the trigger on any trade, it's going to be at edge rusher, although we wouldn't totally rule out an addition at these three spots.
Trade chances for Linebacker: 30% Trade chances for safety: 30% Trade chances for cornerback: 10%

title: Jerry Jones Teases Dallas Cowboys Trade At NFL Deadline Without Going All-In
full_text:
There has been rampant speculation about whether the Dallas Cowboys will make a splash at the NFL trade deadline , with the team needing massive improvements on the defensive side of the ball.
Last season, the Cowboys added All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to the roster, while trading for cornerback Joey Porter Jr . earlier in the season. While those were improvements for the team, there is still a lack of overall talent on the roster.
With the deadline coming up in a matter of hours, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones stopped by 105.3 The Fan to share his thoughts on what could be coming for the team.
Once again, Jones teased a potential move for the Cowboys , but indicated it would not be anything groundbreaking or a headline-making move.
According to Jon Machota of The Athletic, Jones said “don’t count out” the Cowboys potentially making a move at the deadline, but it came with an unfortunate disclaimer.
“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling. It’s really not ringing … but don’t count it out," Jones said. "A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
If the Cowboys were in the process of making a splash, Jones would likely be more excited and teasing the move in order to make headlines. We've seen that is the way that Jones likes to operate. But, for now, the Cowboys appear poised to stand firm with their current roster for the rest of the season, though they could add a few rotational pieces.
We will find out how everything plays out over the next few hours, with the NFL trade deadline coming at 4:00 p.m. ET. If there is a move, let's hope it is to improve the team on defense, because the current NFL rankings are less than inspiring.
Total Defense : The Cowboys currently rank No. 30 overall in total defense, giving up 372.7 points per game. The team has allowed 27 touchdowns.
Passing Defense : Dallas has seen an improvement in recent weeks, moving to No. 18 overall in the league. The Cowboys have allowed 16 passing touchdowns, while giving up 225.2 passing yards per game.
Rushing Defense : The Cowboys have been brutal against the run, ranking No. 31 overall above only the Las Vegas Raiders. Dallas has allowed 147.4 rushing yards per game and 11 rushing touchdowns.
