title: Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade With Chargers Falls Through in Stunning Reversal
full_text:
The Daiyan Henley trade has been called off.
The Denver Broncos made the announcement late Wednesday night, saying the Henley deal with the Los Angeles Chargers had fallen through. The team didn't give any explanation for why the trade fell through, but it did release a statement on X.
"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward," the statement read.
pic.twitter.com/vFJ7MYS2UN
NFL trades are subject to a physical. At this early stage, we don't know whether the trade's ill fate had something to do with a physical, though I can't imagine what else could legally allow the Broncos to back out of the trade.
Did it have something to do with the division rival relationship with the Chargers? There are legalities that teams must follow, enforced by the league, so I can't imagine it was a case of the Chargers somehow pulling the wool over the Broncos' eyes or vice versa.
All we can do is speculate for now.
The Chargers responded by posting a "Welcome back, Daiyan" meme on their X account.
https://t.co/Ewbs7j6Yga pic.twitter.com/QzaZ40ZFF7
The deal for Henley, agreed to in principle ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline , would have sent the Broncos' 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers in exchange. The Broncos will obviously be holding onto those picks.
Henley is about to turn 27 and is in the fourth and final year of his rookie contract. He's a two-time team captain in L.A. and is poised to lead the Chargers in tackles for the third straight season.
Broncos fans were excited about the prospect of Henley working into the linebacker rotation with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, especially given his coverage chops. Alas, unless the Broncos seek to sign him as a free agent in the spring, we'll never know how Henley would have fit in.
The Broncos are on bye, with their next game not until November 21, when they'll host the Las Vegas Raiders at Mile High. The Raiders have a new starting quarterback — Fernando Mendoza — and a pair of tight ends who've combined for over 1,000 receiving yards and seven touchdowns already this season.
Let's hope the Broncos have a better answer for Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer than they have the tight ends they faced in their last three games, to whom they allowed 330 yards and three touchdowns.
As more information about the botched Henley trade comes to light, we'll be sure to update this story and offer further reporting and analysis.

title: Sean Payton Puts Broncos' Starting OL on Notice With Bye Week Warning
full_text:
Since Sean Payton took back the play-calling entering Week 5, Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos' offense have been much better.
It was a gradual burn, and that build-up is still ongoing, but Payton has the Broncos back to playing a semblance of winning offense. Most importantly, Nix's confidence has returned — flooding back in Week 7 after his 62-yard touchdown run.
Each week since then, Nix has looked a little bit better, and after beating the Carolina Panthers on the road last Sunday, I don't think too many people are still worried about his football psyche. He's hunting with the football again , challenging defenses vertically, and playing with confidence.
Payton is happy to see the improvements on offense, but with the Broncos hitting their bye at 7-2, there are still several things he wants to clean up.
"I'm pleased with some of the change. Some of the things we're doing better," Payton told Colin Cowherd during an appearance on The Herd . "There's still that yellow tape around the offense that says 'work in progress.' It just is. And yet, I would say this: so much of what we're able to do offensively—run the ball, have balance—can really make what Bo has to do, make his job easier."
What exactly does Payton want to fix over the Broncos' bye? He pointed to the blocking up front, and even hinted that he and the coaches could consider making changes to the starting five, given the offensive line's ongoing struggles and the unit's depth.
"Now, getting specific, like, man, I'm watching the cut-ups from the game we just played, and we didn't block them very well. I'm just being honest, so that has to improve," Payton told Cowherd. "We've got plenty of depth on the offensive line, so during this bye, we're going to look at all those little things closely because the tape that's surrounding the offense needs to come down and the family needs to move in. So that's kind of where we're at."
You've got to love Payton likening the Broncos' offense to a domicile that's under construction, with the yellow cautionary tape surrounding it and whatnot. As he said, the work on the building has been done, and it's time for the family to move into its new home, meaning that it's time for the Broncos to move beyond the struggles they've had with even the most fundamental things on offense.
Thankfully, the Broncos' bye came as close to the midway point of the season as it gets, giving them plenty of tape to self-scout and enough games left to make the type of meaningful changes that could propel them into the playoffs.
"That's the cool thing about the bye right now is you really get this chance to take a zoom and look real close at what's been going well, what hasn't, why hasn't it been, and let's not kid ourselves," Payton said.
It sounds like Payton and his coaches will be brutally honest with themselves about what they've seen on tape. That being said, I wouldn't expect to see Payton make wholesale changes to the offensive line.
If the Broncos do anything, though, they might want to look at making a change at center. Luke Wattenberg has been one of the NFL's worst centers this season, and as frustrating as that is one year removed from the Broncos giving him a four-year, $48 million extension, they can't "kid" themselves.
Wattenberg has been a liability, and he's made life much more difficult for left guard Ben Powers and All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz, who have had to cover for his miscues, mishaps, and mental errors, leading to some social media backlash. The Broncos have Alex Forsyth under contract through this season, and he's got plenty of starting experience and time with Nix, so it might make sense to let Wattenberg sit for a spell to see if things improve.
Jonah Coleman has sparked the Broncos' run game, but it hasn't led to a sudden reversal in fortunes. The Broncos only rushed for 82 yards as a team last week in Carolina, with an average gain of 3.0 yards, compared to the Panthers producing 96 yards on the ground with an average gain of 4.8 yards.
Coleman can create on his own, and that's a blessing, but he can't do it all by himself, and Payton knows that. Payton and run game coordinator Zach Strief must figure out how to get this O-line rowing in the same direction, but that's partly what the bye is for.
In that same conversation with Cowherd, Payton went to bat for his quarterback, making it clear that the Broncos believe Nix to be their franchise quarterback and pushing back at the critics who question his arm strength.
"I know we have the right quarterback in the building," Payton said of Nix. "In other words, I've just seen it. I've seen the behavior, the things that you need in clutch moments, the arm strength. That was probably the biggest false narrative relative to him coming out was his arm strength, and he's got a way-above-average arm talent."
During Nix's early-season slump, the Broncos reportedly became " concerned " with his hesitancy, but they never lost faith in him as their current and future franchise quarterback. Payton wanted to see Nix " let 'er rip ," and that tide began to turn in Week 7 in the Broncos' road win over the Arizona Cardinals.
Over the past three weeks, Nix has exceeded the 200-yard passing mark in each game, and he's been using his legs more often. The assumption was that Nix's early-season slump was a combination of his psyche healing from his ankle injury suffered last January and the Broncos' brutal initial schedule.
Nix looked spooked and overwhelmed at times, but that was punctuated by outbursts of tremendous quarterback play, as seen in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Week 3 against the Los Angeles Rams, and in the first half of Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Nix's pocket presence was terribly inconsistent; his footwork and technical foundation were out of whack, and he looked like he was pressing.
Entering the Week 10 bye, though, all of that feels like ancient history. And despite the obvious mental struggles Nix was going through in his recovery from ankle surgery, he still found ways to win games, even against some of the NFL's tier-one competition.
Nix's resilience and ability to overcome adversity are two of the intangible traits that drew Payton and the Broncos to him, and they likely play a big part in the club's ongoing faith in him as its franchise quarterback. During the period when Nix was struggling, Payton pulled him aside and talked to him, pointing to the enormity of the schedule the NFL gave the Broncos to start this season.
And yet, Nix prevailed — far more often than not, defeating some great teams.
"The quarterback thing, he's going to be outstanding," Payton said of Nix. "And I shared with him, I said, 'Hey, week to week in our league,' I said, 'Do you realize in three weeks, no one will have a clue—last year, no one could tell you about the Jet game last year. No one's going to be able to tell you one thing. Now, you've just gone through a gauntlet of some of the better defenses in football. You've seen the Chiefs twice, you've seen Jacksonville, you've seen Seattle, like, that's a stretch.'"
It hasn't been easy for Nix, but he has found his footing. The resistance training of the first eight games has built up one heck of a football callus.
Nix is playing with great confidence again, and his aura feels no different than it did last year against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round. Despite all the imperfections, despite all the obstacles of the schedule, Nix has the Broncos at 7-2, leading the AFC West, and in position to wrest the No. 1 playoff seed away from the Bills.
"We're at 7-2, and that's the positive," Payton told Cowherd.
Given the schedule Denver has faced, 7-2 is a triumph of willpower and fortitude. Payton deserves a lot of credit, and so does Nix. But the job isn't done yet.
Payton's got to fix this run game. And as he's said, it's long past due.
We'll see what happens between now and Week 16, but it feels like the Broncos are on a…

title: 7 Things to Know About New Broncos LB Daiyan Henley
full_text:
And just like that, the NFL trade deadline has come and gone.
After weeks of speculation and rumor, the Denver Broncos made a move — but not the one fans were expecting — acquiring fourth-year linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
The Broncos had the vision last year of a three-man linebacker rotation, and it was realized in the form of Alex Singleton, Dre Greenlaw (when healthy), and Justin Strnad. Due to the amount of time Greenlaw missed, though, Strnad saw the field way more than even the Broncos anticipated.
After the 2025 season ended, the Broncos made the tough decision to part with Greenlaw after one injury-riddled season, and reupped with Singleton and Strnad, re-signing both to multi-year extensions. That made Strnad an undisputed starter, but the Broncos didn't have the three-man rotation at linebacker.
What should Broncos fans know about a veteran who, until Tuesday, had been nothing but a divisional enemy? Here are seven things to know about Henley and the trade.
Intra-divisional trades are rare, especially in the AFC West. The Chargers had multiple suitors for Henley ahead of the trade deadline, but the Broncos were reportedly the only team knocking on L.A.'s door that was willing to offer a fourth-round pick plus additional compensation.
Part of the Broncos' rationale was surely the 2027 fourth-round compensatory pick they expect to be awarded for the free-agent departure of defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers. Denver entered the trade deadline with a full complement of 2027 draft picks, but with that comp pick coming back, it'll still end up with a fourth-round selection, provided it isn't traded.
Henley was born and raised in Los Angeles and is the youngest son of Eugene "Big U" Henley, a famous hip-hop influencer and former shot-caller of the notorious Rollin' 60s Crips in Crenshaw . Big U played a part in the success of several famous hip-hop artists, like Nipsey Hussle and Kurupt, and was called the "Godfather" of rap music by Wiz Khalifa.
Big U spent a good chunk of Daiyan's childhood behind bars, which helped to keep the youngster on the straight and narrow. Once freed, Big U went on to coach Daiyan in Pee Wee football, guiding him to success and helping him to avoid the same pitfalls and mistakes he made on the streets.
Henley's family is royalty in South Central L.A., which made his selection by the Chargers so fitting. Big U named Daiyan (pronounced DAY-on), which means "mighty ruler" or "protector" in Arabic.
Henley played most of his collegiate career at Nevada before transferring to Washington State for his red-shirt senior year.
Henley is in the fourth and final year of his contract as a 2023 third-round draft pick. According to The Athletic 's Noah Furtado , the Chargers began extension talks with Henley, but no agreement materialized.
The soon-to-be 27-year-old Henley is nearly four years younger than Strnad. The Broncos wanted to get younger at linebacker, and Henley is another step in that direction.
Time will tell exactly what Henley's role will be with the Broncos, but he will see the field. There's a very good chance the Broncos' front office will look to extend him, maybe even before the 2026 season is over.
On Wednesday, Denver restructured safety Talanoa Hufanga's contract to free up nearly $4 million in cap space, so whether it comes during the Week 10 bye or after the season, look for Henley to be re-signed.
With half the season in the books, the Broncos are only on the hook for $1.84 million, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel . That makes the move even more of a home run for Denver.
The Broncos is getting a three-down linebacker with 41 career starts (Strand only has 28) for under $2 million. Even the draft capital relinquished for Henley will be inconsequential, especially if the Broncos are able to get him extended.
That could come sooner than some people might realize.
Henley was a two-time team captain with the Chargers. He was viewed as the most important voice in that locker room, which is one of many reasons why Chargers fans and L.A. media were so surprised by this trade.
On top of that, Henley also wore the green dot on his helmet, signifying that he had the radio on the field. Only one defender can wear the green dot on the field at one time, and the defensive coordinator relays the plays to that player.
Henley was a team captain in L.A. and the Chargers' defensive signal-caller. His football IQ is off the charts, and he's one of the most athletic linebackers in the NFL, even if he isn't the biggest (6-foot-0, 225 pounds).
Henley led the Chargers in tackles in 2024 and 2025, getting well over the century mark both years. His 51 tackles this season led the Chargers, so he was on pace to lead the team in tackles for a third straight season.
His size can be a detriment at times; Henley can struggle to get off blocks and sort through the trash, but he makes up for it with his smarts, instincts, and explosiveness. He's a reliable tackler, but staying out of the paws of the NFL's big interior offensive linemen will be key.
The Broncos might not use Henley right away on first and second down, but as we'll discuss next, they'd be remiss not to use him in obvious passing situations.
Henley has four career interceptions and 15 pass breakups. The Broncos have been in desperate need of a coverage linebacker for years, and he checks that box as a three-down player with coverage chops and a nose for the ball.
The Broncos have struggled mightily this season to cover tight ends and running backs out of the backfield. Denver has allowed the most receiving yards in the NFL to running backs and the second-most to tight ends.
Over the last three games alone, the Broncos relinquished 330 receiving yards and three touchdowns to tight ends. Coming out of the bye, the Broncos will host the Las Vegas Raiders at home.
The Raiders' two tight ends — Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer — have already combined for 1,046 receiving yards and seven touchdowns this season. Granted, a new quarterback — Fernando Mendoza — will be throwing them the ball when the Broncos meet the Raiders in Week 11, but getting Henley in the fold should be a timely buffer.
Henley wore the No. 0 jersey in L.A., but that belongs to Jonathan Cooper in Denver. At Washington State, Henley wore No. 1 — but that's currently occupied by Evan Engram — and he wore the No. 11 at Nevada — but that's Troy Franklin's number.
It'll be interesting to see what jersey number Henley ends up with, but there aren't too many available, let alone the desirable ones that are often rocked by linebackers. There are no single-digit numbers available, and none in the teens, but No. 56 could be had, with Levelle Bailey on injured reserve.

title: What Could Be Coming After Broncos Restructure Hufanga's Contract
full_text:
The Denver Broncos took care of some necessary bookkeeping almost immediately after acquiring inside linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers.
According to Spotrac , the Broncos have restructured the contract of starting safety Talanoa Hufanga, converting $4.89 million of his current salary into a signing bonus. The move created $3.9 million in salary cap space.
This slightly altered the future ramifications of Hufanga's deal, which runs through next season. He now carries cap hits of $9.5 million, $7.6 million, and $14.8 million for 2026, 2027, and 2028, respectively — the latter technically a void year.
An excellent addition since joining the club, Hufanga has been especially impactful thus far this season, winning Defensive Player of the Week honors following his two-interception effort amid Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams.
"I mean, that’s who he is. He finally caught the ball," defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said on Oct. 1. "That could have been him last year a couple of times, but he worked really hard on his ball skills. He really did, seriously, over the spring and the summer. So it’s paying off. He’s trusting the system, he’s trusting his leverage. When he came to us, he wasn’t a match or man-cover player. He was more of a spot drop, vision and break player. So he’s learned how to play in this system, and the weak part of his game was his coverage, but now it’s a strong part of his game."
Hufanga, who's missed the last four games due to an ankle injury, is likely to be back in action when Denver returns from its Week 10 bye to host the Las Vegas Raiders, who'll be starting first-overall pick, quarterback Fernando Mendoza, in the Mile High City.
Since the Broncos were already under the cap when they landed Henley — and they're only taking on less than $2 million in this year's salary — logic would dictate that the brain trust has another transaction up its collective sleeve.
That transaction is likely to be an extension, and that extension is likely to go to slot cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian, who's among a handful of Broncos players in the final year of their contracts, along with fellow corner Riley Moss, safety Brandon Jones, and wide receiver/returner Marvin Mims.
One of the league's best nickels, McMillian has notched 21 solo tackles, seven pass deflections, three sacks, and an interception in 2026. He's playing on a one-year, $5.76 million restricted free-agent tender ahead of what's scheduled to be his first career foray into an unrestricted market.
The former undrafted defender has objectively earned an extension — and he just may get it in the days ahead.

title: Film Room: Bo Nix Is Finally Hunting Again—and Broncos Are Better for It
full_text:
The Denver Broncos set an NFL record against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday by winning their 16th consecutive one-score regular-season game. It was closer than it should have been, but there was a lot of promising stuff on tape this week.
Bo Nix had a great game , even if the box score doesn’t bear the fruit most fans would expect from elite-level quarterback play. It was abundantly clear that the Broncos' offensive game plan was to push the ball against a banged-up Panthers secondary unit, and that aggression with the vertical passing game helped open things up underneath.
It also didn’t matter that a lot of the shot plays ended in incompletions, either. Denver attacked Carolina’s depth cornerbacks at will, drawing a handful of defensive pass-interference penalties along the way.
That’s the great thing about being aggressive and hunting with the football. You don’t always need an explosive completion to affect the defense and move the football. There are four outcomes to a passing play, and three of them are good for the offense.
Denver’s offense had rhythm against a bad defense in the first half, mounting a handful of scoring drives early and having another cut short by a Nix interception in the red zone. More on that here in a minute.
But the best thing I noticed came on four incomplete passes and that red zone interception. Let’s look at the film.
I love how Payton started the game with shot plays. I wish Bo puts this ball closer to the "red line", because it gives Sutton more space to work his feet, but its still a great ball. Just missed on this one. pic.twitter.com/yRlEZpxSvD
Knowing that the Panthers were down to their fifth- and sixth-string cornerbacks, Sean Payton called a shot play with three vertical routes to open the game. I love this play call because it gets Nix to be aggressive right away and sets the tone for the offense.
Carolina is in Cover 6, playing quarter-quarter-half on the back end, giving Nix a one-on-one shot to Courtland Sutton down the left sideline. Nix sets his feet and lets this thing fly, giving Sutton a great opportunity to make a play at the highest point.
Unfortunately, Sutton landed out of bounds, but the aggressive nature of this play is what I’ve been asking for over the past handful of weeks.
If I had to be critical of anything here, it would be the placement of this ball. This isn’t a bad throw, but I would like to see this put a little closer to the “red line, " which is an imaginary line running five yards parallel to the sideline. That would give Sutton more room to work his feet on the boundary, but that’s just nitpicking.
2nd play of the game. Take another shot. Being aggressive draws DPI, which is just as good as a completion. pic.twitter.com/BdyOWUCwtF
On the next play, Nix stays aggressive with another shot to Troy Franklin. Carolina comes out in a two-high shell, but rotates into a single high man-coverage. Nix sees safety Nick Scott patrol the deep middle as Franklin works the boundary against cornerback Corey Thornton.
Nix lets it fly as soon as he hits his back foot, putting another nice ball out there for Franklin to try to make a play. Thornton is flagged for pass interference on this play, which is one of the three positive outcomes for the offense on a passing play.
Targeting Thornton, who was called up from the practice squad for the game, was a great decision here. Putting pressure on depth pieces to perform early in the game can, and will, lead to positive outcomes.
I like Bo trying to fit the hole shot here. Stay aggressive. A little more air under this and it's completed instead of picked off. Kudos to Thornton for one heck of a play. The other team gets paid to play, too. pic.twitter.com/K0HksfRilW
Some people are going to disagree with me on this play. This is that red-zone interception that took points off the board. While I agree you can’t make a mistake like that, I like how aggressive Nix was with the football on this throw.
Denver runs Sutton on a corner route into Carolina’s Cover 2 defense, and Nix tries to layer a “hole shot” to the boundary. Thornton makes an incredible play by getting great depth in his flat zone to undercut the throw and pick it off.
The reason why I like this play is that Nix is taking a chance with the football, and it’s actually there for the taking. If he gets a little more air under this ball, this could have set the offense up inside the 5-yard line.
Sometimes you win, sometimes you lose. The other team has players who get paid to play the game, too. Chalk one up for the bad guys and move on.
All Go Special on the last play before Half. Bo rips this john to Franklin. Great play by Chau Smith-Wade. Bo likes to rip these seam shots. He needs to do it more. pic.twitter.com/D9R8S1ZS0Z
That interception was critical. Carolina would go on to score a touchdown on their ensuing possession, ultimately taking the lead. But Nix responded on the next Denver drive, operating a nice two-minute drill to get points on the board.
Our next play is an “All-Go Special," with five vertical routes on what was essentially a Hail Mary attempt. But Nix doesn’t throw it up for grabs. He rips a seam shot to Franklin, and it’s broken up at the last second by cornerback Chau Smith-Wade.
This is a great play by Smith-Wade, because this throw is right on the money for a touchdown. You could argue that Nix could put a little more air under this throw, too, but that's nitpicking the result of a great defensive play.
Denver's offense hasn't had these tight-window throws all year, but Nix has had success throwing these seam shots for years. He hit tight end Adam Trautman for a one-handed touchdown catch against the Panthers two years ago on a very similar throw to this one.
This throw is similar to the Franklin seam shot. It's from Bo's rookie year against Carolina. A little more air under it and a great catch by Trautman. pic.twitter.com/LVbnnl6RUX
Glance post to Engram. Love the aggression here. Just another great play by Smith-Wade. Right ball placement and pace. Can't win them all. pic.twitter.com/TlLML0LWYj
Nix tried it again later in the game as well.
During Denver’s first scoring drive of the second half, Payton calls a glance-post route for tight end Evan Engram in the red zone. Nix had to evade pressure from his left and throw this ball on the run, but he rips this ball perfectly.
Nix gets it above the head line, in a place where only Engram can catch it. But Smith-Wade plays it perfectly again, knocking away a touchdown pass.
This is good stuff, even though the pass falls to the turf at the back of the end zone. Denver scored on a nine-yard touchdown run by Jonah Coleman two plays later.
Outside of the Arizona Cardinals game a few weeks ago, Nix hadn’t been pushing the ball vertically all year. He wasn’t hunting with the football like this, and it was causing major issues with the passing game and bleeding into the run game. Denver’s offense was stagnant, even putrid at times.
Taking chances and making teams honor the vertical passing game opens up everything else. You don’t need to complete every one of these plays to make teams have to respect you.
You also get the added benefit of sometimes drawing penalties downfield, which is just as good as a completed pass. Carolina was flagged five times for pass interference, and every one of them was justified.
When Nix is operating within the scope of the offense and taking chances with the football, the Broncos look much better. I hope this is a sign of things to come following the bye week.

title: Broncos' New Linebacker Pecking Order After Daiyan Henley Trade
full_text:
The Denver Broncos made a move ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers.
Denver sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to its division rival for Henley, but that's no skin off GM George Paton's teeth, given that he expects to get a fourth-round compensatory pick back for John Franklin-Myers's free-agent departure.
We've covered the Broncos' biggest winners and losers of the Henley trade and graded the move . Now it's time to examine how the fourth-year veteran's arrival could shake up the Broncos' linebacker depth chart.
The Broncos finally have a coverage linebacker. As exciting as Henley's arrival is, I don't anticipate him replacing either of the starters out of the gates.
Singleton and Strnad will remain the Broncos' starting linebacker duo, but unlike Turner and Reid, Henley is going to play. Much like last season, when Dre Greenlaw was healthy, the Broncos will implement a three-man rotation at inside linebacker, based on down and distance.
It might not happen right away, but I'd love to see Henley start eating into Singleton's coverage snaps. Coverage isn't Singleton's strong suit, and yet, he's played 365 so far this season, the most of any NFL inside linebacker.
Meanwhile, Strnad has played 280 coverage snaps, the seventh-most among NFL linebackers. On one hand, you'd like to tip your cap to Singleton and Strnad for playing so many snaps against the pass. On the other, neither is doing a good job.
The best reflection of that is the amount of yardage the Broncos have hemorrhaged to tight ends this season. In just the past three games alone, they've allowed 330 passing yards and three touchdowns to tight ends.
The Broncos had to do something, and they did, adding Henley just as they hit their bye. That gives him time to settle in and assimilate the playbook on the fly.
Since the Broncos won't be playing again until Week 11's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders, I like Henley's chances of being ready to contribute. I hope we see him early and often because the Raiders have All-World tight end Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, two tight ends who've combined for 1,046 yards and seven touchdowns already this season.
Granted, the Raiders will have a different quarterback throwing them the ball when the Broncos see them, as Kirk Cousins was traded to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday. But No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza shadowed Cousins through the first nine weeks, and even though he's a rookie, he's smart enough to know how the Raiders' bread gets buttered.
As for the bottom two linebackers on the depth chart, the Broncos opted to cut defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. to make room for Henley, instead of one of them. Both Turner and Reid are key special teams contributors, so they'll be sticking around the active roster for the foreseeable future.
Henley begins his Broncos tenure as the third linebacker on the depth chart, but he's started 41 career games since entering the league as a Chargers third-round pick in 2023. He's a two-time team captain and L.A.'s green-dot wearer, meaning he called the signals for the defense. He was also the Chargers' tackles leader twice and was on pace to do it again this year before his trade.
Strnad has been in the league since 2020, and has 28 career starts, just to put things in perspective. Henley has seen a lot of football, and he's played well in all facets of the game.
Henley is going to see the field out of the gate, even if he doesn't replace Singleton or Strnad as a nominal starter. The Broncos traded for him for a reason, and their desperate need to stanch the bleeding in the middle of their passing defense dictates he sees the field in obvious passing situations.
It's going to be interesting to see just how the Broncos balance their new three-man linebacker rotation.

title: Grading Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade: What Denver Really Got
full_text:
For the first time in several years, the Denver Broncos actually made a trade ahead of the NFL deadline.
On Tuesday, the Broncos sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers in exchange for veteran linebacker Daiyan Henley . It's not often that division rivals will trade with each other, especially during the season, but the winless Chargers are in a unique position and the Broncos were smart enough to capitalize.
Henley is a fourth-year linebacker whom the Chargers drafted out of Washington State in the third round (No. 85 overall) back in 2023. He also played some college ball at Nevada.
The Broncos didn't make a trade for a running back, tight end, or offensive lineman, as many fans hoped. Sean Payton said, " I like this team a lot ," after beating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday, and the lack of a trade to help the offense not only reinforces that, but also shows much confidence in the Broncos' skill positions.
The Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie back from injured reserve soon, and beyond them, the team is apparently content with rookie starter Jonah Coleman and veteran complement J.K. Dobbins, even if fans wanted the team to add one more running back while it still could.
The trade deadline has passed, with the Broncos making one trade. What grade should Denver get for the Henley trade? Let's break down how he fits before grading this trade.
At 6-foot-0 and 225 pounds, Henley is not a big linebacker, but that doesn't mean he's afraid to mix it up. He's very physical and offers sideline-to-sideline ability as a three-down linebacker.
Henley is a two-time team Chargers team captain and he led them in tackles thrice — if you count this season (51 tackles). He's only 26, and although he's in a contract year, the Broncos have the flexibility to see how he fits with half the season to go, plus the playoffs, before deciding on whether to re-sign him.
With a 2026 salary of $3.674 million, the Chargers have already paid half of that, leaving the Broncos with only a minor salary-cap liability with Henley. The Broncos had to be smart financially ahead of the deadline, with just $4.6 million in cap space. Henley will fit with plenty of room to spare.
Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad are the Broncos' starting linebackers, so Henley will begin his tenure as a depth player, depsite his experience as a 41-game starter. Much like last season when Dre Greenlaw was healthy and available, the Broncos will employ a three-man rotation at linebacker, based on down and distance.
In a perfect world, I'd like to see Henley on the field more than Singleton in obvious passing situations, but as the defender with the green dot on his helmet, it's hard to see the Broncos taking their team captain off the field much. But Singleton has already played an insane number of snaps, including the most coverage snaps among all NFL linebackers this season, so for more reasons than one, it would behoove the team to carve out some of his snaps for Henley.
That being said, Singleton plays 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps for a reason. I doubt they'll move away from that, so as Henley gets worked into the rotation, it's likely to be at Strnad's expense . I'm okay with that, too.
Henley has proven to be a difference-maker in coverage and a reliable tackler against the run, when he's able to get off blocks cleanly. His nose for the ball is a nice bonus. He has four career interceptions, plus two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery.
Singleton has three career interceptions, three forced fumbles, and five fumble recoveries since entering the league in 2019. Strnad has exactly one career interception and one fumble recovery. Henley is more of a ballhawk with great instincts.
The Broncos have some decisions to make at linebacker after this season, with Singleton about to turn 33 and Strnad already over 30. Both were re-signed this past spring, with Singleton being under contract through 2027 and Strnad through 2028.
Singleton is the one to watch in the offseason, though. He's played quite well this season, earning Defensive Player of the Month honors for October, but he punctuated his 2026 campaign with a stinker to start the year and another in Carolina last week.
Singleton is on pace for a 200-tackle season, but Father Time is undefeated. The Broncos began planning for the future by selecting linebacker Red Murdock with the last pick in the 2026 draft, but he has spent his rookie year competing on the practice squad.
Hopefully, Murdock is developing, too. If things work out with Henley and the Broncos opt to re-sign him, it would give them two under-30 investments to potentially build around for the future, independent of what happens with Singleton after the 2026 season.
Karene Reid and Jordan Turner will be 27 and 25, respectively, when next season starts, so the Broncos have some youth on their side at linebacker, even if their current depth beyond Henley is inexperienced.
The Broncos needed a coverage linebacker. The best illustration is the nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns they've allowed to tight ends over the past three games alone.
Henley may not be a cure-all, but he upgrades the Broncos' defense and gives Vance Joseph a viable weapon to deploy against opponents with athletic, pass-catching tight ends. It just so happens that Henley is also very good against the run, so adding a three-down linebacker at the trade deadline should be celebrated, especially given the cost.
What an INT by Daiyan Henley! LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/qyp5jYJbVF
Things didn't pan out last year with Greenlaw, but Henley could be a totally different story. There's less baggage and no injury jacket, and Henley arguably brings a more reliable resume to Denver than Greenlaw did.
The Broncos are expected to land a fourth-round compensatory draft pick in 2027 for the free-agent departure of defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, which offsets the higher draft pick given up to the Chargers for Henley.
In other words, when it all comes out in the wash, the Broncos just added a three-down linebacker with coverage chops for the price of a fifth-round pick two years from now. How could anyone pan this pick?
Factoring in Henley's age, health, fit, and cap impact, this was a home run of a trade. He fills a big, lingering need, and the Broncos have the flexibility to decide on his post-2026 future after the season ends.
I may be slightly mystified that Denver spurned the opportunity to also upgrade the backfield behind Bo Nix, but that's not what I'm grading here. This is purely a grade of the Henley trade, and the Broncos pass with flying colors.
Let's see how a few of our staff writers graded the Henley trade.
I love this move for the Broncos. Henley was struggling on an 0-8 Chargers team, but his upside as a coverage linebacker cannot be overstated.
The Broncos have needed help in that area for years, and they didn't give up much to get him. The fourth-rounder is probably recouped as a compensatory pick for losing Franklin-Myers in the offseason, so sending a 2028 fifth-round pick for a starting-quality player who could be extended after this season is great work by GM George Paton.
A trade for an inside linebacker is not something I imagine most Broncos fans thought would happen, especially with a division rival. But Henley will help take some of the load off Singleton and Strnad.
And given what the Broncos gave up for Henley, it wouldn't surprise if they extended him at some point. This is a good move by the Broncos.
The Broncos get linebacker depth for basically a fifth-rounder, due to JFM netting them a fourth-round comp pick. Henley is likely a future replacement for Singleton.

title: How Broncos Made Roster Room for Newly-Acquired LB Daiyan Henley
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' acquisition of inside linebacker Daiyan Henley meant the team would need to make a corresponding move on their 53-man roster — someone had to go with Henley arriving.
That someone, the team announced , is defensive back Sean Fresch Jr., who was waived from the active roster, with designs of re-signing to the practice squad. That could happen as early as Wednesday, assuming Fresch clears waivers.
In preparation for such a maneuver, Denver also released DB Ugo Amadi from the practice squad. Amadi was on his second stint with the organization, and it's possible he resurfaces again this season.
Undrafted out of Rice in 2025, Fresch joined the Broncos in June following a successful tenure in the United Football League. Initially on the practice squad, he was promoted to the active roster and made his NFL debut in Week 5. Fresch, too, appeared in last week's victory over the Panthers, returning two kickoffs for 62 yards — including a 41-yard runback on the game's opening play.
"[He's] really smart at the nickel, he’s a returner, got quick change of direction," head coach Sean Payton said of Fresch in June.
In addition to his special teams duties, Fresch was also on the 53 to serve as insurance at the cornerback position, which has been beat up by the injury bug this year. Although the Broncos lost Riley Moss to a concussion against Carolina, Moss is likely to return when the club emerges from its Week 10 bye — rendering Fresch expendable.
Assuming Moss is back against the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 22, the Broncos' primary cornerback room will be at full strength with Patrick Surtain II also recovered from a previous ankle injury. The team also hopes to return CB Kris Abrams-Draine from his own ankle issue.
Henley, meanwhile, is reportedly anticipated to open his Broncos career as the third ILB behind incumbent starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, pushing Karene Reid and Jordan Turner further down the depth chart — one of them, potentially off the roster.
Henley is regarded as a fierce tackler with solid pass-coverage and blitzing chops who wore the green dot during his time with the Chargers. He'll immediately see snaps as a rotational 'backer for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, but it wouldn't at all be a surprise if he's starting over Singleton or Strnad sooner rather than later.

title: Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade Creates Big Winners & Losers
full_text:
Instead of a running back or tight end, the Denver Broncos traded for a linebacker ahead of Tuesday's NFL deadline.
Denver gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for fourth-year linebacker Daiyan Henley . A two-time team captain who led the Chargers thrice (counting this season) in tackles, Henley is a physical presence at the second level of the defense who also brings — finally — some coverage upside to the table.
As with any trade, signing, or draft pick, a roster addition creates some ripple effects. Let's break down the Broncos' biggest winners and losers of the Henley trade.
Joseph has sorely lacked a true coverage linebacker since returning to Denver as defensive coordinator in 2023. The Broncos have tried to mask their tight-end coverage woes with one of the NFL's best secondaries, but the cornerbacks and safeties often have their hands full.
Over the past three weeks alone, the Broncos have allowed nearly 300 receiving yards and three touchdowns to tight ends. That had to be one of the motivating factors behind the Henley trade.
Once Henley gets up to speed on the playbook, Joseph will have a new weapon to deploy in coverage. I don't want to make Henley out to be some miracle salve that will heal all of Denver's coverage wounds, but he's going to be a big, big help.
In terms of coverage, Strnad is the Broncos' best linebacker, but it's relative. He just signed a two-year extension in the spring and has been the team's undisputed starter next to Alex Singleton this season.
Singleton never leaves the field , while Strnad will at times. I'm open to the possibility of Joseph taking Singleton off the field in obvious passing situations, but in all likelihood, the reigning Defensive Player of the Month will continue to play 100% of the snaps.
The Broncos love Singleton, and they rely on him as the defensive signal-caller. I don't expect his role to change, but it should , at least on third down. I'm not talking about benching Singleton, but the Broncos should start giving some of his snaps to Henley.
Henley is going to see the field, but it will likely be at Strnad's expense. If the Broncos were smart, though, they'd start giving the soon-to-be 33-year-old Singleton a few breathers in-game and utilize Henley as their coverage linebacker.
Henley might not have the green dot on his helmet, but the Broncos could work around that, no problem. Singleton never leaves the field, and that's often a good thing.
However, unless he's blitzing, Singleton is a liability in obvious passing situations. Henley, at least, gives Joseph the option of trying other personnel combinations at linebacker in those situations. At the end of the day, when it comes to Singleton's role changing because of this trade, I'll believe it when I see it.
Henley's arrival means fewer snaps for Strnad, but it might not happen overnight. The Broncos have both Strnad and Singleton under contract beyond 2026, while Henley is in a contract year, so the team has to quickly figure out what it has in the ex-Charger team captain.
The Broncos rotated three linebackers down the stretch last season when Dre Greenlaw was still in Denver and healthy. Expect that to be the plan again coming out of the team's Week 10 bye.
One of these linebackers could be waived to make room for Henley on the 53-man roster. My guess is that it'll be Turner, but it's a coin flip between him and Reid.
Reid offers a bit more upside on special teams and defense. Turner contributes on special teams, too, but as a linebacker, he's a one-trick pony. Turner is a true stack linebacker, but the Broncos don't use him on defense.
Reid is more athletic and versatile, but the Broncos could base this decision on which linebacker they view least likely to get claimed on waivers. That's why it's a coin-flip decison.
Then again, the Broncos could opt to keep five inside linebackers on the 53-man roster for now and waive defensive back Sean Fresch Jr., wide receiver Lil'Jordan Humphrey, or rookie tight end Dallen Bentley, the last of whom is yet to dress this season. As a 2026 seventh-round pick, I doubt Bentley would be claimed on waivers, since he was the second-to-last pick in the draft and didn't do much to distinguish himself on tape in the preseason.
Whether the Broncos waive one of their linebackers or keep them all on the roster, though, the Henley trade is still a setback for Turner and Reid, simply because it puts one more obstacle between them and any playing time on defense.

title: Broncos Raid AFC West Rival in Trade for LB Daiyan Henley
full_text:
You don't often see intra-divisional trades, but one just went down in the AFC West.
The Denver Broncos have acquired Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley via trade for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, per ESPN 's Adam Schefter . The Chargers remain winless, so in this unprecedented situation they find themselves in, the Broncos get to benefit.
Schefter forecasted a Broncos move on Monday , and he was right.
Henley, 26, is in his fourth NFL season and the final year of his rookie contract. In 2023, the Chargers drafted him in the third round out of Washington State, and he has 41 career starts under his belt.
In Year 2, Henley became a starter, totaling 147 tackles (84 solo), seven tackles for a loss, a sack, and an interception. He followed that up in Year 3 with 103 tackles (54 solo), five for a loss, 3.5 sacks, and two interceptions.
With eight games under his belt this season, Henley has already totaled 51 tackles, a half-sack, a forced fumble, two fumble recoveries, and an interception. He's a difference-making linebacker, with a nose for the ball and the ability to cover.
Henley led the Chargers in tackles in each of the past two seasons, and exits L.A. as the club's leader in that department this season, too. He's a two-time team captain (including this season), so from a make-up perspective, he checks the boxes Denver covets as well.
That coverage ability is what the Broncos surely coveted, given that they've allowed nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns to tight ends over the last three games. Alex Singleton may be the reigning AFC Defensive Player of the Month , but he's a liability in coverage.
Justin Strnad is better than Singleton in coverage, but not by a long stretch. The Broncos re-signed both Singleton and Strnad this past offseason to serve as their starting linebacker duo, and the results thus far have been a mixed bag.
Henley can step in for Singleton in obvious passing situations and make a huge difference to Denver's passing defense. Singleton plays 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps, as a team captain and the man with the green dot on his helmet, but the team might finally be considering alternatives.
Singleton is a great run-defending linebacker and a bona fide tackling machine, but his coverage is lacking. Strnad is a solid all-around linebacker, but the Broncos need a true answer in neutralizing opposing tight ends, and Henley gives it to them.
With the Broncos on bye this week, Henley will get plenty of time to assimilate the system. The NFL trade deadline came at the most opportune time for the Broncos, especially with them actually making a trade.
After the bye, the Broncos will host the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11, who just traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. That means Denver will face Fernando Mendoza — the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft — for the first time.
I'd expect to see plenty of Henley in that game. Now, what this means for backup linebackers Jordan Turner and Karene Reid remains to be seen, but both are key special teams contributors, so it wouldn't be a shock if the Broncos try to find a way to keep them on the 53-man roster.
But if they have to waive one of them, it'll likely be Turner. And odds are, he'd pass through waivers unclaimed to be re-signed to the practice squad, where he could be elevated on game day.
Broncos fans may have been hoping for a running back or a tight end , but Henley absolutely checks a box and gives the team something it was missing. The Broncos are better with Henley on the roster, and he'll get half the season to prove whether he deserves an extension in the spring.

title: Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff Surprisingly Lands on Week 10 Injury Report
full_text:
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff surprisingly popped up on the initial Week 10 injury report.
Goff was listed as limited due to a chest injury. Others listed as non-participants included Cade Mays, D.J. Reed and Sione Vaki. There is no indication the 32-year-old will miss the game in Germany.
Following a victory against the Miami Dolphins, the coaching staff decided to conduct a walkthrough practice on Wednesday at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
The participation levels reported are an estimate of a players participation level, had the practice been traditionally conducted.
Others limited included Amon-Ra St. Brown, Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch.
Detroit's offensive line had their struggles early in the Week 9 contest against the AFC East squad. Miles Frazier did not have the best showing in his first appearance this season as a starter.
The former No. 1 overall pick was subjected to early hits , as Miami's defense brought pressure and were also able to able to secure an interception.
“Yeah, just settle in a little bit. I thought they did a good job up front applying some of that pressure and forcing a turnover," said Goff. "I wish I would have eaten that probably or checked it down, probably would have served us better there. But yeah, they did a good job, and I thought we just settled in eventually and started running the ball well, had those two explosives back-to-back on that one drive.”
Goff credited the defense postgame for keeping the team in the game, as the offense struggled to find the end zone.
“They've been playing so well," Goff said. "They deserve so much credit and figuring it out and going through the storm that they were going through early on, and now playing at such an elite level. And really keeping us in these games and allowing us to kind of find our footing at times, certainly today, they deserve so much credit.”

title: Arrogance of Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes May Be His Ultimate Downfall
full_text:
Detroit Lions GM Brad Holmes proved various fans and pundits right on Tuesday; he chose to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline instead of upgrading multiple positions of need, particularly on defense.
To be fair, Holmes did acquire N.Y. Jets safety Andre Cisco on Monday. However, the 26-year-old is much more of a solid depth piece than an impact-level defensive back. Consequently, he's not the type of defender who's going to take Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit to the next level.
Holmes direly needed to come out of the deadline with more than just a thrift store-esque acquisition like Cisco. He had several holes to plug across the defensive side of the ball, which were made even more glaring by the recent injuries to cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and linebacker Jack Campbell (neck). Plus, you can easily argue that Detroit's once again void of a reliable EDGE counterpart for Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson, especially with DJ Wonnum being sidelined.
Yet, Holmes decided that the Lions’ roster, as currently structured, is good enough as is. That, to me, was a miscalculation of epic proportions by the sixth-year GM.
Holmes' contract with the Lions ends following the conclusion of the 2027 season. He may earn an extension this summer, but if the team fails to make a deep run in the postseason, it is certain his seat will be getting warmer and warmer.
Fans are not interested in being teased, especially at the current exuberant price of season tickets.
Sure, the Lions are on a four-game win streak, which has certainly been aided by the improved play of the defense. However, that does not mean Sheppard's unit is going to remain productive the rest of the 2026 campaign. More than likely, that's not going to be the case, and I'm willing to predict it will have some hiccups in the weeks ahead, including against Ben Johnson's NFC North-leading Chicago Bears.
It furthers the reason why Holmes should have done everything in his power to add reinforcements to that side of the ball, no matter the valuable draft capital it may have cost.
If Holmes would have been serious about upgrading Detroit's 53-man roster, he would have made an ultra aggressive pursuit of impact defenders like Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks and L.A. Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack. But, did he? No, at least per the reports that came out in the hours leading up to the deadline.
And think about it, Brooks and Mack are exactly the type of difference-making talents that could have elevated the play of Sheppard's unit. However, another deadline came and went where Holmes & Co. erroneously decided that they're all good.
And because of such, the Lions will now be reliant upon a variety of depth pieces – e.g. defensive backs Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin and linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske – in their attempt to catapult the Bears for the NFC North crown . That's hardly a recipe for success.
Once again, Holmes has fallen victim to the “smartest man in the room” syndrome, impeding the Lions’ efforts to take the next step as a franchise.
Detroit does not possess a Super Bowl-caliber roster, and it only has one person to blame for that being the case: Brad Holmes.

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed, Cade Mays
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided health updates on key defenders DJ Wonnum and D.J. Reed, as well as center Cade Mays, ahead of the teams Week 10 contest against the New England Patriots.
The former NFL tight end said Wonnum will participate in practice on Wednesday afternoon. Barring any setbacks, the veteran defender should be ready to play this week against the AFC East powerhouse.
Mays and Reed are considered doubtful at best for the game set to take place overseas in Germany.
When asked, the sixth-year head man said left guard Christian Mahogany will be back with the starters along the offensive line at practice today.
Appearing on 97.1 The Ticket earlier this week, Campbell indicated he needed to stand by his word when addressing the rules broken on multiple times by the former sixth-round draft pick.
Mahogany did not play any offensive snaps against the Dolphins, as he was disciplined for violating team rules.
"Look, if you say you’re gonna do something, you better hold up to it, otherwise you’re gonna lose respect of the people around you," said Campbell. "Because if I’m sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don’t do it, I would immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we’re gonna do here."
Quarterback Jared Goff noted, following the Lions 19-9 victory against Miami, how their Week 9 opponent stifled the offense in the first half, prior to adjustments being made.
“I thought defensively, I thought they did a good job against us and played with good depth, made us keep the ball underneath. I thought they rushed really well and tackled really well," said Goff. "They did a good job, and we certainly had our opportunities to blow it open a little bit earlier than that and didn't take advantage of them. Some self-inflicted wounds, some penalties pre-snap and took us a minute to get going there, obviously, but when we did, did enough to win."
Goff later added, "It has been six different ways and four in a row now in four different ways, and that's the hallmark of a good team is when you're able to find different ways to win repeatedly and just sticking in it. Defense played well, I thought, all day, but I can only speak for us offensively. Like just one more time, chop wood one more time, chop wood one more time. It doesn't matter who you're playing, what their record is, this is NFL and they were giving us all we could handle . We just kept chopping wood, kept chopping wood and felt good about the way we finished it.”

title: 4 Winners, 2 Losers After 2026 Detroit Lions Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone.
For the Detroit Lions , the hours leading up to the deadline saw the addition of former New York Jets safety Andre Cisco. Now in his sixth NFL season, Cisco has logged valuable experience playing multiple spots in the secondary for the Jets and Jacksonville Jaguars.
Detroit's inactivity otherwise left the fan base wanting more, as the team did not address its needs at the cornerback and linebacker position. In particular, the team elected to not add a linebacker after the injury to Jack Campbell.
Here are winners and losers from the Lions' trade deadline decisions.
Detroit's defensive coordinator has his group trending up over the team's four-game winning streak. They capped off this recent run of success with a strong performance in which they didn't allow a touchdown against the Dolphins.
Now, he gets another option in the secondary with Cisco that he can utilize in a number of different ways. It adds more depth to the group, and could also allow him to be flexible with the usage of players like Keith Abney II and Brian Branch.
While the Lions didn't make a splash addition at the cornerback or linebacker spot like some believed they would, Sheppard ultimately got another playmaker that could help the defense.
Because the Lions didn't add a big name cornerback , Rakestraw and company will likely continue to be utilized in a rotation. Rakestraw's playing time has been up-and-down at points this year, but he has worked into a pretty stable role since the Lions went to a rotation in Week 7 against Green Bay.
Now in his third season, Rakestraw has already logged a career-high in defensive snaps played and has shown flashes of being the player Detroit hoped he'd be when they drafted him in the second-round of the 2024 draft.
With no new faces joining the cornerback room, Rakestraw will continue to get opportunities to prove himself in what is a pivotal third season.
With Jack Campbell's injury being a dominant headline over the last week, the Lions were believed to be in the mix to fortify their linebacker room. However, they elected to stand pat and this is a vote of confidence in the Oklahoma State product.
Rodriguez played a season-high in snaps on Sunday, which was the first game without Campbell, and will presumably continue to play a big role for Detroit's defense moving forward.
Furthermore, the addition of K.J. Britt off the Patriots' practice squad feels like more of an upgrade on special teams, so Britt's presence may not cut into Rodriguez's workload even as he acclimates more to the scheme.
There were questions about whether or not the Lions may be willing to listen to trade offers for LaPorta amidst what appears to be a contract standoff. LaPorta has made his desire to get a hefty contract public, and because the Lions haven't done that deal it appeared as though they thought they would be willing to consider a potential blockbuster.
However, reports Monday indicated that the Lions in fact were not willing to listen to these offers and instead still have plans of getting a long-term extension done. This means a pay-day could be coming from the Lions for the talented tight end, even if it's not right away.
Joseph has already been ruled out for the Lions' Week 10 game against New England, which will push the decision of whether or not to activate him right up to the 21-day deadline of his return to practice window.
The safety, who led the NFL in interceptions in 2024 and was a First Team All-Pro selection that year, still hasn't played this season and his long-term future remains in doubt at this point.
He could certainly wind up playing a role for Detroit at some point this season, but the addition of Cisco generates questions about just how impactful he'll be.
Izien has seen his role diminish on the defensive end, with Abney taking some of his safety reps as well as Branch getitng back into the mix. With Cisco now in the fold, it's hard to imagine Izien finding a role on the defensive side of the ball barring an injury.

title: Grading Lions NFL Trade Deadline: Did Brad Holmes Ruin 2026 Team?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made one move before the NFL trade deadline.
On Monday, the Lions swung a deal to acquire defensive back Andre Cisco from the New York Jets. While the move is intriguing, many believed that an additional move could be coming to help fortify their defense in particular.
Ultimately, the Lions elected to stand pat aside from the Cisco trade and elected to not make another move before the 4 p.m. deadline on Tuesday. This came as something of a surprise given how active other teams in the mix were.
As the Lions look to make a push for a third NFC North title in four years and a return to the postseason, their relative inactivity at the deadline appears to be a vote of confidence in their roster along with the addition of Cisco.
Around them, the San Francisco 49ers, Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks were all active in making moves prior to the deadline. The 49ers added a defensive end in De'Forest Buckner, the Vikings added a quarterback in Kirk Cousins, the Bears brought in defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons and the Seahawks bolstered their offensive line with Quinten Nelson.
Now, the Lions will be tasked with running the divisional gauntlet with Cisco providing defensive depth. It will be interesting to see where Cisco fits within their secondary, as Brian Branch is back in the fold and Kerby Joseph is working toward a return.
Cisco has experience playing both as a box safety and a free safety, so he will provide valuable depth even if Joseph is able to return and play at a high level. Joseph won't play against New England in Week 10, meaning the Lions will have to activate him before their Week 11 game or elect to keep him on the Physically Unable to Perform list for the remainder of the season.
Detroit could also elect to activate Joseph and keep him as an inactive if they don't feel that he's able to play right away. Still, Cisco will give them some options even with Branch and veteran Chuck Clark both playing well.
The Lions didn't make the flashiest move at the deadline amongst their NFC counterparts, and these big trade deadline moves have mixed results over the past several seasons.
Additionally, the Lions have a need at the linebacker position after Jack Campbell suffered a significant injury. He leaves a big hole in terms of production as an All-Pro a season ago, and many believed the Lions could be looking to add a linebacker moving forward.
However, they elected not to and thus provided a vote of confidence in the likes of Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske.
Because of how valuable Campbell was to Detroit's defense, the Lions may wind up regretting not adding an option to the linebacker room.
It's hard to call the Lions' decisions at the deadline an abject failure. Their biggest need was the cornerback position, and there wasn't a single cornerback dealt at the deadline. Joey Porter Jr. was the only cornerback traded in season, while the others who were believed to be on the market ultimately remain with their current teams.
Because there wasn't a market for players at Detroit's biggest position of need, it appears as though the Lions made the right move holding on to their valuable draft capital. They were able to make an addition that will help them moving forward, but didn't make the level of splash that a team like the Bears did.
Ultimately, the roster as constructed has been good enough to win two divisional games amidst a 6-2 start. Their cards are now on the table, and it's up to Dan Campbell's team to prove their leadership right.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Detroit Lions Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions wore down and defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9. The Lions kept Malik Willis and the young Dolphins in check, advancing to a 6-2 record on the season.
At points, it was not the prettiest game, but the Lions were able to find a way to keep scoring points and keeping Miami out of scoring range.
Here is the good, bad, and ugly from the contest.
The Lions needed every one of their four field goals on Sunday, and Jake Bates was perfect on his attempts. It was a game where both defenses were delivering standout performances, and points were at a premium.
Fittingly, Bates, long snapper Hogan Hatten, and the unit were at max efficiency every time they were called upon.
The punting unit was not needed much, as they were not called upon in the second half. However, in two times they were called upon, they delivered. The first punt of the game for Jack Fox was a 54-yarder, and then he used his arm on the next time in punt formation, passing to Tay Martin for a first down on a fake punt.
Kelvin Sheppard and the Defense
Facing a Miami Dolphins offense with Malik Willis limited by a groin injury, the Lions were expected to win. However, Kelvin Sheppard’s defense delivered much more than expected, especially with two starting linebackers and both DJ Reed and DJ Wonnum out.
Sheppard’s unit only allowed nine points, all via a field goal. The longest Miami play from scrimmage came on a fake punt. Alim McNeill tallied a sack while rookie Derrick Moore added the first two of his young career. Aidan Hutchinson and Skyler Gill-Howard each forced holding penalties on plays. Undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas added a quarterback hit.
Chuck Clark tallied an interception. The corners held Willis to 125 yards passing on 25 attempts. It was a strong effort all around, with the entire unit playing for Jack Campbell. It is safe to say that the effort by Motown likely made Campbell smile.
In yet another week, the Lions passing offense fell flat . Jared Goff got sacked early along with throwing an interception. Considering Miami statistically has one of the worst teams in passing yards per play, it was a disappointing effort.
Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa combined for two catches for 40 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs was held without a catch for the first time since week four in 2024 and only the fourth time in his career. Sam LaPorta tallied four catches for 32 yards.
The only player producing at their expected level was Amon-Ra St. Brown, with the All-Pro having eight catches for 86 yards.
While the Lions did not need an All-Pro or MVP-level day from Jared Goff, it was not up to the early season standard that Goff has set.
The red zone offense was not ideal. In fact, the saving grace for this is that Jake Bates was perfect on his field goals. The Lions came away with one touchdown on four red zone attempts. If it was not for Sheppard’s defense playing the game of the season thus far, it could have been a much more embarrassing result for Motown.
The shorter fields enabled Miami to be more aggressive, and Drew Petzing had not answers. Even on their lone touchdown drive, the Lions were held to a fourth down, where a well-called fake dive and pitch to Jahmyr Gibbs got a touchdown.
It was not a day to remember in the Miami sun for the offensive line. They gave up three sacks in the first 17 minutes of game action, alongside seeing Miles Frazier whistled for a hold and a false start. First round pick Blake Miller was also whistled for a false start of his own.
Frazier was given a start after Christian Mahogany had violated team rules , and the Dolphins attacked the LSU product. Frazier gave up multiple run stuffs on a two-penalty day.
While the line regained momentum late, pushing for first downs to drain the clock, multiple red zone failures fall on the line not having solid days. In the end, the defense saved the offense and the Lions organization from an embarrassing loss to the one-win Dolphins.

title: Detroit Lions Stand Pat on 2026 Trade Deadline Day
full_text:
The Detroit Lions elected not to make another move on trade deadline day after making one the day prior.
As a result, the Lions will enter the stretch run of their season with one trade made, that being to acquire New York Jets safety Andre Cisco on Monday . To land Cisco, the Lions parted ways with a 2028 sixth-round pick.
However, with Tuesday being the final day for teams to make trades, the Lions did not add another option to the roster. Though there were intriguing options thought to be available, the Lions ultimately did not make any more moves beyond adding Cisco.
The Lions were viewed as a team that may need defensive reinforcements based on the fact that they were without several starters in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum all did not play, and while Campbell is the only one of the three on injured reserve, the depth they have defensively would've benefitted from a re-stock. However, it was not to be as the Lions stood pat.
Detroit has a tough stretch upcoming, starting with a trip to Munich to take on the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots. After that, they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before playing the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving as part of a stretch that includes three games in 11 days.
Currently, the Lions sit in second-place in the NFC North behind the Bears. All four of the NFC North teams currently are in the playoff picture, as all four have winning records and are at least three games above the .500 mark.
The Bears and Vikings both made moves at the deadline. Chicago made a splash by trading multiple picks to the Tennessee Titans for defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons, while the Vikings made a move to reunite with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins.
Detroit's season will be defined by their performance in their four-game stretch to end the year. They will play at Minnesota in Week 15, then finish the year with road games at Chicago and Green Bay after hosting the New York Giants in Week 16.

title: Lions 2026 Midseason Rookie Report Sees DL Ascend Up Depth Chart Quickly
full_text:
With the NFL calendar turning to Week 10, we are beyond the midpoint of the 2026 season.
The Detroit Lions have now had eight games to evaluate their rookie class, with several of their players playing prominent roles in that timeframe. While they still have nine games remaining, meaning their season isn’t quite at its midpoint due to their Week 6 bye, with the NFL season reaching its halfway point it’s time to take a look at the group’s performance.
Here’s an updated look at how Detroit’s rookie class has fared throughout the first eight games of the 2026 NFL season.
Miller has started in all seven of the games he’s appeared in, as he missed the Lions’ Week 2 game against Buffalo with an ankle injury. Thus far, he’s been better in pass protection than as a run blocker. He ranks 23rd among all tackles in Pro Football Focus’ pass-blocking grade, while he’s 73rd in run-blocking.
Relative to his fellow rookies, he ranks first among first-year tackles who have played at least 93 snaps this year in pass-blocking grade but seventh in run-blocking.
It has been somewhat up-and-down at times, most recently with the Lions’ Week 9 win over Miami. He struggled against Chop Robinson, and was called for holding for the first time in his young career in that game.
Overall, Miller has outperformed his rookie counterparts as a pass-blocker opposite one of the game’s best in Penei Sewell, and continues to show growth in the run game.
Moore may have had his breakthrough on Sunday. After a slow start to the season where he played a marginal role at best, an injury to DJ Wonnum opened up a legitimate opportunity for him and he made the most of it.
The Michigan product racked up two sacks against Miami on Sunday, the first two of his career. While Wonnum has also played very well and is expected to return to his starting role upon being healthy, Moore proved himself worthy of another opportunity.
He’s been utilized mostly as a rush end throughout the start of the season, providing pop on passing downs. In his extended role Sunday, he showed that he can set an edge against the run as well. It was a promising showing after a very quiet start to the season.
Injuries have been unfortunately a theme for Rolder in his rookie season. He missed most of training camp with a hamstring injury, and his absence bled over to the start of the season as he was inactive for the first two games.
He debuted in Week 3, and had played a small role on defense in Week 4. Then, he got chances after the team’s bye week to help out in a rotational capacity. He logged his first career sack as well as two tackles for loss in the win over Minnesota by the time the fourth quarter rolled around.
Unfortunately for Rolder, he suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in that fourth quarter that may require surgery. It was an abrupt end to a solid stretch of football for him since the bye week.
The Lions have utilized Abney in multiple ways already this year. For much of training camp and into the start of the regular season, he was a backup cornerback with the ability to contribute as the nickel.
After Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending injury, things changed for Abney. He began to take on more work at the safety position, eventually earning his first start there in Week 5. In that game, a win over the Cardinals, he recorded his first career interception.
Time will tell what Abney’s role is moving forward, as Brian Branch has returned and Kerby Joseph is on his way to coming back as well. Add in the fact that Chuck Clark has played well, and it could be challenging for Abney to get snaps at safety.
At the worst, though, Abney will serve as a super sub with the ability to play boundary corner, nickel and safety moving forward.
Law is out for the season with a torn ACL suffered in offseason workouts. Based on the timing of the injury and recovery, he should be able to participate in training camp next season.
Gill-Howard has been one of the biggest surprises up to this point in the season. He has taken to the role assigned to him very well, as he has been one of the most productive rookie pass-rushers through the midway point of the season.
The Texas Tech product has earned a significant amount of snaps due to his athleticism and ability to win off the line of scrimmage. He and Tyleik Williams, Detroit’s run-stuffing first-round pick in 2025, compliment each other nicely.
Gill-Howard ranks first amongst all rookie interior defensive linemen in pressures, and sixth amongst all rookies in general. His pass-rush win rate is tied-for-fifth at 6.7 percent. He’ll continue to be a big part of Detroit’s defense moving forward.
We've even see Gill-Howard play some on offense, as the Lions have utilized him as a fullback or extra tight end throughout multiple games this year.
O’Neill has remained on Detroit’s roster as an undrafted free agent out of Rutgers, and has carved out a nice role. He is among the leaders in special teams snaps played, and has also mixed in some work on defense.
He has earned a 58.3 PFF defensive grade on his 16 defensive snaps played, 11 of which have been pass-rush snaps. O’Neill has been very solid on special teams, as he’s made seven solo tackles in that phase of the game.
Lucas made his NFL debut Sunday as a practice squad elevation with Wonnum sidelined. He wound up playing 12 snaps, with nine coming as a pass-rusher, and recorded one pressure.
Detroit’s willingness to utilize him as an elevation over Ahmed Hassanein shows that he has impressed the coaching staff. He seems to be an option Detroit is confident in should there be an injury moving forward.
