title: Rams Legend Steven Jackson Reflects on His Career, Kyren Williams and Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have a strong history at the running back position, and one of the best within the last 20 years was Steven Jackson. While Jackson didn’t necessarily play on many good Rams teams, he was always one of the bright spots and remained incredibly consistent. Jackson remains one of six running backs in NFL history to rush for 1,000 yards in eight consecutive seasons.
Throughout the years, Jackson has remained involved in the Rams community. With Los Angeles sitting at 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, Jackson recently talked with Rams On SI to share his thoughts on the team's current running back duo and playoff chances as it starts to get healthy.
Prior to the Rams’ game against the Los Angeles Chargers two weeks ago, Jackson took part in a Rams community event in partnership with Edwards Lifesciences and their Off the Sidelines Initiative, encouraging fans to take charge of their heart health through free heart valve screenings and education.
“At Edwards Lifesciences, we're committed to advancing heart health and helping more people understand the importance of early detection,” said Evan Webber, Vice President of Marketing at Edwards Lifesciences. “Through our Off the Sidelines partnership with the Los Angeles Rams, we're making heart valve failure education and screening more accessible to the community. Together, we're encouraging adults 50 and older to be proactive about their heart health, talk to their healthcare provider, and get screened.”
Jackson joined Torry Holt and Eric Dickerson for the event after previously participating in the initiative during training camp.
“I actually participated a couple of times this year with Edwards LifeSciences. I was screened myself to make sure that my heart passages are clear or if there's any concern to be brought to notice,” said Jackson. “It could be a silent killer…There are the conditions like this heart disease that could kill us quietly if we're not aware of it and not getting checked up…Early screening only takes 5 minutes of people’s time.”
Just met the great Steven Jackson!!! @sj39 🔥🔥🔥 #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/4wgmP2ndrD
While Jackson and Williams have different running styles, the emotion and heart that they play with are very similar. It’s widely known that Williams grew up a Rams fan and there’s a photo of him as a kid in the Edward Jones Dome with Jackson.
The rookie and the legend. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/zYQYDvk2Qq
Williams has since followed in Jackson’s footsteps as a Rams running back and has been a similar model of consistency. Over the past three seasons, Williams has eclipsed the 1,000-yard mark. He is the only Rams running back since Jackson to rush for 1,000 yards in three consecutive seasons.
“Anytime you can have an influence on anybody's life in a positive way, you know, it's one of those things that's a feel-good story,” said Jackson. “I'm happy that my interaction with Kyren has left him in the sense that he thinks fondly of me. And then to go on and see him have his own career and be very, very successful in his own right is even more rewarding to see that just compounding interest and just doing right by people.”
Throughout Jackson’s career, he was a true bell cow at running back. He started his career behind Marshall Faulk, but eventually took over as the lead player in the Rams’ backfield.
However, over the last two years, the Rams have used a running back by committee approach with Williams and Blake Corum. Williams has remained the steady presence while Corum has provided some elusiveness.
“Having Corum back him up, you see why the longevity of why they use them interchangeably and why you try to bring them both to the postseason healthy,” Jackson said. “They're both dynamic runners, but Kyren does an unbelievable job of finding the end zone.”
During Jackson’s career with the Rams, he didn’t experience a lot of team success. The Rams made the playoffs in Jackson’s rookie season, but never had a winning record. Still, Jackson was a model of consistency despite not always getting the individual recognition.
In 2009, the Rams went 1-15 and Jackson had one of the best years of his career. Jackson ranked third in the NFL in rushing yards with 1,416 and scored four touchdowns. In their lone win, Jackson rushed for 149 yards and scored the game-winning touchdown against the Detroit Lions.
“There are certain things that we have a standard or we have beliefs or something in our inner core that we live to and hope to be a beacon of and we try to aspire to be that each and every day,” Jackson said. “For me as a kid that grew up wanting to play professional football, wanting to be an NFL running back, and having that answered and having that given to me with the opportunity, I didn't think it would be right in honoring what I worked so hard for and praised for to then take it for granted.”
Some of the more fun battles to watch throughout Jackson’s career were his yearly matchups with San Francisco 49ers linebacker Patrick Willis. The two players faced off 17 times between 2007 and 2012.
While the Rams-49ers rivalry has taken on new life since the Rams moved back to Los Angeles, Jackson and Willis had their battles.
“I view playing against Patrick Willis and the 49ers defense as that me giving me the chance to rise to the occasion against someone that's a Hall of Famer,” said Jackson. “When you play with the passion that I try to show up with each and every Sunday, It lets everyone know that, you know, there's pride taken into what we put on the field. And that's how I carry myself in my career.”
The Rams have had an up-and-down season to say the least. They’ve dealt with injuries and lost some close games. However, after beating the Washington Commanders, they have won three straight and are above .500 for the first time this year.
Despite losing Puka Nacua to injury, the Rams also got Myles Garrett back and should continue to get healthy over the next few weeks and after their bye. At 5-4, the Rams control their own destiny and should have a good chance to make a late-season push at the playoffs.
“The Rams definitely had some tough losses, right? You know, you had the longer week one travel to Australia, and then you had a couple of games where you could say officiating was something to be raised,” Jackson said. “When you think about a head coach, a quarterback, a general manager, all the decision makers, you have the right people in the right places. And I think as far as a roster, you're having guys get back healthy, speaking mostly about Myles Garrett, getting ready to come back to make a late push in this run.”

title: Rams Restructure Pair of Contracts, But Could Another Move Be Coming?
full_text:
Following Tuesday’s trade deadline , the Los Angeles Rams opened up cap space on Wednesday as they restructured two contracts. According to Spotrac, The Rams converted $2 million of Kyren Williams’ salary into a signing bonus, adding two void years to create $1.7 million in cap space. The Rams did the same with Kam Curl’s contract, creating $1.3 million in cap space.
Despite restructuring the contracts, the Rams still have flexibility with both. They have an out with Williams’ deal following the 2027 season, while Curl’s contract also provides flexibility after 2027.
With both moves, the Rams have opened up around $3 million in cap space. While it’s natural to look at the moves and wonder if the Rams have a pending move planned, this was always inevitable. The Rams have consistently been among the teams with the least amount of available cap space this season. They have spent a large portion of the season cap-strapped and under $1 million. They were under $10,000 at one point.
It was never going to be sustainable for the Rams to go the rest of the year with that little amount of cap space. Throughout the season, the Rams have dealt with several injuries, forcing them to make weekly roster moves.
With eight games remaining, it was always unlikely that they would get through the rest of the season without needing to make additional, low-level signings. Whether that's signing a player to the active roster, adding depth at an injury-riddled position, or elevating someone from the practice squad, those moves require cap space. At some point, the Rams were going to have to restructure at least one contract.
These moves also show why the Rams' limited cap space was never going to prevent them from making a trade at the deadline. While the Rams didn’t have a lot of cap space to work with, there were ways to open up space as needed.
Now, that isn’t to say that the Rams can’t still sign a big-name player if they become available. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams are interested in Brandon Aiyuk when the San Francisco 49ers eventually cut him. If Aiyuk signs for the veteran minimum with incentives, that’s a move the Rams could afford. The same can be said if Stefon Diggs demands a release out of Washington.
At the very least, it gives the Rams flexibility to make a late in-season signing if that’s something they want to do. Previously, that would not have been an option.
The timing of these moves may raise some eyebrows, especially coming one day after the trade deadline and Aiyuk’s pending release. However, this was more about necessity than anything else. The Rams simply couldn't continue operating with so little cap space. While the additional flexibility could allow them to make a move if the right opportunity presents itself, the restructures were something the Rams needed to do regardless.

title: The Rams Made Their Choice at NFL Trade Deadline, and It Wasn't Matthew Stafford
full_text:
For much of the last two years, the Los Angeles Rams have had one foot in one timeline and one foot in another . The Rams have tried to do what they can to surround Matthew Stafford with a roster capable of winning the Super Bowl while also preserving their future for Ty Simpson.
At Tuesday’s trade deadline, the Rams appeared to finally choose a path , and that was the one with Simpson.
It seems odd that a front office that has historically been so aggressive in the past could just sit content at the trade deadline the last two years. With Matthew Stafford playing at an MVP level in 2025 and an obvious need at cornerback, the Rams traded for Roger McCreary while Sauce Gardner went to the Indianapolis Colts. McCreary spent most of the season injured, was not brought back in free agency, and the Rams allowed 346 yards and three touchdowns to Sam Darnold in the NFC Championship Game.
It’s true that the Rams traded picks and took an “all-in” approach by trading for Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett in the offseason. However, it can be argued that the move for McDuffie was six months too late. In those moves, the Rams gave up one first-round pick in 2026 and a second-round pick in 2027.
When the Rams drafted Ty Simpson with the 13th overall pick, they told everyone that they were starting to look ahead at life post-Stafford. That’s not to say that was the wrong choice. It has been widely reported that the Rams taking Simpson allowed them to take Myles Garrett . Despite remaining competitive under Sean McVay, the Rams still found itself with a top-15 pick.
During the draft, the Rams had two choices. They could take a wide receiver and continue pushing the quarterback decision down the line. Had the Rams done that, they likely would have faced a future similar to Minnesota's, relying on discarded veteran quarterbacks in hopes that the offense could elevate them. That could still happen, but with Simpson, the Rams at least have some control of the outcome.
However, that’s still a path they could have taken. The Rams could have given Stafford a wide receiver like Makai Lemon, KC Concepcion, or Omar Cooper Jr. Instead, they looked toward the future and drafted his eventual replacement.
By taking Simpson, the Rams would be doing him a disservice by not taking the future into account. They can’t empty the cupboards or they risk setting Simpson up to fail. The result has been treating Stafford like a bridge quarterback instead of one that can win them the Super Bowl.
The Rams’ actions over the last two years have basically said that they will support him in the best way they can, but they aren’t going to completely mortgage the future in the way that they might have back in 2021. They have given Stafford their 2027 resources, but don’t appear eager to mess with 2028, when they are set to have eight draft picks in addition to whatever comp picks they receive.
Look no further than how the Rams have structured their contracts. The 2028 season appears to be the 'reset'. The Rams have seven non-rookie contracts on the books in 2028 and have potential outs in all but one of them.
It’s certainly fair to wonder if the Rams hadn’t won in 2021 if they would be as content with doing nothing as they are currently.
Yes, the Rams acquired Garrett and McDuffie in the offseason, but they only used one pick in 2028 to do so. They acquired McDuffie for a top pick in 2026 and Garrett for a top pick in 2027. While the Rams could have dove into 2028 at the trade deadline, they opted not to.
In what was supposed to be an all-in year, the Rams seemed to wave the white flag rather than address an obvious need. With Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as the team’s top receivers, the Rams wouldn’t match two Day 3 picks for a player like Josh Downs. Even if Downs isn’t a WR1, he’s still an upgrade over every wide receiver on the roster and fills a need at punt returner. Instead, the Rams brought back Xavier Smith, who was cut after Week 3.
This was always the risk the Rams took by drafting Simpson. It gave them a safety net to fall back on. The Rams can no longer risk the future because Simpson is the future. The front office now has another quarterback to consider when making decisions that could impact the franchise for years to come.
Many point to the Rams following the approach of the Green Bay Packers with Aaron Rodgers and Jordan Love. In both cases, the Packers didn’t win a Super Bowl with both quarterbacks on the roster. In the end, it resulted in an ugly and awkward breakup.
The Packers made it to the playoffs one time with both Favre and Rodgers on the roster. After making back-to-back NFC Championship Games, the Packers lost in the divisional round the year they took Love before going 8-9 in Rodgers’ final year.
When a team starts to look ahead at the quarterback position, it rarely works out well. It almost always ends in an ugly breakup and the decision looks worse if that quarterback fails. Look at the Vikings and how they handled Sam Darnold and JJ McCarthy. Tom Brady is the exception.
As John Madden said, “If you have two quarterbacks, you have none.” The Rams don’t necessarily have a quarterback competition creating tension between Stafford and Simpson. However, it has arguably created tension between the coaching staff, front office, and the quarterback. It’s hard to build a roster around two quarterbacks in two different timelines.
The Rams don’t know how many more swings they are going to get with Stafford and instead of giving him more help, they’ve preserved the future. When they drafted Simpson, McVay didn’t necessarily look pleased during the press conference. As a class act, Stafford hasn’t been publicly upset with the Simpson pick, but it has to be hard for him to look at the current wide receiver situation and be a little bit frustrated.
There’s nothing wrong with the Rams’ decision to prepare for life after Stafford, but it was always going to be impossible to live in two separate timelines. That preparation for the future has come at the expense of the present. The Rams standing pat at the trade deadline told everyone what they needed to know.
They may eventually be rewarded if Simpson develops into a franchise quarterback. However, if Stafford's time with the Rams ends without another Super Bowl appearance, it will be hard not to wonder whether they sacrificed their best opportunity to win for a future that was never guaranteed.

title: Rams Trade Deadline Winners and Losers: Les Snead Fails Matthew Stafford
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams entered the NFL trade deadline desperately needing help at wide receiver. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on injured reserve, the Rams had an opportunity to make a move that could help save their season. Instead, the Rams stood pat with their roster as it was . Here are the biggest winners and losers from the Rams' trade deadline.
This is not the Les Snead that we are accustomed to seeing. The Snead that we’ve seen operate over the past several years would have made a move for a wide receiver, even if it wasn't for a big name. It’s hard to fathom how the offense could lose Puka Nacua for several weeks and the front office could look at the roster and come to the conclusion that it was enough. Not doing anything felt like the Rams are punting on the 2026 season.
There is not a bigger winner than Konata Mumpfield. He is now the top wide receiver on the depth chart and will get an opportunity to show what he can do in a larger role. It’s very clear that the coaching staff likes him in the offense. An argument can be made that Mumpfield hasn’t seen many opportunities because of Stafford’s comfort level with Nacua. Now is his chance to show what he’s capable of.
The Rams failed Matthew Stafford at the trade deadline. They don’t know how many more chances they’re going to get with Stafford and seem to be treating him like a bridge quarterback instead of one that can win them a Super Bowl. They didn't use one of their Day 2 draft picks on a wide receiver or address the position in free agency. In a hot wide receiver market, the Rams once again stood pat at the position and didn’t give Stafford any help. The Rams could have and should have done more for their quarterback.
It will be interesting to see if the Rams utilize CJ Daniels more or if he remains limited in his role. The Rams haven’t used the rookie wide receiver at all in the passing game and this will be his best chance to get involved. Daniels impressed throughout training camp and the preseason. With Adams and Nacua out, it's time to see what he can do.
How can the Rams look at Aaron Donald after this and say they did everything to try and win him one more ring? Donald came out of retirement this season, and it hasn’t gone the way that he expected, to say the least. It took nine weeks for him to finally play alongside Myles Garrett. The Rams owed it to Donald to make this season worth it for him by making a trade at the deadline. Instead, they did nothing.
Once the trade deadline had passed, the Rams announced the signing of Xavier Smith . Smith is back on the roster and presumably will resume his role in the offense and as the team’s primary punt returner. Had the Rams made a move, they may not have brought back Smith. By standing pat, the Rams are relying on a familiar face at the position.
It’s hard to see the Rams surviving the next four games without Puka Nacua and with Davante Adams not at 100 percent. They are entering a grueling part of their schedule in which they will face the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers. To make the playoffs, the Rams likely need to win at least two of those games. That’s a tall task as it stands. It’s going to take Matthew Stafford to play some of his best football of the season

title: Rams Place Another Wide Receiver on Injured Reserve, Bring Back Familiar Face in Xavier Smith
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams didn’t do anything at the trade deadline . However, once the deadline had passed, the team announced that Jordan Whittington had been placed on injured reserve and that it had signed wide receiver Xavier Smith in a corresponding move.
On Tuesday, head coach Sean McVay noted that Whittington had been dealing with some soreness in his back.With Whittington headed to injured reserve, his season is likely over as the Rams won’t have enough return designations to bring him back. Whittington had two catches for 12 yards on the season and was averaging 26.3 yards per kickoff return.
The Rams losing Whittington is another hit to the wide receiver position.They were already without Davante Adams, who has been on injured reserve, and then lost Puka Nacua as well . While Whittington doesn’t offer a lot in the passing game, he is arguably the best blocking wide receiver on the team and provides value on special teams.
Given the current injury situation at wide receiver, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth over the next month. With Nacua and Adams sidelined, players like Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels could take on larger roles. Losing Whittington only makes that situation more difficult.
Still, bringing back Smith is certainly an interesting choice. While Smith has experience in the offense, his size limits what he can offer as a receiver. The Rams previously cut Smith this season as they looked to make improvements at punt returner.
With the Rams needing depth at wide receiver and in need of a punt returner again, it’s possible they saw Smith as the best available option. After cutting Alex Bachman, the Rams had Kyren Williams returning punts against the Washington Commanders.
Smith will likely take Whittington’s place on kick returns and could go back to returning punts as well, despite his previous struggles in that role. It’s possible he could see snaps on offense as well, taking away from Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels.
The Rams opted not to make a move for a receiver at the trade deadline and instead signed Smith. While Smith provides some familiarity with the offense, it's difficult to see how he significantly improves a wide receiver group that was already lacking depth.
Over the last few weeks, the Rams have dealt with a handful of injuries at wide receiver and are running out of options. Smith at least provides someone with experience in the offense. With no outside help coming at the trade deadline, the Rams will have to find a way to make it work with what they have.

title: Grading the Rams NFL Trade Deadline: Was Doing Nothing the Right Decision?
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams found out that wide receiver Puka Nacua was likely to end up on injured reserve , their entire trade deadline plans changed. They went from a team content with waiting to get healthy to one that may need to make a move just to get by.
“I think you have to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up,” said head coach Sean McVay. “A lot of new things occur on a daily basis, so I would never rule it out.”
Despite the injuries that have put their championship hopes in jeopardy, the Rams still have reason to believe they can compete. Nacua will be out at least four weeks, but it will likely be more. When Nacua was out in 2024 with a PCL sprain, he was out for six weeks.
Davante Adams also remains on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury against the Arizona Cardinals. Adams was given a 6-to-10-week timeline with optimism that he could return on the shorter end of that. A six-week timeline would put Adams back following the Rams’ Week 12 matchup with the Packers. Even then, hamstring injuries can be difficult to return from.
Coming into the season, the Rams were seen as a team looking to compete for a Super Bowl. Had the Rams made a move at the trade deadline, it could have been seen as them trying to chase their losses. The Rams went to Vegas and bet the house on themselves to win it all. Each time they’ve won a hand, they’ve lost two more.
At this point, were the Rams better off walking away from the table and accepting their losses, or continuing to throw chips on the table when they had none to lose? Sitting at 5-4 and on the outside looking in at the postseason, it’s possible the Rams realized that the best-case scenario was a first- or second-round playoff exit rather than the championship run they were hoping for.
It makes sense that the Rams wouldn’t want to overpay for Brian Thomas Jr. or trade for an aging Keenan Allen. However, the Kansas City Chiefs traded for Josh Downs for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. That seems like a manageable price.
With that said, it’s hard to fathom this front office and coaching staff looking at a wide receiver depth chart of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Jordan Whittington and being content with that. Those four make Brandon Gibson, Tavon Austin, Austin Pettis, and Chris Givens look good.
The Rams may not make the playoffs, but doing nothing at the trade deadline makes it seem as though they’re waving the white flag. The team certainly won’t quit, but the front office has seemingly come to the conclusion that the roster is too hurt to do anything meaningful.
Again, it’s fair that the Rams wouldn’t want to overpay for a player like Thomas. However, with Downs going to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth, that’s a deal the Rams could have done. One day after Puka Nacua went on injured reserve, the Rams did nothing to replace him. The Rams don’t know how many more swings they’re going to get with Matthew Stafford. Aaron Donald certainly deserved the Rams doing more at the trade deadline.It may be hyperbolic to call their inactivity a failure, but it was fair to expect more from this front office.

title: Rams Trade Rumors: Rashod Bateman Emerges as Last-Minute Wide Receiver Target

Earlier on Tuesday, it was reported that the Jacksonville Jaguars would not be trading Brian Thomas Jr. Additionally, the Indianapolis Colts sent wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.
The Rams already had limited options at wide receiver heading into Tuesday's trade deadline. With Thomas and Downs no longer available, those options have become even more limited. With Thomas and Downs no longer available, that was especially the case.
However, with less than an hour remaining before the trade deadline, the Rams appear to still be working the phones. According to Pierce DeLuna of the 1st and Tuna Substack, One name the Rams are exploring is Baltimore Ravens' wide receiver Rashod Bateman.

title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza Opens Up About His New Opportunity
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) are set to host the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks (5-4), at Allegiant Stadium.
It is truly a baptism by fire for the 2026 No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza, whom NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect in the last four years.
Great, look at @fernandomendoza and his 1st practice as "THE MAN" today pic.twitter.com/dlEIP7uiB8
The Raiders' burgeoning young superstar has blossomed since the Raiders made official what we had reported for months: that they had pegged him as their potential choice.
With the trade of Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday, the franchise has handed the reins to the reigning Heisman Trophy winner, and fans who see their fandom as a way of life couldn’t be happier.
The youngster is well known for the way he handles pressure. He didn’t flinch when his Indiana Hoosiers needed a touchdown to beat the Penn State Nittany Lions, nor in the National Championship game versus the Miami Hurricanes.
In both cases, and multiple others, he has always gone back to his deep-rooted Christian faith for his calm-under-pressure demeanor.
On Sunday, he will fulfill a lifelong dream of starting a game as an NFL franchise QB—certainly another emotional moment in a young career overflowing with them. I asked the rookie if he would handle this moment as he has the previous ones, and despite now being a multi-millionaire nearly 50 times over, he hasn’t changed one bit.
“This is a once in a lifetime opportunity, and I get my strength from Jesus Christ, and I can’t thank everybody that supported me up to this point. And a huge part of that is faith, and that’s my motto – faith, family, and football. So, to have faith and gain strength from my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, it is a fundamental part of my prior success.”
Mocked by some for his genuine demeanor and raw appreciation for life, Mendoza is the real deal in a fake world. That is hard for some to conceptualize because so many are fake and don’t even know who they are.
For his age, he is a rarity in that he isn’t looking for likes and follows on social media; he is focused on doing things the right way. So when asked about Kirk Cousins, his deep emotional bond with the new Vikings starting quarterback was heartfelt.
“Yeah, I wanted to make a statement where I really, truly, from the bottom of my heart, wanted to thank Kirk [Cousins] and the entire Cousins family, whether it was Julie, Cooper, Turner. As a family, they’ve done so much for me. They’ve essentially taken me into their household when they were here, and they welcomed me with open arms.”
The gesture of my friend, Cousins, wasn’t lost on Mendoza. “And it would have been really easy for Kirk, being a veteran quarterback and having already proved everything, to be a little bit more dismissive. But he had me with open arms and has taught me so many things.”
Like what you might ask? He explained, “Whether it’s film study, how to operate as a starting quarterback, all the different multifaceted approaches that have made him so successful throughout his career, he has shared with no restrictions or no constraints. So, I really appreciate him, and it was heartfelt to see him as he was a great mentor.”
Mendoza has always dreamed of piloting his own NFL franchise, but that is only a road sign on his map to success. So, with the emotion of another goal checked off his bucket list, he knows there are far bigger ones down the road, so he is focused on keeping the important things front and center and shutting out the things that aren't.
“I believe in the principles in the quarterback room that Coach [Andrew] Janocko, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan always preface is you’re always one play away, always be prepared. And Kirk [Cousins] was a great example and leader of that on how to be prepared and how to make no moment too big. And so those are all lessons that I believe Aidan [O’Connell] and I will take into this next chapter.”
The Raiders loved Mendoza coming out of the NFL Draft, just like the multiple executives that were mentioned above. But that doesn’t compare to what they think of him today.
For nearly three weeks, people inside the building have quietly said he's ready, and as he has grown every day, he has gotten himself to this point.
He reflected on his growth since touching down in the desert.
“In the quarterback room, sometimes Coach Sully [Mike Sullivan] will reference back to Spring Fernando. I don’t want to talk about myself in the third person, but it just shows how much improvement there’s been, and I’m a lot more confident as a quarterback, and I feel more developed."
"Whether it’s under center, connecting with teammates, understanding an NFL scheme, there’s so many areas that I’ve improved on, and I look forward to keep on improving because there’s still a lot of work to do.”
Kirk Cousins taught Mendoza that they weren’t competing against each other, but with each other. That allowed the two to build a close bond, and it helped Mendoza get to where he is today. He explained the concept brilliantly.
“That compete-with approach, I think, was a fundamental part of our relationship and the entire quarterback room’s relationship altogether, and the quarterback room that we have and that we had with Kirk [Cousins] was such a special moment, and it was like a nice family away from home, and so we’re all getting each other better. And honestly, it was more like Kirk and Aidan [O’Connell] giving me tips and tricks. So, I’m forever thankful.”
Klint Kubiak made it clear that Mendoza is the Raiders' starting QB, and with that comes the entire playbook. In fact, it may even expand with Mendoza’s arm and mobility, but the young man is ready for it, and the moment isn’t too big for the protégé who has had many big moments.
“I believe one of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared. And that’s something that all three of the quarterbacks, when we were all here, we always, all three of us, prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we’d like to make.”
“I believe one of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared. And that’s something that all three of the quarterbacks, when we were all here, we always, all three of us, prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we’d like to make.”
Mendoza wasn’t done; as the leader he is, he reminded people that as Cousins worked with him, he would be working with Aidan O’Connell. “And so, I believe Aidan [O’Connell] and I will continue that rhythm in order to prepare and do our job and execute the offense. Because at the end of the day, the quarterback is only 1/11th, and I need to do my job to best showcase all the other talents we have on the offense and on the team.”
Because of Mendoza’s ever-present faith, the moment isn’t too big because he is grounded. So when asked about the enormity of the moment and the whirlwind around him, he wasn’t buying the narrative.
“I believe starting an NFL game is a new step, but a whirlwind? No. I would agree with Coach [Klint] Kubiak. Coach Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan, and everyone in the quarterback room, including Kirk [Cousins], have done a fantastic job in aiding my development, and I can’t thank them enough. And now it’s my turn to do my 1/11th. And we have such a great offensive staff, and we have such a great offense.“
He continued to praise this franchise, “Whether it was leaders in the offensive line, leaders in the receiver room, leaders in the tight end room, or leaders in the running back room that I believe that they’re going to help me along the way to…

title: Raiders Get Fantastic News on Injured Starter
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders traded veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings just before the trade deadline on Tuesday. Las Vegas' front office got a top-tier return on their investment in Cousins, as he led them to a 4-5 record with some of the best quarterback play in the league.
The Raiders' front office was able to reel in a third-round pick for a veteran quarterback that was highly unlikely to be on the team past this season. John Spytek and the Raiders' front office have already found great value in the third round of the past two NFL Drafts.
Trading Cousins was a win for all three parties. With Cousins under center, Las Vegas has already won more games in half a season than they did all of last season. They are in position to win as many games as, if not more than, they have in the past two seasons combined and walk away with a third-round pick.
The Vikings get an experienced quarterback the franchise knows well. Cousins returns to the city where he had his best years as a professional. He also goes to a team with a winning record and one that could potentially go on a deep playoff run with the right quarterback.
With Mendoza headed back to Minnesota, the Raiders will finally turn to the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft, Fernando Mendoza. Among other things, Cousins' play over the first half of the season bought the Raiders more time to see what they had under a first-year coaching staff.
The extra time gave the Raiders' brass and coaching staff an extra couple of months to develop Mendoza and work with the rookie quarterback. Instead of throwing him onto the field with a roster filled with questions, Las Vegas can move forward with certainty.
The Raiders' roster still needs significantly more. Las Vegas' remaining roster issues will likely hurt Mendoza at some point. However, with him now the team's starting quarterback, the Raiders can finally take another step toward a brighter future overall.
Mendoza's first start doesn't erase the many problems Las Vegas' roster still has. The rookie will not be enough to overcome a Raiders roster that was the league's worst last season, which is how Mendoza landed in the desert in the first place.
However, the Raiders' final eight games will show how far they've come after an offseason of wholesale changes. Mendoza is the only part of the Raiders' massive offseason haul that hasn't played significant minutes this season.
That will change this Sunday, as Mendoza will get his very first start as a professional against Klint Kubiak's former team, but at Allegiant Stadium. It is hard to miss the irony of it all, or how full-circle a moment Sunday will be for many players and coaches.
Sunday is bigger than just the game or its results, as it marks the official start of a new era in the Raiders' storied history. Yet Wednesday's practice was quietly an important day as well.
Last week, the Raiders' injury report was the lightest it has been this season. Wednesdays are usually the day that Las Vegas' roster gets the most rest in, as most of the players who are listed throughout the week generally play on Sundays. That should still be the case for the most part this week.
The Raiders will need all hands on deck against a solid Seahawks team that, on paper, already possesses most of the game's competitive advantages. On Wednesday, several players were listed on the injury report.
Thomas Booker, Foley Fatukasi, and Trey Zuhn were limited participants on Wednesday. Ian Thomas was listed on the report but was a full participant. Booker and Thomas are dealing with ankle issues. Fatukasi is dealing with a shoulder issue, and Zuhn is dealing with a concussion-related issue.
Zuhn's status will be worth keeping an eye on, as he has started the past two games for the Raiders at right guard. This is despite not being listed on the depth chart as the team's starting guard. “Trey [Zuhn III] will be the starter if he can go," Kubiak confirmed on Wednesday.
Kubiak offered further insight into the guard position, specifically veteran offensive guard Bryce Cabeldue, a former Seahawks offensive lineman the Raiders may have to turn to on Sunday, should Zuhn be unable to play.
"He is doing it, and he’s doing a fantastic job. Since the time he got here, he’s been professional. He’s showing improvement, and he’s just waiting for an opportunity," Kubiak said Wednesday.
The Raiders hope a relatively healthy roster, their home crowd, and a potential spark from Mendoza are enough to catch the Seahawks off guard. Las Vegas is 4-5 but hasn't beaten a team with a winning record this season.
Heading into Week 10, they have several things working in their favor that could be enough to unexpectedly swing momentum in their favor. Cousins played well in his time with the Raiders. However, Mendoza's skill set could be enough to help Las Vegas negate roster deficiencies.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Hondo’s Raiders Mailbag: Fans Make Expectations for Mendoza Clear
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) are staring at a steep climb into the NFL Playoffs, but with the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4) coming into town this Sunday, things are far from dismal.
The Raiders traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings and are ready to embrace the future.
In part because of their No. 1 overall 2026 NFL Draft selection, the young man NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect of the last four years, Fernando Mendoza. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner has been ready, according to people within the organization, for just over two weeks, allowing the team to make a trade and reassure the locker room of its intention to win.
The players see what Mendoza is doing, and they are pleased.
Every week I ask Raider Nation for their thoughts on the Silver and Black via my X account, @HondoCarpenter, and as always, you responded in masse, even with me spelling Mendoza, “Medoza.” So let’s dig in.
I expect growing pains, a few boneheaded trying-to-do-too-much plays, a handful of wow plays and a 3-5 record or better.
This is a great point. He is a rookie. The next 25 regular-season games for Fernando are about growth and maturity. I can assure you that you will see the wow plays, and conversely, you will see those mistakes as well.
Raider Nation, not all, but many, turned on Ashton Jeanty very hard, even after a good rookie season and an offensive line whose run blocking is offensive.
Just like with the other young players, the rookie head coach, and the offensive and defensive coordinators, the name of the game is to embrace the growth and the process.
Every mistake made this year and next shortens the learning curve. Great take.
This would fall close to my prediction for the year, but I want to add this.
After Sunday, the schedule gets significantly easier. While that does not negate the fact that Mendoza is a rookie, if the underperforming veterans step up, I think things could get very interesting.

Run game is about to open up. The lack-of is difficult to root for.   If Mendoza is half the qb i think he's gonna be... we're gonna be just fine.
I have said since the Raiders selected the Nandolorian that his mobility is an underrated part of his skill set. The issue will be him learning patience if he runs no more than four times a game; that is ideal.
If he does that, the Raiders will be in great shape. Remember this: if he gets sacked, that counts as a rush on the stat sheet, but not for me. No more than four legitimate runs per game is great for the Raiders and Fernando.

title: Buckle Up: The Fernando Mendoza Era Has Begun For Raiders
full_text:
A few days ago, the Las Vegas Raiders were down in the dumps after their 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, with trade rumors around the organization persisting. As the Minnesota Vikings fell to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night with a putrid quarterback performance, the signs began to show of a potential reunion in the making.
On Tuesday, before the NFL trade deadline, the Raiders ushered in a new era by trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for a third-round pick. It all but handed the offense and franchise to the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza , who will get his first opportunity to start against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.
One of the bright spots of the Raiders' offense this season has been their passing game, which is fifth in passing yards per game (259.7). It has been an impressive unit to watch, with head coach Klint Kubiak calling plays and putting the offense in positions for success this season, and Cousins playing a big role .
However, Cousins was never going to keep his starting job, despite throwing for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns to begin the season. Kubiak stated a few points this year that Mendoza would get his opportunity when the time was right. Sure enough, the Vikings needed a quarterback and added someone with great familiarity, opening the door for Mendoza to become the starter.
In Tuesday's post-trade press conference, Kubiak and general manager John Spytek noted in the preparation that Mendoza had to be ready for this moment. Both thanked Cousins for his contributions, but Spytek noted the obvious.
"With that, we did want to say and confirm that Fernando [Mendoza] will be the starting quarterback going forward."
Kubiak and Spytek shared similar sentiments about Mendoza's preparation. Spytek told reporters that he "passed every test," while Kubiak noted how well his rookie signal-caller has practiced, acknowledging the work habits that have allowed him to have the opportunity to make his first career start. Those work habits have a direct link to Cousins, as Kubiak shared.
"Work habits, preparation, ways to take care of your body, ways to connect with your teammates, progressions, blitzes to expect, things to expect from coordinators," Kubiak said. "We could go on and on, but there’s a lot more to playing the position than what your coaches tell you in your meeting room, and I think Kirk [Cousins] embodied all the right things there: how to prepare and how to be a professional, and really, when things aren’t going well, what buttons to push on your teammates and what questions to ask your coaches. It’s an endless list of all positive things.”
Cousins was a big piece of the Raiders' offensive puzzle, but it was never permanent, and both Kubiak and Spytek suggested as much before the season and during Tuesday's press conference. Cousins was a great bridge quarterback for the team, providing some great moments during the season with some terrific games against quality opponents. Raider Nation can appreciate those moments.
Moving on from Cousins now is a clear signal that Las Vegas wants to get the evaluation process started for their top draft pick. Mendoza is much more physically gifted as a passer than Cousins and could do more inside and outside the pocket, which could open up the passing game more than we've seen to date.
The arm arrogance, poise, and football intelligence will be on full display this weekend against a vaunted Seahawks defense. I'm excited for what Mendoza could showcase in his first start, but like any rookie quarterback, there will be some rough patches, whether that be standing too long in the pocket, making indecisive reads, making bad throws, etc.
The move also doesn't change the approach for the rest of the season.
"And then the last point to make is, and this is for Raider Nation and for this entire building, this in no way signifies that we are punting on this season or looking forward to 2027," Spytek said. "That is not the intention of this. We have a big game this week against the defending world champs, and we intend to attack it like we would any week."
The Raiders want to compete while growing their foundation and youth in the process. Losing the veteran leadership of Cousins is a blow, but a necessary one. With that, a new era has dawned in the desert.
It is officially time for the Fernando Mendoza era to begin.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: The Biggest Decision Kubiak Got Right vs. 49ers in Week 9
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have lost four of their last five games after starting the season 3-0. Las Vegas' Week 9 road matchup against the San Francisco 49ers was a long day on both sides of the ball for the Silver and Black, as they fell behind early and were unable to catch up.
Las Vegas' Week 9 loss looked eerily similar to most of their other four losses. A slow first half led to a panicked second-half effort that was simply too little, too late. Slow starts have been one of the biggest issues for the Raiders this season.
Las Vegas struggled in many regards against an elite 49ers team. Klint Kubiak noted that a subpar first half put the Raiders on their heels. They had a chance to mount a comeback in the second half, but that was quickly ended, largely by their own mistakes.
“Overall, you look at just the play count. It was like 38 to 16 or 38 to 17. That’s the exact opposite of how you want time of possession to go in a first half. But then you get the game to 21 to 11 with the ball coming right back to you, and you put yourself in position and we turned the ball over five times in the second half as an offense,” Kubiak said on Monday.
“So, that’s not going to give you opportunities to win any games. Even late in the game, defense gets an interception, we get a stop on fourth down, and there’s two chances to make that a 28-24 ballgame, and we turn the football over. So, shot ourselves in the foot.”
The biggest decision that Kubiak and the Raiders got right against the 49ers was deferring until the second half after winning the coin toss. Although Las Vegas lost in blowout fashion, the sequence of events showed that even when it starts poorly, it can work out in the Raiders' favor later.
After the 49ers received the opening kickoff, they proceeded to march right down the field against Las Vegas' defense. The Raiders were down by a touchdown when their offense took the field for the first time on Sunday. Then, their offense quickly punted the ball back to San Francisco.
The 49ers marched the ball down the field again, jumping out to an early 14-0 lead. It could not have been a worse start for Las Vegas on either side of the ball. Still, shortly before halftime, Las Vegas connected on a long field goal to stay afloat. Las Vegas was only down by 11 at halftime.
Las Vegas started the second half with the ball, but Kirk Cousins threw an interception that was returned for a touchdown. Still, starting the second half with the ball put the Raiders in a position to compete, even after a bad start. Not scoring hurt; scoring for the other team all but ended the game.
Few other decisions made on Sunday against the 49ers that had as much of an impact as that one call. The Raiders faced a superior 49ers team that was also coming off of its Bye Week. Las Vegas could have done little to realistically avoid the outcome.
However, if they win the coin toss, deferring to the second half bodes well for a Raiders team that has had trouble producing productive first halves of games. It also allows their defense to either set the tone, or shake off any nerves they may have.
It is much better for the Raiders to let their defense take the field first. If they are able to force a punt or even a field goal, it is a win. If they cannot do so, Las Vegas could still potentially get a possession before the end of the first half, in addition to starting the second half with the ball.
Electing to defer until the second half may not seem like a big deal, but they have played better when they do. Las Vegas is undergoing a change of the guard at quarterback, which will change things, but with a rookie quarterback stepping in, deferring until the second half makes even more sense.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Rookie, Sophomore Power Rankings: Growing Pains Continue
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders needed to get younger this offseason, and they did just that. Las Vegas added a wave of talented free agents and draft picks this offseason, most of whom were years younger than the players they were replacing on the roster. However, with that youth also came inexperience.
It was a trade-off the Raiders desperately needed to make across their roster. However, their past month of play has put the reality of that trade-off on display for four full quarters. This offseason, Las Vegas' front office decided to lean heavily on the young players on the roster.
Most of those players were added in the two most recent NFL Drafts, Las Vegas' first two drafts under general manager John Spytek. Their 4-5 record has both been aided and burdened by the talented but largely inexperienced wave of talent that Las Vegas is depending on.
Still, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak explained that even with that being the case, his team has taken an aggressive approach to improve throughout this season.
“I think one thing that I’m proud of is that we’re not talking about rebuilding. We’re talking about being in every game and winning every game. That’s how we treat it. We’re not looking at the future as coaches or players,” Kubiak said.
“You develop the future on the way, but every game we’re talking about winning that game. We are not satisfied with a rebuilding process, so that’s the mentality I want our players and coaches to have.”
Below are the power rankings for Las Vegas' rookie and second-year players who played enough to have an impact in Week 9.
Stukes' continued development is on display weekly. Sunday, against the 49ers, Stukes' interception helped keep the Raiders in the game. Stukes is proof that practice is valuable but not nearly as valuable as letting young players get on the field, for better or for worse.
Zuhn continued to look like arguably the team's best option at offensive guard. If the rookie can keep improving, that would be huge for a Raiders offense that has struggled to get going on the ground this season.
Assuming Zuhn is healthy and able to play this week, Las Vegas must keep him in the starting lineup to help further his development. So far, Zuhn looks like a solid addition to the offensive line for the second half of the season.
Jeanty continues to make an impact when he can. Although he led the team in rushing yards on Sunday, the team only ran for a total of 24 yards. However, Las Vegas stopped running the ball early in the second half after Kirk Cousins' interception that was returned for a touchdown.
Las Vegas' inability to run the ball well has more to do with its offensive line than anything else.
Entering the season, Las Vegas' defensive backfield was well known as the team's biggest weakness. The season's first nine games have confirmed as much, as the unit's overall youth stands out weekly. Although the Raiders have skilled players, they need more from those players.
Week 9 was another long outing for Las Vegas' group of young defensive backs. With the first half of the season in the books, Kubiak expressed his confidence in the position group following Sunday's loss.
“I do think Zeke [Hezekiah Masses] is doing some good stuff too. I know Zeke got beat on a touchdown, but I think we’ve got young guys that are playing good football that we’re going to keep playing all of them. Zeke and DP [Darien Porter] and Jermod [McCoy], and we’ll let the cream rise to the top and those guys will play more,” Kubiak said.
The Raiders only made one move at the trade deadline, and it was not to add a cornerback. This should make it clear how confident the Raiders' front office is in the group. Kubiak elaborated on the unit, noting that even rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy is coming along nicely.
“Jermod [McCoy], just a player that’s ascending. That’s making us play multiple DBs because he’s covering at a high level, he’s improving. Again, is a guy that we all didn’t know if he’s going to play football this year, and he’s not missing practice. He’s playing in games. He’s staying healthy. He’s progressing, getting better with reps," Kubiak said.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Pros and Cons of Raiders Turning To Fernando Mendoza Now
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick, subsequently triggering the beginning of the Fernando Mendoza era.
Moving the 38-year-old quarterback was always a possibility, but based on how the Raiders' season has unfolded in recent weeks and the Vikings' desperation for a reliable quarterback, this move had to happen. Not to mention, the Raiders received a third-round pick, which is incredible value for Cousins at this stage in his career.
Nevertheless, Mendoza is slated for his first career start in Week 10, and barring anything unforeseen, he is Las Vegas' starting quarterback moving forward. With that in mind, here are the pros and cons of the Raiders thrusting the No. 1 overall pick onto the field at this specific time.
If you look at the history of the NFL, especially in recent memory, sitting rookie quarterbacks for the season has proven beneficial for those players. For example, Patrick Mahomes and Jordan Love sat behind seasoned veterans - Alex Smith and Aaron Rodgers. Mahomes started the season finale, while Love learned from the bench for multiple seasons.
Sitting Mendoza for the entire season was the coaching staff's original plan, but as Las Vegas continued to lose games and the Vikings came to the table with an offer too good to turn down, the Raiders' hand was forced.
The writing has been on the wall for several weeks now, with Las Vegas losing four of its last five games . That said, Mendoza will now have eight weeks of on-field experience to provide film for himself and the coaching staff to assess. Assuming Mendoza stays healthy for the rest of the season, he'll have extensive experience heading into the 2027 season when the Raiders should have more pieces in place to support the franchise signal caller.
Mendoza won't be afforded an acclimation period. The Indiana product will make his debut on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, who arguably have the league's best defense. The Raiders follow that game with a two-game road slate against the Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns.
Ideally, a team wants to provide their incoming rookie quarterback with a soft-landing opponent. Based on the timing of the trade deadline, Las Vegas can't do that for Mendoza. It's important to note that if Mendoza struggles during this span, which is legitimately possible, Raider Nation shouldn't panic. Growing pains are part of the development process, and these upcoming opponents all have above-average defenses.
Logan Lazarczyk is a graduate of the University of Missouri-Kansas City, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies with an emphasis in Journalism. Logan joined our team with extensive experience, having previously written and worked for media entities such as USA Today and Union Broadcasting.

title: Inside Scoop: How the Kirk Cousins Trade Unfolded for the Raiders
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) made a move that is familiar on The Strip in this city, but not always common in the National Football League, as they moved all in on both the present and the future.
Kirk Cousins was brought to Las Vegas in order to be an example to the 2026 NFL Draft's number one overall pick, whom NFL executives ranked the best QB prospect of the last four years: Fernando Mendoza.
Cousins and Mendoza quickly hit it off, and the relationship became not only that of two teammates, but two friends. Close friends.
From Monday night team bible studies to early morning review sessions, Cousins and Mendoza worked well together, and each day the relationship blossomed.
Credit the work ethic and attitude of Mendoza that won Cousins, and credit Cousins for showing a willing heart to offer anything he could to the man, waiting in the wings to take his temporary hold on his job.
Before we dig into the details of the trade, yesterday would not have happened without both men performing at their very best.
For just over two weeks, sources in the building have made it abundantly clear that Mendoza was ready. The impediment to his playing was that Cousins was performing at a career-rejuvenating high level.
Mendoza didn’t pout; he continued to work at a very high level to be ready.
A fact that wasn’t lost on Cousins. One of the fiercest competitors ever known, Cousins is also a realist. He knew exactly why he was brought in, and that was to warm the seat for Mendoza, who was ready.
The locker room knew it, and so did everyone else.
While Mendoza won’t be as ready this Sunday versus the Seahawks (5-4), he was as ready as could be, and then some.
The details of how this went down are amazing, and it should make all of Raider Nation proud.
I was told three weeks ago that the Raiders were going to ask an “exorbitant” price for Cousins. That came down, but not by much.
I can tell you that even as reports surfaced recently that allegedly people hadn’t called the Raiders, that is the typical spin of the NFL and the semantics of word salad that NFL executives love.
GM John Spytek didn’t say that in those words, but he did allude to it when talking about how it all unfolded.
“I don’t want to get too far into that, but really, this morning, Nolan [Teasley] and I spoke for a while, and we figured out kind of the framework of it, and if it made sense for both teams, and obviously we ultimately agreed that it did. But I talked to a lot of the guys around the league for a long time, but I would say this morning.”
I started reporting last week that Cousins, after Sunday’s game with the 40ers, could be got for a third . I am NOT calling Spytek a liar, far from it. But you can have calls in which no offers are made, and clearly everyone on the call knows the details.
I was reporting what NFL people were telling me, “They perceived.”
You can also never make a call, but take all of them.
As one NFL executive told me last night, “John is smart. He didn’t have to call anyone; he wasn’t shopping him. You have nice calls, and say hi, and you know who is a serious player and who is a bargain shopper. Cousins ain't a Dollar General guy; he was playing like Neiman Marcus, and when it was time, a team with a Neiman Marcus defense, and other weapons came calling.”
Spytek essentially said that, “I got a few phone calls, but one real one this morning.”
The point was that Spytek played this perfectly. Had he held on to Cousins, all was good. If he made the move, the Raiders got all of the efforts of Cousins, on and off the field, for essentially free thanks to Tom Delaney, who is one of the NFL's elite contract and salary cap brains, and picked up a third-round pick.
Spytek explained what he has seen in Mendoza that told him that he was ready when I asked, and he didn’t hold back.
“Well, I’m not in the meetings every day with him, but I hear all the reports about how well he does in there. But just to watch him go out and practice, and the level at which he operates the scout team, and the unselfishness and his ability to throw the football, and I think we’ve both seen him improve as a passer as well. So, again, he worked really hard and performed at a level in practice that was hard to ignore, impossible to ignore, and he put us in a position to make a really hard decision today.”
I asked Klint Kubiak the same question, and his answer, while echoing the sentiments of Spytek, offered even more analysis.
“Fernando [Mendoza] has everything we’ve asked him to do in practice. I think he’s exceeded those expectations, and we all know that live bullet Sunday is far different from practice. However, he showed us that he’s ready, not only physically but mentally. He’s up there studying right now like he would any other game. He puts a lot of work in. His teammates know how prepared he is. It’s not just lip service, but he has shown it on the practice field.”
The fact is that I wrote months ago what just happened. I told you all that Cousins would only be here a short time, but his impact would be felt for years with the development of Mendoza. Kubiak explained that very well.
“Work habits, preparation, ways to take care of your body, ways to connect with your teammates, progressions, blitzes to expect, things to expect from coordinators. We could go on and on, but there’s a lot more to playing the position than what your coaches tell you in your meeting room, and I think Kirk [Cousins] embodied all the right things there, how to prepare and how to be a professional, and really, when things aren’t going well, what buttons to push on your teammates and what questions to ask your coaches. It’s an endless list of all positive things.”
Spytek didn’t sugarcoat or bloviate about the move. The fact was that Mendoza was ready, and the deal benefited both the Raiders and Cousins.
“Well, we had to make a hard decision. And I mean, we’re all kind of staring the future in the face here with Fernando [Mendoza], and Kirk [Cousins] was very open with that when we got him. We had to basically decide do we want to go forward here over the last eight games, or do we want to take what Minnesota is offering right now? Ultimately, we decided to do that.”
Perhaps the most underrated Raider in the entire organization is Tom Delaney. Universally respected around the NFL as a contract and salary cap genius, his masterful handling of the Cousins deal (mentioned above) got a great contract for Cousins and a remarkable deal for the Silver and Black. I asked Spytek about it.
“Yeah, it was a unique negotiation with Kirk [Cousins] last year, given his contract that he was coming off of in Atlanta and what we were trying to get accomplished as well, and we found a middle ground to make it work, where some of the compensation would be due next year had he finished today on our roster. That was something that we were thoughtful about, that we were willing to do because we felt like this is the kind of player we were signing, and he could bring what he brought to our organization. That was $10 million we were willing to pay, ownership was willing to pay, and then today things changed, and now that’s Minnesota’s contract now.”
Kubiak broke down the progress he has seen in his young QB, and the undeniable truths that proclaimed he was ready to take the next step.
“Yeah, well, every day he’s going against a live pass rush with Maxx [Crosby] and with Kwity Paye and Quay Walker and number 17 [Nakobe Dean] coming up the E gap, so he’s got a lot of game speed reps. I see him progress in his accuracy, in his total command of our system, his ability to get in and out of a huddle, operate two-minute drills, situational football. I think, just every aspect, like any rookie, you’ve seen growth. But his most important piece of production is his ability to throw a football accurately and make good decisions, and I’ve seen those two things really jump out.”
Kirk Cousins' 15 years in this league speak for themselves. There…

title: Kirk Cousins Delivers Heartfelt Message to Mendoza After Raiders Trade
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders weren't hyperactive during the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but they did make one significant move.
On Thursday, the Raiders agreed to trade quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. Las Vegas was not actively shopping Cousins, and we reported here that it would take a third-round pick to get him. That's exactly what Minnesota gave up.
This now paves the way for Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, to begin his tenure as the Raiders' franchise quarterback, while Cousins has a chance to chase a deep playoff run in Minnesota.
Cousins was brought to Las Vegas to serve as a mentor for Mendoza, as the franchise patiently waited before giving him the keys to the offense. As the Raiders' starter so far in 2026, the former Michigan State Spartan has been fantastic. Cousins currently ranks fifth in the NFL in passing yards (2,340) and second in passing touchdowns (20). The 15-year veteran has tallied a QBR of 62.8 and a completion percentage of 64.1%.
Simply put, Cousins did his job while in Las Vegas. Now, it's the former Indiana Hoosier's turn. However, on his way out, Cousins delivered a heartfelt message to the Raiders and wished Mendoza the best as he begins his journey as an NFL starting quarterback.
Following the deal that sent Cousins to Minnesota, Cousins posted a picture of himself and Mendoza on his Instagram story. The caption read, "Thank you Raider Nation! Go get 'em [Fernando Mendoza]."
It's a class act from a stand-up veteran in the National Football League who will now have an opportunity to chase a deep run in the playoffs with the Vikings. Back in Las Vegas, Mendoza takes the reins.
Everyone knew Mendoza would take over the quarterback position at some point, and that time has come. The rookie top pick's first start will come against the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks at home, who are 5-4 to begin the 2026 campaign.
The Raiders were patient, waiting for the right time and the right move to give Mendoza the opportunity to take over. At 4-5, following a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Raiders are not out of the playoff mix this season, which is already a success. However, the franchise is clearly looking toward the future. Get ready, Raider Nation. Your star rookie's time has arrived.
Hugh Straine is an accomplished writer and proud Bucknell University alumnus, holding a Bachelor of Arts in Creative Writing. He has served as editor of The Bucknellian, worked as an analyst for ESPN+ and Hulu, and currently reports on college sports as a general reporter for On SI.

title: Raiders Trade Kirk Cousins to Vikings: Here Are the Details
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders have traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings.
As we first reported when Cousins was originally signed, the 15-year veteran was brought in to prepare Fernando Mendoza to become the starter and franchise QB, and the deal was structured to make him a fully tradable commodity.
We have reported for weeks that Cousins was available, and that it would take a third-round pick.
As we have been reporting, the Raiders were holding firm on a third-round pick, and that is exactly what the Vikings are giving up in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Raiders essentially got all the benefits of Cousins, gained a third-round pick, and paid him essentially nothing, thanks to the creative genius of Tom Delaney, SVP of football administration.
The Raiders kept three QBs on the roster, as we have told you, because of this exact situation.
Aidan O’Connell will now be the backup to the new starter: the 2026 NFL Draft No. 1 overall pick and the youngster NFL executives ranked the best QB prospect in the last four years, Fernando Mendoza.
Coach Klint Kubiak recently spoke about what it would take for Mendoza to get his shot, and he didn’t mince words.
“Yeah, eventually Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football. We have a plan. We don’t have a timeline for that. Kirk [Cousins] is playing really well, and we’re in the hunt. It’s really important that we keep playing really well behind him and continue to develop Fernando, but Fernando is going to play at some point. It’s not going to be this week.”
Each week, Mendoza looks more ready and capable than the week before. He has a stronger arm and significantly better mobility than Cousins, and with the terrific example that Cousins provided, he is much more prepared for the role.
Raiders GM John Spytek made it clear the night he took the reigning Heisman Trophy winner that he loved him and staked the future of the franchise on him.
"Just a great person. Raised the right way, great family. He's about the right things, it's about his team, it's about winning, it's about doing the right thing, being accountable to the whole organization. It's very little to do with all the accolades he got after they won all those games. And he's really smart. He works really hard."
"This means a lot to him. And I don't that being the first overall pick and winning the Heisman and all the things that he's gotten will change him. I think that it'll actually make him work harder to prove that he's worth all that and then earn even more."
Mendoza played in October against the Patriots to get his first meaningful action of the season, and he spoke about the opportunity and what it means.
“It wasn't a great experience because of the overall outcome. I wanted to do my part any way I could help the team. I was called upon and I really appreciate all my teammates, especially some of the stars going out there, still having a fight to win and a fight and a fighting effort. So I really appreciate all those guys putting their best effort for that last drive.”
Mendoza will start this Sunday versus the defending Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks, and a new era of Raiders football begins.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience. He serves as the Senior Writer for NFL and College sports, and is the beat writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders. Additionally, he is the editor and publisher for several sites On SI. Carpenter is a member of the Pro Football Writers Association (PFWA), the Football Writers Association of America (FWAA), and the United States Basketball Writers Association (USBWA).

title: Positive Progress Report For Achane Highlights RB Possibilities For 2027 And Beyond
full_text:
Mid-November has been a difficult period for the Miami Dolphins in terms of injury news, with Malik Willis and Zach Sieler both placed on IR this week and Sieler out for the season. At the very least, though, there's some positivity for 2027 with the expected return of one of the biggest stars Miami has to offer.
Jeff Hafley spoke to the media Wednesday about running back De'Von Achane, including how he's progressing since suffering a torn ACL against Kansas City back on September 27. Achane hasn't played a snap of football since, but has made as much of an impact as he can on the team around him.
The loss of Achane has been as impactful as one might assume, but it has allowed the backup, Ollie Gordon II, to showcase his skill set week in and week out. When Achane is back, there are lots of positives that would point to him and Gordon being one of the nastiest running back duos in football.
"He had his surgery," Hafley said. "He's in the training room every morning. He sat in the team meeting last Monday. He was sitting in the front, which was cool to have him there. He's been around the players. He's in our weight room. I'm sure he wishes that he were out there, but his attitude's been great. I've seen him doing his rehab, and he's working really hard to get better. He's doing well."
The news from Hafley is positive, including what Achane's been doing in the meantime. Well before the season, Hafley noted he wanted an expanded leadership role for the 25-year-old, specifically being a vocal leader to a hodgepodge of rookies on both offense and defense. It seems that Achane is still making that a point despite what he's going through.
Finding anything positive about Achane's injury is moot, but at least it occurred as early as it did in the season. There isn't a monetary concern thanks to the four-year contract extension he signed back on May 13. Barring any major setbacks during his rehab, he'll likely have the opportunity to be back playing football ahead of the 2027 preseason.
Rehab is different, time-wise, for every player, but a best-case scenario would likely be similar to what Chris Bell went through when he tore his ACL with Louisville back in late November 2025. He had surgery in December, then returned to the field after nine and a half months. For Achane, that would place his possible return as early as June-July 2027.
Another player who will more than likely be returning in 2027 is Gordon, who is currently in the second year of his four-year rookie contract. Barring any offseason moves from the front office, Achane and Gordon will be the duo at running back for the Dolphins next season.
It hasn't always been smooth sailing for Gordon this season, but considering the sudden increase in demand, it's been mainly positive. He currently stands at 463 yards and four touchdowns on the ground. If he wants to reach 1K rushing yards, he'll need to average around 60 yards for the final nine games of the season, starting at Indianapolis on November 15.
Gordon has flashed the speed and agility fans picked up on in 2025. Even against top-notch defenses like Detroit, he still found ways to occasionally shake the first wave of would-be tacklers for solid pickups. The problem is that this is very dependent on the gaps that Miami's offensive line creates, and against the Lions, that was rare. Hence, a disappointing 55 yards on 16 carries.
A major strength of Gordon, though, is his durability. He's been recording high snap counts, partially due to the lack of a dependable backup right now — Jaylen Wright was struggling to provide quality snaps even before the quad injury that sidelined him Sunday. With Willis on IR, Gordon's already high snap count might go up even more to ease some pressure off quarterback Kyle McCord.
One of the biggest differences between Achane and Gordon is physicality in the trenches. Achane is powerful enough to bully past the defensive line even with a lack of sizeable gaps, whereas Gordon falls short on occasion. Being six inches shorter (5-9 to 6-2) and 30 pounds lighter (195 to 225), Achane can be harder to bring down both on the initial tackle and at max speed.
Achane will be the starter who dominates the snap count, with Gordon coming in to give the workhorse an occasional rest. The plan is that opposing defenses won't have time to breathe and adjust when Achane steps off the field over the course of the game, let alone on a single offensive drive.
Jake Gibson is a writer for the Miami Dolphins on SI.
