title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Gives Update on A.J. Brown's Travel Status
full_text:
It hasn't been the greatest start to the season for A.J. Brown . The New England Patriots traded two picks for him in June and he was expected to be one of the offensive catalysts for this unit all season long.
Instead, he's nursed ankle and knee injuries and has only played in three games. In those three games, he's caught just nine passes and no touchdowns. Brown hasn't lived up to the mark just yet.
But he could make his return to the field after a two-game absence in Germany. The Patriots missed Brown for their games down in Miami and against Green Bay at home . For both of those weeks, Brown didn't suit up for practice once and was only spotted briefly in the locker room when reporters were present.
Could Brown end up making the trip across the Atlantic Ocean for the Patriots' Week 10 matchup with the Detroit Lions?
"Yeah, I think that that's the plan. Certainly, there's no decision on that, but I would imagine that that's the plan," head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday. "We'll continue to work to get guys back, be healthy and help the football team. That's the goal.
"So, to be able to answer that right now, today, I can't do that with a few guys. But, I know that the plan is to try to get everybody that can help us to get on the plane on Wednesday, go over there and help us win."
Without Brown (and Romeo Doubs, who's on IR with a shoulder injury), the Patriots' WR corps have been bare bones. DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III held down the fort until Mack Hollins (calf) could be activated off of IR. Still, getting Brown's talents and size back into the lineup can only unlock a new level of offense that the Patriots certainly need.
They got the bye week coming up after their international trip, so that will be a perfect time for some of the banged up players — including Brown — to get fully healthy for a playoff push. The Patriots are trying something different when it comes to their flight to Germany, as they're heading over one day earlier than the Patriots teams of 2023 (Frankfurt) and 2024 (London) did.
"We're going over a day early. We want to try to get work in here as much as we can get done Wednesday, walkthrough Thursday," Vrabel said. "Then maybe have a day where we're acclimated, where Friday can resemble what we feel like is a Friday practice here. In my past, I think you travel, you land and try to have a Friday practice. I don't know if that necessarily mirrors a Friday practice that we would have here. So, the hope is to try to get over there and to get acclimated enough to where we can have a good day on Friday."
With the Patriots leaving Wednesday night, that means that there isn't long for a decision on Brown to be made. We'll see if the talented wideout can try and make his highly-anticipated return to play.

title: Patriots' Stand-Still Trade Deadline Looks Worse as Many AFC Rivals Improve
full_text:
Through nine weeks in the season, the New England Patriots find themselves at 5-4 and struggling to perform against good NFL teams.
The NFL trade deadline was an opportunity for New England to put together a more competitive roster . Since that deadline has passed — meaning trades can no longer happen in the NFL until the next season begins — the Patriots will be stuck with their current roster and any players they can acquire through waivers or free agency.
New England found itself in a similar situation last year, making just two moves before the trade deadline, which was trading EDGE Keion White to San Francisco and S Kyle Dugger to Pittsburgh. Last year's roster was much healthier and in the middle of a historic win-streak, so it made sense for the Patriots not to change around the roster.
This year's Patriots team is quite the opposite. They're the most injured roster in football and have dropped two of their last three games. With challenging opponents ahead, Head coach Mike Vrabel's limited roster will have no reinforcements entering through trades.
Ultimately, New England can look at this year's trade deadline as a loss , despite not giving up anything. While the team held out from acquiring big-name trade targets, multiple AFC playoff contending teams were very active ahead of the deadline.
The move that may have the most impact on the Patriots is the Buffalo Bills acquiring S Amani Hooker from Tennessee. Potentially the biggest threat to New England's playoff status, New England's AFC East foe solved a lot of defensive issues with Hooker, who leads the league in interceptions with five.
Another AFC threat that strengthend their defense is the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Patriots, who already lost to the Jaguars in humiliating fashion, will not want to travel to Duval County in January.
Jacksonville traded for DT Jordan Davis from Philadelphia, S Jessie Bates III from Atlanta, and DT Davon Godchaux from New Orleans. Jacksonville is the biggest example of a team that saw an opportunity to compete this postseason, and acted on it — unlike New England.
Jacksonville Jaguars’ trades today: 🏈Traded a 2nd and 5th to the Falcons for S Jessie Bates. 🏈Traded a 1st and 2nd to the Eagles for DT Jordan Davis. 🏈Traded a 6th to the Saints for DT Davon Godchaux. https://t.co/dbsP3sN9kp
Another threat that got better was the Kansas City Chiefs, who acquired a player many speculated the Patriots to have interest in. Kansas City brought wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts to their roster. The Chiefs adding another deep threat for Patrick Mahomes is concerning for a Patriots defense that just let up 350+ yards passing and has to travel to Kansas City in late-December.
The Raiders, while not acquiring any new players, won at the deadline as they moved on from quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Patriots easily beat the Raiders earlier this season, but sending Cousins to Minnesota means that first overall pick Fernando Mendoza's regime has begun in Las Vegas. If Mendoza can be a productive rookie quarterback, then the Raiders pose a threat to the Patriots' potential wildcard spot, which they're currently clinging to.
Sticking in the AFC West, the Broncos upgraded their already dominant defense. They acquired linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers. The Broncos are another AFC team the Patriots will have to face late in the season, and are competing for a playoff spot.
One thing learned from Tuesday's trade deadline is that the Patriots have faith in their current roster, and faith in their players to rehab their injuries. For the second year in a row, Vrabel and Eliot Wolf invest in their current roster — we'll see if it pays off for them like it did last year.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers After Patriots Don't Make Deal During Quiet Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 4 p.m. deadline has came and went, and the New England Patriots didn't end up making a move . Mike Vrabel spoke at length about how the team would try to make any decision to better the team, but at the end of the day, they didn't end up moving the needle.
"I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren't here, to continue to improve," Vrabel said this week. "That's the focus here after nine weeks. We played some really good games, have been competitive, and then other days where it just wasn't good enough as a whole."
Instead, the 5-3 Patriots will head into this week with the same roster they've rolled out to begin the season. They'll fly to Germany tomorrow for their Week 10 battle with the Detroit Lions and then have a bye week following that. Then the playoff push begins — this time without any external additions.
Now that the trade deadline is over, let's examine which Patriots came out of it winners, and which ones came out on the losing end.
At the end of the day, this is a Patriots team that went to the Super Bowl a season ago , has dealt with a ton of injuries and feels like they're knocking on the doorstep. There really wasn't a big reason to make a giant trade, considering how they already gave up a first rounder for A.J. Brown during the summer.
Sure, the Patriots could have tried to make a move for a big name guy to help in the short term window. But when you factor in how many players are (or should be) coming back this season from IR, you'll be getting reinforcements sooner or later.
Four losses through nine weeks isn't ideal and some might have wanted the Patriots to patch that up with a new shiny player. That might not have been the best plan in the long term, considering you're already down a premier pick in 2028. Smart to stand pat and not be a prisoner of the moment.
Because the Patriots didn't end up swinging for the fences a la Derrick Henry or Jonathan Taylor, it shows that they have plenty of faith in the current running backs they have right now. Even with Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined , the Patriots aren't as internally worried about that spot than expected.
Corey Kiner (50 rushes, 244 yards, one touchdown) and Lan Larison (three rushes, 10 yards) remain on the 53-man roster, while Terrell Jennings is on the practice squad. Ideally, Stevenson's injury won't hold him out for an extended period of time, so despite the group being a bit patchwork, Kiner and Larison clearly have the team's trust .
"I think Corey is working extremely hard. I think Corey has done a really nice job," Vrabel said Monday. "But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, just like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw yesterday, for example."
Look past the turnovers . Drake Maye has kept the Patriots in most every game this season and has also led them to some impressive AFC East comebacks. He's playing at a high level when you consider the lack of true top-tier talent around him.
No one expected to be this far into the year and his core group guys heading into Week 10 are Kiner, Larison, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III, Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. You would have hoped Brown, Romeo Doubs, Stevenson and Henderson were healthy to make an impact. Nope. It's been very topsy-turvy offensively.
So at face value, adding help in some capacity for Maye could have been a smart move . Maybe an extra lineman or an additional running back to help pick up the slack. Instead, a lot of how the Patriots move forward will be on the shoulders of the 24-year-old quarterback.
The inside of the Patriots' offensive line has taken a beating nine weeks in. Mike Onwenu broke his ankle, Greg Van Roten continues to work his way off of IR, Alijah Vera-Tucker still has a few more games to go before he can be activated and Ben Brown got hurt on Sunday. Long story short, it's been a lot for the Patriots to deal with.
So it wouldn't have been surprising to see them potentially make a deal for a depth center/guard. Instead, they stood pat — seemingly placing their trust in Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor. Vera-Tucker is able to return following Week 11, but should be back before the end of the year.
When you also factor in Van Roten's potential to return, the Patriots feel comfortable where they are health-wise along the interior. It might get a bit dicey, but both Rouse and Pryor — who have started games this year at guard — should remain in the lineup this weekend.
Through nine games, Ponder has been one of the team's brightest breakout stars. The 2025 undrafted free agent leads the team with 7.5 sacks and has continued to get better each week.
The Patriots have been banged up off the edge this year, with Quintayvious Hutchins (IR) and Harold Landry (PUP) sidelined. Dre'Mont Jones has been a warrior and played through several injuries, so it's been a lot of Ponder and rookie Gabe Jacas rushing the passer.
Names like Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu and Josh Sweat have been linked to trades ahead of the deadline closing and Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer mentioned that that was a position to watch, but the Patriots didn't choose to pay up for any of them. Ponder's breakout year should continue to progress at a nice rate with the large role in front of him.
Breer also reportedly earlier this year that both Barmore and Davis, two of the veterans on this Patriots defense, were players to monitor when it came to trades. After the deadline, both of them remain on the 53-man roster.
Barmore hasn't had the most productive of seasons in a decreased role, but his talent earned him a hefty contract a few seasons back — one of the reasons why he was mentioned as a possible trade candidate. Davis also is owed a lot of money, but a knee injury on Sunday might have dampened his market.
At the end of the day, both players will remain with the Patriots for the end of the season.
Everyone wants their team to make a move, no matter how big or small. That's just the nature of being a fan of the NFL. So after the Patriots stood pat, that's not the ideal thing for a fanbase that's starting to grow restless after Sunday's loss .
Chatter for Taylor or Henry, or anyone else for that matter, continued to ramp up — especially after the Patriots remain injured beyond belief. They'll get some players back (and if A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs come back firing, cooler heads will prevail), but for now, the fanbase won't like the team's Tuesday radio silence.
We will see if the lack of moves pays off heading into the stretch run.

title: Patriots Week 9 Snap Count Analysis: Injuries, Poor Play Leads to Backups

Instead, by the end of the night, they were forced to put in a lot of backups on both sides of the ball once the 45-27 game got wildly out of hand .
"We lost, and we got our asses kicked. There's no two ways around it," Mike Vrabel said postgame. "That's what happened tonight, and I give (the Packers) credit, and also know that we can play and have to play much better. We have to play much more sound, and tackle, and affect the quarterback, and create some turnovers, and we have to find ways to be balanced offensively."
Here's a look at how the Patriots , battered, bruised and beat-up, managed their snap counts across all three phases on Sunday:

title: Patriots Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Nugget, Rumor and Deal for New England On Final Day
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline was pushed back a week this year, so the New England Patriots and 31 other teams will have until Nov. 10 to try and get deals done this season.
The Patriots , currently sitting at 5-3 and in second place in the AFC East, could end up being active on the market. Injuries across the board and potential depth issues at other places could led Eliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel to try and improve the team somehow, someway.
Aleady in this calendar year, the Patriots have made a few trades. Back in March, they shipped away Garrett Bradbury and Marte Mapu before acquiring A.J. Brown in a block buster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles three months later. During the summer, Kayshon Boutte was dealth to the Houston Texans and during roster cuts, the Patriots also sent draft picks for Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse.
So could they end up making a deal mid-season? Here's all the rumors, quotes and storylines that are surrounding the Patriots as the trade deadline looms.
The Patriots faced off against Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins in Week 5, beating the veteran 45-17 in a blowout. Now that the Raiders have traded Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, the Patriots may end up facing him again.
It's only happened seven times in NFL history that a quarterback has faced the same team twice in one year for two different teams, most recently last season (Joe Flacco played the Packers both as a member of the Browns and the Bengals). If Cousins starts against the Patriots in Week 14 on Thursday Night Football, he'll become the eighth ever.
In that Week 5 matchup, Cousins went 18-for-28 for 243 passing yards and one passing touchdown. Fernando Mendoza, who played his first NFL snaps in mop-up duty in that game, is now slated to be Las Vegas' starter under center.
Considering how banged up the Patriots' wide receiver room is, names like Brian Thomas Jr. were tossed around as potential options via trade. On Tuesday, that door was shut. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Jacksonville Jaguars won't be moving the 2024 first round pick.
This season, Thomas has slid down on the Jags' depth chart, recording just 10 receptions for 117 yards and one touchdown. The Patriots could have used his abilities to help replace the hole left by A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder). Instead, they'd need to pivot elsewhere.
One day before the trade deadline, Vrabel was asked about adding some pieces after injuries continue to hurt the Patriots. Against the Green Bay Packers , they lost Rhamondre Stevenson, Ben Brown, Brenden Schooler and Carlton Davis to injuries, along with some other players that got banged up.
Vrabel's tune the last few weeks hasn't changed when it comes to making a deal: If it helps the team, they'll think about it.
"I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren't here, to continue to improve," he said. "That's the focus here after nine weeks. We played some really good games, have been competitive, and then other days where it just wasn't good enough as a whole."
The Patriots signed Carlton Davis last year to a three-year deal, but his name has now been thrown around in deals two years in. The veteran cornerback, who's missed several games with a neck injury, could be on the move — according to SI's Albert Breer.
"This is about the age of the team and if you look at the roster big picture," Breer said . "They’ve gotten older at a lot of key spots and they aren’t exactly flush with draft capital over the next couple of years. ... They’re going to have to find a way over the next, three, four, five years to make the roster younger particularly after they pay Drake Maye. They’re trying to creatively look at this."
Davis has been the Patriots' most physical cornerback when he's healthy, but the 29-year-old is one of the older players on the roster. The Patriots could try and offload both his playing abilities and his expensive contract for a chance to get younger in the secondary.
The Patriots have a lot of money tied up to the interior of their defense line, with Milton Williams ($28.5 million) and Christian Barmore ($17.1 million) being paid very well for this season. But Barmore, who's played just 41.9% of the snaps this season, hasn't been someone that's been a consistent player so far.
According to Breer , the defensive tackle "could be had" on the trade market after falling behind Cory Durden on the depth chart. Barmore has two more years after this season on his four-year, $84 million extension he signed in 2024 before hitting the open market.
This season, the 27-year-old has six total tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble.
Could the Patriots — the team with Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve — end up adding a wideout? ESPN reported that Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs requested a trade after a pair of his teammates were shipped away on Tuesday.
Downs spent two seasons with Drake Maye at North Carolina, scoring a career-high 11 touchdowns during the 2022 season. The Patriots only have four healthy wide receivers on the active roster right now, but adding Downs for what could be a cheap deal might help elevate the passing attack.
Seven games in, Downs has 26 receptions for 307 yards.
A few days after the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears , Vrabel spoke with reporters about how the team is stacking up prior to their Week 8 game with the Miami Dolphins. One of the questions posed was about if the Patriots will be active on the phones.
His answer left the door open for a deal being made, but the head coach also didn't officially dig a potential move into the sand. Like most coach-speak, Vrabel discussed how the Patriots would make moves to try and improve the overall roster in totality, and not try to single out a certain spot that needs upgrading.
"We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team," Vrabel said. "I don't know if we will or we won't. I would imagine that we'll try to do everything that we can to help us, within reason, and makes sense for us. I don't know how you want to interpret that, but I'm sure we'll listen and talk, just like everybody else does."
Some positions that the Patriots could end up attacking are running back, offensive guard (with a myriad of injuries hitting that group), interior defensive line and some backup cornerbacks.

title: Patriots Should Be in RB Trade Market With Stevenson, Henderson Out
full_text:
Injuries have defined the first nine weeks of the New England Patriots season that's seen five wins and four losses. In the past few days, another position group suffered major losses, which is something New England will have to address.
Last week, TreVeyon Henderson took to social media to announce that he had been hospitalized with a neurological condition. While the team nor Henderson has shared how long he's expected to be out, the second-year running back is still on the Patriots active roster.
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
Additionally, a report came out Monday night that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a plantoris tendon issue in the back of his knee, meaning he'll be sidelined for several weeks — including the team's Week 10 game in Germany and their bye one week later..
That leaves New England with running backs Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, as well as Terrell Jennings on the practice squad.
Prior to the news about Henderson and Stevenson, the Patriots might have been in talks of acquiring a running back before the 4 p.m. trade deadline on Nov. 10. Now, the discussion for the Patriots to purchase a running back vamps up for a team looking to field a more competitive offense.
On Monday, Mike Vrabel spoke to repoters about the plans heading into the deadline.
"I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren't here, to continue to improve," he said.
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has brought an emergence of talented running backs not seen at a trade deadline before. The group of rushers available for teams to inquire about is much stronger than year's past, which presents a great opportunity for the Patriots to upgrade their roster ahead of the second half of the season.
The biggest name available is Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts. Taylor is an accomplished running back, who has notched four 1,000-plus yard seasons. Whatever team acquires Taylor will see an immediate impact from the seventh-year veteran.
New England has emerged as favorites for Taylor across several sports books and internet discussions. After the Colts loss to Dallas on Sunday, Taylor seemingly gave his farewells to Indianapolis in his post-game media availability.
One downside for New England is that Taylor carries an average cap hit of $17 million during the next two seasons, which will be difficult for the Patriots to afford. Taylor is also one of the most expensive players at the deadline, meaning the Patriots will have to fork up a valuable player and at least a day two pick.
#Colts RB Jonathan Taylor gave a farewell to Indianapolis and Colts fans after today’s game, in case it was his last with the organization. Don’t see this often. (🎥 @WISHNews8 ) pic.twitter.com/n4uf3C3W7f
There are much cheaper options that provide a similar —  though less — impact as Taylor. Derrick Henry is another trade candidate that Vrabel will certainly be interested in. Henry and Vrabel have ties from their time in Tennessee together, and the long-time NFL running back brings a powerful downfield attack that the Patriots offense could use.
Henry is a part of a Baltimore Ravens team that is without its starting and backup quarterbacks. They're the last place team in the AFC North and may be looking to plan for upcoming seasons under new head coach Jesse Minter.
However, a different Titans running back could be on New England's radar, as Tony Pollard presents an opportunity for the Patriots to upgrade their running back room. Pollard is on an expiring contract and has been an efficient rusher this year, on pace for over 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 12 touchdowns.
The eighth-year running back has five seasons of 1,000-plus yards and is a shifty runner with great vision. Due to Pollard's age and his rental status, New England could acquire this Titans player for a low value.
There are other options that the Patriots and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf could explore. If the team is looking for more depth or a temporary replacement while Stevenson and Henderson get healthy, there's a few names with less than $1 million remaining on their contract that could fill the position.
ELIOT WOLF HAS APPARENTLY PUT IN THE BEST OFFER FOR JONATHAN TAYLOR. 👀👀👀👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/o9W7VpMFpD
The Giants, who are currently in first place in the NFC North, have an abundance of running backs dealing with a multitude of injuries. Devin Singletary is a veteran name with a minimal contract that the Patriots could pursue.
The Jaguars, who have been very active in trade talks, may want to move on from Ameer Abdullah. There's also Isaiah Davis of the Jets, who finds himself third on New York's depth chart.
Being the most injured team in the NFL, the Patriots will look to improve several position groups ahead of the trade deadline, but it remains to be seen which areas will be most prominently addressed.

title: Patriots Must Trade for WR After Embarrassing Loss to Packers (And Here's Why)
full_text:
Just about everything went wrong for the New England Patriots on Sunday, who dropped a 45-27 game against the Green Bay Packers —  in part, due to four costly turnovers.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, the Patriots may look at other team's rosters to turn around the lack of success they've experienced the last three weeks.
On Monday, Mike Vrabel said that Sunday's performance wouldn't change how aggressive New England would be at the trade deadline, but also shared in his media availability that, "we gotta start putting ourselves in a position to start playing meaningful games in January."
Currently sitting at 5-4, the Patriots are on the brink of being a playoff team, with many challenging opponents ahead. To secure a spot playing "meaningful games in January," New England will have to find a way to revamp an injury-riddled and underperforming roster.
In Sunday's loss to Green Bay, the larger issues centered around turnovers, unsuccessful pass defense , and an inability to protect the quarterback. However, one piece of information many are forgetting to discuss is the underwhelming performances from Patriots wide receivers.
On Sunday, Drake Maye targeted his wide receivers 24 times and only completed 13 of those passes. Certain passes, like Maye's interception to Evan Williams on pass intended for Kyle Williams, were catchable balls that the receiver couldn't come down with.
Additionally, the four sacks allowed are the most the third-year quarterback has taken all season. The Packers weren't able to apply quick pressure on Maye; but rather, the pocket collapsed before any receivers could find openings.
Fox's coverage of Sunday's game pointed to multiple angles where receivers were unable to find separation from their defenders or a break in the zone defense.
Not excusing the turnovers they’re a massive issue but it’s astounding the level of difficulty Maye has on a snap to snap basis. Constant pressure, no one separating. 70% or more of the Pats explosives have gotta be Maye just making something happen
With Romeo Doubs on injured reserve for the next two weeks, and A.J. Brown struggling with a knee injury, reinforcements aren't expected to assist in creating more separation for this receiver room.
That's why one reaction from Sunday's loss could be to explore a trade for a wide receiver before the 4 p.m trade deadline on November 10.
1. Josh Downs (Indianapolis Colts)
Downs has formally requested a trade from Indianapolis , who finds itself in a position to sell as much talent as possible at the deadline.
A 2023 third round pick, Downs came out of the same North Carolina program as Maye, and has admitted that he didn't explore the transfer portal because he wanted Maye to be his quarterback.
While never a top wide receiver option in Indianapolis, Downs has been a reliable pass-catcher during his four-year NFL career. His ability to create space and be shifty downfield answers the problem the Patriots faced yesterday in having their receivers get open.
2. Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers)
The Los Angeles Chargers have reached an astonishing 0-8 record to begin the season after having a playoff bid one year ago. The Chargers are at the point of no-return with their current roster and should be looking to move on from some of their pieces.
Johnston is a striking name that many teams will have interest in at the deadline. The former first round pick is a deep-threat target that hasn't seen much production this season, scoring his first touchdown of the year in LA's most recent game.
The fourth-year player has been criticized in the past for his pass-catching ability and unreliable hands. But his separation downfield and 6-foot-2 frame creates a hopeful opportunity for Johnston to fit into New England's passing game.
3. Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars)
Another former first-round pick, Thomas' production in Jacksonville has been overshadowed by the emergence of Parker Washington as the top wide receiver option.
Jacksonville has been the biggest buyer at the deadline, making three massive trades on defense in one day. But with three newly acquired players, the Jaguars front office may look to make room for their new talent by moving on from other players.
Thomas has generated a lot of buzz across the NFL as a player that the Jaguars are looking to move. The Patriots could be in on the mix of teams calling about Thomas before the 4 p.m deadline.

title: Despite Loss, Drake Maye Passes Mac Jones in Patriots Record Books
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots spent a first round pick on a quarterback who'd don No. 10 and lead them into the playoffs early in his career. Of course, I'm talking about Mac Jones and Drake Maye.
Obviously, the careers of both those two players are vastly different in 2026, but they were linked together during the Patriots' 45-27 drubbing at the hands of the Green Bay Packers . Despite Maye's ugly showing — where he threw three interceptions — he climbed up in the franchise's all-time passing yards leaderboard.
Maye finished the game with 299 yards, pushing his total career yardage to 8,952. That put him past Jones' 8,918 and moved Maye into seventh-place in Patriots history.
Through nine games, Maye has had a season to remember (or forget, depending on the week). He's completing 65.4% of his passes and has thrown for 2,282 yards. He's scored 21 times, but turnovers continue to plague him.
The sky looked like the limit for Jones, who the Patriots selected 15th overall back in 2021. Beating out Cam Newton as a rookie, Jones led the Patriots to a winning record and a trip to the postseason after a one-year hiatus. He finished that season with 3,801 passing yards, 22 passing touchdowns and a trip to the Pro Bowl.
But his career started to unravel in the next two seasons. An ankle injury opened the door for Bailey Zappe to jump into the starting spot in 2022 and after a strong start to 2023, Jones eventually faded away into the backup job. He finished his three-year stint with New England going 864-for-1,308 for those 8,918 passing yards, 46 touchdowns, 36 interceptions. He'd be traded away to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2024 sixth round pick.
Maye can easily surge forward when it comes to his placement on that list. Jim Plunkett is one spot above him with 9,932 yards, and Tony Eason is just a little bit further out (10,732). Considering how this is just Maye's third season and he's already in the top seven, the outlook remains sunny .
It wasn't a good night for Maye, who acknowledged it postgame. After a short run on the game's opening play, Maye got impatient and hucked up a bad interception to Xavier McKinney. He'd later throw another one to McKinney in the second quarter — which came after one thrown to Evan Williams.
"They've hunted a lot of turnovers on, eyes on the quarterback, in zone coverage. And I knew that coming into it and forced the first one," Maye said. "And then like I said, they jumped some crossers ... I think the bad ones hurt more than the good ones, unfortunately."
It was Maye's second-career game with three interceptions and both have come this season against really stout defensive units. He's up to 11 on the season, the most in the league, as the Patriots teeter into an international battle with the Detroit Lions.
Considering how the first three years of Maye's career have gone, he's set to rewrite the record books on a weekly basis. He also accounted for three touchdowns for the sixth-straight game, a personal best.

title: Saints Stock Up: Audric Estimé Makes a Statement, Pass Rush Keeps Rolling
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints gave their home crowd reason to celebrate on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, clinching a thrilling 23-22 victory in overtime over the Cleveland Browns .
While improving the Saints to 3-5 and snapping a home slump, the win was far from flawless.
The result grants head coach Kellen Moore a brief reprieve, but ongoing flaws demonstrate that his standing stays uncertain.
With a tough slate ahead, New Orleans needs to fix key errors to sustain progress.
Below are the Saints players and units whose stock rose after Sunday's thrilling finish.
Despite rejoining the Saints via waivers after getting cut after training camp, running back Audric Estimé made a compelling argument for an expanded role in New Orleans' backfield despite being back in New Orleans for a week.
The second-year running back rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per attempt.
His biggest contribution came late in regulation when he powered into the end zone from 2 yards out to give New Orleans a 16-13 advantage.
Beyond the touchdown, Estimé provided the physicality and downhill running that the Saints have struggled to establish consistently.
Charlie Smyth made the most of his opportunity after he became the starter after the Saints released Daniel Carlson .
The Irish-born kicker connected on three of his four field-goal attempts against Cleveland, converting from 30, 27 and 48 yards.
With both offenses struggling to finish drives, Smyth accounted for all nine of New Orleans' points through the first three quarters.
His 48-yard field goal in the fourth quarter briefly gave the Saints a 9-6 advantage.
The Saints' pass rush continues to emerge as one of the team's biggest strengths, with Carl Granderson and Chase Young leading a pass rush that made life miserable for Cleveland quarterback Shedeur Sanders .
Granderson recorded two sacks against the Browns, extending his streak of games with multiple sacks to four. According to the Saints, he became the first NFL player since 2013 to accomplish that feat.
Young added his eighth sack of the season, while Kaden Elliss and Khristian Boyd also got into the action as New Orleans finished with five sacks.
The Saints' defensive front also made its presence felt against the run, limiting Cleveland to 95 rushing yards while consistently disrupting the Browns' offensive rhythm.
Perhaps the unit's most impressive moment came near the goal line, when New Orleans delivered a critical fourth-down stand to keep Cleveland out of the end zone.
Although the Saints' secondary remains vulnerable to explosive plays, the defensive front has become a reliable source of pressure and physicality.

title: Saints Trading DL Godchaux to Jaguars Signals Continued Youth Movement on Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints are finalizing a trade that will send veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars , another move signaling the organization's willingness to prioritize its future over veteran experience.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that New Orleans will receive a 2028 sixth-round draft pick that could become a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one through a trade or the compensatory process.
The deal comes just one day after the Saints secured a thrilling 23-22 overtime win over the Cleveland Browns , improving to 3-5.
While the trade provides New Orleans with additional draft capital, it offers little immediate financial relief.
For salary cap reasons, the Saints had restructured Godchaux's contract by converting the bulk of his pay into a signing bonus, leaving only $650,000 of his $1.3 million base salary.
As Godchaux turns 32 this week and approaches the final year of his deal, he became an expendable veteran for a team placing greater emphasis on nurturing younger talent.
New Orleans initially acquired the Plaquemine, Louisiana native from the New England Patriots in March 2025, surrendering a 2026 seventh-round pick while assuming the remaining two years and $11 million of his contract following a restructuring.
Although Godchaux appeared in all eight games this season, his role has gotten smaller and smaller by the week. Godchaux started the first five games, but hehas  played just eight, 18 and 12 defensive snaps over the last three games.
However, Godchaux still contributed to one of the Saints' biggest defensive plays Sunday, helping stop Cleveland on a critical fourth-and-goal opportunity.
The departure of Godchaux opens up substantial playing time for the Saints' younger defensive linemen, most notably Khristian Boyd and rookie second-round selection Christen Miller .
Boyd, who recorded a sack and a tackle for loss Sunday and played a key role alongside Godchaux in the goal-line stand, is expected to see an expanded workload at center of New Orleans' defensive line.
At the same time, accelerating Miller's progress becomes more urgent, especially since the rookie was a healthy scratch for the matchup against Cleveland.
Ultimately, this deal signifies more for New Orleans than just swapping a veteran player for late-round draft compensation.
It reflects a clear strategic shift by the front office to assess its youth roster while continuing to stockpile future draft assets.
How well New Orleans fills the void left by Godchaux upfront will largely hinge on whether Boyd and Miller can take full advantage of their new opportunities.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' Wild Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally gave their home crowd something to celebrate Sunday, securing a thrilling 23-22 overtime victory over the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome.
But while the Saints improved to 3-5 and snapped their home winless streak, the victory was far from pretty.
For Kellen Moore , the victory provided some much-needed relief, but it also exposed several problems that continue to plague his team and will keep him on the hot seat.
With a difficult stretch of the schedule ahead, the Saints have plenty to clean up if they want to build momentum.
Here’s a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from New Orleans' dramatic overtime victory over Cleveland.
Tyler Shough continues to show his clutch gene, even if the organization he plays for is in shambles.
Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries. While he didn’t do much for most of the game, it’s when his team needed him the most he stepped up. His composure in critical situations stood out.
Trailing 13-9 late in the fourth quarter, Shough orchestrated a 55-yard touchdown drive in just 50 seconds, highlighted by a 33-yard completion to Chris Olave that set up Audric Estimé 's 2-yard touchdown run.
After Cleveland forced overtime, Shough responded again, leading an 11-play, 74-yard touchdown drive capped by a perfectly placed 15-yard pass to ever-reliable tight end Juwan Johnson . That drive was his fifth game-winning drive of the season.
The performance was particularly encouraging, given that Shough was sacked five times and played late in the game without starting center Erik McCoy .
Estimé also provided an unexpected spark, rushing for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries just days after being claimed off waivers.
Despite scoring 23 points, the New Orleans Saints ' offense struggled again.
The Saints didn't score a touchdown until Estimé’s run with 58 seconds remaining, settling for field goals despite moving the ball effectively at times. The Saints also only converted on two of their five red zone opportunities.
Their struggles were particularly evident in the first half, when New Orleans outgained Cleveland 176-80 but entered halftime tied 3-3.
The offensive line also had its share of problems, surrendering five sacks and repeatedly forcing Shough to escape pressure.
Even with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. back, the Saints struggled to protect their quarterback consistently.
Sure, several individuals had encouraging performances, but New Orleans still lacks inspiration on offense and the ability to put opponents away.
Without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , the Saints had multiple chances to take control against Cleveland but instead needed late-game heroics.
The Saints won't always be fortunate enough to overcome those shortcomings. The Carolina Panthers are up next, but the following three games: two road games back-to-back against the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals and a home matchup against the Green Bay Packers .
If there's one area that should frustrate Kellen Moore more than anything else, it's the Saints' inability to protect the football.
New Orleans committed two costly second-quarter turnovers, both involving rookies, that completely changed the complexion of the game.
First-round pick Jordyn Tyson , making his NFL debut after missing the first seven games with a hamstring injury, fumbled near Cleveland's goal line moments after making his first career reception on the same play.
The turnover wasted a promising scoring opportunity after Shough connected with Barion Brown for a 52-yard gain.
Things somehow got worse moments later.
After the defense forced a punt, Brown fumbled the return, giving Cleveland possession at the Saints' 19-yard line.
Fortunately for New Orleans, the defense bailed out the offense and special teams, stopping Quinshon Judkins on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line.
But the mistakes weren't limited to turnovers.
The Saints' defense also surrendered a 64-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to KC Concepcion Jr. immediately after taking a 9-6 lead in the fourth quarter.
Then, after Estimé put New Orleans ahead with 58 seconds remaining, the defense allowed Cleveland to move into position for a game-tying 51-yard field goal.
And even after Shough delivered an overtime touchdown, the Saints surrendered a 39-yard touchdown reception to Harold Fannin Jr. , forcing the defense to make one final stand.
New Orleans escaped with a victory, but the combination of turnovers, blown coverage and late defensive breakdowns nearly turned a much-needed win into another devastating loss.

title: Saints Turn Snoozefest Into Thriller, Escape With Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints secured their first home victory of the season in thrilling fashion on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, defeating the Cleveland Browns 23-22 in overtime.
Quarterback Tyler Shough connected with tight end Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown pass with 4:17 remaining in the extra period, giving New Orleans a seven-point lead. Cleveland quickly countered with a touchdown drive of its own, but the Saints’ defense shut down the Browns’ potential game-winning two-point conversion attempt to seal the dramatic win.
With the victory, the Saints improved to 3-5 while snapping a frustrating home winless streak. The loss dropped the Browns to 5-4. What began as a sluggish defensive battle turned into one of the wildest finishes of the NFL season, featuring 20 fourth-quarter points and an overtime showdown after three quarters dominated by field goals.
Shough delivered an impressive performance, completing 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries.
On the other side, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders was equally stellar, throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns on 19-of-31 passing.
However, running back Audric Estime proved to be New Orleans’ secret weapon. Re-joining the team just days before kickoff after being cut following training camp, Estime provided a massive spark with 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown to open up the offense.
The game reached peak chaos late in the fourth quarter. Up 9-6, New Orleans watched Cleveland reclaim the lead on a dramatic 4-yard touchdown connection from Sanders to receiver Concepcion with 5:21 left. Sanders hit Concepcion on a deep route before the receiver cut left and sprinted into the corner of the end zone, stunning the home crowd.
Unfazed, the Saints executed a swift scoring drive that took just 50 seconds. Shough found wideout Chris Olave for a 33-yard completion to Cleveland’s 10-yard line, setting up Estime’s 2-yard touchdown run with 58 seconds remaining to put New Orleans ahead 16-13.
Cleveland answered immediately as Sanders orchestrated a quick drive into field goal range. Browns kicker Andre Szmyt drilled a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to tie the game at 16-16 and send it into overtime.
In overtime, Shough led the Saints downfield and found Johnson for a touchdown to take a 23-16 lead. Sanders responded once more, connecting with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown pass to make it 23-22.
Rather than kicking the extra point to force a possible tie, Cleveland aggressively went for two. However, a crucial holding penalty pushed the Browns back, and Sanders’ forced pass attempt fell incomplete to preserve the Saints’ victory.
The frantic second half stood in stark contrast to the opening two quarters, which ended in a 3-3 deadlock. Despite outgaining Cleveland 176-80 in total yards during the first half, the Saints struggled to finish drives due to costly mistakes.
Saints kicker Charlie Smyth opened the scoring with a 30-yard field goal midway through the first quarter after missing a 52-yard attempt earlier in the game. Szmyt answered for Cleveland with a 41-yard field goal with 10:30 remaining in the second quarter.
New Orleans had multiple opportunities to take control early. Following Szmyt’s field goal, Shough hit receiver Barion Brown for a 52-yard completion to Cleveland’s 11-yard line. However, rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson fumbled at the Browns’ 2-yard line, turning the ball over and squandering a prime scoring chance.
The Saints’ defense provided key plays to keep Cleveland contained. Linebacker Kaden Elliss executed a goal-line stand late in the second quarter, stopping Browns running back Judkins for no gain on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line to preserve the tie entering halftime. Defensive end Cameron Jordan and edge rusher Carl Granderson also recorded key sacks on Sanders during the game.

title: Postgame LIVE Reaction: Saints Win Overtime Thriller Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints win their first home game of the season with a 23-16 win over the Cleveland Browns .
Make sure to follow along for all of the reactions from head coach Kellen Moore, quarterback Tyler Shough and other players as well as you, the fans!
The New Orleans Saints (3-5) earned their first home win of the season, beating the Cleveland Browns (5-4) 23-22 in overtime at Caesars Superdome.
Saints win a wild one at home 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/eZ52EBujMt
After three field-goal-dominated quarters, the game erupted with 20 fourth-quarter points. Cleveland took a 13-9 lead on a 4-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to Concepcion with 5:21 left. New Orleans answered 50 seconds later with a 2-yard touchdown run by Audric Estime —set up by a 33-yard pass from Tyler Shough to Chris Olave . Cleveland’s Andre Szmyt hit a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to force overtime tied at 16-16.
In overtime, Shough threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson with 4:17 remaining. Cleveland responded with a 39-yard touchdown pass from Sanders to Harold Fannin Jr. , but after a holding penalty on their two-point conversion attempt, Sanders’ pass fell incomplete to secure the Saints’ victory.
Shough finished with 265 passing yards, a touchdown, and 51 rushing yards. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Estime, re-signed days before kickoff after being cut in training camp, added 72 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.
Moore: "We spent all week just talking about, hey, we're coming off a bye week. It's all going to be about response, eyes forward, moving forward, what's in front of us. And that's all you've got to focus on.
"Proud of our guys, the way they battled. Obviously, we lost the turnover battle, and that was a huge indication of where this game went, but our guys battled, and really proud of them."
Moore: "Obviously, had a few different things that we were adjusting, and so putting Will in, I thought it gave us something there.
"I thought Audric ran really hard. I thought Alvin had some really good runs in there as well. Timely runs, especially late in the game. I thought he did an excellent job of getting some dirty runs there.
"I thought our guys played a physical brand of football. We've got to sustain that, and I thought that was a good thing for our football team."
Moore: "I think there were some positives in there. Again, every week's going to be its own challenge, so we've got to continue to evolve and get better.
"But I thought the physicality in which we ran the football, downhill runs, particularly against the structure in which those guys play, I thought there were some positives there."
Moore: "Once he went to practice on Wednesday and basically recalled everything, we really had no expectation of potentially — we didn't even say he was going to be up for the game necessarily when we claimed him.
"We just brought him in, and I thought he had a couple really physical runs at Wednesday's practice. Kind of set the tone. Seemed like he knew every single assignment. He was dialed in.
"It became a no-brainer to me that, all right, let's roll. Let's get him ready to go. I thought his juice and physicality were real."
Moore: "I think he'll be a great one to ask those questions. He did break the team down about being back home.
"There's a business side of this thing that's always a challenge, and when you lose guys like Audric, you're kind of sitting there, 'Oh man, our whole team loves that guy.'
"We had an opportunity to bring him back. It was a no-brainer. I thought the way he broke that team down, it's a special locker room for him."
Moore: "It's incredible, to be honest. I don't know how many guys can do that, especially for the amount of plays that he played.
"He's a special person, special player. I think our whole locker room's fired up that he's back in there."
Moore: "Two really big drives there. Obviously, we were scoring points. We unfortunately did not handle the plus range and red zone and those sorts of things. We missed our opportunities there.
"But the two-minute drive right before the end of regulation, big plays. C.O. [Chris Olave] on the catch. Incredible throw and catch there.
"I thought Alvin had a really good route out of the backfield, and we were able to finish it in the end zone.
"Then a team comes back, they get a field goal, game's in overtime, and again, you've got to respond. You've got to reset.
"I thought our guys did a good job of just playing really clean football there. Tyler getting completions, the run game, I thought it was really good tied in together."
Moore: "I think there's an emotional stability and ability to take away all the things that happened in the past and be present in the moment.
"I think Tyler does a phenomenal job of that. I thought our team did a phenomenal job of that as the game went on.
"There's opportunities we're going to learn from. There's going to be red-zone things that obviously we want to do better and score down there because it's going to be a different game if that's the case.
"But to clean-slate it and say, 'Hey, we've got the ball with a chance to go take the lead late in the game,' that's all you can ask for.
Moore: "I think that's a potential anytime you play a team with man. They're defending players. They're not eyes on the quarterback.
"If you can get out of the pocket, you're going to have opportunities to run, and I thought Tyler did a good job of that."
Moore: "The NFL, it's tough. All these teams are talented. There's good players on every team, and you've got to compete every single opportunity you have.
"Just proud of our guys to stay with this and be resilient.
"I think that's the type of stuff you need because, again, moving forward, these games are going to continue to get challenging, and we've got to keep responding the right way.
"Just proud of the way our guys fought all the way to the end."
Moore: "Again, eyes forward. This was all our focus was. Hey, we're where we are coming out of the bye week. Let's respond the right way.
"Found a way to get this one in, and we've got more opportunities ahead of ourselves.
"We've just got to focus on the task at hand, one step at a time, and this will be a fun journey."
Moore: "Obviously, this place is special. Having a chance to play in the Caesars Superdome is always a special opportunity for our guys.
"They know that responsibility. It was awesome to feel the energy, especially late in that game.
"We're going to have another opportunity here next Sunday, and we'll just keep this thing going."
Moore: "I thought relentless effort. Make them earn it all.
"I thought the run game was a very important part of that thing.
"They were able to make some plays downfield, obviously, but I thought our pass rush was just relentless.
"I thought it was awesome by those guys. Showed up all the way to the last play of the game."
"Kaden, it's just awesome to have him back. He's a general. He leads this whole thing. His versatility is incredible.
"And then Granderson's relentlessness. Even the sacks, but even when he got Shedeur [Sanders] down on that scramble, he's going to run for a first down, and he's able to get his foot.
"He's just playing a really awesome brand of football."
Moore: "Big plays. The whole sequence, I think, not just the last play, but the sequence there.
"Again, physical football, the response, never let up. Just keep looking at the opportunity right in front of you."

"One obviously an unfortunate one where we get a penalty on a punt return opportunity, and then we got a stop there.
"That was huge by our defense because obviously we were getting the ball back, and now we had to play another hard down."

title: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will take on the Cleveland Browns at noon Sunday.
The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson .
Here are our staff predictions.
This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change.
Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints.
Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin .
Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase.
This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up.
However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis .
The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing.
This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend.
The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game.
These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no.
The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going.
This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept).
I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win.
I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too.
And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it.

title: Saints vs. Browns: 3 Things to Know About Cleveland's Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will look to get their offense back on track Sunday when they face a Cleveland Browns defense that has experienced its share of ups and downs this season.
Despite losing superstar defensive end Myles Garrett , Cleveland has remained a formidable defensive opponent, especially at generating pressure and creating turnovers.
However, the Browns have also struggled to stop the run, giving the New Orleans offense an opportunity to exploit that weakness.
For quarterback Tyler Shough and the Saints, exploiting Cleveland's weaknesses while limiting costly mistakes could be the difference between another frustrating offensive performance and a much-needed bounce-back win.
With New Orleans preparing for its first game following the bye week, here are three things to know about the Browns' defense heading into Sunday's matchup.
Cleveland made significant offseason changes, but none were bigger than trading superstar defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams.
Garrett was coming off a historic 2025 season in which he established an NFL record with 23 sacks and recorded 33 tackles for loss.
His departure, combined with defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz's resignation, raised questions about whether Cleveland could maintain its defensive identity.
However, the Browns have remained competitive defensively under first-year coach Todd Monken .
Cleveland has recorded 21 sacks through eight games, ranking ninth in the NFL, while collecting six interceptions.
Several young defensive players have also contributed, including defensive end Jared Vers e, who arrived from Los Angeles as part of the Garrett trade.
The Browns are allowing 126.9 rushing yards per game and 4.7 yards per carry, ranking among the league's bottom 10 in both categories.
Those struggles were especially apparent against Pittsburgh, which rushed for 200 yards in Sunday's victory.
That's an encouraging matchup for New Orleans, which has struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack throughout the season.
The Saints managed just 18 rushing yards in their 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh before entering their bye week.
If New Orleans can exploit Cleveland's defensive weaknesses on the ground, it could take considerable pressure off quarterback Tyler Shough and create more opportunities through the passing game.
Although Cleveland has struggled against the run, its secondary remains one of the defense's more dependable units.
The Browns are allowing 214.6 passing yards per game and have surrendered 11 passing touchdowns through eight games.
However, they have also intercepted six passes and held opposing quarterbacks to a relatively modest 6.6 yards per pass attempt.
Much of Cleveland's success in coverage begins with veteran cornerback Denzel Ward .
Ward has continued to establish himself as one of the NFL's premier coverage defenders, earning a 91.6 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, the highest among qualified cornerbacks entering Week 9.

title: Giants Seek Redemption Against Commanders, With Cam Skattebo Eager to Make Amends
full_text:
Determination has been written all over the New York Giants' faces for the past three weeks. That’s what happens when you settle for a tie against Washington and respond with a dud, losing to New Orleans in back-to-back games.
Coach John Harbaugh and his team quickly stopped what could have been the start of a slide that ruined their season. They responded with gritty road wins over Houston and Philadelphia that set up a rematch against the Commanders, building belief that they belong atop the NFC East.
Indeed, the Giants are 5-2-1 and have a three-game lead in the loss column over the rest of the division. They virtually buried the Eagles last Sunday, ending a 13-game losing streak at the Linc. And this came after they upset a revived Texans team in overtime.
But few may be looking forward to Thursday night’s home game more than running back Cam Skattebo, who fumbled away the ball at the Washington 24 with two minutes left during their 27-27 tie in Week 5. The miscue cut his playing time against New Orleans.
He received six snaps without any touches vs. the Saints before exploding for a career-high 124 yards on 17 carries against the Texans. He capped his outing with a 42-yard overtime jaunt into Houston territory, running so hard that he injured his hamstring and was forced to sit out the Eagles game.
“Obviously, we had that one-week hiccup where I got in trouble. That was it. I came back that next week and handled business,” Skattebo said this week. “They [the coaches] know what I’m capable of. They know what I can do.
“When I come out, and I’m ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that.”
Giants receiver Malik Nabers stood out in their first meeting, posting 11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown on a career-high 20 targets.
“We want to go 1-0, but this game is more than 1-0. It’s [almost like] 2-0, just because the last game ended in a tie that we should have had. So, both of us are fighting to get this game.”
The forecast calls for a nasty storm, much stronger than the heavy mist that may have affected Dominic Zvada’s three missed field goals, including what would have been the winner in overtime, at Washington.

title: J.J. McCarthy Gets Ready for His First Home Start With the Giants
full_text:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy has enjoyed a fresh start since arriving in East Rutherford five weeks ago.
It started with the former No. 10 pick adjusting to a whole new playbook after he was traded from Minnesota, albeit one the team believed would suit his skill set better than it did Jameis Winston’s. Winston had taken over as the starter after Jaxson Dart went down for the season with a knee injury in Week 2.
With Winston unable to push the Giants over the finish line in close games against the Commanders and Saints, calls for McCarthy to step in grew louder, and head coach John Harbaugh moved to see where the young signal caller’s progress in his Matt Nagy crash course stood.
In 11 minutes during the Saints game, McCarthy almost did the unthinkable, carrying the Giants’ offense back from a 34-10 deficit with 243 passing yards and one touchdown pass, only to fall one more six-point conversion short of completing the ultimate comeback.
The effort was enough to convince Harbaugh to hand the reins to McCarthy, who has since rewarded his coach’s trust with a 2-0 record as the starter, thanks to two impressive road wins over the Texans and Eagles that have the Giants running away with the NFC East lead at 5-2-1.
Now, on a short week with the Washington Commanders on deck for a rematch at MetLife Stadium on Thursday night, the 23-year-old McCarthy aims for 3-0 in his first full home game as the Giants’ starter.
“I haven’t thought about it until now, but I’m just so blessed to be a part of this team,” McCarthy said.
“I say it over and over again, and I just can’t thank the Giants organization and the fanbase for welcoming me. At the end of the day, I’m running out there to do my job at a high level and get a win on Thursday night.”
When the Giants needed another gunslinger, it didn’t take long for them to go after McCarthy, whose time with the Vikings hadn’t met the expectations that followed him out of college.
It helped that Harbaugh got a glowing endorsement from his brother, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, who had coached McCarthy at the University of Michigan, where the duo captured the school’s 12th national championship in 2023.
Unfortunately, the quarterback’s first foray into the pros wouldn’t match that success, as McCarthy missed seven games during his rookie season with the Vikings due to multiple injuries. He finished with 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.
Still, Harbaugh and the Giants found enough reason to trade a fifth-round pick to Minnesota in hopes of more security at quarterback as they aimed to remain competitive.
For both parties, the move has more than paid off. In two starts, McCarthy has been throwing it around the yard, completing 67.3% of his passes for 389 yards while adding 23 yards on the ground, giving the Giants’ offense an extra threat that has forced opposing defenses to account for him in both phases.
The lone blemish on his early résumé has been the lack of a passing touchdown, with the only six-point toss coming from Winston’s arm during the win over Philadelphia.
McCarthy will have another chance to notch that first one on Thursday, with support from the home crowd that went wild during his epic rally against New Orleans the last time they saw him play.
“You have to,” McCarthy said. “To really let go of those emotions, you have to accept them, let them be, and then let them go. Just being able to be real with yourself and realize they’re human emotions, it’s completely natural.
“That’s when you can let them go and move past them as quickly as possible. If you try to avoid them and resist them, then they tend to linger.”
Putting on a game face amid all the pomp and circumstance that will engulf MetLife Stadium is only half of the challenge for McCarthy as he braces for his first home start.
The other half is the fact that it is coming on a short week and just days after he took a bit of a bruising against the Eagles, including a moment where he looked to be in intense pain as he tried to toss a few practice throws along the sidelines during the Giants’ third-quarter touchdown drive led by Winston.
McCarthy returned to the game and pushed the Giants into field goal range on two succeeding drives to seal a huge 19-11 win over their division rivals. He credits the team’s medical staff for helping him get back on his feet and has no concerns about giving his all against the Commanders.
“I feel really good,” McCarthy added. “Obviously, Sunday, it’s football, it’s a physical game, but just credit to the athletic training staff for getting me back to feeling really good as quickly as possible.”
With his health improving, the rest of the time leading up to his first home start is purely about preparation and nailing the details that will help New York get a third consecutive win and maintain their strong record in the division.
“Obviously, it’s about the preparation and knowing your stuff over everything. It’s really nice to have a division opponent, especially [Commanders defensive coordinator] Daronte [Jones],” McCarthy said.
“I have so much respect for him, and just being with him in Minnesota in the past and seeing what he’s doing with these guys, it’s really cool, and just being able to really hone in on the game plan is the number one thing.
“But at the end of the day, it’s getting the body turned over and just going out there and playing fundamentally sound (blocking, throwing, catching, all the things that move the football down the field), and that’s really what we’re focused on.”

title: Arvell Reese Earns NFC Defensive Player of the Week Honors After Historic Game
full_text:
To no one’s surprise, New York Giants rookie linebacker Arvell Reese has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week.
Reese had himself a day last week in the Giants’ 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. The former Ohio State star recorded a team-leading 12 tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble.
At 21 years and 70 days of age, Reese, who is already in the discussion for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, became the youngest player in NFL history (surpassing Vernon Maxwell, 21 years and 321 days on Sept. 11, 1983 with the Baltimore Colts) to register at least three sacks in a single game since sacks became an official statistic in 1982.
Reese is also just the second Giants rookie since B.J. Hill on Dec. 2, 2018, vs. Chicago to register three sacks in a single game and is the first NFC rookie to accomplish the feat since James Houston did so on Jan. 1, 2023 with Detroit.
He is also the only rookie to have a game with at least 10 tackles and three sacks since 1994, when tackles first became an official stat. Since then, only four players overall have achieved that stat line.
This season, Reese has 66 total tackles (47 solo), eight tackles for loss, five quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, four passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.
His 47 solo tackles are tied for the second-most in the NFL and lead all rookies.
This is Reese’s first-career Defensive Player of the Week award. He becomes the third Giants rookie linebacker to earn the honor, joining Devon Kennard (Week 14, 2014) and Kayvon Thibodeaux (Week 15, 2022).
Reese also becomes the fourth former Ohio State player, and second linebacker, to win a Defensive Player of the Week award as a rookie, joining Nick Bosa (two-time winner), Dre’Mont Jones (Week 16, 2019), and Sonny Styles (Week 3, 2026).
Reese becomes the second member of the Giants defense to win POTW honors, joining cornerback Deonte Banks, who won the award in Week 4.
Safety Jevon Holland was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Month for September. More recently, Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers was named Offensive Player of the Month for October.
The Giants host the Washington Commanders on Thursday night.

title: Why the Giants’ Quiet Trade Deadline Was a Sign of Strength
full_text:
With the dust having settled on yesterday’s NFL trade activity, the biggest takeaway from what the New York Giants did and didn’t do is that head coach John Harbaugh, general manager Joe Schoen, and the rest of the team’s braintrust are rooted in reality.
There were no illusions by the brass regarding the state of the roster, which, while overall solid, undoubtedly could have benefitted from reinforcements at running back and defensive tackle, not just for this year but for the future, when players currently on the team at both positions will hit free agency.
This resulted in no panic moves and no blinking first. As tempting as it might have been to cave to the Indianapolis Colts’ reported demands for more than the second- and fifth-round draft picks the Giants were said to be offering for running back Jonathan Taylor, New York held firm, realizing that as good as Taylor is, there will be other options to pursue.
In the meantime, the group they currently have (Cam Skattebo, Gregory Desrosiers, and Devin Singletary, who are on the roster at the moment, and Tyrone Tracy Jr., who has another three weeks to go before he’s eligible to come off IR) should be able to carry them through the remainder of the season.
The same can probably be said of the defensive tackle group, where, of late, the Giants have gotten much more solid play from Darius Alexander, while youngster Bobby Jamison-Travis has started to make plays regularly.
While the Giants didn’t get anything done at the deadline, and it wasn’t due to a lack of trying, their biggest acquisition came back in September when they picked up young quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round pick.
McCarthy, who in Week 7 took over the starting quarterback role from Jameis Winston (who was thrust into the starting role following the season-ending knee injury suffered by Jaxson Dart seven snaps into Week 2), has played well enough to keep the Giants afloat, with McCarthy proving to be this year’s feel-good story as he seeks to resurrect a career that stalled out in Minnesota.
And while this is not to say that the Giants’ season was in jeopardy of slipping away with Winston at the offense’s controls, the threat of McCarthy’s mobility has forced opposing defenses to account for him as a runner.
From a bigger-picture perspective, the offense under McCarthy has been more productive. Since taking over in Week 7, the Giants have a +14-point differential in their games, tied for 13th best in the NFL.
By contrast, with Winston at the helm, the Giants had a +10-point differential over Weeks 3–6 (we are tossing out Week 2, when he had to step in for Dart and the game plan was clearly not tailored to Winston’s strengths).
No roster is ever fully complete in the NFL. But the Giants, keeping their feet on the ground, struck a nice balance between having faith in what they have for the short and long term and saving valuable draft assets to reinforce what needs reinforcing moving forward.
In other words, after several false starts brought on by a major misjudgment of the roster’s talent following the surprising 2022 season and then the turnover of the coaching staff, things are finally heading in the right direction thanks to the Schoen-Harbaugh team.

title: Giants' Grade Out Well After Standing Pat at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The New York Giants put themselves out there ahead of the NFL trade deadline , perhaps even more so than their current Super Bowl prospects warrant. They took their fishing pole to the big pond and tried to reel in a marlin on offense and defense.
Once John Harbaugh’s pursuits of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and running back Jonathan Taylor went awry, there seemed to be no other star players the Giants could realistically acquire. But they could have done something.
The clock struck 4 p.m., and there were no deals to report. New York didn’t even snag a low-cost option to fortify a thin interior defensive line or a banged-up, largely inefficient backfield.
The Giants were reportedly willing to give a second-round draft pick and more for Taylor before the Indianapolis Colts refused, causing the Giants to withdraw the offer .
In the end, the Giants wisely avoided a massive overpay and exercised some good old-fashioned common sense.
Given their first-place standing in the NFC East, Big Blue could have felt incentivized to go all in and win the deadline. The cost was too high, however. The San Francisco 49ers and the entire NFC North appear to pose serious threats, and New York is still repairing its culture and remembering how to be a competent franchise.
Spoiling that mission with trigger-happy trade tendencies would have been irresponsible. But not making any moves after the J.J. McCarthy acquisition also feels a bit risky.
The Giants did not have a fourth- or fifth-round pick in their 2027 draft class to include in a trade, but they do own two sixth-round picks. That wasn’t enough to free even a lesser player buried on another team’s depth chart who could have bolstered the Giants’ depth at a position of need.
And so, with the Giants not having addressed running back or defensive tackle, they will lean heavily on what they have at both positions, hoping it will be enough to get them into the postseason and keep them there for a while.
The good news is that running back Cam Skattebo, who erupted in Houston before suffering a hamstring injury in overtime, is ready to roll against the Commanders.
Defensively, defensive tackle Darius Alexander recorded the game-ending sack last Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, and rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis is progressing quite nicely. So perhaps the Giants feel they can get by with that arrangement.
Harbaugh’s talent evaluation and leadership skills have paid dividends so far. He deserves fans’ trust.
There is an old saying that the best trades are the ones that don’t get made. So if we look back and include the trade for J.J. McCarthy in our analysis, the Giants come out of this year’s trade cycle with a solid B grade for landing a reclamation project that is already paying dividends.
