title: Giants’ Third Straight Power Rankings Jump Sets Up a Real Test
full_text:
The New York Giants returned from their bye week and picked up where they left off in the win column, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles 19-11 on Sunday. It was their first victory at Lincoln Financial Field in 13 years and improved their record to 5-2-1 overall.
The long-awaited result kicked off a huge week for Big Blue, which not only unofficially knocked its rivals out of NFC East contention but also delivered a massive performance from Dennard Wilson’s tireless pass rush.
As a result, SI senior writer Conor Orr gave New York its third elevation in as many weeks, lifting Harbaugh’s group to one spot shy of the league’s 10 best teams in his latest MMQB NFL power rankings poll ahead of a short Week 10.
“The Giants soar up the Power Rankings not just because of a gritty win over the Eagles, but because John Harbaugh seems prepared to move heaven and earth to trade for someone—anyone—at the deadline,” Orr said. “And he will call your manager.”
Orr, of course, was referring to Harbaugh’s gutsy move to call Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about their now-former defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Giants didn’t make any trades at the deadline, with Harbaugh telling reporters that any such move would have needed to fit in terms of player and cost.
That said, because they didn’t make any trades on deadline day (they did trade for quarterback J.J. McCarthy well before the deadline), New York is ready to buckle up and forge ahead with what it has. That starts with Thursday night’s home game against Washington. A win would be the Giants’ first over the Commanders since 2023 and would ensure they bury another division opponent.
After that, the real test of the Giants’ mettle begins. They’ll face opponents with winning records in four of their next five games, starting with a Week 11 home date against Jacksonville that has already been flexed to national TV.
After a game against old friend Daniel Jones and the flailing Colts, the Giants have San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland and Detroit on deck.
How the Giants fare in those games against opponents they would likely face in the postseason will reveal a lot about whether they deserve continued promotion in the weekly power rankings or begin a descent back toward the bottom.

title: Malik Nabers Doubles Down on Defense of Body Language: “I’m an Ultimate Competitor”
full_text:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers is going to have his good games and an occasional bad game once in a while, but the last thing he wants to be known as is a bad teammate.
The Giants’ 19-11 road win over the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday was far from a perfect one for Nabers, who was targeted a team-high eight times but caught only five passes for 43 yards and dropped a beautifully placed ball from J.J. McCarthy that would have given him his third touchdown of the season.
It was a frustrating change of pace after the LSU product had rattled off four consecutive 100-yard games, matching a franchise record, including two contests in which he was targeted at least 15 times and caught double-digit passes.
As the Giants offense’s struggles to move the football against Philadelphia’s aggressive pass rush stretched into the middle of the fourth quarter, that frustration appeared to follow Nabers to the sideline, where the FOX broadcast cameras took notice.
The moment went viral when analyst and former NFL tight end Greg Olsen and broadcast partner Joe Davis questioned Nabers’ body language and sideline demeanor during the Giants’ game in Philadelphia.
That prompted Nabers to respond on social media to what he perceived as Olsen’s depiction of him as a bad teammate during the win.
The receiver doubled down on his defense in front of the media scrum on Tuesday.
“As far as speaking about who I was intending the message to be received by, I think I said all I wanted to say,” Nabers said regarding his Instagram story.
“I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. I’ve never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of, so I would implement that too because I couldn’t speak up for myself during the game when these things were said about me.”
Olsen also took to social media to push back on the idea that he viewed Nabers as a bad teammate.
Despite Nabers’ costly drop, the Giants built a large enough lead over the Eagles in the second half thanks to a 14-play drive led by Jameis Winston, who replaced McCarthy shortly after the starter took a huge hit to his right side while running with the football. The drive ended in a wide-open connection to Isaiah Likely for the team’s lone touchdown.
Beyond that impressive possession, the Giants’ passing game was held to 198 total yards, with no receiver tallying more than 54 yards on the day, which ended Nabers’ streak of four games with 100-plus receiving yards. New York also had six drives stall in under three plays, leaving the rest of the scoring to Dominic Zvada, who went four-for-four on long-distance field goal attempts.
Even when the Giants’ first win inside Lincoln Financial Field in 13 years seemed imminent, Nabers wanted to see more from his teammates to keep their winning momentum going at a critical point in the season, as they aim to capture their first NFC East title since 2011.
He offered reassurance that his mood on the sideline wasn’t about being dissatisfied with an inability to get more touches, but rather that neither he nor the rest of the offense fully capitalized on the opportunities the defense was providing to stack the scoreboard.
“My body language is the same all the time,” Nabers added. “Whether I’m having a good game, bad game, losing, winning. You can go to the games, and you can see it for yourself if you want to go look.
“But as far as the bad body language and things being said that I was saying on the sideline, especially from people that’s watching the game, they don’t know what’s going on down on the field, what is being said. You don’t know if I’m mad, you don’t know if I’m not.
“I’m an ultimate competitor, whether it’s going well or if it’s going bad. If I make a play, my body language is I’m a mean guy, raging, slapping my helmet, screaming, never really smiling, but that’s just how I play the game of football.”
Nabers is still an important part of the Giants’ offense, and there should be no doubt he will shake off his bad outing and the unwanted controversy it has attracted to help New York rebound quickly in an impending rematch with the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium on Thursday night.

title: Breaking Down Jets’ Injury Report Coming Into Week 10 (Who’s Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Bills)
full_text:
The Jets extended their losing streak to four with Sunday’s 35-12 loss to the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium.
While there were few positives to take away from the team’s disappointing performance, one was that New York left Arrowhead Stadium without suffering any significant injuries. Gang Green has constantly had to deal with key players missing time, which has played a small part in the team’s disappointing season.
With that said, let’s take a look at the Jets’ injuries heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Bills.
One reason the Jets struggled against Kansas City was that they were without star receiver Garrett Wilson. The five-year veteran was placed in the concussion protocol after taking a hit to the head on the second-to-last play of New York’s Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Without Wilson, the Jets’ offense had little success through the air, as the other receivers couldn’t consistently create separation. Although Omar Cooper Jr. recorded a season-high eight receptions on nine targets, the majority of them came on screen passes.
ESPN’s Rich Cimini reported earlier Wednesday that Wilson returned to practice , although he was limited. While this doesn’t guarantee Wilson will play on Sunday against the Bills, it’s a positive update on his recovery.
It’s been a really disappointing year for Joseph Ossai, and injuries have played a large role. A ruptured plantar fascia forced him to miss the first two games. Then an ankle sprain in Week 5’s win against the Browns sidelined him for the last four weeks.
Although Ossai missed last week’s game against Kansas City, he practiced with the team in a limited role leading up to the game, which suggests he’s close to returning. If he can be a full participant in either Thursday's or Friday’s practice, we should expect him to suit up against Buffalo.
But Ossai will have to step up, as he’s been extremely underwhelming in limited action. In just three games (107 defensive snaps), Ossai has recorded nine total tackles and zero pressures, earning a career-low 50.9 pass-rush grade and 54.3 run-defense grade , per Pro Football Focus .
New York must hope that Ossai can turn things around if he returns this week, as the Bills’ offensive line has allowed just 17 sacks.
With Andre Cisco traded to the Lions on Monday, it’s opened an opportunity for VJ Payne to fill his role as the Jets’ backup safety behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick.
The 2026 sixth-round selection, who had been on injured reserve with a significant bone bruise since Aug. 30, opened his 21-day practice window last Wednesday and was a full participant in the team’s three practices.
The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt reported that Payne was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, suggesting he is trending toward making his NFL debut against Buffalo. However, New York must officially activate him to the 53-man roster before he’s eligible to play in Sunday’s matchup.
Harrison Phillips won’t practice today. Omar Cooper, Joe Ossai, Garrett Wilson and Nahshon Wright are all limited. VJ Payne will be a full participant.
If he does play, we should expect to see him primarily on special teams, considering the Jets have leaned on Belton and Fitzpatrick at safety. Payne could potentially earn a rotational role as the season progresses if New York keeps losing.
Missing last Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with an ankle injury, Harrison Phillips was trending towards being ruled out for last week’s matchup against the Chiefs. However, he was a full participant in Friday’s practice and ultimately suited up in Week 9, recording one total tackle in a season-low 27 snaps.
According to Jets website reporter Eric Allen, Phillips did not participate in Wednesday’s walk-through . While this doesn’t rule him out for Sunday’s game, it suggests he’s still dealing with the injury. If he logs another full participation on Friday, there’s a good chance he plays.
The only other player to miss Wednesday’s walk-through was Trevin Wallace, who’s dealing with a groin injury. Wallace was a limited participant in last Wednesday’s practice, but didn’t participate in the following two practices and was ultimately ruled out for the team’s matchup against Kansas City.
The 23-year-old has been a critical member of New York’s special teams, logging three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade. With no clear timeline for his return, we should expect the team to be cautious and ease his workload in practice before clearing him to suit up.
David Onyemata was placed on injured reserve after suffering a groin injury in Week 2’s loss to the Packers. The 11-year veteran underwent core muscle surgery and wasn’t initially expected to return until December, but Rosenblatt reported last Friday that Onyemata was at practice working with trainers.
While this is an encouraging step in his recovery, it doesn’t mean he’s close to playing. He’ll have to clear some hurdles before New York inserts him back into the lineup. Fourth-round selection Darrell Jackson Jr. has done well in his absence and has flashed potential to become a key rotational player.
The Jets have a long list of players on the injured reserve.
Kingsley Jonathan, Kiko Mauigoa (quad), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Max Mitchell (head/concussion) and T’Vondre Sweat (knee) are all candidates to return this season.
However, we won’t get to see Braiden McGregor (torn pectoral), Arian Smith (torn ACL), and Chip Trayanum (neck) for the rest of the year.

title: Kenyon Sadiq Needs to Be Jets' X-Factor to Help Upset the Bills in Week 10
full_text:
Following a quiet trade deadline that only saw the Jets trade safety Andre Cisco to the Lions and keep the rest of their roster intact, it is time for Gang Green to turn its attention to the second half of the season and make some improvements on the field after a 2-7 start.
Despite the lack of movement ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, it was not entirely bad, as the doors opened for some on the roster amid the missed opportunities . Still, that does not account for the poor coaching that has been the prevailing theme each week and the lack of execution on the field over the course of a full game.
As the Jets take a four-game losing streak into Sunday's home tilt against the 7-1 Bills at MetLife Stadium, head coach Aaron Glenn's 0-8 record against divisional opponents will once again be a talking point. That said, any chance the Jets have of competing in this game and having a shot to pull off the upset could reside on the shoulders of rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq.
While Sadiq has struggled to receive a consistent amount of targets each week since his breakout Week 3 performance when he went off for seven catches, 105 yards and a TD against the Lions, he is coming off his best game since then in the Week 9 loss to the Chiefs when he came down with four receptions for 49 yards.
That is nowhere near the level of performance expected of the talented and athletic TE, but it is important for him to keep his foot on the gas to help the Jets beat the Bills and pull off the stunner.
Granted, the Jets were without WR1 Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell had zero catches on seven targets against the Chiefs, so the pass game was essentially nonexistent in the Week 9 loss. That said, Sadiq stepped up when nobody else did, aside from rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (eight catches, 58 yards), and showed that he has still not lost a step amid a crowded receiving room.
There is no denying the freakish athleticism that the No. 16 pick out of Oregon brings to this team and the fact that he was the first offensive player the Jets drafted back in April. If anything, his inconsistent lack of usage has more to do with the coaching staff's lack of creativity in distributing the ball to him and getting each of their playmakers involved each week.
Despite that, Sadiq still has 21 catches (on 31 targets) for 235 yards and one receiving TD, plus a three-yard TD run in the season opener that showcased his versatility in both the pass game and as a physical runner. Simply put, he has shown some bright spots as part of a talented 2026 draft class and his numbers should be even greater if more opportunities were coming his way.
Kenyon Sadiq makin it look easy 📺: #NYJvsKC on @NFLonCBS | @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/VzYXDSx5VU
At the same time, Sadiq has to cut back on his penalties. He was called for a false start in Chiefs' territory on the opening drive of last Sunday's game and was flagged for a facemask penalty on a second-and-five with 53 seconds left in the first half, which negated a seven-yard run from Breece Hall and ultimately led to a missed 53-yard field goal by kicker Jason Sanders.
There are still some growing pains and areas that need to be corrected for the immensely talented TE , but he appeared to get back on track against the Chiefs and showed why he could be key to the team's success going forward when he is more involved and the mistakes are limited.
While a lot of the attention on the Bills has been on their league-leading scoring offense (32 ppg) and the MVP-caliber play from QB Josh Allen, the Buffalo defense ranks in the bottom half of the league in points allowed and gives up the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8 ypg).
Furthermore, the Bills are allowing the sixth-most yards to TEs and 11.2 yards per catch to the position this season, so this could be an opportunity to capitalize on for a player who is plenty capable of taking advantage. Although Pro Football Focus only gives him the 27th-ranked overall grade (64.3) out of 37 qualified TEs, he has been efficient in picking up yards after the catch and could make the Bills' secondary pay on Sunday.
In Buffalo's last road game, the Bills' secondary allowed a combined 11 catches for 165 receiving yards to Raiders TEs Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer. Perhaps Sadiq and Mason Taylor could have similar success.
While the recently acquired Amani Hooker, who is tied for the league lead in interceptions (five), could give the Bills a boost, Sadiq could be the true difference-maker for the Jets this week. A lot will depend on Wilson's status and how the Jets continue to use Taylor, but if the targets do come his way, Sadiq will need to attack the Bills downfield and wear them down with his sheer athleticism.

title: 3 Jets Likely Leaving in the 2027 Offseason Despite Surviving Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Jets were quiet during the trade deadline compared to years past. The Jets were involved in only one deal despite their 2-7 record. Making only one move has left them with many roster questions that may be answered come the offseason.
Gang Green will look much different going into 2027. They already have 22 players on expiring contracts and a player requesting a trade. As the organization plans for next season, here are three Jets who likely will not be a part of those plans, regardless of their current place on the roster.
The Nahshon Wright experiment has been a failure . The Jets signed the 28-year-old to a one-year, $3.5 million contract after the corner led his position in interceptions in 2025. That success has not followed Wright to Florham Park.
The veteran corner has yet to take a snap for New York . Someone who was supposed to be a game-changer in the secondary has not stepped onto the field for the team. Wright is clearly not in the Jets' plans currently or in the future. While it's surprising not to see him moved at the deadline, the former Bear will likely be a one-season unused rental for New York.
Wright is clearly not a part of head coach Aaron Glenn's plan, and it is hard to believe he would re-sign with a team that didn't let him see the field all season. Wright is coming off the best season of his career; he isn't looking to fade into anonymity in New York.
Even though he wasn't traded, the Jets can expect Wright to be one of the first out the door come the offseason.
Geno Smith was a surprise deadline opportunity when teams started looking for a quarterback. It was always unlikely to see him traded, but the fact that it gained traction shows what trajectory the veteran is on. As the season progresses, it seems increasingly possible that Smith won't be a Jet come 2027.
Smith has been sufficient at QB, but he isn't the long-term answer New York needs. The signal caller is 36, and it's not like the Jets are winning games because of him. The Jets have been looking for a franchise player at the position since before he was on the team the first time, and the second time around, he is still unfortunately not that guy.
New York already has a rookie sitting behind Smith, Cade Klubnik, whom they drafted in the fourth round. As the Jets continue to lose, calls will get louder for Klubnik to get his shot . That doesn't bode well for Smith. Either Klubnik is good, and the Jets roll with the rookie, or he isn't, and the team looks to draft a first-round QB in the upcoming draft.
Either way, it looks like the Jets will be going in a different direction come 2027.
Will McDonald IV's contract isn't out after this year, but the defensive end requested a trade that wasn't granted . He's disgruntled with his role on the Jets, but the team declined to fulfill his request. However, the road to a happy McDonald come 2027 seems more treacherous than the one to a trade.
New York has three first-round picks, which all currently sit in the top 13. It is hard to believe that one of those won't be used on an edge rusher. McDonald is upset about playing time and usage; it seems those issues will only grow as New York continues to rebuild.
McDonald could be on his way out if the Jets are to use a high-value pick on the edge. Holding the former first-rounder hostage for two more years as a second-choice edge rusher just wouldn't be smart. It may not have happened at the deadline, but it would be surprising to see McDonald in Gotham green come 2027.
Barring a change of heart, McDonald looks to be on his way out of New York.

title: What the Jets' Inactive Trade Deadline Says About Their Plans for 2027
full_text:
The Jets stood pat during the trade deadline on Tuesday . It shouldn't come as a surprise, considering head coach Aaron Glenn announced as much following their loss to the Chiefs.
Aaron Glenn on tomorrow's trade deadline: "Never say never, but right now I know we're going to stand pat. Listen, we're in the business of keeping good players. That's how I see it...But you never know what's going to happen." #Jets
But as countless trades poured in over the wire, New York's inactivity, particularly pertaining to several players on expiring deals, left some confused. They didn't trade edge rusher Will McDonald despite a reported trade request; they didn't move Nahshon Wright or Jarvis Brownlee, and watched as other struggling teams moved off key players.
Gang Green's actions were clear. They wanted to keep as much of the talent on the roster to give Glenn the best chance to keep his job.
But is it really that simple? Does failing to trade McDonald actually hurt the Jets' chances beyond 2026?
Many Jets fans were frustrated with the team's lack of moves on Tuesday. But their frustration ignores the reality that the team had been living with over the last several months. Owner Woody Johnson wants Glenn to succeed. Because of that, he wants to give him as much talent as possible.
That means keeping players who are helpful role pieces or borderline starters.
Despite a 2-7 start, the Jets are more comfortable keeping their already heavy treasure trove of draft picks—including three first-rounders in the 2027 draft. In their eyes, Glenn still has eight games remaining to show he's capable of being kept on for a third year.
But the record and on field problems tell a different story.
Few coaches in NFL history have had as bad a start to their careers as Glenn has with New York. He's 5-21 in his first 26 games, has yet to win a division contest, and has few answers for how to fix the problems New York has. Before he was first hired, Glenn was known as someone who could build a great staff full of competent coaches around him, but after dismantling his first failed staff, his second has shown little improvement. If the team continues to lose this season, there can be no argument that Glenn has failed to earn a third season with the team.
The caveat here is that while the Jets are trying to win with Glenn, their inability to do so has shown it doesn't matter how much talent they have. But their push also means a few more things we'll get to.
Many Jets fans have drawn their ire not just at Glenn but also at general manager Darren Mougey for the team's lack of a sell-off as the Colts and Eagles have previously done.
In their minds, Mougey not making a deal is a sign that he and Glenn are a package deal. If Glenn ends up being fired, Mougey's mistakes shouldn't absolve him either.
But that couldn't be further from the truth.
There are several reasons the Jets failed to make any trades at the deadline. Ownership could have voiced their opinions to push one final time behind Glenn, and players may have requested that they still try to openly compete. A general manager has to weigh all of that together when making decisions.
In the case of Will McDonald, for example, New York Post 's Brian Costello reported  that the Jets had offers for as high as a second-round pick . McDonald has a trade request out and played under 50% of the snaps last week in Kansas City. So why didn't Mougey make a move?
What if he did and the Jets' front office opted not to move him? What if Mougey believes in McDonald's abilities as a pass rusher and is willing to keep him on the roster for the team's next head coach? If McDonald is a scheme liability under Glenn, could the Jets hire a coordinator with a 4-3 background who incorporates the wide-nine approach? All of a sudden, McDonald could be seen as an important piece again.
The idea that Mougey failed at the deadline is a farce. New York is set up for success now just as much as they were last week. Trades for later picks would have done nothing to change that.
If anything, the lack of moves shows the Jets still value Glenn's input on the roster, and it is as much a 50-50 split with Mougey as once originally thought. Should the team continue to bottom out, Mougey will have plenty more to point to as a way to show he should be given more responsibility over the roster and the head coach.
Here's what many people forget:
The Jets are a bad football team. They will remain a bad football team even after the trade deadline . While it would've been nice to ship off players on expiring deals, the team still has plenty of cap space and three first-round picks—more than enough ammo to entice a strong coach and come away with impact players to alter the team's fortune.
New York's desired defense of Glenn should also matter little to the fanbase at this point. The coach has proven himself incapable of putting a team in a position to win football games; the best way forward for the team to actually lose for the remainder of the season is to keep everything the way it is, however harsh or realistic that may be.
By the end of the year, it's expected that the Jets will move on from Glenn and his coaching staff. Mougey will have an opportunity to bring in a coach who fits his vision for the roster. The trade deadline will mean very little when it comes to these outcomes.
Especially with the Colts (the team the Jets own the first-round pick of) already selling off key starters across both sides of the ball.

title: Jets Winners & Losers After the Trade Deadline: Doors Open Amid Missed Opportunities
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has officially passed , and while the Jaguars and Vikings made some big moves and the Colts continued to clean house, the Jets remained quiet and kept their roster mostly intact despite a frustrating 2-7 start to the season.
Even though players like Harrison Phillips, Will McDonald IV and Jarvis Brownlee Jr. were on the list of those who could be traded, safety Andre Cisco was the only Jet let go, as he was acquired by the Lions . While that did not come as much of a surprise given his diminished role and expiring contract, it was a little shocking to see the rest of the roster go unchanged amid a four-game losing streak.
Coming off their latest blunder against the Chiefs in a 35-12 loss , it is now or never for the Jets to show what they've got at the season's midway point. With that in mind, here are the biggest winners and losers following the trade deadline.
Although Moore has primarily played on special teams this season and has been productive in that role with eight tackles, he has only played nine defensive snaps in eight games and has clearly taken on a reduced role due to the additions of Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton.
Combine that with Cisco also being on the roster until he was traded, and Moore essentially became an afterthought in the secondary despite recording the second-most tackles on the team during his rookie season (101). While Cisco's departure could also open the door for rookie VJ Payne to get some opportunities after starting the season on injured reserve due to a bone bruise in his knee, Moore is in line to be the direct backup behind Belton and Fitzpatrick.
Fitzpatrick may have picked up the team's lone interception earlier this season, but the secondary has been a weak spot for the Jets with numerous blown coverages and undisciplined play. As Moore moves up the depth chart, he should see an uptick in sub-package defensive snaps and have some additional opportunities to try and build on the bright spots he showed last season.
Even though McDonald still has another year remaining on his contract and appeared to be someone who was going to be packing his bags before the deadline , that ultimately did not come to fruition as he remains in Gotham. For someone with 24.5 sacks in just three-and-a-half seasons, it is understandable that New York would want to hold onto him.
That said, the 2023 first-rounder out of Iowa State has played less than 50% of the snaps for the defense this season and has been relegated to more of a situational role. While McDonald expressed his frustration about wanting to take his talents somewhere else, head coach Aaron Glenn addressed the deadline uncertainty with a vote of confidence toward his DE.
" I just know we're in the business of keeping good players, so Will's going to be here ," Glenn said, per Jets on SI's Nick Faria.
Still, McDonald has gone from a primary pass rusher to a third-down specialist with fewer opportunities. While some of that is on a coaching staff that continues to mismanage its roster, a lot also has to do with the emergence of rookie David Bailey and the fact that he is receiving more snaps as a result
The Jets may have kept their pieces in place despite not making any significant trade deadline moves, but that is not necessarily a bad thing for their long-term future. They already have three first-round picks (their own, the Colts' and the higher of the Cowboys' two picks), and they only benefited that much more as the 2-7 Colts have gone through a fire sale by trading away most of their top players and likely getting an even higher pick by season's end.
Even teams like the Eagles and Jaguars could be playing a role for the Jets as it relates to the draft. Given the needs the Eagles currently have and the likelihood that they stick with Jalen Hurts at QB, combined with the fact that Atlanta only has one first-round pick, the Jets could still be sneaky winners with the power they currently have in their draft capital.
Wright was signed to a one-year, $3.5 million deal in the offseason following a breakout 2025 campaign that featured a career-high five interceptions and his first Pro Bowl nod. However, he was expected to see his way out the door from Gotham after being a healthy scratch in more games than he's played this season.
Instead, the Jets decided to keep him around, perhaps with the hope that his playmaking abilities and tendency to create takeaways in his career could prove beneficial for a defense that has struggled in that area. Therefore, it seemed like a no-brainer move for the Jets to get him into the lineup for Week 9 against the Chiefs, even if that ended up being far from the case.
That said, Wright remains mired on the depth chart, looking for playing opportunities. An interested party would have only needed $833,333 in cap space to make a deal work, per Spotrac , but the Jets did not budge and chose to keep him on the roster, even if his opportunities remain few and far between.
While execution on both sides of the ball continues to plague Glenn this season , particularly his lack of aggressiveness and inability to adjust to what is happening on the field, he was certainly one of the biggest winners to emerge from the trade deadline due to the quiet approach the Jets took.
He may only be 5-21 during his brief tenure in Gang Green and 0-8 within the AFC East, a clear sign of a coach who is just getting by at this point until the Jets eventually let him go. The decision to retain QB Geno Smith and RB1 Breece Hall, specifically, gives him the best possible roster to try and finish out the season with some positives.
The talent, as we have seen, does not mean anything if the coaching does not utilize it correctly and execute in key situations. The writing may already be on the wall for Glenn, regardless of what happens for the rest of the season, but at least he gets the benefit of having a talented roster that is essentially the same as when the season began.

title: Jets Report Card: Regrading 2026 Draft Class Halfway Through First Season
full_text:
We're past the midway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the Jets should have a pretty good indication of where their rookie class is at this time.
Spoiler alert: they've been very encouraging .
From late-round production to the team's top talent early, the Jets have gotten everything they should want to see from their deep rookie class. So let's take out the report cards and see who has stood out the most.
The debate between if the Jets should've taken David Bailey or Arvell Reese will go on for many years beyond their rookie season.
Through nine games, though, it's clear the Jets made the right choice for them. Bailey has had a transcendent start to his first season with the team, recording 7.5 sacks and forcing five fumbles. His run defense isn't the greatest, but it's light-years better than what people originally thought it would be like coming out of college.
Bailey remains a blue-chip talent for the team going forward. As he develops, he could be the next great pass rusher this league is waiting to see. It's been a joy to watch him make big plays whenever he steps on the field.
It's been a frustrating year to judge Sadiq. Not because of what he's put on the field, but because of the lack of creativity in getting him the football from the Jets' coaching staff. They seemingly aren't entirely sure how to coordinate their offense with so much talent to choose from.
Because of that, Sadiq's numbers are a bit overlooked. The 16th overall pick has recorded 21 receptions for 235 yards and a touchdown. It should be more, though, if the team understood how to use his freakish athleticism.
Much like many players on this list, Omar Cooper Jr. has had a case of the injury bug early in the year. That said, his production while on the field has been superb. He was the first Jets receiver with back-to-back 100-yard receiving games since 1985, and he is already showing his skill set to be a big-play playmaker.
On the season, Cooper has recorded 20 receptions for 306 yards and two touchdowns. The more he plays, the better he will be. Cooper is a major part of the Jets' future.
Ponds is a difficult player to judge through his early snaps. The second-round corner out of Indiana missed all of training camp and the start of the season with an injury. Since his return to the field, the Jets have worked Ponds primarily out of the slot, a position he does not have a ton of experience in.
That said, the work we've seen so far from Ponds this season has been solid. He hasn't done enough to generate any coverage grades from Pro Football Focus, but has some solid reps in coverage. He's been penalized twice this year.
As of now, there is more tape on Ponds than some of the other late-round selections, so he'll get an average grade with room to grow moving forward.
New York's struggles with drafting quality day three talent have been well documented. For the first time in years, it seems like they may actually be correcting that mistake.
Jackson has not been dominant or the second coming of a Hall-of-Fame defensive tackle. However, he has been a quality piece to the defensive line rotation and one of the lone bright spots for the entire front seven this season. Jackson led the team in run stops last week in Kansas City and has an above-average grade (58.7) from Pro Football Focus , one of the highest of all current players in the Jets tackle room.
New York should be excited to see his development continue.
Perhaps we eventually see Klubnik out on the field once the season is nearly over (a final two games type of deal), but we aren't there yet. Instead, the Clemson product will have to take solace in sitting behind Geno Smith for the remainder of his first season. There's a lot to like out of Klubnik from his work in the preseason, but still. He gets an incomplete grade until we can actually see him get meaningful snaps.
New York's offensive line is a strength this season, but Cooper hasn't been healthy enough to play. He's been on short-term IR for most of the year. Cooper is a project offensive lineman with the potential to be an impact player in a few years.
Like many late-round rookies, it's unfair to even put a grade on Payne, considering he hasn't been healthy or played at all so far this season. Perhaps he will get some time now that Andre Cisco is no longer with the team , but that remains to be seen.
This has been one of the better draft classes the Jets have enjoyed in recent years. Almost every rookie who has seen playing time has gotten a chance to excel in some way. With stronger coaching and more development, the path is there for the 2026 class to be more impactful in a positive way than the 2022 one was.
There are, of course, questions. What would a new coaching staff do with some of these players? Is there hope they can get the most out of this talent?
But from a sheer report card basis, the Jets' future is very bright with this class.

title: Grading the Jets' NFL Trade Deadline: Quiet Day for New York Doesn't Move Needle
full_text:
The Jets were relatively quiet at the trade deadline compared to the past two years. New York made just one move, sending Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a sixth-round pick. The Jets made headlines at the past two deadlines with the Davante Adams trade and by sending away Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams.
This year pales in comparison.
New York's inactivity at the deadline was neither good nor bad. They didn't lose much talent, but they also were incapable of boosting an already stacked draft chest. The Jets were holders rather than buyers or sellers, leaving them in limbo as questions linger about job security at the coaching position.
Gang Green made one trade during the deadline. The move sent safety Cisco to Detroit for a sixth-round pick. It was nothing sexy, but a fair return for a player clearly outside the starting lineup. The Jets were able to flip an expiring contract for a sixth-round pick, which they can use to find safety depth if needed.
Per the league transaction wire, the Jets' compensation in the Andre Cisco trade has been changed to a 2029 sixth-round pick from the Lions. It was previously listed as a 2028 sixth-round pick. #Jets
Cisco and the Jets were clearly not a match made to last more than a season. The veteran safety has played only 191 snaps this season; 168 of those came in the first three weeks. New York got draft value for someone who likely won't be on the team next year.
While it does hurt the depth of the Jets' secondary, this move doesn't affect the team much. Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick are locked in at the starting safety positions. Barring injury, this trade should be a net positive for New York.
New York's leadership is in must-win territory. The Jets are 5-21 in the Aaron Glenn era, and that has come with constant criticism. It makes sense that New York wouldn't make moves with the coaching staff in jeopardy. But with some of the opportunities they have, the lack of selling from the Jets does raise eyebrows.
Will McDonald IV requested a trade, and teams showed interest . The Jets allegedly declined a "significant offer for him", which doesn't make much sense for a player who ranks 60th in snaps played at his position. The edge rusher wanted out, and it seems like the Jets are holding him hostage for a project that looks like it's at the end of its leash.
There was also talk about New York maybe trading Geno Smith.
Smith has been a fine signal-caller for the Jets, but the 36-year-old doesn't seem like the long-term answer at QB. The Jets already seem likely to draft at the position in the 2027 draft. It would have made sense for them to get capital to bolster an important upcoming draft.
New York also declined to trade Breece Hall despite rumors of interest. Braelon Allen took over the offense when Hall was out, and many thought that it would lead to Hall being traded. Instead, the Jets are now looking at a split backfield where both running backs do their best work as primary ball-carriers.
The Jets didn't lose any talent, but they may have held back the talent they do have. Instead of getting rid of a player who doesn't want to be there, an aging quarterback, and a running back who looks to have been eclipsed, the Jets stuck with their guns, which has led them to the cellar of the AFC.
The Jets stood pat at the deadline, leaving them where they were: a 2-7 team looking ahead to 2027. It seems Aaron Glenn and company are on their last leg. The Jets didn't get worse, but it does raise the question of what the plan is for the future.
The playoffs seem out of the question, and New York had a chance to amass even more draft capital than they currently hold. Instead, it seems like moves weren't made to protect a head coach with a 5-21 record.
The lack of activity didn't truly hurt or help New York; it just left the Jets in limbo, waiting for the offseason to begin.

title: 3 Jets Who Deserve Bigger Roles After New York's Quiet Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone , leaving the Jets focused on finishing the second half of the season. Organizations like New York decided whether to part with players no longer in their long-term plans or stand pat. Outside of trading Andre Cisco on Monday, Gang Green did nothing.
To his credit, head coach Aaron Glenn shed some light on the subject on Monday.
"Never say never, but right now I know we're going to stand pat," Glenn said. "Listen, we're in the business of keeping good players. That's how I see it... But you never know what's going to happen."
But things can certainly change when offers come flying in. And if the Jets had made more moves on Tuesday, it could've created opportunities for other players on the roster to get more playing time.
Despite the lack of moves, here are three Jets who still deserve more snaps moving forward.
If the Jets traded Jarvis Brownlee, then there would be no player to start over second-round rookie D'Angelo Ponds. The Indiana prospect was called for a penalty that gave Kansas City a first down in Sunday's loss, but otherwise was not targeted in the game.
Ponds's role is going to expand regardless as we get to the second half of the season, and a move away from Bownlee could've shown that the team sees him more as a nickel corner than a boundary one for the remainder of his career.
Things can certainly change, and based on Brownlee's recent play, Ponds should see a significant uptick in snaps following the deadline.
Jackson is another rookie who should see his snap count increase significantly after Tuesday's deadline. Harrison Phillips is on an expiring deal and Jowon Briggs is an RFA. If the Jets decide neither is in their long-term plans, they could cut their playing time and shift it over to the rookie tackle in the second half.
In Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, Jackson played 43% of the defensive snaps and actually led the team in run stops. He has been a surprise addition to the interior defensive line of the Jets. He isn't a perfect prospect, but he's shown enough for the next coaching regime to find a place for him going forward.
It's also worth mentioning that with injuries to T'Vondre Sweat and David Onyemata, the Jets will need to give Jackson more snaps regardless.
Lynn logged just 12 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs. But the preseason standout could've seen his role increase tremendously over the final few weeks of the season if the Jets had found a way to move Will McDonald for the right price.
Lynn recorded a sack in the team's loss to the Dolphins back in October and is someone who certainly has the burst to make plays. But if the Jets had taken the best offer on the table for McDonald, another hole along their defensive line would've opened. It would've been a perfect opportunity for Lynn to show he's worthy of a roster spot going forward.
Hopefully, the Jets realize what they have in front of them and find a way to play Lynn more frequently down the stretch.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings: New Face Takes Over the Top Spot Before Week 10
full_text:
Unsurprisingly, the Jets' skid has reached four games after losing 35-12 to the Chiefs on Sunday . Questionable coaching decisions, poor execution, and failing to score a touchdown in the red zone were just a few of the ongoing issues that continue to show up in the team’s losses.
With the loss, New York drops to 2-7, and head coach Aaron Glenn is now 5-21 since taking over in 2025. With the playoffs out of the horizon and Glenn all but out of a job after the season ends, there isn’t much to look forward to other than the young players.
Speaking of which, several rookies and sophomores stood out despite the team’s loss . With that said, let’s take a look at where they rank heading into Gang Green’s Week 10 matchup against the Bills.
Note: Anez Cooper and VJ Payne are currently excluded from the list. Cooper is on injured reserve but is eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season. Meanwhile, Payne hasn’t played in a game.
Barring a Garrett Wilson trade request in the offseason, he should be among the Jets’ top receiving options in 2027, alongside Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell. Isaiah Williams could also be in the mix, but he’ll have to earn that spot. The same goes for Arian Smith.
Although he couldn’t prove his worth this season, Smith’s play was extremely underwhelming in his rookie campaign, recording just seven receptions for 52 yards.
With New York likely to strengthen the receiver corps in the offseason, Smith is unlikely to remain with Gang Green unless he makes significant progress as a receiver.
With each Jets loss, Cade Klubnik’s chances of playing this season increase. After Sunday’s defeat, his odds have reached an all-time high.
Even though Geno Smith wasn’t to blame for the loss, New York simply has no incentive to continue putting him out there. He’s shown that he can still play at a high level and lead an offense, but the Jets’ coaching and the team’s poor execution consistently let him down.
As long as Glenn remains head coach, they likely won’t turn to Klubnik anytime soon, as Glenn needs wins to secure his job. But if things continue as they have been, don’t be surprised if they name Klubnik the starter coming out of the bye week against Denver.
A five-game sample against some of the league's best defenses should give New York a better idea of what it has in him.
Kiko Mauigoa has been on the injured reserve since reinjuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots.
In the three games the former 2025 fifth-round selection appeared in, Mauigoa exclusively played on special teams, as New York has primarily stuck with two inside linebackers this season. But with the Jets continuing to drop games, there’s a chance Mauigoa could earn reps on defense if he returns this season.
With Demario Davis continuing to show that he’s regressed dramatically this season, it’s time the team tried someone else alongside Jamien Sherwood. Mauigoa could be an option.
Andre Cisco had been the Jets’ third safety behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick.
But things seemed to change on Sunday, when Malachi Moore received a season-high 17 defensive snaps against the Chiefs while Cisco exclusively played on special teams. While some may have viewed this as a reward for his incredible performance on special teams, posting eight tackles and earning a 79.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus , it was actually an effort to keep Cisco healthy before eventually trading him to the Lions on Monday afternoon.
Playing his first defensive snaps since Week 5, the former 2025 fourth-round selection didn’t necessarily stand out, recording just one tackle and allowing a catch for 19 yards in 12 coverage snaps.
Even with Cisco gone, it doesn’t guarantee Moore as the backup safety. With rookie VJ Payne making his return to practice last week, Moore must continue to make the most of his opportunity.
The Jets’ usage of D’Angelo Ponds has been intriguing, to say the least.
Since returning from a calf injury in Week 3, Ponds has played sparingly, appearing in just 87 defensive snaps across seven games.
The former Indiana Hoosier played in a season-high 30 snaps in Week 7’s matchup against the Dolphins, playing particularly well against the run, before seeing just one snap against the Raiders last week
On Sunday, Ponds played 22 snaps, recording two tackles and giving up a touchdown. He also committed a costly illegal contact penalty on third-and-11; however, David Bailey forced a turnover two plays later.
Even though it was an underwhelming game from Ponds, we must cut him some slack. He’s transitioning from outside corner to nickelback, a position at which he lined up at just 28 times in college.
Ponds will experience more growing pains, and New York must learn to live with it by giving him consistent playing time. It's the only way he’ll develop.
Kenyon Sadiq was more involved in New York’s loss to Kansas City than he’d been the past few weeks, but not all of it was for the right reasons.
The former Oregon Duck hauled in all four of his targets for 49 yards, finishing second on the team behind Omar Cooper Jr.
Kenyon Sadiq makin it look easy 📺: #NYJvsKC on @NFLonCBS | @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/VzYXDSx5VU
The bad news is that Sadiq was penalized twice.
His first penalty came on the opening drive, where he committed a false start in Chiefs’ territory. This wasn’t costly, as New York came away with three points. Meanwhile, his second penalty did cost the Jets points.
On second-and-five with 53 seconds left in the first half at Kansas City’s 25, Sadiq was called for a facemask penalty, negating a seven-yard run by Breece Hall. Although the Jets still managed to stay in field goal range, Jason Sanders missed a 53-yard kick.
The two flags shouldn’t draw major concerns, but Sadiq must learn from his mistakes.
Mason Taylor played extremely well in his first three games back from a thumb injury, recording 12 catches for 114 yards and two touchdowns.
In the past two games, however, the former LSU Tiger has been quiet, posting just four receptions for 30 yards. Although Taylor wasn’t involved much in the passing game in the team’s loss to Kansas City, he ended up hurting the Jets with two costly penalties.
His first penalty was a false start in Chiefs’ territory, which stalled the drive and led the Jets to kick a field goal. Down nine in the third quarter, Taylor was called for an illegal shift on third-and-four, negating a 19-yard reception by Adonai Mitchell. On the next play, Smith was sacked on third-and-nine, and New York was forced to punt.
Although his penalties weren’t the reason for New York’s loss, Taylor must clean things up moving forward.
Despite playing a career-high 47 defensive snaps against the Chiefs, Darrell Jackson Jr. was relatively quiet, recording just three tackles and one pressure.
His presence in the middle is critical, with David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat on the injured reserve. However, Jackson and the Jets' defensive line struggled against Kenneth Walker and Kansas City’s ground game, which combined for 163 rushing yards on 32 carries.
Even though Jackson hasn’t consistently made noteworthy plays, he’s displayed flashes of being a quality rotational player. Between his run stuff on fourth down against Las Vegas last week and his two batted passes and a sack against the Browns, Jackson is a player worth keeping an eye on over the next few weeks.
After starting the season strong in coverage, Azareye’h Thomas’ play has taken a significant step backward over the past few weeks.
The former 2025 third-round selection struggled to cover Kansas City’s pass-catchers, allowing five catches (six targets) for 63 yards and earning a 48.3 coverage grade , per PFF . His worst play came on the first play of the Chiefs’ ninth offensive drive, where he got burnt by 37-year-old Travis Kelce for 38 yards.
Thomas wasn’t even close to Kelce when he caught it, and he just looked completely lost several times. He didn’t fare any better…

title: Jets Could Be Sneaky Winners After Falcons & Eagles Deadline Trades
full_text:
If the Jets decide to do nothing by the NFL's trade deadline , they will still be set up for success in a major way going into 2027 and beyond. That's what happens when you own three first-round picks in the upcoming draft.
But that also doesn't mean the team can't be affected by other trades that happen around the NFL.
The Falcons and Eagles made major headlines on Monday afternoon when they traded key pieces on their defense to the Jaguars. First, it was Jessie Bates leaving Atlanta for the top price of a second-round pick. Then, defensive tackle Jordan Davis was shipped out for a first- and second-round pick to Philadelphia.
The Jaguars aren't something the Jets will have to worry about come draft day, but the deals they made with the Eagles and Falcons could actually help Gang Green moving forward.
At first glance, the Eagles selling off top talent and acquiring an extra first-round pick can be seen as a problem for the Jets . Philadelphia could very well take a quarterback to restart their true rebuild and that takes New York out of the equation, especially with the Eagles slated for the fifth pick if the year ended today.
But if the Eagles' losses continue (almost a certainty due to their rash of injuries), the team's needs are a perfect pairing for a team like the Jets.
Philadelphia needs defensive line and offensive line help. With Jalen Hurts under contract and expected to return from his blood clots, the team could keep him on the roster in 2027 and punt their quarterback debate for 2028. Should that happen, the Eagles could simply trade back with their current top pick to a quarterback-needy team... like the Jets.
The same could be said about Atlanta as well. The Falcons do not own an additional first-round pick, so even if they finish ahead of the Jets in the 2027 draft order, New York has plenty of ammo to move up ahead of them.
In a race to get the top quarterbacks of this upcoming draft class, you want to be a team like the Jets with three picks slated in the top 15 overall picks compared to the Falcons or even the Eagles.
And if the Eagles keep losing, it's far more likely they trade out of their top pick to acquire more capital, which is perfectly fine for the Jets.
Much of these two trades have little to no effect on the Jets, but the biggest pieces of news surrounding these organizations that matter most will be the health of Hurts beyond his current blood clot problems.
The Eagles believe that Hurts will be back to 100% by the end of the year once he comes off blood thinners, but there's no guarantee that will solve the problem. The team could look to trade for a top veteran on the open market, but they could also draft a quarterback.
With the Eagles as bad as they are, the most important update for Jets fans and the organization will be about Hurts.
The good news for New York is that they remain in a strong position to draft a quarterback regardless of what Philadelphia does. Indianapolis continues to crumble and could trade Jonathan Taylor this afternoon, and Dallas has struggled with mediocrity throughout the season. Gang Green could be looking at three picks inside the top 15, and two inside the top five by season's end.
It's more than enough ammo to transform their roster going forward.

title: 5 Necessary Changes the Eagles Must Make After Their Bye Week
full_text:
Eight games remain in an Eagles season that resembles a Talking Heads song: "We’re on the road to nowhere." It will be more than two months since they last won a game when they return from their bye week to play the Steelers on Nov. 22.
Their last win was Sept. 20, when Jalen Hurts led the Eagles on a magnificent game-winning drive against the Titans.
This won’t help turn things around, but here are five things I’d like to see happen over the Eagles' final eight games once they come out of their bye week.
Even when/if DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks return from injury, the rookie should see a healthy number of targets. He has improved with each game played and is one of the bright spots on this horrid offense.
With Smith missing four of the team’s nine games, Lemon is now the Eagles’ leading receiver with 312 yards, two more than Smith has.
It’s a small sample size, but since Week 7, Lemons has had three straight games with at least six catches and 50-plus yards, joining Puka Nacua and Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the only three on that sort of streak.
That Dallas Goedert wasn’t traded for something—anything—is curious. Maybe nobody wanted to give up anything for the veteran tight end.
Even more curious is why Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra are still on the roster. Maybe Zach Ertz doesn’t have anything left, but wouldn’t fans rather see him out there threatening to break a franchise record for most catches in a career that has stood since 1983, when Harold Carmichael had 589? Ertz has 582.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
Even with Goedert still on the roster, Stowers needs more of a role. That the second-round pick only played seven snaps against the Giants in Week 9 is ridiculous.
Goedert played 57 snaps (81 percent). Come on, the odds are he won’t be back on a third straight one-year deal, so why shouldn’t Stowers cut into that kind of workload?
The trade of Jordan Davis will likely make this happen. The defensive tackle has played just 61 defensive snaps in his second season, but has held up well in a rotational role. He needs to play more just to see what the Eagles have in him over the next two years of his rookie contract.
Zion Wilson spent the preseason with the Eagles but was waived on cutdown day despite recording nine tackles, two tackles for loss or no gain, and four QB pressures in three preseason games. He was signed to the practice squad on Oct. 13.
Wilson, who is 6'3" and 315 lbs, was denied another year of college when he tried to transfer from East Carolina to Virginia, so he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. In 2025, with East Carolina, he had seven sacks. It would make sense to either elevate him from the practice squad or just sign him to the roster to take Davis’s place.
Barring Joe Milton leading the Eagles to a win or two, play Cole Payton in the final two games. Heck, even if Milton wins a game or two, playing Payton should happen. It’s evaluation time, after all.
Same thing for outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski, who has one practice squad elevation remaining. Why play Marcus Epps? He’s not part of the future. James-Newby has done some decent things in limited opportunities.
Then there’s guard Micah Morris. Why not give him some reps, too? He’s a big guy at 6'5" and 335 lbs.
Let’s see what these players have.

title: 3 Eagles Coaches' Jobs Should Be in Jeopardy During the Bye Week
full_text:
Bye weeks are a time for NFL players and coaches to rest and prepare for the second half of the season. For the Eagles, it'll be a time for reevaluation, too. A disastrous seven-game losing streak has Philadelphia sitting at the bottom of the NFC East. Glaring problems remain on both sides of the ball.
The front office can only change the roster so much midway through a season. That move came in the form of trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars . Bigger changes can be made in the coaching staff. That could be as simple as shifting responsibilities or as impactful as firing someone .
Here's a look at three Eagles coaches whose jobs should be in jeopardy during the bye week.
Moving on from veteran offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland has proven to be more difficult than the Eagles expected. Philadelphia's hire of Chris Kuper wasn't considered a big splash. He took on the same role in Minnesota last season, when the Vikings allowed the second-most sacks in the NFL (60).
Philadelphia is suffering from similar issues, allowing the third-most sacks in the league (30). The Eagles entered Week 9 with the highest percentage of pass plays with unblocked pressure (18.2%). That was before New York's Arvell Reese had a free run to blast quarterback Joe Milton.
The issues go beyond pass blocking. The Eagles rank 27th in both rushing yards per carry (3.7) and rushing yards per game (88.6). This is a team that cruised to a Super Bowl title just two years ago with a historic ground game. Nowadays, Saquon Barkley is lucky to tally a few yards before being leveled.
It's fair to point out that Lane Johnson's retirement, Landon Dickerson's injuries, and Cam Jurgens' trade to Baltimore have made Kuper's job tough. The results on the field go beyond excuses, though. Improvements need to be made, and it has become clear that they won't be with Kuper at the helm.
Special teams should be a part of football that provides a team with an advantage, or at least keeps them in the fight. Instead, the Eagles have been getting undone by their special teams unit on a weekly basis. That includes poor kick/punt coverage, missed field goals, and costly penalties.
There's at least one setback to point out in every game. As of late, a false start penalty turned Jake Elliott's 36-yard field goal make into a 41-yard field goal miss in Week 8. A bad snap from Rocco Underwood forced punter Braden Mann into a rugby-style boot that went -2 yards in Week 9.
Mistakes happen, but constant mistakes show that there's a lack of adjustment. Special teams coordinator Michael Clay has been with the Eagles since 2021. It would make sense to give him a longer leash if Philly were winning games. It isn't. A new voice is needed in special teams meetings.
The hype surrounding offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was real during training camp. The 34-year-old former NFL quarterback was expected to bring a fresh, modern offensive scheme to a team that desperately needed one. However, the offense has looked far from fresh through nine weeks.
The Eagles have averaged 260.2 yards and 16.4 points per game, which are bottom-three marks in the NFL. They also check in below Philly's 2025 marks (311.0 & 22.1). While it's easy to blame injuries, the offense performed poorly even when the roster was fully healthy. It's been a season-long disaster.
Now, firing Mannion would be a much more substantial move than firing either Kuper or Clay. A first-time play-caller should be given the chance to work out the kinks. With that said, the Eagles need to shake up the game plan. Tailoring the system to their personnel would be a good place to start.

title: Pressure Is Rising for Eagles' Recent Draft Classes Now That the Trade Deadline Is Over
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — With the trade deadline behind them and eight games left in a season gone bust, the Eagles will emerge from the bye week on Nov. 22 with shifting priorities.
The recent trades of Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis have stripped some veteran production while loading up on future draft capital .
Quarterback Jalen Hurts is likely sidelined for the season. The offense is sputtering under new coordinator Sean Mannion. The defense under Vic Fangio has been uneven. In the midst of seven consecutive losses after a 2-0 start, wins would be nice, but the real work will be evaluating the recent draft classes under live-fire exercises.
Start with the 2026 class, which is already getting meaningful snaps for two of the premium picks.
Makai Lemon, the first-round wide receiver out of USC , is the clearest immediate contributor. After a quiet start, he’s become the most reliable target during the stretch without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Lemon has put together consecutive games with six-plus catches and 50-plus yards, scored his first NFL touchdown against Dallas, and led the team in targets and yards in recent losses to the Commanders and Giants.
In recent weeks, Lemon has shown nice hands (although the concentration drops have been problematic), route-running, and the slot ability the Eagles targeted when they traded up to get him. The yards-per-catch are modest so far. But in a post-A.J. Brown offense that needs a young WR to step forward, Lemon is doing a solid job.
The rest of the season will show whether Lemon can sustain his recent improvement with Smith and Wicks involved as the more important priorities. It's also a test for Mannion to keep Lemon in mind.
Eli Stowers, the second-round tight end from Vanderbilt, is further behind because of early injuries that landed him on injured reserve to start the season.
The athletic former college quarterback has shown some flashes, namely three catches for 53 yards against Washington, including a 34-yarder, albeit in garbage time. You can at least envision the ability to stress linebackers.
Stowers is not displacing Dallas Goedert yet, but the long-term goal is clear. More snaps in 12 personnel or flexed out will tell the staff how quickly the Vandy product can be counted on for a real role in the offense.
Markel Bell, the third-round tackle from Miami, got thrown into the fire at right tackle after Lane Johnson’s retirement. The 6-foot-9, 345-pounder had a rough debut but has somewhat stabilized since. He’s not a finished product by any means—pressures and penalties remain an issue—but the size and improving processing are obvious.
With the offensive line in flux, Bell’s remaining games will serve as an extended audition for whether he can be a long-term starter or settle in as a backup swing tackle.
Evaluating key components of the 2025 class, which is supposed to be further along, is all about piling repetitions on Jihaad Campbell and Andrew Mukuba.
Campbell, a first-round linebacker from Alabama, had a solid rookie year (All-Rookie consideration, productive when starting) and was set for a full-time weakside role next to Zack Baun after Nakobe Dean left in free agency.
Year 2 has been interrupted by lingering hamstring and quad issues, but the tools are there. The questions surrounding Campbell involve his instincts. When healthy, the rest of the season should clarify whether Campbell is a true three-down starter or just an athlete.
Mukuba, the second-round safety from Texas, is already a primary piece in the secondary, but the results have been mixed—missed tackles and coverage lapses have shown up.
Fangio has spoken well of Mukuba’s trajectory, but outsiders often see something different. Mukuba’s remaining snaps will determine how much the coaching staff trusts him in the back end of a defense that needs more consistency.
Ty Robinson, a fourth-round defensive tackle from Nebraska, has been buried on the depth chart behind Jalen Carter, Davis, Moro Ojomo and Byron Young.
In a defensive line room that just lost Davis, Robinson should join the rotation and every snap will help determine if he should stay a part of it in 2027.
Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has always built through the draft. With extra premium picks coming in 2027 and beyond, the next eight weeks are the best chance to separate the keepers from the most recent drafts from those who won’t be part of any solution.
The record might not improve much for the Eagles, but the information gathered on these younger players should help determine the future.

title: 3 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Gone in the Offseason Despite Surviving Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is now in the rearview mirror, and outside of the surprising trade of star defensive lineman Jordan Davis , it was a relatively quiet deadline for the Eagles.
The Eagles held on to several players who were predicted to be traded away , but that doesn't necessarily mean that those guys are part of the long-term plan in Philly.
Here's a look at three Eagles players who will likely still be gone over the offseason, despite surviving the trade deadline.
The Eagles benching Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton after three starts this season tells you everything you really need to know about how the organization views McKee at this point in time. If they viewed McKee as a long-term piece, they would have prioritized his development and allowed him to continue to play in Jalen Hurts' absence, even through some struggles.
Instead, they handed the offense over to a guy who had been on the roster for less than a month.
It should have been obvious that the Eagles were down on McKee when he entered the season as the third QB on the depth chart behind Andy Dalton, but his benching has made things crystal clear. McKee will be a free agent over the offseason, and we shouldn't expect to see him back in Philadelphia next season.
It came as a surprise to many, likely including Brown himself, that the veteran pass-catcher wasn't traded prior to the deadline , but he wasn't, which means he'll finish out the campaign as a member of the Eagles.
Perhaps Brown will be more of a factor for Philly over the final eight games than he was during the first nine, when he tallied just five receptions for 53 yards. Either way, it seems like the writing is already on the wall when it comes to his future in Philly.
There will be a lot of moving parts for the Eagles over the offseason, and bringing back an aging receiver who has had little impact probably won't be a priority for general manager Howie Roseman and company.
The Eagles agreed to trade linebacker Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals prior to the trade deadline, only for the Bengals to back out of the deal after learning that they might lose a compensatory pick as a result.
Bengals are expected to back out of the trade for Arnold Ebiketie. The Bengals would have lost a third-round compensatory pick that they were receiving for Trey Hendrickson signing with Baltimore. Now this trade is expected to fall through. https://t.co/1Enn5jLpDD
So, Ebiketie will remain in Philly for the rest of the season, but the fact that the team tried to flip him for a sixth-round pick is pretty indicative of his future with the franchise.
The Eagles couldn't recoup any value for Ebiketie, but it still seems exceedingly unlikely that they'll bring him back over the offseason. He's as good as gone.

title: Confidence Meter: How Close Are Eagles to Firing Nick Sirianni During Bye Week?
full_text:
The Eagles' 2026 season has spiralled out of control.
The Eagles have lost seven consecutive games heading into their bye week, a streak that dates back to late September, and head coach Nick Sirianni has been unable to stop the bleeding . As a result, some have suggested that the Eagles should move on from Sirianni in the middle of the current campaign, despite the fact that he led the team to a victory in Super Bowl 59 just last year.
But would the Eagles actually make such a drastic move involving the most successful coach in franchise history? That seems very doubtful.
During his first five seasons on the sideline in Philadelphia, Sirianni led the Eagles to five playoff appearances, two Super Bowl berths and one win in the big game. He has the highest regular-season winning percentage in franchise history and the second-most playoff wins.
If nothing else, his previous success should afford Sirianni the dignity of not being fired midseason, especially a season in which injuries have absolutely ravaged the roster. Sirianni hasn't had his starting quarterback for the past month, and a plethora of other key contributors have missed legitimate time due to various ailments. That's not necessarily an excuse, just a fact. Sirianni hasn't been dealt a full deck this season, and while he's been unable to maximize the deck he has been dealt, it's fair to wonder whether that's a fireable offense, especially since we've seen what he can do with a full deck.
The Eagles aren't going anywhere this season, anyway, and they're not in danger of missing out on the franchise's next great coach if they don't act quickly. It's not like there's a mastermind waiting in the wings to take over the team.
On the contrary, firing Sirianni in the middle of the season would do little for the franchise other than to send a message, but the message might not even be one that the organization wants to send. How would other coaches, and potential Sirianni replacements, feel after seeing a Super Bowl-winning coach thrown out the door at the first sign of turbulence? Why would a prime coaching candidate want to come to an organization that treats successful coaches that way? If the Eagles want to move on from Sirianni, they should absolutely wait until the offseason to do so.
Plus, moving on from coaches in the middle of the season simply isn't the Eagles' M.O. under owner Jeffrey Lurie. Since Lurie took over as the owner of the team in 1994, he has fired five head coaches. Four of those coaches—Rich Kotite, Ray Rhodes, Andy Reid and Doug Pederson—were all fired directly after the season came to an end.
Chip Kelly is the only coach who was fired by the Eagles during the season under Lurie. He was fired with just one game remaining in the 2016 season, and he hadn't experienced a fraction of the success with the organization that Sirianni has. So, the decision to move on from Sirianni mid-season would buck a major trend for the Eagles as an organization, which makes the move seem even less likely.
For what it's worth, Sirianni doesn't seem especially concerned about his future in Philly. While speaking prior to Philadelphia's Week 9 game against the Giants, Sirianni stressed that he continues to feel full support from Lurie despite the team's struggles this season.
“I’ve always felt I have nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie, in everything, through good times, through bad times. That’s huge, right? That’s huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all these situations," Sirianni said.
He likely wouldn't acknowledge any difference publicly, but it certainly sounds like a midseason firing would come as a surprise to Sirianni himself.
Crazier things have happened, but it would be extremely surprising if the Eagles moved on from Sirianni during the current campaign, both because of his previous success and the lack of other options available at the present time.

title: I’m Shocked the Eagles Didn’t Trade These 3 Players at the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and it's safe to say that it felt like a normal day for Eagles fans. Outside of a failed deal that would've sent EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a sixth-round pick, Eagles general manager Howie Roseman stuck with the status quo, deciding Monday's blockbuster Jordan Davis trade with the Jaguars was all that needed to be done.
While the return for Davis was great, it's hard to be too excited about Philadelphia's trade deadline performance. After all, it isn't often that the Eagles have an opportunity to blow things and restock their draft capital, given that they're usually firmly in the Super Bowl conversations.
With that in mind, it's a surprise to see that the Eagles decided to keep this trio rather than trade them when they had the chance.
When it came to potential trade chips, Riq Woolen was among the Eagles' likeliest candidates to be moved . A one-year contract made him the perfect rental option for contending teams, while his Super Bowl-winning experience from his time in Seattle only added to what he could've brought to the table.
Instead, Woolen will remain in Philadelphia until the end of the season, at least. NBC Sports Philadelphia' s Ryan Fowler reported that even though "multiple teams" attempted a trade , "a deal that made sense for both sides never progressed beyond initial conversations."
It'll be interesting to see what Woolen does in the second half of the season; either giving the Eagles more reasons to keep him or walk away in March. His 52.7 coverage grade is a new career-low performance , according to Pro Football Focus , meaning he'll need to seriously step up if Philadelphia doesn't want to regret keeping him.
Despite spending all of his career in Philly, Dallas Goedert was another veteran viewed as one of the Eagles' biggest trade candidates .
Like, Woolen, Goedert is on an expiring deal, and no one would've blamed the team if they had done right by the 31-year-old tight end and trade to a Super Bowl contender. That didn't happen, though, forcing Goedert to spend the rest of the season on one of the more uncompetitive Eagles teams he's played for in the last nine seasons.
Goedert has now played on one-year contracts in back-to-back seasons, so it remains to be seen whether the Eagles will attempt the hat trick. Goedert is averaging career lows in yards per catch (9.9) and success rate (45.2%), so he'll likely need significant improvements if he wants to reach Year 10 in Philly.
With all the changes that the offensive line has undergone, Eagles fans were prepared to see guard Landon Dickerson shipped out of town this week. Several teams around the NFL needed interior O-line help, so why not turn to a former Super Bowl Champion with over 90 games between the regular season and playoffs under his belt?
Fast-forward past the deadline, and Dickerson is still an Eagle as he finishes the first season of his three-year, $58.5 million extension. In theory, that's plenty of time to get back on track, but a 54.4 PFF grade —ranking 54th among 75 qualified OGs—suggests that a fresh start likely would've benefited both sides, especially if Philadelphia could've gotten a decent return.
Given the term remaining on his contract, the Eagles likely want to give Dickerson more time before making a decision to cut ties. Let's hope, for their sake, he turns things around ASAP. Otherwise, not trading him on Tuesday might eventually look like a mistake.
