title: McMullen: Jordan Davis Trade Cements Why Howie Roseman Is One of NFL's Best GMs
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Actions always speak louder than words.
Eight months after Howie Roseman handed Jordan Davis a three-year, $78 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid interior defensive linemen in football, the Eagles shipped him to Jacksonville for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round selection.
That isn’t just a roster tweak. It’s a clear signal that Philadelphia would rather build around Moro Ojomo than live with the massive commitment they just made to Davis.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI what the market already suggested: the Jaguars checked in on Ojomo first. They were told he wasn’t available. From there, the talks evolved to the point that the Eagles were willing to part with Davis , as long as James Gladstone played into his reputation for the overpay.
Behind the scenes, the Eagles’ posture for weeks had been that Ojomo was staying. However, most considered that to be straight out of the Roseman playbook of shooting for the stars in an attempt to generate a second-round pick for the Texas product.
The trade of Davis confirms Philadelphia is choosing the younger, cheaper, more versatile player they can actually keep next to Carter long-term.
This is also a clear indication that the Eagles believe this will be defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s last season in Philadelphia. Fangio always wants a pure nose tackle he can plug into variable fronts when needed.
Davis was that guy—the space-eating, two-gap presence who lets Fangio play the light-box looks and disguise coverages he’s built his reputation on. When the production didn’t match the contract this year, it makes sense that the organization decided it wasn’t worth locking into that personnel profile for the next three seasons if Fangio isn’t going to be the one drawing it up.
The disappointment in Davis’ 2026 tape is real. After a career year in 2025—career highs in sacks, tackles for loss, and overall disruption—the Eagles thought he had turned the corner as a more complete player. Instead, he’s been a solid-but-limited run-stuffer who has struggled to stay in ideal condition and has barely played on third down unless it’s short-yardage.
Through nine games, he ranked third among Eagles defensive tackles in snaps behind Carter and Ojomo. On obvious passing downs he has been a non-factor for most of his career.
That’s not the profile you pay $26 million a year to keep when you already have Carter locked up on a much bigger deal and a rising player like Ojomo ready to take a bigger role.
Roseman should take a hit for crafting the original extension but recovered quickly by continuing to tap into the same market inefficiency he’s exploited for years: the systematic devaluation of future draft capital.
The 2029 second-round pick is the kind of asset most GMs treat as monopoly money. Roseman treats it like currency .
Ultimately, Davis is a two-down player who generated a little less than what the Titans extracted for Jeffery Simmons—a more accomplished, higher-usage player who fetched two firsts and a fourth.
The Jaguars may win a Super Bowl this year after loading up with Davis, safety Jessie Bates, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. That doesn’t change the fact that this is one of the biggest overpayments we’ve seen in years. Jacksonville is paying a premium for a two-down player,
Former NFL executive Andrew Brandt noted that a general manager with a business and negotiating background like Roseman will continue to take advantage of GMs whose backgrounds are primarily scouting or personnel.
This trade seems to be the latest example of that.

title: Eagles NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors, and Latest News
full_text:
Before the 2026 NFL season, few people expected the Eagles to be in seller mode at the NFL trade deadline . After all, Philadelphia was coming off four consecutive 11-plus-win seasons, which included two Super Bowl appearances and one win. Fast-forward to Tuesday, though, and the Eagles are 2-7 and at the bottom of the NFC East, leaving general manager Howie Roseman with only one option this week .
It's rare that the Eagles are in a position to acquire so much draft capital, but doing so will put them in a solid spot to return to prominence next season. That's why Roseman & Co. must effectively figure out who no longer fits with the team's long-term plans and move on before it's too late.
Here's are the lates rumors and news surrounding the Eagles now that the NFL trade deadline is here.
UPDATE (Nov. 10, 12:28 p.m. ET): In a major twist, NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Eagles-Bengals trade for Ebiketie will no longer be going through . Rapoport followed up by saying that Cincinnati called off the trade to avoid losing a compensatory pick.

Sports Illustrated 's Ed Kracz broke down the trade after it was announced, giving it an A+ for the impressive return the Eagles managed to recoup. Davis will be missed, no doubt, but it can also be said that trading him was the right choice to keep the team competitive for as long as possible.

title: 3 Eagles Winners & 2 Losers After Trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars
full_text:
It wouldn't be the NFL trade deadline without blockbuster deals. The Eagles entered the fold by trading defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars on Monday, according to ESPN 's Adam Schefter. Philadelphia received a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick in return.
It's a move that would've shocked fans before the season began. Davis was inked to a three-year, $78 million extension in March, and the Eagles had Super Bowl hopes. Philadelphia sits at the bottom of the NFC East, though, with a 2-7 record through nine weeks. The time has arrived to retool for the future .
Trades are always a double-edged sword in the NFL. In this case, the Eagles lose a vital run defender and locker room mentor. They also gain valuable draft assets and open up chances for others to earn more playing time. Here's a deeper dive into the Philly winners and losers of the Davis deadline deal.
There was chatter that Moro Ojomo would be the Philadelphia defensive tackle dealt at the deadline . Instead, he moves forward as one member of a dynamic duo with Jalen Carter before entering free agency next offseason. The 2023 seventh-round pick has worked hard to climb the depth chart.
Ojomo has showcased a high ceiling as a pass-rusher and run-stopper. He has logged 62 tackles, six sacks, and 10 tackles for loss since the start of 2025 (26 games). Consistent play down the stretch could lead to an extension for the 25-year-old. He'll have every opportunity to prove he's worth one.
The hole left by Davis' departure cannot be filled by one player. Ojomo is going to see his snaps increase, as should second-year pro Ty Robinson. The Nebraska product has played sparingly in his first two NFL seasons, tallying 10 tackles and one pass breakup in 20 games (13% of the defensive snaps).
. @T_ROB99 is COOKING rn pic.twitter.com/67Zm5ElLAT
A preseason sack against the Patriots showcased what Robinson can bring to the table. Strong hands helped him shed an initial block and work around the edge. Increased snaps will only help Philly's coaching staff determine what level of contributor Robinson can be in 2027 and beyond.
Howie Roseman is capitalizing on his chances to retool Philly's roster . The Davis trade follows a Cam Jurgens trade that netted a 2028 second-rounder and an A.J. Brown trade that netted a 2028 first-rounder. In total, the Eagles now own 10 picks within the first two rounds of the next three NFL drafts.
#Eagles upcoming draft picks: 2027 (9): 1st round, 1st, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 5th, 5th, 7th 2028 (9): 1st, 1st, 2d, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th 2029 (8): 1st, 2d, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th
The picks give Roseman some much-needed flexibility. He could package them to acquire a superstar or move up in the draft. He could hold onto them and add exciting prospects to the Eagles' aging core. In any scenario, the picks provide hope that a complete rebuild isn't necessary in Philly.
One weakness has now grown weaker. The Eagles allowed at least 100 rushing yards in each of their first eight games for the first time since 1968, before they stifled the Giants' ground game in Week 9. Philly enters its bye week ranked a disappointing 24th in rushing yards allowed per game (126.1).
Losing Davis will take a physical and mental toll on the Eagles' rush defense. His massive frame (6'6", 325 lbs) erased running lanes and caused opposing backs to second-guess themselves. It'll be up to players like Ojomo and Robinson to make their presence felt on the interior of the defensive line.
The loss of a monster defensive tackle is never going to be a good thing for a defensive coordinator. Vic Fangio will have to make adjustments. Whether or not those adjustments will work is a question no one can answer. It's worth pointing out that Fangio reportedly considered retiring last offseason.
The Eagles went as far as checking in with former Philly defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz , per The Philadelphia Inquirer 's Jeff McLane. Davis is someone who fits in Fangio's scheme, but he's not someone who fits in every NFL defensive scheme. The trade could be a sign of eventual change.

title: 3 Eagles Who Could Be Traded Next After Jordan Davis
full_text:
Each NFL trade deadline is often filled with offers that some general managers simply can't refuse , and that appeared to be the case for Eagles general manager Howie Roseman on Monday.
With the defensive tackle trade market heating up, the Eagles pulled the trigger by trading star DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, according to ESPN 's Adam Schefter . Philadelphia acquired a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second-round pick in the massive trade, making it clear that Roseman & Co. are thinking about the future.
Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT
Davis's trade could signal the start of the Eagles moving away from more veteran pieces, especially those with expiring contracts and unguaranteed futures in Philly. With action likely picking up even more as we get closer to the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Tuesday, a few more current Eagles might become part of the team's past sooner rather than later.
That said, to quote former WCW World Heavyweight Champion Bill Goldberg, "Who's next?"
If any team is looking to add a dependable tight end to their offense, there's a good chance the Eagles will field some calls for Dallas Goedert. The ninth-year TE is a standard rental option ( expiring contract, affordable $7 million cap hit , per Spotrac ), and with Philly not looking competitive, it might be worth sending him to a contender.
After all, Goedert remains a solid contributor at this stage of his career. The 31-year-old playmaker has converted 31 catches into 308 receiving yards and two touchdowns this season, all while drawing a 100.1 passer rating when targeted. It might not be a career performance for him, but the fact that he's averaging his second-most yards per game (44.0) over the last four seasons is pretty impressive.
Throw in the fact that he has 13 postseason games (11 starts) and a Super Bowl ring under his belt, and it's easy to see why the Eagles should be open to shopping him around.
This week not only marks the trade deadline but also the Eagles' bye. It's a good time to think about moving on from certain players, and Tanner McKee might fit the bill after being benched for Joe Milton in Week 9.
Milton's performance against the rival Giants wasn't perfect , but a lot of his struggles come from the rough shape that the Eagles' offensive line is in. He also didn't have a ton of time to prepare between being named the start and the game itself, which Sports Illustrated 's John McMullen made as clear as day on Monday.
Now that the bye is here, the Eagles can work harder to put Milton in a spot where they can take advantage of his big arm and mobility. At the same time, that could open the door to trading McKee, who's on an expiring contract and might not be re-signed in March. If the Eagles don't see him as part of their long-term plans anymore, why not trade him for something (even if it's a seventh-round pick)?
No one would blame the Eagles for starting their offensive line over from scratch after how this season has progressed. The group has already been hit by Lane Johnson's retirement and Cam Jurgens's trade, and even Landon Dickerson's name has picked up buzz before the deadline . That's why it won't be a surprise if Tyler Steen is the next departure.
Drafted 66th overall in 2023, the Alabama product hasn't been the same player he was last year for the Eagles. His 67.4 overall and 63.5 run-block grades on Pro Football Focus have regressed from last year's effort (73.3 and 73.0, respectively), and he's already allowed two sacks on 559 offensive snaps after allowing the same number over 1,080 opportunities in 2025.
Like Goedert and McKee, Steen will be an unrestricted free agent in March. With teams like the Vikings, for example, looking to strengthen their offensive line's interior, it's likely worth the Eagles' effort to see if they can get a decent return for a veteran who's potentially declining and out of time in Philadelphia.

title: Steelers vs. Super Bowl Champions: One Mark Isn't Good Enough
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were urged to add to their roster before this year's NFL Trade Deadline. Instead, they stood pat. They made no trades for a pass-catcher or any bolstering additions to an already impressive defense. The front office sent a crystal-clear message: the main pieces they assembled in the offseason are the ones they are relying on to finish the job in 2026.
That could be seen as a vote of confidence or an admission, depending on how you view the Steelers' roster. Now that we know who the team is running with, barring any free-agent additions, it's worth asking if this offense has what it takes to support a postseason run.
Looking through the past 10 teams to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, their offenses all shared one thing in common - they finished the regular season averaging at least 350 yards of offense per game. Sadly, the Steelers' offense isn't there yet, and without any upgrades at the deadline, it's unlikely they reach that point in 2026.
They say defenses win championships, and while that is certainly an important piece of winning in the NFL, having a well-structured and balanced offense is just as important.
The past 10 Super Bowl winners all had that in common. They didn't rank in the top five across all offensive statistical categories, but they did stand out in more than one way.
Total yards were consistent across all 10 winners. Each of those offenses averaged at least 350 yards of total offense per game at the end of the regular season. According to data compiled through ESPN, the Seattle Seahawks and the 2023 Kansas City Chiefs were the lowest-performing offenses in terms of total yards. Both teams averaged just over 351 yards per game. Last season, the Seahawks finished eighth in the NFL with 351.4 yards per game, while the '23 Chiefs finished ninth in the NFL that year with 351.3 yards per game.
The number 350 remains the benchmark for a Super Bowl-winning offense.
Through eight games, the Steelers are not meeting that mark. They have posted a respectable 328 yards per game, currently 16th in the NFL. It's also 23 yards more than they averaged in 2025 and nine yards higher than their 2024 offense.
Even with those improvements, the Steelers are still a bit short on reaching that 350 yards per game.
The best part of the Steelers' offense is undoubtedly the running game. Led by Jaylen Warren , the ground game wears defenses down and consistently puts up yards. Warren has single-handedly posted at least 90 rushing yards and 100 all-purpose yards or more in five of the last six contests.
That's led to the Steelers averaging 117.9 rushing yards per game, which ranks 12th in the NFL. That's the highest they rank in any major offensive category (yards per game, rushing yards per game, passing yards per game and points per game), and it's what the Steelers are putting all of their hope in for a postseason run.
But can the running game add even more to what is already an outstanding performance for the rest of the season?
If the Steelers are serious about a Super Bowl, they need to improve their offensive output by 22 yards per game. The run game might take them there, but a better path to that total yardage is improving their pedestrian passing game.
That's what made the Steelers' inaction at the NFL Trade Deadline so maddening. They have a glaring hole and draft capital that could have filled the void, but they took the passive route.
As a result, they don't have the personnel to reach that next level. So, despite the surprising record and plenty of positives to build on for the second half, it's hard to take this team seriously as a Super Bowl contender after another quiet deadline performance.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Defense Could Get Huge Boost for Bengals Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense could be receiving some major reinforcements ahead of a crucial Week 10 matchup on Sunday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that the Steelers are opening the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot), who is currently on the reserve/injured list.
It's not necessarily a guarantee that Harmon will be activated off of IR in time to play the Bengals, though it's certainly a huge step in the right direction and would signal that there's at least a solid chance that he'll return to the 53-man roster in the coming days.
Harmon was placed on IR after suffering his foot injury in the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.
The 2025 first-round pick has missed the required minimum of four contests while on IR, meaning he is eligible to be activated from IR at any time.
Before going down with his injury, Harmon had recorded 12 total tackles and 1.5 sacks. He also has a forced fumble, which came at the end of the fourth quarter vs. Cincinnati in Week 3 on a sack of Joe Burrow and clinched a 30-27 victory for the Steelers.
With Harmon's return appearing rather imminent, Pittsburgh is inching closer to having about as clean of a bill of health as it has had all season long.
Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is making progress while also residing on IR, and the same could be said for fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger).
Wilson cannot be activated until Week 11, though Pittman Jr. has missed the required minimum of four games, just like Harmon.
Pittman Jr.'s practice window has yet to be opened, and it appears as though he is trending towards missing this week's bout with the Bengals, but he should be back in the not-too-distant future.
Gennings Dunker (knee) also could potentially work his way back sooner rather than later, as he's at the end of his initial four-to-six week recovery timeline for an MCL sprain that landed him on IR in Week 3.
Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) might be staring down a long-term absence , perhaps for the entire season after being placed on IR in Week 7, though Harmon's impending return could help offset that loss.
While the Steelers opted not to swing any trades at the deadline, they're still set to supplement their roster in the back-half of their season considering the likes of Harmon, Pittman Jr. and Wilson are all progressing.

title: Ex-Steelers HC Mike Tomlin Leaves Door Open for Coaching Return
full_text:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin isn't thinking about his future in coaching at the moment, though he at least kept the door open for a return in that regard.
During a conference call with NBC correspondents before the Steelers ' Week 10 road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which Tomlin will be in attendance for as part of the network's "Football Night in America" crew, he stated that he hasn't "given one iota" of thought towards returning to an NFL sideline while admitting that it is a topic of discussion that will likely pop up down the line.
"I haven’t given one iota of thought to coaching," Tomlin said. "I’m sure some of that is going to come up in the not-so-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I get there."
While the end of his tenure with the Steelers wasn't always smooth, Tomlin's overall body of work with the franchise will undoubtedly be enough to make the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the future.
In his 19 years at the helm in Pittsburgh before stepping down after the 2025 campaign, not once did Tomlin finish with a losing record while compiling an overall record of 193-114-2 in the regular season.
The Steelers lost seven straight postseason games under Tomlin to close out his run with the team, but that shouldn't take away from the fact that he won Super Bowl XLIII with them in 2008 in addition to notching seven additional victories over 13 total trips to the playoffs.
Tied for the ninth-most head coaching wins in NFL history with fellow Pittsburgh legend Chuck Noll, Tomlin's legendary resume will always stand tall regardless of if he takes another job in the coming years or not.
If Tomlin does decide to jump into the coaching carousel, whether that be in 2027, 2028 or beyond, there's some uncertainty around whether or not Pittsburgh would be able to trade his rights and receive assets in return.
The New Orleans Saints were able to do so when Sean Payton stepped away after the 2021 season and was later hired by the Denver Broncos in 2023, but it's unknown if the Steelers can follow suit.
Should Pittsburgh still retain his contractual rights, it could potentially land a first-round pick (if not more) for Tomlin's services from whichever team hires him, which would greatly aid the organization's potential pursuit of a franchise quarterback.
Even if the Steelers can't trade Tomlin, his destination in the event that he returns to coaching could impact the team if he takes a job in the AFC and thus would have to face the black and gold semi-frequently.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Former Steelers Player and Coach Dick Hoak Passes Away
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Former Pittsburgh Steelers player and coach Dick Hoak passed away at the age of 86.
The native of Jeannette, Pennsylvania spent nearly five decades with the Steelers in some capacity, winning five Super Bowls with the franchise. He earned Pro Bowl honors once over his 10 seasons as a running back in the NFL, and he followed his playing career with a tremendous stint as a coach in the organization, helping the franchise capture five of their six Lombardi Trophies.
The former Pro Bowl running back was a legendary of the franchise’s history, and Steelers President Art Rooney II offered some heartfelt words on Hoak’s passing. The team shared his official statement via their team social media channels.
“We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family,” he stated. “Dick respresented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick’s contributions to the organization spanned generations.”
Steelers President Art Rooney II on the passing of Dick Hoak: pic.twitter.com/sPXZk1vtoB
Hoak first entered the Steelers organization during the 1961 NFL season, when the team drafted him out of Penn State in the seventh round of the 1961 NFL Draft.
As a rookie he played in 14 games, kicking off a career that spanned 10 seasons and 135 NFL games played. As a tailback, he amassed over 1,100 carries with the Steelers, producing 3,965 rushing yards and 25 touchdowns. He also added 146 receptions over his career for an additional 1,452 receiving yards and eight touchdowns.
The 1968 was Hoak’s peak season as a player. He ran for 858 rushing yards and three touchdowns, plus 253 receiving yards and another score. Those numbers earned him his sole Pro Bowl selection.
He ranks eighth on the Steelers' all-time rushing leaders.
It didn’t take long for Hoak to find an impact in a new role. He retired from the NFL following the 1970 season, but two years later he was right back with the Steelers. Head coach Chuck Noll hired Hoak as the running backs coach ahead of the 1972 campaign. The team went on to win four Super Bowls under his coaching.
Decades later, Noll retired and was replaced by Bill Cowher . The only position coach Cowher retained was Hoak.
He ended his coaching career with 35 seasons at the helm and earned his place as an inaugural member of the Steelers’ Hall of Honor.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Could Really Get Brandon Aiyuk Crazy
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers didn't end up with anyone at the NFL trade deadline. They had three names in mind at wide receiver, decided to pull away from each one for different reasons, and found themselves with the same 53-man roster they had going into deadline day.
They feel that's fine. Many fans feel the same way. And there's justification for not overpaying for a Brian Thomas Jr. or Josh Downs, and deciding not to pursue Calvin Ridley after an incident at the Nashville International Airport just days before the trade deadline.
Well, 24 hours ago, you'd laugh at the idea of Brandon Aiyuk. The thought seemed like a joke as the San Francisco 49ers welcomed him back to their building and now have a decision to make following the NFL's reinstatement of the 28-year-old wideout.
But what if it's not that far-fetched? What if the Steelers really could get Brandon Aiyuk crazy after the trade deadline?
Brandon Aiyuk speaks to the media. pic.twitter.com/mPZqaFdXXR
Speaking on the Steelers Collective podcast, I tossed Aiyuk out there, somewhat as a joke. My co-hosts Mark Kaboly and Ray Fittipaldo weren't laughing.
"I was told that that craziness that he did with the 49ers doesn't matter at all to them," Kaboly said.
"They don't care," he added.
Why wouldn't the Steelers consider Aiyuk? They chased him all summer in 2024 because they wanted him to come to Pittsburgh and be their WR1. They wouldn't need to sign him to their active roster, but instead to their practice squad.
If he shows he can still play at a high level and is maintaining a good attitude in the locker room, you add him to your 53-man roster. And if he's even close to as good as he was before the injury, the Steelers just landed the best available wide receiver at the deadline without making a trade.
It's a huge win for Pittsburgh at a time when everyone thought they lost.
This team likes their wide receiver room when everyone is healthy . They don't need a superstar but rather quality depth, just in case they find themselves in the same boat they're in now, later in the season.
Aiyuk does that and more, if he can still play well. And when you factor in the minimal risk you take in adding a player like that to your practice if/when he's released by the 49ers, it makes all the sense in the world.
Maybe the Steelers really will land Brandon Aiyuk after all.

title: Former Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson Takes Shot at Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from former third-round draft pick Kaleb Johnson before the regular season began. After an uninspiring performance in training camp and the preseason, the team decided to cut ties with the second-year running back.
After that decision, the Steelers sent Johnson to the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a draft pick. It was an unceremonious end to his time in Pittsburgh, but it was clear he’d get a better shot at playing time in Green Bay.
With the Packers starting running back, Josh Jacobs, leaving their Week 9 contest with an injury, it allowed Johnson that chance. In response, he had a career game, posting 68 rushing yards on 14 carries and his first NFL touchdown.
After the game, Johnson shared some major love for his quarterback, Jordan Love. According to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman, Johnson has a clear preference when it comes to the two quarterbacks he’s played with, and it’s not Aaron Rodgers.
”I’ve had two good quarterbacks,” he said. “Aaron and him, but I like Jordan better.”
Kaleb Johnson on Jordan Love: "I’ve had two good quarterbacks, Aaron and him, but I like Jordan better."
While Johnson has had the privilege of playing with two good quarterbacks, he hasn’t had the luxury of being a good running back with two franchises.
During his time with the Steelers, he was a bust of a draft pick. Despite having a ton of talent and a hard-working attitude every day he was a member of the franchise, he couldn’t produce or build trust. In 10 games as a rookie, he carried the ball 28 times and posted just 69 yards. That was good for an average of 2.5 yards per carry and the longest run he broke off was a nine-yard rush.
The nail in the coffin came early into his rookie season. Being used as a kick returner, he fumbled an attempt and that cost him the rest of the 2025 campaign. From that point on, he was relegated to the bench or inactive on game day.
Meanwhile, the Steelers have found new life in their ground game thanks to Jaylen Warren. Heading into the 2025 season, there was a belief that Johnson could supplant Warren as the go-to back in Pittsburgh.
Fast forward one year later, and Warren is one of the best running backs in the NFL this season. He’s almost single-handedly leading the Steelers’ offense, exceeding 100 yards from scrimmage in five of the last six games and 704 total rushing yards through eight games.
It might sound harsh, but the Steelers don’t miss Johnson, even as he finds success in Green Bay.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Wanted Three WRs and Failed
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers did nothing at the NFL trade deadline . That wasn't the goal, but it's how it ended, and they didn't look good because of it.
Going into the deadline, the Steelers had two positions they were targeting: wide receiver and cornerback. Wideout was the frontrunner for an addition, while cornerback was more of a best-case-scenario outcome. If something worked out for both, great. If not, no big deal.
But they didn't walk away with anyone. That doesn't mean they didn't try, though.
General manager Omar Khan had his sights on three names as November 10 approached. Those names were Josh Downs, Brian Thomas Jr. and Calvin Ridley.
Ridley became an afterthought after an incident at the Nashville International Airport happened It over the weekend. Once that occurred, the Steelers pivoted, removing Ridley from their list and focusing on Downs and Thomas Jr.
Eventually, the Jacksonville Jaguars made it clear that they weren't dealing Thomas Jr., and the Kansas City Chiefs landed Josh Downs with fourth- and fifth-round picks.
And the Steelers left with nothing.
The Steelers have a decent wide receiver room when healthy, and they weren't going to make the over-the-top move to add to that room that they needed. WR1 couldn't happen with any of the options available via trade.
But depth could've been added, and it was needed for Pittsburgh. This team has already been hit with multiple injuries and have half the season left. Now, they need to hope they don't find themselves shorthanded once again.
If they do, they look like deadline losers, plain and simple.
Targeting three wide receivers and not walking away with anyone is a bad look. It shows that they were too narrow in on certain names, and truthfully, those names were so all over the place that they could have, and should have, pivoted.
Why only chase Ridley and not Jauan Jennings or Keenan Allen? Why only chase Thomas Jr. and not Quentin Johnston or Dontavion Wicks? And why not try to match the offer for Downs?
The names were too abundant to miss and yet the Steelers did. And don't get it wrong, not enough names got moved, but that doesn't mean they weren't available. Chances are, they were.
Pittsburgh watched plenty of other AFC contenders get better at the deadline while they didn't. Now, it's about hoping they're good enough to beat them.
Only time will tell, but leaving November 10 and heading into the back half of the season, the Steelers sure look like they failed.

title: What If Steelers Wait for Brandon Aiyuk?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have stayed quiet at the NFL trade deadline to this point. Maybe they'll stay quiet the entire time, not adding a name via trade and moving into the back half of their schedule without an addition.
Or maybe they wait for Brandon Aiyuk.
According to NFL insider Mike Florio, the San Francisco 49ers will likely release Aiyuk. Aiyuk was reinstated by the NFL this week after returning to the 49ers over the weekend. He passed his physical and, if released, would be available to sign with another team - if another team is interested.
There's no hiding Aiyuk's troubled past in the NFL. After signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers in 2024, Aiyuk played just seven games before suffering a torn ACL. He then didn't return to the team in 2025 as the two sides feuded throughout the summer.
He never returned until last week when he began working with the team to be reinstated.
We all watched the Steelers chase after Aiyuk during the 2024 summer, trying to land the wide receiver in a trade with the 49ers. They were close, but never finalized anything, pushing Aiyuk toward a deal with San Francisco and beginning what has felt like an endless loop of trying to find a veteran wideout in Pittsburgh.
So, what if they go after him now? If Aiyuk becomes available, why wouldn't the Steelers consider it? They still need veteran depth in their wide receiver room, have had interest in him before and wouldn't need to trade anything for him.
Instead, they'd be signing him to a vet minimum contract, and chances are, he'd start on their practice squad. Once brought up to speed, he's only 28 years old and who knows what he has left in the tank, but it could definitely be a lot.
If the Steelers like their wide receiver room , which they clearly do, why not consider a younger addition for depth? That's all they were looking for all along. And Aiyuk is very clearly the most exciting option with the most upside.
At one point, the hope that Pittsburgh would land Aiyuk felt like it lasted months, maybe years. It's been a while, but why not have that desire emerge again? It certainly makes sense for what they're looking for.
Great news for the Rams, the Seahawks and the Chiefs. https://t.co/h2afpBAsti
The Steelers are Super Bowl contenders in the AFC . They watched the Buffalo Bills, Denver Broncos and Jacksonville Jaguars make moves at the trade deadline. They didn't do anything to respond.
But that opportunity hasn't passed them by. Because if Aiyuk becomes available, they could consider a name with plenty of talent who could truly change the upside of this team in 2026.
A move that could could taken them to the next level. And one that comes without a big trade.
So, what if the Steelers wait for Brandon Aiyuk?

title: Another Trade Deadline With Nothing to Show for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were supposed to go for it ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. With quarterback Aaron Rodgers bidding farewell to the NFL after this season, plus a Super Bowl-caliber defense, it should have been enough to compel general manager Omar Khan to go get that missing piece.
Then the Steelers went 6-2, exiting their bye week at the top of the AFC North standings. Things are going swimmingly for head coach Mike McCarthy halfway through his first season with his hometown team. A trade felt imminent. The roster deserved a dose of positivity for the stretch run.
Yet in the most Steelers fashion ever, the team did nothing. Plenty of players were available, but instead of going all-in, Khan stood pat. Now we can say definitively that the key additions during the 2026 season are headlined by plucking a pair of defensive backs from other teams' practice squads and bringing back wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling after the Los Angeles Chargers released him. Another deadline passes with an unsatisfying conclusion, and at this point we are all fools for believing they would do anything other than what they always do at the deadline.
The Steelers' big move was staring us in the face all along. Following their Week 6 victory, they signed the recently released MVS to their practice squad. This marked his second time with the organization, following a five-game stint in Pittsburgh in 2025.
During those five games, quarterback Aaron Rodgers targeted MVS a total of 21 times, connecting for 10 receptions. That amounted to 80 yards and a touchdown, far from the type of game-changing production the offense needed.
This season hasn't been any different for the former 690-yard receiver with the Green Bay Packers. He appeared in three games with the Chargers at the beginning of the 2026 campaign, collecting just two receptions for 22 yards.
Despite all of that, he has the one thing that means more than talent or productivity in Pittsburgh: a connection with Rodgers and McCarthy. Thanks to their time together in Green Bay, Rodgers trusts him, and McCarthy believes in him.
The Steelers are at the top of the AFC North, and if they defeat the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, they have a strong chance of winning the division for a second consecutive season. And they've gotten there without a strong passing game.
Despite that, their inaction at the deadline proves that they are not legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Compare it to the other top AFC teams - the Buffalo Bills and the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Steelers watched those contenders upgrade their rosters. The Bills added a starting safety, and the Jaguars added multiple pieces to their defense.
Meanwhile, the Steelers provided no roster upgrades. They didn't give their vulnerable secondary any depth reinforcements, and they didn't give Rodgers any better options to throw to.
But we shouldn't be surprised by this at all. The Steelers do nothing at the trade deadline, save for adding random parts like they are at the checkout line of a grocery store. It's a yearly occurrence. This year felt different, partly because so much has changed around the organization, but some things remain completely the same.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Trade Rumor Tracker: 2026 Deadline News & Updates
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline mere hours away at 4:00 p.m. EST, the clock is ticking for the Pittsburgh Steelers to swing any deals.
Sitting in a tie with the Cincinnati Bengals atop the AFC North at 6-2, with a matchup between the two sides on Sunday Night Football in order in Week 10, the Steelers have an incentive to go out and add to their roster.
Whether it's for a wide receiver , which has long felt like Pittsburgh's priority, or even for a cornerback, it's no sure thing that general manager Omar Khan will find a suitable deal out there.
Khan has made trades in three of his four trade deadlines as the Steelers' GM, with the most recent example coming last year when he sent a 2026 sixth-round pick to the New England Patriots for safety Kyle Dugger and a 2026 seventh-rounder.
While Pittsburgh is on a four-game win streak as it exits its Week 9 bye and gets ready to face the Bengals on the road in primetime, an upgrade somewhere across its roster could do wonders for the team as it looks to cement itself as a top contender in the AFC.
With that, let's take a look at the rumors surrounding the Steelers before the deadline arrives.
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer has reported that the Tennessee Titans are doing making moves and that wide receiver Calvin Ridley will remain with the team, meaning Pittsburgh will not be acquiring him.
With less than half an hour to go before the deadline passes, the Steelers lost out on yet another potential wide receiver target.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Indianapolis Colts have traded Josh Downs and a seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for a package including a fourth-rounder.
ESPN's Adam Schefter later confirmed that Kansas City would also be sending a fifth-round pick to Indianapolis as part of the deal.
BREAKING: The #Colts are trading WR Josh Downs to the #Chiefs for a package that includes a 4th-round pick, per sources. A new weapon for Patrick Mahomes. https://t.co/SepYaJPiA6 pic.twitter.com/Iod5l2hBav
Downs was arguably Pittsburgh's top target at the position and was connected to the team on multiple occasions, but the organization struck out in its pursuit of the 25-year-old.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts are trading wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
Trade! The Colts are sending six-time Pro Bowl WR Keenan Allen to the 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/tDt5H7HgId
Allen (who has 351 yards and a touchdown over eight games this season) was one of several veterans on expiring deals who were at least hypothetical targets for Pittsburgh, though the organization will now have to look elsewhere if he was on its radar.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jacksonville Jaguars plan on holding onto wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. through today's trade deadline after acquiring Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux on November 9.
"The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources," Fowler wrote. "They have relayed that to interested teams.
"Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise."
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
Thomas Jr. was one of the top receivers involved in trade rumors over recent weeks given his dwindling role in Jacksonville.
The 2024 first-round pick, who had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie, had been floated as a potential fit for Pittsburgh as it looks to upgrade its receiver room and generate more explosive plays in the passing game.
For now, though, it seems as though the Steelers won't have the opportunity to acquire him ahead of the deadline.
During an appearance on "The Aftermath" on November 9, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated that Pittsburgh "doesn't want to give up a lot of draft capital" in order to acquire a receiver while naming Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley as a player who might "make sense in that regard."
The Steelers have 18 picks between the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, though their lack of a fourth-rounder in the first of those two years could hurt their pursuit of some of the top receivers on the trade block, such as Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts.
The names who could entice Pittsburgh at a cheaper price include Ridley and Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) now that Allen is heading to San Francisco.
In addition to their pursuit of a wide receiver, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on November 9 that the Steelers also want a cornerback.
My over/under on trades by tomorrow is 10.5, and I’m taking the over. Here’s everything I’ve heard on who’s buying and which positions they’re targeting after speaking with sources: pic.twitter.com/KbrHfUNVLo
Pittsburgh could use another option on the boundary alongside the likes of Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette after previously trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.
Riq Woolen (Philadelphia Eagles), Donte Jackson (Los Angeles Chargers) and Mike Sainristil (Washington Commanders) are among the top names to watch if the Steelers do go out and bring in a corner.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Has Great News For Multiple Key Starters
full_text:
It’s time for the first injury report of the week courtesy of the Seattle Seahawks and Las Vegas Raiders. Obviously, the Seahawks are in a fairly injured state , and the fanbase is eager to see at least some of those players start going in the right direction so they can play again. We won’t get everything we want today, but we definitely got a few things we needed.
A.J. Barner (finger) was added to the report, quite possibly from the touchdown ‘catch’ last week, but is a full participant regardless. The highlight of the day is definitely Rashid Shaheed (knee) getting to full status, after not practicing at all last week . It’s a strong indication that he’ll be on the field this Sunday, to help an offense that could really use his downfield speed.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Jarran Reed both sat for non-injury reasons. That’s the easy stuff. The pool of limited players includes Anthony Bradford (knee), Derick Hall (back) , Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Connor O’Toole (foot). Offhand, I would expect all five of those players to play on Sunday, but any injury is noteworthy.
Nwosu’s return to practice is particularly significant, as he attempted a similar timeline last week with a limited practice on Wednesday before getting banished back to DNP the next two days. Hopefully this time, whatever setback or occurrence caused him to hit the bench doesn’t happen and he’s able to progress. The other injuries strike me as management ones.
Finally, Charles Cross (ankle), Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep), Quenton Nelson (knee), Brandon Pili (back), and Leonard Williams (stinger) were the DNPs of the day. Pili and Williams apparently did some light work before practice, so progress is being made and they still have a chance this week. I would assume the first three, however, are waiting for after the bye week.
The Raiders have been among the healthiest teams in the NFL this year, and they’re currently sitting quite pretty in terms of possible absences this weekend. The team had only four players listed on their report, and one of them was a full participant. That player, Ian Thomas (ankle), is a third string tight end who sees only occasional snaps.
Thomas Booker (ankle) and Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) are limited today, and that’s not an insignificant one-two, since they combine to be a significant chunk of the Raiders’ interior defensive line. Trey Zuhn (concussion) was also limited, the backup center who has gotten little action so far this year. Otherwise, the Raiders look quite healthy and ready to roll.

title: Seahawks Standing Pat At Trade Deadline is Good News for Rashid Shaheed
full_text:
Personally, I think the Seattle Seahawks sitting the trade deadline out was probably the right thing to do. I wouldn’t have objected to a move (although I would have objected to some), but I’m just not convinced a player acquisition moves the needle right now. Some may disagree, which I can certainly understand. But consider the implication of standing pat.
Per reports leading into the deadline , the Seahawks were believed to be on the lookout for a wide receiver. Whether those reports were accurate is debatable, but it’s fairly believable. Once you get past the great Jaxon Smith-Njigba, things aren’t great in the receiver room. The report even directly said they wanted a wide receiver to complement JSN.
Cooper Kupp is too old to get much done on the field, Tory Horton isn’t ready for a bigger role, and Montorie Foster Jr is a fun training camp story that hasn’t shown up in games yet. Yet still, the Seahawks did not make a trade. Perhaps they simply couldn’t find a deal worth making, but also consider the one Seattle wide receiver I didn’t mention in this section yet.
Rashid Shaheed injured his knee a couple weeks ago against the Kansas City Chiefs and has been absent from the field on gameday since. When the report about the Seahawks wanting a wide receiver came out, it was a reasonable assumption that the injury was serious. Given that the team was willing to come up empty-handed, perhaps that’s not the case.
Perhaps the desire to acquire a wide receiver was more about the long-term. Maybe they wanted someone young and promising who could spend the rest of this season acclimating themselves to the team, and then be able to slide right in to take Kupp’s job in 2027. A good idea, but not something so dire that it absolutely had to get done right this moment.
If this read is correct, then Rashid Shaheed should be back soon. As in, after the bye week at the latest. And once he gets back, he’ll be able to play effective football. Good enough to suffice as this offense tries to find itself on the back half of the season. Despite his low production thus far, Shaheed remains a great speed threat with excellent hands.
To my eyes, Shaheed is getting open and doing his job, he’s just not getting the ball very often due to JSN getting all the targets. He’s also not exactly a clean fit for this offense right now, with much of his value coming as a deep threat and this offense rarely pushing it down the field . Hopefully, when he gets back on the field, that changes.

title: Seahawks Have Clear Game Plan vs. Raiders in Week 10
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 10 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders , which will require them to really dig into the team's depth.
It's the final game before their bye week, so injuries are beginning to pile up . They need to lock in and compete against a Raiders squad that is hungry to beat them. Coached by former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, the Raiders should be pulling out all the stops and tricks up their sleeve this week.
The big key for a Seahawks victory will be relying on the run game to take the lead with Sam Darnold and Drew Lock both dealing with injuries.
"He has some sort of oblique," Macdonald said of Lock. "We're going to put a game plan together and we expect him to be able to play. So it should be a similar approach to last week, I would imagine."
No team allows more rushing yards per game than the Raiders this season. Las Vegas has given up 1,361 yards on the ground in nine games, good for around 151.2 per contest. It's by far the most in the NFL and part of the reason the team has won just one of its last six games.
On top of that, the Raiders rank 29th in the league in time of possession, only holding the ball for 28:33 per game. Meanwhile, the Seahawks are 9th in the league at 30:40. The Seahawks will be able to play into that by racking up yards on the ground with their two-man rushing attack that has been trying to build momentum over the last two weeks.
Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price have only been back for two games, and they are still trying to figure out what roles each will play. In Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, Price had more of a workload than Charbonnet, but their roles flipped in Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals.
The Seahawks were forced to play from behind against the Bears, but when they held a lead against the Cardinals, they ran for 120 yards as a team while holding possession for 31:39. That's the kind of game plan that wins football games, and it's what they will need to lean into as they face off against the Raiders in Week 10.

title: Why Nick Emmanwori is Seahawks X-Factor on Defense vs. Raiders
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive back Nick Emmanwori is the jack-of-all-trades when it comes to the team's defense.
Emmanwori can play safety, linebacker, and even defensive end. His ability to play on all three levels of the defense makes him one of the most dangerous players in the league. His versatility was on full display against the Arizona Cardinals , where he was tasked with defending All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, holding him to 54 yards during the game.
"We asked him to match up a few times and he did a great job," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said in a press conference.
"I think he had a great mentality throughout the week. He was on his details and I think you saw that kind of manifest itself in the game by him just letting it rip and playing a great game. I mean, we asked him to blitz, we asked him to cover. Obviously the play in the red zone was awesome and then we had a plan for him to rush as well. We just weren't able to get to some of those situations that we wanted to."
After dealing with an early-season ankle injury, Emmanwori is 100 percent and slowly getting better as the season rolls along. His ability to defend strong tight ends like McBride will come in handy in the second half of the season.
It wouldn't be a surprise to see the Seahawks utilize Emmanwori in a similar way in Week 10 when the team takes on the Las Vegas Raiders, who boast one of the best tight ends in the league in Brock Bowers.
In seven appearances with the Raiders this season, Bowers has recorded at least 70 yards in each of his games. His 658 yards rank ninth in the NFL and first among tight ends. If the Seahawks want to win in Week 10, containing Bowers will be the key to their success. Based on how they lined up against the Cardinals, it looks like Emmanwori should be part of the plan.
Kickoff between the Seahawks and Raiders is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: Why the Seahawks Didn't Act in the Final Hours of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made a big trade during the regular season for the fourth consecutive year. The Seahawks traded for guard Quenton Nelson a few weeks before the NFL Trade Deadline was set to pass.  With the Seahawks being a fringe playoff team, there was some debate that the team would make one more move in the final hours of the Trade Deadline .
​The Seahawks’ front office decided to hang back and avoid any more trades while other teams bought for their chance to win now or sell for the future. Whether the front office made the wrong decision remains to be seen. Regardless, the Seahawks like their plan ahead of them with their roster and their future with their draft plans.
​There were reports in the weeks leading up to the Trade Deadline, after trading for Nelson, that the Seahawks were looking into upgrading the roster. There were reports on Tuesday that Seattle was looking for a legitimate No. 2 wide receiver . The Seahawks had every option to get traded players like wide receiver Caleb Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Other veterans could have been available, such as Cleveland's Jerry Jeudy or Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr.
​Ultimately, the Seahawks might be confident in their roster; this includes wide receiver. Among some of the biggest reasons for the sloppy first half of the season are the struggles from offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and the injuries on both sides of the field.
The Seahawks might have more plans for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed once he recovers from his knee injury. Two starters are also out along each of the offensive and defensive lines. Once injuries aren’t a factor, there is some stability.
​One of the biggest and most likely reasons for the Seahawks to avoid making more trades at the deadline is because they like the talent coming out of the 2027 NFL Draft. The Seahawks are likely going to have potentially 9-to-12 first-round picks due to compensatory picks from the departing players, coaches and front office personnel. There is a real conversation that the Seahawks avoided those trades in order to keep multiple picks.
​The Seahawks need the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft to draft a potential franchise edge rusher, a No. 2 receiver, some help at the offensive line, including a potential starting center and some depth along the defensive line. There might need to be a conversation about the Seahawks going for a franchise quarterback, with Sam Darnold struggling and having the final expensive year and Drew Lock set to be a free agent.
​General manager John Schneider makes excellent trades, as indicated by the four veteran trades. He also uses the draft to quickly reload and build for the future. The Seahawks can remain competitive now and in the future.

title: 3 Positions Seahawks Should Have Targeted at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were quiet at the trade deadline , making their Oct. 27 deal to acquire guard Quenton Nelson their only move . It was rumored the Seahawks had interest in multiple other players, but they either backed off or were turned down in each of those potential deals.
With injuries piling up midseason, a few positions stood out as priorities for Seattle at the deadline. The Seahawks don't have any blatant holes, but there were some potential missed opportunities if they're hoping to bolster another Super Bowl run.
Here are three position groups the Seahawks could have tried to get better at before the trade deadline.
Even when Uchenna Nwosu is healthy, the Seahawks essentially only have three high-quality players to fill two spots. Nwosu has missed the last two games, and it's hurt Seattle's pass rush overall. Seattle totaled 17 sacks in its first seven games, but has just four over the last two since Nwosu has been out.
The Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat, Los Angeles Chargers' Khalil Mack and New York Jets' Will McDonald were all names floated around the league as potential trade options, and all would have made the Seahawks' defense better.
For now, the Seahawks will continue to rely more on Dante Fowler Jr. and Connor O'Toole as their options behind DeMarcus Lawrence and Derick Hall until Nwosu returns.
This isn't an absolute need, but Rashid Shaheed's absence has taken a slight dimension out of the Seahawks' offense. Shaheed has now missed two games in a row, making the Seahawks' top-3 receivers Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton.
The Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley and Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs, among others, could have been depth options for the Seahawks, but they likely couldn't have justified the price of either player. Especially if Shaheed comes back soon, they would quickly fall to fourth on the depth chart.
In the short term, it would have been a win. However, in the long term, it wouldn't have made enough sense for the front office to pull the trigger. Most targets will continue to flow to Smith-Njigba anyways.
Trading for a running back would have been a premium move. Before this season, the Seahawks have had a ton of high-quality depth since 2022. That's what's been lacking this season, even with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back healthy.
Charbonnet and Price can be a good duo, but they've both been injured. Acquiring a running back could have provided some insurance at the position that is better than George Holani or Emanuel Wilson.
Obviously, Jonathan Taylor would have been the swinging-for-the-fences type of move, but the Colts wouldn't let him go. And there's no solid evidence that the Seahawks were even still inquiring late in the trade cycle. However, it would have been a potential season-altering deal.

title: Why the Seahawks Didn't Trade for Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are sitting back as Jonathan Taylor stays put while the NFL trade deadline comes and goes.
The Seahawks were reportedly interested in trading for the Indianapolis Colts' star running back, but the team opted not to make the deal. Instead, they acquired Quenton Nelson in exchange for a third- and fifth-round pick. Here is why the Seahawks ultimately chose to move on:
The Seahawks were unwilling to negotiate a contract with Kenneth Walker III in free agency. Walker signed a $43 million contract over three years, while Taylor is on the books for a two-year, $44 million contract.
If the Seahawks were unwilling to pay Walker's contract, they certainly weren't going to do the same for Taylor. The team also has several other options in the running back room.
The main reason behind the Seahawks not making the Taylor trade is because they believe in Charbonnet and Price as a dynamic backfield that can get the job done.
Price is a first-round pick who is under team control for the next five seasons at a reasonable cost. Charbonnet, although he is a free agent at the end of the season, is someone they have relied on for the past four seasons.
Charbonnet recorded 77 yards on 16 carries in the team's Week 9 win against the Cardinals, which is a sign that he is slowly getting back in a groove after he tore his ACL during the team's Divisional Round matchup against the San Francisco 49ers back in January.
"Super happy for Zach," Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba said postgame via the team's website . "Everyone has seen the work and all the grit it takes for him to get back on the field. He played great today. We're going to need him throughout the remainder of the season. So, happy for him today."
The Seahawks are also excited to see what Price can do as he continues to grow in his first season.
"I thought he was decisive with his runs," Macdonald said of Price via the team's website.
"Sometimes he's the primary in some of those pass concepts. Sometimes he's kind of at the end of the progression and when the ball finds him, if you can make a guy miss, it's a great example. It doesn't have to be some extraordinary play to create explosives, but let's just be efficient with our decision making and get it in our player's hands and let him do the rest. So again, he's another example. I think he's just going to continue to get better now that he's kind of stacking weeks and he's getting healthier, that'll help us."
The Seahawks are investing a lot in Charbonnet and Price , and to throw all of that away for half of the season of Taylor would not be a wise investment.

title: Seahawks Are NFL Trade Deadline Winners After Kirk Cousins Deal
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are facing off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 , but they won't be facing off against quarterback Kirk Cousins.
The Raiders traded Cousins just hours before the deadline to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft , which opens the door for Fernando Mendoza to make his first career start.
Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, now has the reins of the Raiders offense, but he won't have it easy facing off against the Seahawks in his first game.
This will mark the second straight week the Seahawks will face off against someone in their first start of the season. Gardner Minshew made his first start for the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, and his team clearly struggled by only getting up by three points during the game. The Seahawks went on to win 17-3.
Mendoza was placed behind Cousins on the depth chart, and he could have moved on to the rookie at any point, but Las Vegas got a lot out of the veteran. The team started out 3-0, but they have won just one of their last six games, though Cousins was not the reason behind their struggles.
In nine games this season, Cousins threw for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He joins the Vikings, who are looking to lead them to the playoffs as a 6-2 team, but it doesn't affect the Seahawks current schedule since Minnesota does not play Seattle at any point this season.
With Mendoza under center for the Raiders, the Seahawks' chances of winning the game should greatly improve. A win would take them to 6-4 going into their Week 11 bye. The Seahawks can't underestimate the No. 1 overall pick, who will have a strong game plan formed by former Seattle offensive coordinator and now-Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, but they will likely smell blood in the water.
Mendoza will make his first start for the Raiders as they are set to host the Seahawks on Sunday at 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: NFL Playoff Picture Update Provides Hope for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are creeping closer to the playoff picture after their 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals.
While they may not be in the playoff picture after Week 9, they have a strong outlook as they enter the second half of the season. Here's a look at what the playoff picture looks like at the halfway point:
1. San Francisco 49ers, 7-1-0 (1st NFC West) 2. Chicago Bears, 7-2-0 (1st NFC North) 3. New York Giants, 5-2-1 (1st NFC East) 4. Carolina Panthers, 3-5-0 (1st NFC South) 5. Detroit Lions, 6-2-0 (Wild Card) 6. Minnesota Vikings, 6-2-0 (Wild Card) 7. Green Bay Packers, 6-3-0 (Wild Card) 8. Seattle Seahawks, 5-4-0 9. Los Angeles Rams, 5-4-0 10. Dallas Cowboys, 4-5-0 11. New Orleans Saints, 3-5-0 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 3-6-0 13. Atlanta Falcons, 3-6-0 14. Arizona Cardinals, 3-6-0 15. Washington Commanders, 2-5-1 16. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-7-0
The Seahawks are not in the same position they were in a year ago, as they have already racked up more losses this season than they had all of last year. In a competitive NFC playoff picture, that puts them on the outside looking in. That said, the second half of the season should provide many opportunities for the team to jump into the top seven, with a chance to return to the postseason.
As the weeks go by, their chances of winning the NFC West are becoming slimmer. The San Francisco 49ers are 2.5 games ahead of the Seahawks and hold the tiebreaker following their Week 5 win against Seattle at Lumen Field. This means the Seahawks are likely targeting a wild card spot, which is more attainable just one game behind the Green Bay Packers for the No. 7 seed.
The NFC North occupies four of the top seven spots in the NFC at the moment. All four of those teams have the strongest schedule difficulties left in the season, mainly because each team still has 3-4 divisional matchups left in the second half of the year.
The NFC North teams are bound to beat up on each other, which means at least one will likely fall by the wayside and miss the playoffs. Since the NFL adopted the 14-team playoff format which made it possible for all four teams to reach the postseason, it has not been accomplished. However, a third-place team has qualified for the playoffs, much like the 49ers did last year in the NFC West.
On top of that, the Los Angeles Rams are arguably their biggest competition in the NFC West, especially with two games in the final three weeks of the season on Seattle's schedule. The team just placed star wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve, which means the team is down another top target after Davante Adams went down a few weeks back.
The Seahawks will still have to execute themselves , but their outlook is promising given how the stock is dropping with other contenders alongside them.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Why Seahawks Are Down Despite Win vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back over .500 after a 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 inside Lumen Field.
Their 5-4 record keeps them in the hunt for a playoff spot, but there are certainly causes for concern. Here's a look at where the Seahawks stand in power rankings across the internet.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 6
Conor Orr moved the Seahawks down six spots despite their win, which is more of a sign as to where the team stands with their quarterback situation than anything.
"It’s the Drew Lock show for Seattle once again," Orr wrote. "I think it’s time to revisit a Sam Darnold column we wrote at the beginning of the season. How soon before we have the conversation about Seattle’s QB situation?"
ESPN moved them back one more spot after going down three spaces last week, which shows that winning isn't everything when it comes to the power rankings.
The power rankings also highlight the team's Week 12 contest against the San Francisco 49ers, citing it as the most important game in the second half of the season.
Ranking: 11 | Last week: 9
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff worked together for The Athletic and says the Seahawks need to start stacking some wins as they go into the second half of the season.
"They’re still weathering the storm of Sam Darnold injuries (and now Drew Lock may have to play through an injury), but the defense remains a top-five group, and there’s hope for what the running game will become now that Jadarian Price is back. Still, they haven’t won consecutive games since the first two weeks of the season," The Athletic wrote.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 13
Bleacher Report contributor Moe Moton highlighted the team's inconsistencies on offense as the reason why they aren't higher, even though they take one step forward in the website's power rankings.
"Entering Week 10, Darnold is nursing quad and rib injuries, and Lock has an oblique injury. With so much uncertainty at quarterback and the passing game's recent limitations and inefficiencies, it's hard to feel confident about the Seahawks' short-term outlook," Moton wrote.
Ranking: 14 | Last week: 14
Pete Prisco has Seattle at No. 14 for the second straight week, but he thinks things could turn around in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
"They are fighting through quarterback injuries, but it looks like Drew Lock will play against the Raiders this week. The Raiders might be the perfect tonic to get the offense going," Prisco wrote.
No matter how good the Seahawks' defense is performing, the team will always be looked at for their quarterback situation. As long as Darnold is underperforming, the Seahawks will not be viewed as a true Super Bowl contender in the NFC.
This year, there are several teams in the NFC that have improved from a year ago, and the Seahawks aren't one of them. That said, if they can stack some wins in the second half of the season and stay healthy after their bye week, they should be a team nobody wants to face come playoff time.

title: Why the 49ers May Regret Choosing Keenan Allen Over a Younger WR
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have announced a trade to acquire Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
On paper, the move makes sense. It gives San Francisco a potential future Hall of Famer for the short term while only costing a sixth-round pick. To be fair, it's about as straightforward a move as you might expect.
That said, the 49ers were linked with multiple other receivers, many of whom were considerably younger. There are a few reasons to suggest San Francisco could end up regretting its decision not to pursue one of those alternatives.
Targeting someone younger could have given the 49ers a potential long-term replacement for Ricky Pearsall . He's entering his third season, and there's no guarantee San Francisco will exercise his fifth-year option following the 2027 season.
Injuries have plagued his career so far, making his long-term future with the team less certain given his lack of availability. His rookie season can be excused, but the injuries suffered over the past two seasons are something the 49ers will have to keep in mind when deciding whether to commit to him long-term.
Allen will likely only be on the roster until the end of this season, but it proves a point about their receiving corps in general.
The vast majority of the receivers playing for San Francisco are already 30 or older. George Kittle, Mike Evans and Brandin Cooks are all 33, DeMarcus Robinson is 32, KhaDarel Hodge is 31, and Deebo Samuel is 30.
Bringing in another veteran does little to address the team's longer-term needs at the position. Sooner rather than later, a massive rebuild will have to be made on offense.
Bringing in someone with Allen's experience is certainly a positive, but there's a legitimate argument that experience shouldn't necessarily outweigh the potential of a younger receiver who has also impressed.
Ultimately, the decision to bring Allen in reinforces the idea that San Francisco is reluctant to part with significant draft capital ahead of what could be an inevitable partial rebuild. That transition could arrive sooner rather than later, making the decision to prioritise a short-term veteran over a younger option all the more questionable.
Can they rely on De'Zhaun Stribling and Jordan Watkins to become the future of the franchise in this position? I'm not so sure. Let's see what unfolds.

title: Why the 49ers Traded for Keenan Allen Instead of Josh Downs
full_text:
It was clear that the San Francisco 49ers wanted to add a wide receiver prior to the NFL trade deadline.
They attempted to acquire Jauan Jennings from the Minnesota Vikings a week ago, but he declined. The 49ers needed to pivot and ultimately brokered a deal with the Indianapolis Colts for 34-year-old veteran Keenan Allen .
It's a bit odd the 49ers went after Allen and not Josh Downs. Not only is Downs younger, but he’s the more explosive and better receiver. He would’ve helped the 49ers stretch the field and delivered a greater impact.
However, the reason the 49ers traded for Allen instead of Downs is simple — he was cheaper. The 49ers sent the Colts a 2027 sixth-round pick for Allen, while Downs went for a 2027 fourth- and fifth-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs.
Downs is a better receiver than Allen, but he isn’t that much better to justify that haul of draft picks. I had advocated for the 49ers to acquire Downs, but for a fifth-round pick and nothing more.
If the Colts wanted multiple Day 3 picks from the 49ers, then they were right to stand pat. They’re not going to give up multiple picks for a player who will only help them for 8-plus games.
Besides, the 49ers going after Allen means they like his fit over Downs, and it has to do with Mike Evans , who will most likely be out for a few more games with Achilles tendinitis. They’ve lost their go-to receiver for short-yardage conversions.
Allen is one of the best receivers in that realm. On throws under 10 air yards, Allen has caught 31-of-38 targets for 230 yards and one touchdown, the seventh-most yards among wide receivers, per NFL Pro.
Brock Purdy will regain an outlet he can go to quickly for a first-down conversion or around the goal line. Allen can’t dominate with the goal-line fade like Evans, but he’s still a fairly sharp route runner.
He’s probably their second-best route-running receiver now. He can create enough space for Purdy to connect with him. The timing of a route is everything in Kyle Shanahan’s offense, which must have enticed the 49ers to acquire Allen.
Plus, being the wily veteran that he is, it shouldn’t take him that long to get the playbook down, as complicated as it is. All in all, trading for Allen isn’t going to needle too much.
But his addition will help Purdy and the 49ers’ offense enough.

title: Kyle Shanahan Shares Why the 49ers Traded for Keenan Allen
full_text:
Adding a wide receiver became obvious for the San Francisco 49ers when they attempted to trade for Jauan Jennings.
The need for one grew after their Week 9 win against the Las Vegas Raiders. They couldn't continue to trot out Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing.
That led the 49ers to trade for Indianapolis Colts veteran receiver Keenan Allen . His addition isn't anywhere close to a significant move, but he will contribute nicely.
However, it's unclear why the 49ers wanted to trade for Allen over anyone else, like Josh Downs. On Wednesday, Kyle Shanahan shared why they traded for Allen and how he fits.
"Trying to get the best receiver you can," Shanahan said. "It always starts with separating, catching the football. He's always been as good as anyone at separating. Always had as good hands as anyone, and then how good he plays without the ball. He's a guy who blocks. He never takes a down off and is extremely competitive. A very smart, aware football player."
The keyword in Shanahan's explanation is "separating." Despite being 34 years old, Allen is still a fairly sharp route runner. After Mike Evans , he's probably the second-best on the 49ers at it.
The 49ers needed someone who could carve out space for Brock Purdy to throw to. They couldn't rely on him to make tight-window throws throughout the game.
Purdy can make some of those throws, but it's not what the 49ers want to do. It isn't a sustainable formula for success. It becomes more likely for drives to get stalled out or, worse, an interception is created.
Allen won't be a downfield threat. That's never been his game, but he will be proficient around 10 yards beyond the line of scrimmage.
Whenever the 49ers need a quick outlet or a short-yardage conversion, they can look to Allen. Purdy now has George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Allen has his trio until Evans returns.
The fit makes a lot of sense for the 49ers. Having Downs would've been nice to stretch the field, but having a player who can separate almost at will fits the 49ers better.
"We were really excited to get him. We think he makes us a lot better," Shanahan said. "Keenan has obviously had an unbelievable career. It was cool to turn on his tape and watch him in Indy and still see the same guy, so we were pumped to get him.
